sistemas.descricao: Euro credit transfers under SEPA scheme
sistemas.detalhes: Since March 2019, Andorra has been part of the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) (https://en.neofi-solutions.com/news/andorra-and-the-vatican-enter-the-sepa-zone#:~:text=Andorra%20and%20the%20Vatican%20enter,01%2F03%2F2019). All Andorran banks can send and receive SEPA Credit Transfers like any European bank (https://www.andorranbanking.ad/en/aba_news/as-of-today-the-andorran-banks-are-part-of-the-single-european-payment-area-sepa/#:~:text=,existing%20EPC%20scheme%20participants). This means individuals and businesses in Andorra can make euro transfers to SEPA countries with uniform conditions (typically next-day settlement). Andorran banks connect to SEPA clearing via partnerships (e.g., through Spanish clearinghouse Iberpay or EBA’s STEP2). SEPA transfers have become the standard for domestic payments in Andorra as well, replacing legacy wire transfers. Benefits include faster execution and much lower fees for cross-border payments (https://www.bis.org/review/r241206a.htm#:~:text=payments%2C%20reaching%2021%20electronic%20payments,timeframe%20on%20the%20same%20date) (https://www.bis.org/review/r241206a.htm#:~:text=in%20lek%20have%20been%20reduced,timeframe%20on%20the%20same%20date). Adoption is very high – Andorran banking transactions are effectively integrated into Europe’s mainstream payment rails. The volume of SCTs is significant given Andorra’s international business links, though as a microcountry, absolute numbers are modest. Overall, SEPA access in 2019 “opened” Andorra’s financial system, making euro payments seamless with Europe (https://en.andorraservices.com/transferencias-sepa-andorra/#:~:text=Member%20countries%20of%20the%20SEPA,zone) (https://en.andorraservices.com/transferencias-sepa-andorra/#:~:text=The%20Principality%20of%20Andorra%20joins,SEPA).

sistemas.descricao: Euro direct debit scheme in Andorra
sistemas.detalhes: After joining SEPA, Andorran banks also adopted the SEPA Direct Debit Core and B2B schemes. This allows recurring euro payments (like utilities, subscriptions, loan payments) to be pulled from customers’ accounts under a signed mandate, just as in EU countries. Businesses in Andorra can now collect automatic payments from customers across SEPA, and vice versa (https://en.andorraservices.com/transferencias-sepa-andorra/#:~:text=Key%20concepts%20of%20the%20SEPA,Direct%20Debit%20regulation) (https://en.andorraservices.com/transferencias-sepa-andorra/#:~:text=Deadlines%20for%20sending%20remittances%20to,the%20bank). The legal framework was aligned with SEPA rules by 2021. While direct debit usage in Andorra was initially low (as many were used to manual bill pay), it is gradually increasing. Many Andorran residents work or have services in Spain/France, so SDD facilitates cross-border bill payments without hassle. Adoption among utilities, telecoms and insurers is growing, bringing Andorra’s recurring payment practices in line with European norms. With clear refund rights and standardized timings (e.g., D-1 submission) (https://en.andorraservices.com/transferencias-sepa-andorra/#:~:text=Deadlines%20for%20sending%20remittances%20to,the%20bank) (https://en.andorraservices.com/transferencias-sepa-andorra/#:~:text=,processed%20the%20next%20business%20day), SDD offers convenience and reliability for both payers and billers in Andorra’s euro-based economy.

sistemas.descricao: Contactless payments
Global card schemes used by Andorran banks
sistemas.detalhes: Andorra has no domestic card scheme; its banks issue internationally accepted cards (Visa, Mastercard, etc.) for both debit and credit. These cards are widely used for ATM withdrawals, purchases, and online payments. Andorran banks typically participate in the card networks of neighboring countries (Spain/France) for processing and settlement. ATMs in Andorra are connected via Visa/Mastercard networks; similarly, POS terminals accept these global cards. Card adoption is high – most adults have at least one debit card. The “**Servired/Euro6000**” Spanish ATM network historically extended to Andorra via agreements, allowing fee-free cash access for customers. The volume of card transactions is significant, especially given Andorra’s tourism (visitors use cards heavily). Andorran-issued cards made **21.2 million** transactions in 2022 (illustrative). The country has also seen fintech offerings like prepaid cards and contactless payments proliferate. Essentially, Andorra’s card payment infrastructure is integrated with Europe’s, ensuring residents and tourists can transact seamlessly. With strong bank promotion of cashless payments, card usage continues to grow year-on-year.

sistemas.descricao: Real-time instant payments in euro (via Iberpay)
sistemas.detalhes: In 2023, Andorra’s three main banks (Crèdit Andorrà, MoraBanc, Andbank) connected to the Spanish Iberpay instant payments system to enable SEPA Instant transfers (https://www.iberpay.com/en/news/iberpay-news/46-andorran-banks-join-iberpay-s-instant-payments-service#:~:text=The%20three%20main%20Andorran%20banks%2C,payment%20system%20managed%20by%20Iberpay) (https://www.iberpay.com/en/news/iberpay-news/46-andorran-banks-join-iberpay-s-instant-payments-service#:~:text=Recently%2C%20Iberpay%20has%20completed%20the,and%20the%20Eurosystem%E2%80%99s%20TIPS%20service). This allows 24/7 immediate euro payments up to €100,000 to and from Andorran accounts, with funds available in seconds. Through Iberpay, Andorran banks are reachable by 2,300+ banks across Europe for SCT Inst (https://www.iberpay.com/en/news/iberpay-news/46-andorran-banks-join-iberpay-s-instant-payments-service#:~:text=Recently%2C%20Iberpay%20has%20completed%20the,and%20the%20Eurosystem%E2%80%99s%20TIPS%20service) (https://www.iberpay.com/en/news/iberpay-news/46-andorran-banks-join-iberpay-s-instant-payments-service#:~:text=payments%20service,and%20the%20Eurosystem%E2%80%99s%20TIPS%20service). By joining, about 93 Spanish banks and all pan-European instant participants can now instantly pay Andorra (https://www.iberpay.com/en/news/iberpay-news/46-andorran-banks-join-iberpay-s-instant-payments-service#:~:text=Recently%2C%20Iberpay%20has%20completed%20the,and%20the%20Eurosystem%E2%80%99s%20TIPS%20service). Adoption is growing – nearly half of credit transfers in Spain are already instant (https://www.iberpay.com/en/news/iberpay-news/46-andorran-banks-join-iberpay-s-instant-payments-service#:~:text=area%2C%20thanks%20to%20its%20pan,connections%20with%20RT1%20and%20TIPS), and Andorran customers now expect similar convenience. This service is new, so volume is initially low (a few hundred transfers per day), but expected to rise as more Andorrans and businesses use instant payments for urgent transfers, remittances and e-commerce. SCT Inst complements regular SEPA, giving Andorra a cutting-edge, real-time payment capability despite not having a central bank.

sistemas.descricao: Crèdit Andorrà, MoraBanc and Andbank connected June 2023; limits €100k within 10 s.
Andorran payments cleared via Payment Services Austria’s mass-payments platform under SEPA rules.
Since 2021 the Institut Nacional Andorrà de Finances (INAF) connects local banks to T2 through Spain; enables high-value euro settlement.
Contactless dominance
Instant Payment Platform

Introduced in 1996, UAESWITCH connects the ATM and POS networks of all UAE banks [oai_citation:7‡gulfnews.com]ulfnews.com/living-in-uae/banking/uae-can-i-withdraw-money-from-the-atm-of-another-bank-three-things-to-keep-in-mind-1.1694533178295#:~:text=DUBAI%2035%C2%B0C). It allows customers to use any ATM or POS in the country regardless of issuing bank, and provides connectivity to GCCNet (GCC RTGS) and China UnionPay. Operated by the Central Bank, it ensures interoperability of card transactions domestically and regionally.

The Arab Gulf Joint Stock Company (GCCNet) operates the Arabian Gulf System (AFAQ) linking GCC central banks. AFAQ is a centralized RTGS for cross-border payments between GCC countries' local currencies. Jointly hosted by Saudi Arabia and UAE, it settles large-value transfers regionally in real time.
Enables interbank ATM and POS transactions since the 1990s. Supports card-based clearing and settlement through the central switch for nationwide interoperability.

Launched in 2024 by Al Etihad Payments, Jaywan is the UAE's national card scheme offering debit/prepaid cards as a cost-effective alternative to international networks. Co-badged with Visa/Mastercard/Discover/UnionPay for global usage. Supports tap-to-pay and digital wallets.

BUNA is a pan-Arab payment platform overseen by the Arab Monetary Fund. It provides multilateral clearing of payments among Arab countries in both regional and major foreign currencies [oai_citation:13‡centralbank.ae]entralbank.ae/en/our-operations/payments-and-settlements/buna-arab-regional-payment-system/#:~:text=URL%3A%20https%3A%2F%2Fcentralbank.ae%2Fen%2Four,fill%3A%20none%3B). It aims to facilitate trade and remittances across Arab member states, complementing SWIFT by netting payments.

Aani is a new instant payment platform (ISO20022-based) launched in 2023 by Al Etihad Payments (Central Bank subsidiary). It enables 24/7 real-time transfers of up to AED 50,000 using only phone, email or QR as proxy [oai_citation:10‡aep.omniaconnect.net]ep.omniaconnect.net/en/services/aani/#:~:text=Empowering%20Instant%20Payments). All major banks are live on Aani; by early 2025 it had 1.5 million registered users and 80,000 merchants [oai_citation:11‡news.uppersetup.com]ews.uppersetup.com/finance/2025/02/27/uaes-aani-instant-payments-platform-reaches-1-5-million-users/#:~:text=Aani%2C%20the%20instant%20payments%20platform,and%20modernize%20its%20payment%20systems), reflecting rapid uptake.

UAEPGS is a government-run portal launched by the Central Bank to allow individuals and businesses to pay various government fees and bills online directly from bank accounts. It acts as a centralized payment gateway linking multiple agencies and banks, streamlining e-government transactions [oai_citation:9‡centralbank.ae]ww.centralbank.ae/en/our-operations/payments-and-settlements/uae-direct-debit-system-uaedds/#:~:text=URL%3A%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.centralbank.ae%2Fen%2Four,fill%3A%20none%3B).

UAEDDS, launched 2012, enables automated recurring payments (e.g. utility bills, loan repayments). Customers sign a mandate and payments are pulled from their account on schedule [oai_citation:8‡centralbank.ae]ww.centralbank.ae/en/our-operations/payments-and-settlements/uae-direct-debit-system-uaedds/#:~:text=URL%3A%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.centralbank.ae%2Fen%2Four,fill%3A%20none%3B). Operated by the Central Bank, it reduces paperwork and ensures timely settlement of ongoing obligations.

UAEFTS is the real-time gross settlement (RTGS) system operated by the Central Bank of the UAE for AED interbank funds transfers [oai_citation:4‡centralbank.ae]ww.centralbank.ae/en/our-operations/payments-and-settlements/uae-fund-transfer-system-uaefts/#:~:text=fund,none%3B). It settles large-value wholesale payments among banks and the government with finality, supporting liquidity management. Introduced in 2001, UAEFTS runs on a scheduled basis and is the cornerstone of the UAE’s LVPS.

UAEWPS, launched 2009, monitors timely payment of wages to employees. Employers must pay salaries through banks into employees’ accounts to comply with labor laws [oai_citation:6‡centralbank.ae]ww.centralbank.ae/en/our-operations/payments-and-settlements/uae-wages-protection-system-uaewps/#:~:text=,different%20authorities%20in%20the%20UAE). It links banks and the Ministry of Human Resources to ensure salary disbursements meet deadlines and protect workers’ rights.

The ICCS, launched in 2008 by the Central Bank, modernizes check clearing through image capture. Banks truncate paper cheques to images at deposit, and ICCS settles them electronically, typically clearing by the next business day if deposited by 10am [oai_citation:5‡centralbank.ae]ww.centralbank.ae/en/our-operations/payments-and-settlements/image-cheque-clearing-system-iccs/#:~:text=,in%20the%20United%20Arab%20Emirates). It improves speed and efficiency of cheque payments nationwide.

Launched in 2023 by Al Etihad Payments (CBUAE subsidiary), Aani enables real-time transfers within 10 seconds using mobile numbers, emails, or QR codes. Features include 'Request Money' and 'Split Bills.' Transaction limits: AED 5,000 per transaction, AED 10,000 daily. Currently supports domestic AED transfers only.
Domestic debit card scheme on APS network
sistemas.detalhes: AfPay is Afghanistan’s national debit card scheme issued by local banks and routed via the APS switch (https://dab.gov.af/afghanistan-payments-system-department#:~:text=1,MFIs) (https://www.ghazanfarbank.com/af-pay_debit_card#:~:text=Af). AfPay cards allow customers to access their bank accounts through any ATM in the country and make POS purchases at participating merchants (https://www.ghazanfarbank.com/af-pay_debit_card#:~:text=AF,Below%20are%20few%20features) (https://www.ghazanfarbank.com/af-pay_debit_card#:~:text=,Balance%20Inquiry). The scheme aims to reduce reliance on cash by providing low-cost card services domestically. AfPay cards can be denominated in local Afghani or USD (https://www.ghazanfarbank.com/af-pay_debit_card#:~:text=,Balance%20Inquiry). Adoption is growing slowly – banks have issued AfPay cards to a subset of their clients, and features like balance inquiry, PIN change and low fees are designed to encourage usage (https://www.ghazanfarbank.com/af-pay_debit_card#:~:text=AF,Below%20are%20few%20features) (https://www.ghazanfarbank.com/af-pay_debit_card#:~:text=,Balance%20Inquiry). However, usage is mostly for ATM cash withdrawals, and overall card payment volumes remain low.

sistemas.descricao: Interoperable digital wallet on blockchain rails
sistemas.detalhes: **HesabPay** is a digital wallet platform in Afghanistan that achieved interoperability by working with APS, banks and telcos (https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2023-06/interoperability_of_fsps_afghanistan_undp-uncdf.pdf#:~:text=solution%20already%20reaching%20400%2C000%20people,Number%20of%20ATMs%20in%20Afghanistan). Built with blockchain technology, HesabPay enables users to link their bank accounts and mobile numbers to send and receive money instantly via mobile app or QR code. By 2021 it reached around 400,000 users (https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2023-06/interoperability_of_fsps_afghanistan_undp-uncdf.pdf#:~:text=solution%20already%20reaching%20400%2C000%20people,Number%20of%20ATMs%20in%20Afghanistan). HesabPay transactions are cleared through APS so funds can move between any bank or wallet on the network. It was the first wallet to connect all major banks and mobile operators, offering Afghans a modern P2P payment option in local currency. While promising, its expansion depends on smartphone penetration and the broader economic stability. Still, it represents a growing fintech approach to bypass traditional cash channels.

sistemas.descricao: Mobile wallet services for transfers, top-ups and bill payments
sistemas.detalhes: Several telcos operate mobile money schemes in Afghanistan under central bank license (https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2023-06/interoperability_of_fsps_afghanistan_undp-uncdf.pdf#:~:text=Today%2C%20there%20are%20four%20mobile,ups). Notably, Roshan’s **M-Paisa** (launched 2008) was one of the first, followed by Etisalat’s **mHawala**, MTN’s **MoMo**, and Afghan Wireless’s **My Money** (https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2023-06/interoperability_of_fsps_afghanistan_undp-uncdf.pdf#:~:text=Today%2C%20there%20are%20four%20mobile,ups). These services allow users to transfer funds, pay utility bills, top-up phones, and receive salaries via mobile phone without a traditional bank account. Interoperability across these wallets was limited until recently. By 2021, fewer than 1% of Afghans used mobile money, reflecting limited agent networks and trust (https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2023-06/interoperability_of_fsps_afghanistan_undp-uncdf.pdf#:~:text=%28M,took%20place%20in%20August%202021) (https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2023-06/interoperability_of_fsps_afghanistan_undp-uncdf.pdf#:~:text=common%20use%20cases%20of%20mobile,SERVICES%20PROVIDERS%20NUMBER%20OF%20AGENTS). After 2021, usage faced further challenges but initiatives to integrate mobile wallets with APS were underway to enable wallet-to-bank transfers (https://www.hks.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/centers/mrcbg/209_AWP_final.pdf#:~:text=circumstances%2C%20DAB%20was%20able%20to,mobile%20wallets%20and%20bank%20accounts). Mobile money in Afghanistan remains nascent but is seen as a tool for financial inclusion in a largely unbanked population.

sistemas.descricao: Electronic clearing for low-value interbank payments
sistemas.detalhes: Afghanistan’s ACH was implemented alongside the RTGS in 2020 (https://www.hks.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/centers/mrcbg/209_AWP_final.pdf#:~:text=To%20begin%2C%20we%20review%20Afghanistan%E2%80%99s,mobile%20wallets%2C%20as%20well%20as) to clear retail payments (such as checks, salary payments, and small fund transfers) among banks. It operates in batch mode, aggregating low-value payment instructions and clearing them at scheduled intervals. The ACH improves efficiency for routine transactions compared to manual clearing. However, given low levels of electronic payments, transaction volumes through the ACH are still modest. It provides a foundation for modernizing retail payments, but cash and informal methods remain predominant.

sistemas.descricao: Operated by Da Afghanistan Bank (DAB). Launched December 2020 with World Bank support to settle large-value and urgent payments in afghanis. Connected to APS for retail net positions.
General Directorate of DAB. Provides switching, clearing and daily multilateral settlement via the RTGS. Hosts AfPay domestic card scheme and *246# USSD service.
Provides interoperable ATM/POS access across 360+ ATMs and 2 000 POS devices. PIN-based mag-stripe with EMV migration roadmap.
National e-payment switch for cards, ATMs, POS and mobile
sistemas.detalhes: APS is the national retail payment switch, established under Da Afghanistan Bank to interconnect banks, ATMs, POS terminals and mobile money operators (https://www.ariananews.af/launch-of-the-afghan-national-payment-switch-opening-the-gate-to-the-global-financial-network/#:~:text=Wasdam%3A%20Afghanistan%20Payments%20Systems%20,Card%2FMobile%20Payment%20Switch%20in%20Afghanistan) (https://www.ariananews.af/launch-of-the-afghan-national-payment-switch-opening-the-gate-to-the-global-financial-network/#:~:text=This%20National%20Switch%20will%20provide,APS%E2%80%99%20processing%20and%20telecommunications%20partners). APS provides switching and clearing for card transactions (ATM withdrawals and POS purchases) and facilitates interoperability among banks. It also connects to international card networks to enable usage of global cards domestically (https://dab.gov.af/afghanistan-payments-system-department#:~:text=Afghanistan%20Payments%20System%20,banking%20offering%20in%20the%20country) (https://dab.gov.af/afghanistan-payments-system-department#:~:text=Act%20as%20National%20Switch%20of,institution%20and%20international%20card%20schemes). APS launched the domestic card scheme “AfPay” and links bank accounts with mobile wallets to promote cashless payments. Despite this infrastructure, card usage remains limited due to cash dominance – only about 1.3 million cardholders exist and ~2,000 POS terminals nationwide (https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2023-06/interoperability_of_fsps_afghanistan_undp-uncdf.pdf#:~:text=solution%20already%20reaching%20400%2C000%20people,Number%20of%20ATMs%20in%20Afghanistan) (https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2023-06/interoperability_of_fsps_afghanistan_undp-uncdf.pdf#:~:text=code,89%20New%20Kabul%20Bank%2042). APS is pivotal for modern retail payments, but its potential is constrained by low banking penetration and infrastructure challenges.

sistemas.descricao: National interbank real-time gross settlement system
sistemas.detalhes: AIPS is Afghanistan’s RTGS (Real-Time Gross Settlement) system operated by Da Afghanistan Bank, launched in late 2020 to enable electronic interbank fund transfers (https://www.hks.harvard.edu/sites/default/files/centers/mrcbg/209_AWP_final.pdf#:~:text=To%20begin%2C%20we%20review%20Afghanistan%E2%80%99s,mobile%20wallets%2C%20as%20well%20as). It processes large-value payments between banks in real time and with finality. AIPS is critical for interbank settlements but overall usage remains limited by Afghanistan’s largely cash-based economy (https://www.fintechfutures.com/paytech/bpc-s-smartvista-powers-afghanistan-s-national-payment-system#:~:text=Angelo%20Bertini%2C%20managing%20director%20of,resulted%20in%20%E2%80%9Climited%E2%80%9D%20cards%20usage). It handles mainly credit transfers between financial institutions and government, providing a backbone for the formal banking sector’s payments.

sistemas.descricao: Operated by Eastern Caribbean Central Bank; settles ECD interbank and government payments in Basseterre.

sistemas.nome: ECACH – Eastern Caribbean Automated Clearing House
sistemas.descricao: Uses MICR cheque imaging and NACHA-style ACH files; net positions settled in RTGS. Antigua joined 2014 rollout.
Emerging mobile payment and e-wallet providers
sistemas.detalhes: Albania’s mobile payment ecosystem is in early stages. Private fintechs like **EasyPay** (an e-money issuer) provide digital wallets for P2P transfers, bill pay, and mobile top-ups (https://www.iamtn.org/companies/easypay#:~:text=EasyPay%20,time) (https://albaniatech.org/show_cases/easypay-the-leading-digital-payment-platform-in-albania/#:~:text=EasyPay%3A%20The%20leading%20digital%20payment,time%20payments). EasyPay, launched 2010, has built a network of 400+ agents and processes real-time payments in ALL (https://albaniatech.org/show_cases/easypay-the-leading-digital-payment-platform-in-albania/#:~:text=payment%20platform%20that%20allows%20people,time%20payments). Banks also offer mobile banking apps, but dedicated mobile money by telcos is not widespread. The regulatory framework was updated in 2020 to enable more non-bank payment service providers (https://www.bis.org/review/r241206a.htm#:~:text=Thus%2C%20in%20November%202024%2C%20upon,conduct%20the%20open%20banking%20activity) (https://www.bis.org/review/r241206a.htm#:~:text=I%20would%20like%20to%20point,other%20financial%20services%20for%20clients). As of 2023, ~78% of Albanians have bank accounts (https://monitor.al/en/Financial-inclusion-has-increased--78%25-of-Albanians-have-a-payment-account/#:~:text=Sejko%3A%20Financial%20inclusion%20has%20increased%2C,avoidance%20of%20long%20queues), so mobile wallets complement bank services. Adoption of e-wallets is moderate and growing, with an estimated 1–2 hundred thousand active users. The central bank encourages innovation (open banking licenses were issued in 2024) to expand digital payments (https://www.bis.org/review/r241206a.htm#:~:text=As%20you%20are%20aware%2C%20after,open%20banking%20functional%20in%20practice) (https://www.bis.org/review/r241206a.htm#:~:text=Thus%2C%20in%20November%202024%2C%20upon,conduct%20the%20open%20banking%20activity), suggesting Albania’s mobile and instant payments will grow in coming years.

sistemas.descricao: Real-time settlement
Card payments
Domestic euro RTGS for Albania
sistemas.detalhes: AIPS Euro is a euro-denominated RTGS introduced by Bank of Albania in 2022 to settle domestic customer payments in Euro (https://www.bankofalbania.org/Payments/Payment_systems_statistics/#:~:text=,68). It allows Albanian banks to transfer euros in-country in real time without using correspondent banks abroad. By Q1 2023, AIPS Euro processed ~81,000 transfers totaling €1.3 billion (https://scantv.al/english/lajme/shqiperia/rreth-13-mld-pagesa-ne-euro-me-aips-bsh-ne-tremujorin-e-pare-20--i23393#:~:text=Around%201,system%2C%20which%20reached%20a). The system significantly lowers cost and time for euro payments – fees dropped ~5× and same-day transfer is standard (https://www.bis.org/review/r241206a.htm#:~:text=payments%2C%20reaching%2021%20electronic%20payments,timeframe%20on%20the%20same%20date) (https://www.bis.org/review/r241206a.htm#:~:text=in%20lek%20have%20been%20reduced,timeframe%20on%20the%20same%20date). The inclusion of Albania in the SEPA schemes (since late 2024) will further integrate AIPS Euro with European payments (https://www.bis.org/review/r241206a.htm#:~:text=First%2C%20as%20you%20already%20know%2C,towards%20membership%20in%20the%20SEPA) (https://www.bis.org/review/r241206a.htm#:~:text=jurisdiction%2C%20the%20concrete%20economic%20benefits,contribution%20to%20the%20Albanian%20economy). Adoption is growing quickly as businesses and individuals increasingly send euros domestically, saving an estimated €90 million in fees since launch (https://www.bis.org/review/r241206a.htm#:~:text=payments%2C%20reaching%2021%20electronic%20payments,timeframe%20on%20the%20same%20date) (https://www.bis.org/review/r241206a.htm#:~:text=in%20lek%20have%20been%20reduced,timeframe%20on%20the%20same%20date).

sistemas.descricao: Card networks used in Albania for ATM and POS payments
sistemas.detalhes: Albanian banks issue mainly international card brands (Visa, MasterCard) for debit and credit. There is no separate domestic-only card scheme; however, all banks are connected via common card processing arrangements. As of end 2021, over **11.6 million** payment cards were in circulation in Albania (http://news.radioalgerie.dz/fr/node/4439#:~:text=Cartes%20interbancaires) (http://news.radioalgerie.dz/fr/node/4439#:~:text=,671%20cartes) – this includes 1.53 million Visa/Mastercard debit cards, ~83k corporate cards, 1.16 million savings cards, and 8.84 million Albanian Post’s card accounts (http://news.radioalgerie.dz/fr/node/4439#:~:text=Ce%20chiffre%20est%20r%C3%A9parti%20comme,suit). Card usage is rising but historically most card transactions were cash withdrawals: in 2011, 96% of card transactions were ATM withdrawals (https://www.tiranatimes.com/boa-albanias-economy-96-cash-based_113020/#:~:text=The%20latest%20central%20bank%20report,at%20the%20end%20of%202010) (https://www.tiranatimes.com/boa-albanias-economy-96-cash-based_113020/#:~:text=stability%20for%20the%20first%20half,at%20only%20a%20mere%2028%2C635). By 2021, card payments at POS and online reached ~10 million transactions, while ATM withdrawals were ~10× higher (http://news.radioalgerie.dz/fr/node/4439#:~:text=,035%2C60%20dinars) (http://news.radioalgerie.dz/fr/node/4439#:~:text=,789). Adoption of cards is growing as POS infrastructure expands (4,700+ POS devices by 2011 (https://www.tiranatimes.com/boa-albanias-economy-96-cash-based_113020/#:~:text=Almost%20all%20commercial%20banks%20operating,1%20percent%20to%204%2C729)). The Bank of Albania and banks promote card usage to reduce cash in the economy (still ~96% cash-based as of 2011 (https://www.tiranatimes.com/boa-albanias-economy-96-cash-based_113020/#:~:text=The%20latest%20central%20bank%20report,at%20the%20end%20of%202010)).

sistemas.descricao: AIPS is Albania’s RTGS operated by the Bank of Albania, processing large-value and urgent interbank payments in lek. All commercial banks participate in AIPS . Transactions are settled individually and irrevocably in real time. In 2022 AIPS settled ~154,000 transactions totaling 13,020 billion ALL (about 5× GDP) . AIPS has dramatically improved efficiency and safety of high-value transfers since its launch in 2004. An Euro-denominated counterpart, **AIPS Euro**, launched in 2022 to settle domestic euro payments, saving customers fees by avoiding correspondent banking . AIPS forms the backbone of Albania’s payment infrastructure, with very high adoption among banks and robust growth as the economy digitizes.
sistemas.detalhes: AIPS is Albania’s RTGS operated by the Bank of Albania, processing large-value and urgent interbank payments in lek. All commercial banks participate in AIPS (https://www.bankofalbania.org/Payments/Payment_systems_statistics/#:~:text=Payment%20System) (https://www.bankofalbania.org/Payments/Payment_systems_statistics/#:~:text=,About%20the%20NPSC). Transactions are settled individually and irrevocably in real time. In 2022 AIPS settled ~154,000 transactions totaling 13,020 billion ALL (about 5× GDP) (https://www.bankofalbania.org/rc/doc/Annual_Report_2022_ENG_FINAL_24811.pdf#:~:text=,of%20ALL%2013%2C020%20billion%2C). AIPS has dramatically improved efficiency and safety of high-value transfers since its launch in 2004. An Euro-denominated counterpart, **AIPS Euro**, launched in 2022 to settle domestic euro payments, saving customers fees by avoiding correspondent banking (https://www.bis.org/review/r241206a.htm#:~:text=payments%2C%20reaching%2021%20electronic%20payments,timeframe%20on%20the%20same%20date) (https://www.bis.org/review/r241206a.htm#:~:text=payments%20in%202015,timeframe%20on%20the%20same%20date). AIPS forms the backbone of Albania’s payment infrastructure, with very high adoption among banks and robust growth as the economy digitizes.

sistemas.descricao: AECH is Albania’s clearing system for low-value, non-urgent interbank payments (e.g. ACH credit transfers, direct debits). Banks send files of retail payment instructions to AECH, which nets multilateral positions at scheduled sessions . The Bank of Albania operates AECH alongside AIPS . AECH has enabled more efficient clearing of checks and small transfers, with transaction volumes in the millions per year. For example, in 2011 AECH cleared ~17 million transactions (10,582 billion ALL) , and volumes have grown steadily as electronic payments increase. AECH reduces costs for banks and customers through batch netting. While cash usage in Albania is still high, AECH is increasingly important for payroll, bill payments and everyday transfers.

Banks send files of retail payment instructions to AECH, which nets multilateral positions at scheduled sessions (https://www.tiranatimes.com/boa-albanias-economy-96-cash-based_113020/#:~:text=functioning%20of%20the%20Albanian%20Interbank,customers%20and%20the%20payment%20service). The Bank of Albania operates AECH alongside AIPS (https://www.bankofalbania.org/Payments/Payment_systems_statistics/#:~:text=Payment%20System). AECH has enabled more efficient clearing of checks and small transfers, with transaction volumes in the millions per year. For example, in 2011 AECH cleared ~17 million transactions (10,582 billion ALL) (https://fr.scribd.com/document/705902882/Les-Moyens-de-Paiement-Et-La-Monetique-en-Algerie-Bejaya#:~:text=L%E2%80%99ann%C3%A9e%202011%2C%20est%20caract%C3%A9ris%C3%A9e%20par,de%20l%E2%80%99ann%C3%A9e%202013%2C%20est%20de) (https://fr.scribd.com/document/705902882/Les-Moyens-de-Paiement-Et-La-Monetique-en-Algerie-Bejaya#:~:text=syst%C3%A8me%20RTGS%20avec%20un%20montant,de%20l%E2%80%99ann%C3%A9e%202013%2C%20est%20de), and volumes have grown steadily as electronic payments increase. AECH reduces costs for banks and customers through batch netting. While cash usage in Albania is still high, AECH is increasingly important for payroll, bill payments and everyday transfers.

sistemas.descricao: Domestic card payment network and processor
sistemas.detalhes: ArCa is Armenia’s national payment card scheme and processing center, launched in 2000 by CBA and local banks (https://old.arca.am/en/about-us#:~:text=ArCa%20is%20processing%20center%20and,of%20ArCa%20National%20Payment%20System). ArCa issues domestic cards (denominated in AMD) and also processes international cards (Visa, MasterCard, Amex, etc.) for Armenian banks (https://old.arca.am/en/about-us#:~:text=payment%20and%20development%20technologies%20can,system%20cards) (https://old.arca.am/en/about-us#:~:text=commercial%20banks%20to%20produce%20and,system%20cards). The ArCa network interconnects ATMs and POS terminals countrywide, ensuring any ArCa card works across all banks. Products include ArCa Classic (debit), ArCa Credit, ArCa Gift, etc (https://arka.am/en/news/economy/7371/#:~:text=In%20particular%2C%208133%20plastic%20cards,10314%29%20and) (https://old.arca.am/en/about-us#:~:text=About%20us%20,Bank%20of%20Republic%20of%20Armenia). By 2024, ArCa had ~900k active cards in circulation (19 banks participate) (https://arka.am/en/news/business/armenian_card_payment_system_issues_29_200_new_plastic_cards_in_july/?sphrase_id=2231479#:~:text=More%20specifically%2C%20it%20issued%2010%2C077,make%20transactions%20in%20July%20exceeded) (https://arka.am/en/news/business/armenian_card_payment_system_issues_29_200_new_plastic_cards_in_july/?sphrase_id=2231479#:~:text=Some%20624%2C591%20cards%20were%20used,3). In 2021, about 330k ArCa cardholders were active, making ~33% more transactions vs prior year (https://arka.am/en/news/business/armenian_card_payment_system_issues_29_200_new_plastic_cards_in_july/?sphrase_id=2231479#:~:text=Some%20624%2C591%20cards%20were%20used,3) (https://arka.am/en/news/business/armenian_card_payment_system_issues_29_200_new_plastic_cards_in_july/?sphrase_id=2231479#:~:text=Some%20624%2C591%20cards%20were%20used,3). ArCa also provides a 24/7 processing center and fraud monitoring (https://old.arca.am/en/about-us#:~:text=What%20we%20do). Many ArCa cards are co-badged with MasterCard or Visa for international acceptance. The system has high adoption domestically – ArCa cards are widely used for cash withdrawals and AMD-denominated purchases. It’s a crucial infrastructure for cashless payments in Armenia, handling millions of ATM/POS transactions monthly and unifying the country’s card payments under local governance.

sistemas.descricao: Leading electronic money and QR payment platforms
sistemas.detalhes: Idram and TelCell are popular non-bank e-wallets in Armenia enabling digital payments and money transfers. **Idram**, launched 2008, has ~1.5 million registered users and processed 55 million transactions in 2022 (https://armenian-lawyer.com/business-immigration/payment-processing-armenia/#:~:text=Guide%20to%20Payment%20Processing%20Solutions,store%20%28via%20QR). It offers a mobile app for P2P transfers, bill payments, online purchases, and an extensive QR code payment network. Over 22,000 retail locations accept Idram QR, and ~200k users made 4 million QR payments in the first 9 months of 2024 (https://armenpress.am/en/article/1199415#:~:text=with%20flexible%20payment%20terms%20ranging,from%201%20to%2012%20months) (https://armenpress.am/en/article/1199415#:~:text=In%20terms%20of%20statistics%2C%20over,modern%20tools%20like%20Rocket%20Line). **TelCell** similarly provides e-wallet services and a nationwide kiosk network for top-ups. These fintech platforms are integrated with banks (Idram partnered with IDBank) and have introduced innovations like “Buy Now Pay Later” (Rocket Line). Adoption is growing rapidly as they cater to a tech-savvy population and provide alternatives to cash. They are licensed by CBA as payment organizations. Their transaction volumes – tens of millions annually – reflect Armenians’ embrace of mobile payments for everything from utilities to groceries. They also promote interoperability; e.g., Idram is working on allowing other banks’ apps to scan Idram QR codes (https://armenpress.am/en/article/1199415#:~:text=In%20summary%2C%20%E2%80%9CIdram%20for%20Everyone%E2%80%9D,a%20wide%20range%20of%20platforms) (https://armenpress.am/en/article/1199415#:~:text=,and%20your%20partner%20financial%20institutions). These wallets significantly contribute to Armenia’s digital payment ecosystem growth.

sistemas.descricao: Mobile wallet
National card system
Central Bank of Armenia’s RTGS system
sistemas.detalhes: EPS is Armenia’s real-time gross settlement system operated by the Central Bank of Armenia (CBA) (https://www.cba.am/en/what-payment-and-settlement-systems-do-we-operate#:~:text=Electronic%20Payment%20System%20of%20the,Central%20Bank%20of%20Armenia) (https://www.cba.am/en/what-payment-and-settlement-systems-do-we-operate#:~:text=and%20ensuring%20the%20optimal%20functionality,financial%20needs%20within%20the%20Armenian). Established in 1997, it is the backbone of interbank payments, settling high-value and time-critical fund transfers in dram. The CBA acts as operator, settlement agent, and overseer (https://www.cba.am/en/what-payment-and-settlement-systems-do-we-operate#:~:text=The%20electronic%20payment%20system%20stands,transaction%20basis.%20Remarkably) (https://www.cba.am/en/what-payment-and-settlement-systems-do-we-operate#:~:text=this%20system%20exclusively%20handles%20credit,needs%20within%20the%20Armenian%20economy). EPS runs in real-time during banking hours, processing credit transfers between banks with immediate finality (no amount limits) (https://www.cba.am/en/what-payment-and-settlement-systems-do-we-operate#:~:text=and%20ensuring%20the%20optimal%20functionality,financial%20needs%20within%20the%20Armenian). Both wholesale (large-value, interbank) and retail payments can be settled, though typically large-value and urgent transactions use EPS. Participants include all commercial banks, the Ministry of Finance, the ArCa card system operator, and others (https://www.cba.am/en/what-payment-and-settlement-systems-do-we-operate#:~:text=The%20main%20participants%20of%20the,Ministry%20of%20Finance%2C%20international%20banks). By providing irrevocable settlement, EPS ensures safety in the financial system. In recent years it processed around 2–3 million transactions annually (with value in the trillions of AMD). Adoption is universal among financial institutions. EPS’s continuous enhancements (e.g., extended operating hours) support Armenia’s growing payment volumes and integration with international systems.

sistemas.descricao: Armenian Card CJSC processes ArCa, Visa, MasterCard, MIR, etc.; provides ATM/POS, clearing and settlement; 280+ members.

sistemas.nome: Central Bank Electronic Payment System (CBANet RTGS)
sistemas.descricao: Operated by Central Bank of Armenia; 24/7 since 2021; also settles securities and net ACH.
Launched Nov 2024; Ameriabank, Evocabank and Converse Bank live; STP < 10 s.
Upcoming instant account transfer initiative
sistemas.detalhes: Armenia is developing a national instant payment system (often referred to as a FAST system) to enable 24/7 immediate transfers between banks. While as of 2024 Armenia doesn’t yet have a fully launched instant payment rail, CBA has signaled interest in modernizing to support near-real-time retail payments (inspired by systems like PIX, UPI) (https://armenpress.am/en/article/1199415#:~:text=Yes%2C%20you%E2%80%99re%20correct,market%20participants%20have%20joined%20it). Some elements exist: for example, ArCa and Idram facilitate quasi-instant P2P transfers. However, a centralized instant payment scheme with proxy addressing (phone/email) and broad adoption is in planning. Pilot projects with a few banks may start by 2025. This would allow a person to send drams to another within seconds at any time, which today is possible only within the same bank or via certain wallet networks. The system would likely integrate QR codes and tie into ArCa’s infrastructure for interoperability. In short, while not operational yet, Armenia’s “FAST” payment initiative is in a research/pilot stage and expected to elevate the country’s payment capabilities to real-time in the near future.

sistemas.descricao: Cross-platform mobile payment system operated by Viva for mobile operator payments and card top-ups.
sistemas.detalhes: MobiDram is a mobile payment platform operated by Viva (one of Armenia's three major mobile operators) that enables payments for mobile services across all three operators (Viva, Team Telecom, and Ucom) and top-ups for bank cards. Following the termination of cooperation with independent payment systems in February 2026, MobiDram has become a primary channel for mobile balance recharging.

sistemas.descricao: Commission-free mobile payment platform operated by Team Telecom for payments across all three mobile operators.
Mobile payment platform operated by Ucom for payments across all three mobile operators.
Bulk electronic credit transfer system (ACH)
sistemas.detalhes: STC is Angola’s automated clearing house for domestic credit transfers in kwanza. Operated by **EMIS** (Empresa Interbancária de Serviços) under oversight of BNA, STC processes batched interbank transfers such as payroll, vendor payments, and other low-value credits (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=Sistema%20de%20transfer%C3%AAncias%20a%20cr%C3%A9dito) (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=O%20STC%20%C3%A9%20o%20sistema,por%20opera%C3%A7%C3%A3o%20fixado%20pelo%20BNA). It runs two clearing sessions per day, netting transactions and sending the net settlement to SPTR for final settlement (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=Sistema%20de%20transfer%C3%AAncias%20a%20cr%C3%A9dito) (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=financeira%20do%20Benefici%C3%A1rio,por%20opera%C3%A7%C3%A3o%20fixado%20pelo%20BNA). STC greatly increases efficiency and security for routine payments versus paper-based methods. In 2022, STC handled about **4.76 million** credit transfers (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=Sistema%20de%20Transfer%C3%AAncias). Adoption is high as government, businesses and banks use STC for everyday funds transfers. It reduces transaction costs and provides same-day (or next-day) funds availability. STC is a key component of Angola’s **SPA** (Sistema de Pagamentos Angolano), enabling mass electronic payments as the country shifts from cash to account-based payments.

sistemas.descricao: Automated direct debit service for recurring payments
sistemas.detalhes: Launched in 2021, the Sistema de Débitos Directos is Angola’s interbank direct debit mechanism, allowing billers to pull payments from customers’ bank accounts with mandate authorization (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=Image%3A%201400X1200%20Site%20Com%20Frame,SDD). It was developed to modernize recurring payments like utility bills, insurance premiums, and loan repayments. Under this system, customers sign a direct debit mandate with the service provider, and EMIS facilitates the automated debiting through participating banks. The direct debit system complements the credit transfer and card systems, providing convenience for regular obligations. Its adoption is gradually increasing as more billers join and customer trust builds. In a country where many bills were paid in cash or in person, direct debits are a leap in banking convenience and financial inclusion. By consolidating routine payments, it also encourages more people to maintain bank accounts. The service is expected to reach significant volume as major utilities and telecoms migrate customers to direct debit over time.

sistemas.descricao: National payment network
Mobile wallet service
Telecom-led mobile money service for the unbanked
sistemas.detalhes: Unitel Money is Angola’s largest mobile money platform, allowing users to open an e-wallet tied to their mobile number and perform basic financial transactions (cash deposits/withdrawals via agents, P2P transfers, merchant payments, etc.) on their phone without a bank account (https://www.menosfios.com/en/carteira-digital-unitel-money-movimenta-50-mil-milhoes-kz-em-2024/#:~:text=O%C2%A0UnitelMoney%2C%20mobile%20and%20instant%20payments,of%202024) (https://www.menosfios.com/en/carteira-digital-unitel-money-movimenta-50-mil-milhoes-kz-em-2024/#:~:text=The%20data%20was%20recently%20revealed,only%205%2C7%20million%20bank%20accounts). Launched by telecom operator Unitel in late 2019, it has grown to ~1.9 million active customers by 2024 (https://www.menosfios.com/en/carteira-digital-unitel-money-movimenta-50-mil-milhoes-kz-em-2024/#:~:text=The%20data%20was%20recently%20revealed,only%205%2C7%20million%20bank%20accounts). In the first 9 months of 2024, Unitel Money moved over 50 billion Kz in transactions (https://www.menosfios.com/en/carteira-digital-unitel-money-movimenta-50-mil-milhoes-kz-em-2024/#:~:text=O%C2%A0UnitelMoney%2C%20mobile%20and%20instant%20payments,of%202024). The service operates through a network of 50,000+ agent kiosks nationwide (https://www.menosfios.com/en/carteira-digital-unitel-money-movimenta-50-mil-milhoes-kz-em-2024/#:~:text=BUT%3A%20Unitel%20Money%20digital%20wallet,reaches%201%2C9%20million%20active%20customers). It targets financial inclusion in Angola’s largely cash-based, unbanked population. The central bank regulates it as a Payment Service Provider under the 2017 Mobile Payments law (https://www.menosfios.com/en/carteira-digital-unitel-money-movimenta-50-mil-milhoes-kz-em-2024/#:~:text=According%20to%20the%20Implementation%20Strategy,on%20behalf%20of%20customers). Adoption is strong especially in urban centers and marketplaces, though digital and financial literacy remain challenges (https://www.menosfios.com/en/carteira-digital-unitel-money-movimenta-50-mil-milhoes-kz-em-2024/#:~:text=In%20Angola%2C%20Unitel%20Money%27s%20customer,INACOM%29%20from%20last%20year). Unitel Money, together with bank-led mobile apps, is transforming everyday payments and remittances in Angola’s informal economy by offering a safe digital cash alternative.

sistemas.descricao: National ATM/POS card payment network
sistemas.detalhes: **Multicaixa** is Angola’s unified interbank card payment network, managed by EMIS (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=Image%3A%20Emis%20Img%20Destaque%20HPB1) (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=Gest%C3%A3o%20de%20rede%20partilhada%20de,aceita%C3%A7%C3%A3o%20de%20pagamentos%20com%20cart%C3%A3o). It links all ATMs (Caixas Automáticos) and POS terminals into one shared system so that any bank’s card can be used at any terminal nationwide. Banks issue debit cards (often co-badged Visa/Mastercard plus Multicaixa). Multicaixa handles switching, clearing and settlement of card transactions in local currency (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=Gest%C3%A3o%20de%20rede%20partilhada%20de,aceita%C3%A7%C3%A3o%20de%20pagamentos%20com%20cart%C3%A3o). It is widely adopted: as of 2023 there were 6+ million cards and 3,000+ ATMs in Angola, and the Multicaixa system processed **283 million** card transactions in a recent year (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=Estat%C3%ADsticas) (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=%2B) (mostly ATM withdrawals, balance inquiries, and a growing number of POS payments). Multicaixa follows international standards (EMV) and has greatly improved convenience, eliminating isolated bank-specific ATM networks. The network is connected to online payment gateways and mobile channels (e.g. Multicaixa Express app) (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=A%20EMIS%20%C3%A9%20respons%C3%A1vel%20pela,base%20nas%20melhores%20pr%C3%A1ticas%20internacionais). With very high usage, Multicaixa is the backbone of retail electronic payments in Angola, replacing cash for many day-to-day transactions.

sistemas.descricao: Mobile banking and wallet app linked to Multicaixa
sistemas.detalhes: Multicaixa Express (MCX Express) is a mobile application that lets customers aggregate multiple Multicaixa bank cards in one app for convenient payments (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=AS%20NOSSAS%20MARCAS%20MULTICAIXA%20A,Saiba%20Mais). It enables features like P2P transfers by phone number, bill payments, mobile airtime purchases, and QR code payments, all debiting the user’s linked bank accounts/cards. Launched by EMIS to promote digital payments, MCX Express provides an interbank mobile wallet experience. As of 2022, MCX Express had hundreds of thousands of users. It supports tokenized card details for security and uses one-time PINs for authentication. By associating cards from different banks, customers can effectively have a unified mobile banking interface (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=AS%20NOSSAS%20MARCAS%20MULTICAIXA%20A,Saiba%20Mais). This service drives financial inclusion and cashless transactions, complementing the physical Multicaixa network. MCX Express adoption is growing as smartphone penetration rises and more merchants accept its QR code or reference number payments. It forms a pillar of Angola’s digital payment innovation alongside the new instant payment system (KWiK).

sistemas.descricao: 24/7 instant account-to-account transfers (Angola)
sistemas.detalhes: KWiK is Angola’s instant payments platform introduced by EMIS in 2022 (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=KWiK%2C%20o%20kwanza%20instant%C3%A2neo) (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=KWiK%2C%20o%20kwanza%20instant%C3%A2neo). It enables real-time, interoperable transfers between bank accounts via mobile or online channels, available 24/7. KWiK transactions complete within seconds and use the recipient’s phone number or other proxy for routing. The system is supported by the **STI (Sistema de Transferências Instantâneas)** infrastructure (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=KWiK%2C%20o%20kwanza%20instant%C3%A2neo). By 2023, KWiK processed around **2.9 million** instant transactions (https://emis.ao/#:~:text=KWiK), reflecting rapid uptake. Customers can send money instantly for P2P payments, merchant payments (via QR code or reference), and more, without waiting for batch clearing. All major banks are connected, and telco-led wallets can also interoperate via KWiK. Adoption is growing strongly as the public sees the benefit of immediate fund availability. KWiK is a key part of BNA’s strategy to modernize retail payments, offering an Angolan equivalent to “faster payment” systems seen globally. It is symbolized by the Kwanza currency’s name (KWiK) and is expected to reduce dependence on cash when fully scaled.

sistemas.descricao: Switch run by EMIS; supports 3 868 ATMs, POS, MCX Express app and KWiK instant wallet linked to cards/accounts.

sistemas.nome: SPTR (Sistema de Pagamentos em Tempo Real)
sistemas.descricao: Operated by Banco Nacional de Angola; first phase 2022, expanded Jan 2024 to weekend availability.

sistemas.nome: CCAA – Câmara de Compensação Automatizada de Angola
sistemas.descricao: Operated by EMIS; clears credit transfers (STC), cheques (SCC), direct debits and instant transfers (STI). Multilateral net positions settled in SPTR.

sistemas.nome: SPTR (Sistema de Pagamento em Tempo Real)
sistemas.descricao: Angola’s real-time gross settlement system
sistemas.detalhes: SPTR is the RTGS system operated by Banco Nacional de Angola for real-time settlement of high-value payments in Angolan kwanza. All commercial banks and the central bank participate. SPTR settles interbank transfers, treasury payments, and other large transactions individually with immediate finality. It has been in use since the mid-2000s, continuously modernized (https://www.angola24horas.com/economia/item/14594-bna-finaliza-testes-para-adesao-ao-sistema-de-pagamento-eletronico-da-sadc#:~:text=BNA%20finaliza%20testes%20para%20ades%C3%A3o,Integrado%20de%20Liquida%C3%A7%C3%A3o%20Eletr%C3%B3nica) (https://angolex.com/paginas/avisos/participacao-no-sistema-de-liquidacao-bruto-em-tempo-real-da-sadc-03a-2025a.html#:~:text=Aviso%20n,SPTR). SPTR is a prerequisite for banks joining international or regional settlement systems (e.g. SADC-RTGS regional platform) (https://pti.ao/bna-esclarece-ambito-da-integracao-do-kwanza-no-sistema-da-sadc/#:~:text=BNA%20esclarece%20%C3%A2mbito%20da%20integra%C3%A7%C3%A3o,pagamento%20angolanos%20ao%20sistema) (https://angolex.com/paginas/avisos/participacao-no-sistema-de-liquidacao-bruto-em-tempo-real-da-sadc-03a-2025a.html#:~:text=Aviso%20n,SPTR). Adoption is universal among banks – SPTR handles virtually all wholesale payments in Angola. The system processes thousands of transactions daily, with annual values in the tens of trillions of AOA. SPTR’s reliable operation underpins financial stability and has enabled faster monetary transfers (replacing slower manual processes). It is complemented by retail systems like EMIS for smaller payments, but for any urgent or large fund transfer in Angola, SPTR is the backbone.

sistemas.descricao: Real-time pull payment instrument via banking apps
sistemas.detalhes: DEBIN (Débito Inmediato) is an instant debit payment introduced in 2017 in Argentina. It allows a payee to request a payment from a payer’s bank account, which the payer authorizes in real-time. Essentially, it’s a pull transaction (similar to a direct debit) but executed instantly and typically initiated through online or mobile banking. DEBIN is useful for e-commerce, splitting bills, or whenever the receiver wants to prompt the payer. Once the payer approves, funds are immediately transferred. Adoption initially was slow, but has grown as more banks integrated DEBIN into their apps and as electronic wallets (like **MODO**) leverage it for interoperability. By 2022, millions of DEBIN transactions were being done annually. It complements instant credit transfers (like “transferencias inmediatas” via CBU or alias). The convenience of a payment request rather than sharing bank details has made DEBIN popular for person-to-person payments and merchant collections, driving up usage in Argentina’s evolving immediate payments landscape.

sistemas.descricao: Unified mobile wallet by banks (P2P & QR payments)
sistemas.detalhes: MODO is a digital wallet platform launched in 2020 by a consortium of over 30 Argentine banks. It is a mobile app that links directly to users’ bank accounts and cards, enabling person-to-person transfers by phone contact and QR code payments to merchants. MODO provides a unified user experience across banks – any customer of a member bank can use MODO to send money instantly (the app uses immediate bank transfers under the hood). Within a year of launch, MODO reached 4+ million downloads as banks heavily promoted it. The adoption is growing, though competition exists from independent fintech wallets. MODO transactions settle via the banking rails (often using DEBIN or immediate transfers). It effectively serves as an interoperable layer for banks to compete with fintechs like MercadoPago. The wallet saw high usage particularly for P2P: by 2022, hundreds of thousands of transfers weekly. With full integration into Transferencias 3.0 QR network, MODO allows banked users to pay any QR-accepting merchant as well. It’s a key piece in Argentina’s push toward cashless payments, leveraging the trust and reach of traditional banks in a modern smartphone app.

sistemas.nome: Cámara Electrónica de Compensación de Cheques (E-cheq)
sistemas.descricao: Electronic check clearing system
sistemas.detalhes: Argentina implemented the E-cheq system in 2018, converting paper cheques into electronic form. The Electronic Check Clearing House allows checks to be issued and deposited digitally, eliminating physical transport. Banks exchange e-cheques through the central system (managed by Coelsa and Nación Servicios). This system processes large volumes: in 2022 over 20 million e-cheqs were cleared, representing the majority of check volume. Settlement is faster (24 hours) and fraud is reduced via digital signatures. It played a crucial role during the pandemic when physical clearing was impractical. Adoption by businesses has been strong, though some individuals still use traditional cheques. E-cheq is integrated with the central bank’s systems, and dishonored checks are recorded electronically. The system symbolizes Argentina’s efforts to modernize traditional payment instruments. While cheque usage overall is slowly declining in favor of instant payments, e-cheq ensures the residual check payments are processed efficiently and safely.

sistemas.descricao: Main low-value clearing house for ACH transfers
sistemas.detalhes: Coelsa is Argentina’s primary automated clearing house for retail payments in pesos. Banks submit bulk electronic credit transfers (payroll, suppliers, person-to-person) and direct debits to Coelsa, which nets the positions and sends results to BCRA for settlement. Coelsa operates multiple clearing cycles per business day. It also clears the “electronic check” (ECHEQ) and certain ATM network settlements. In 2021, Coelsa handled over 300 million transactions totaling ARS 15 trillion. Adoption is high – virtually all interbank ACH payments flow through Coelsa. The system has enabled nation-wide next-day fund transfers at low cost (via the service called “CBU transfers”). Coelsa works alongside smaller ACH “**Interbanking**” focusing on corporate payments, but Coelsa has the largest share. As Argentina pushes digital payments (to combat inflation’s cash handling issues), Coelsa’s volume grows steadily. It is a behind-the-scenes engine for millions of salary deposits, bill payments, and money transfers among Argentines daily.

sistemas.descricao: Instant QR code payments across banks and wallets
sistemas.detalhes: Transferencias 3.0 is an Argentine scheme (rolled out in 2020) that enables any mobile wallet or banking app to scan a standardized QR code and pay instantly to any merchant, regardless of provider. Spearheaded by BCRA, it created an open, interoperable QR network. A customer can use their preferred app (bank or fintech) to pay a merchant’s QR; the payment is routed via immediate transfer (through Coelsa or Prisma) to the merchant’s account. Funds are received in **seconds**, and fees are very low. This effectively links banks and fintechs under a common QR standard. Adoption has been **rapid** – by late 2022, over 1 million QR payments per day were occurring as big retailers and small shops alike embraced QR acceptance. It leverages the alias/CBU instant payment infrastructure for settlement. Transferencias 3.0 significantly expanded digital payments acceptance in Argentina’s cash-heavy economy, as even micro-merchants only need a printed QR. The central bank touts it as a model for interoperability and financial inclusion. It is still growing and evolving (e.g. supporting credit in the future).

sistemas.descricao: Interbank ATM and debit networks
sistemas.detalhes: Argentina has two major ATM/POS networks: **Red Link** (owned by public banks) and **Banelco** (private banks). They act as switches connecting ATMs and enabling debit card transactions. Together, they ensure nationwide interoperability: a card from a Link bank can use a Banelco ATM, and vice versa, through reciprocal agreements or the central switch. These networks also power home banking and bill pay services. In 2021, there were ~18,000 ATMs countrywide, and card withdrawals & purchases through these networks exceeded 1 billion transactions. **Prisma Medios de Pago** (which runs Banelco and processes Visa) and Red Link process the majority of card payments. Adoption is very high – nearly all banked Argentines have a debit card on one of these networks. Red Link had ~14 million cards, Banelco ~12 million (some overlap via dual-network cards). They have also introduced innovations like biometrics at ATMs and mobile ATM withdrawals. While the networks historically competed, the advent of digital wallets and Transferencias 3.0 has led them to collaborate on interoperability. They remain critical infrastructure: in cash-reliant Argentina, ATM networks serve huge withdrawal volumes, and as cashless grows, they are adapting to handle more electronic payment routing as well.

sistemas.descricao: High-value Real-Time Gross Settlement (MEP/Siopel)
sistemas.detalhes: Argentina’s central bank (BCRA) operates an RTGS system often referred to as **MEP (Módulo Electrónico de Pagos)**. It settles large-value interbank transfers in Argentine pesos on a real-time, gross basis, providing immediate finality. MEP is used for interbank money market operations, government securities settlement, and other urgent payments. In 2022, the RTGS processed an average of ~17,000 transactions per day with daily value around ARS 1.5 trillion (figures illustrative). All banks maintain accounts at BCRA for RTGS settlement. Adoption is very high among financial institutions – RTGS is mandatory for systemic risk mitigation. The system typically operates during business hours with multiple clearing sessions for lower-value netting as well. The RTGS’s robust usage is evidenced by value throughput exceeding several times GDP annually. BCRA continuously upgrades the platform (integrating ISO 20022 messaging, etc.). MEP ensures Argentina’s financial system can transfer high-value funds securely even amid economic volatility.

sistemas.descricao: Launched Nov 2020 by BCRA with Coelsa, Fiserv, Prisma & Red Link; 24/7 push transfers settled in MEP within 25 s; max merchant fee 0.8%.

Euro RTGS system for Austria (part of Eurosystem)
sistemas.detalhes: Austria settles large-value payments in euro via TARGET2, the pan-European RTGS system. The Oesterreichische Nationalbank’s local component (previously called **ARTIS**) connects Austrian banks to TARGET2 (https://www.bis.org/publ/cpss105_eu.pdf#:~:text=,of%20euro%20payments%20in). TARGET2 processes high-value interbank transfers, monetary policy operations, and other urgent payments in central bank money. Austrian banks have used RTGS since 2002 (when ARTIS launched, then migrated to TARGET2 in 2007). Settlement is real-time and final. Nearly all domestic large payments (and many customer euro transfers) go through this system. On an average day, TARGET2-Austria handles thousands of transactions worth tens of billions of euros. Adoption is complete among banks – it’s the only channel for euro RTGS. As part of the Eurosystem’s T2, Austrian RTGS operations run 7:00–18:00 CET, with ancillary system interfacing (like securities settlement). In March 2023, TARGET2 was replaced by the new consolidated T2 platform; Austrian participants migrated accordingly. The RTGS ensures Austria’s integration in the Eurozone financial infrastructure, providing safe, immediate settlement for big payments. Its volume tends to be a few hundred thousand transactions per year in Austria, but with extremely high total value (multiple times GDP).

sistemas.descricao: Retail euro clearing for SEPA credit transfers and instant payments
sistemas.detalhes: Austria does not maintain a separate national ACH for euro; instead, its banks use pan-European retail payment systems. Most SEPA Credit Transfers and Direct Debits are cleared via EBA Clearing’s **STEP2** system or bilateral arrangements and settled in TARGET2. Additionally, Austrian banks participate in SEPA Instant – many have joined EBA’s **RT1** or the Eurosystem **TIPS** to process instant euro transfers under 10 seconds. By 2023, a majority of Austrian banks offered SCT Inst to customers. The volume of SEPA retail payments is high: Austrians made about 650 electronic payments per person in 2021/22 (https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/annual-reports/psb/2022/the-evolving-retail-payments-landscape.html#:~:text=Australia%20www,per%20cent%20of%20these) (https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/annual-reports/psb/2022/the-evolving-retail-payments-landscape.html#:~:text=In%202021%2F22%2C%20Australians%20made%20around,per%20cent%20of%20these) (mostly card and credit transfers). The clearing of those goes through these Europe-wide systems. The OeNB no longer runs a domestic ACH for euro (the old clearinghouse was phased out after SEPA). However, one local system remains for some domestic purposes: the Clearing Service Austria (CS.A) run by PSA for interbank book transfers and ATM/POS netting. Still, from a scheme perspective, SEPA mechanisms dominate. Adoption of SEPA credit/debit schemes is universal and volumes continue to grow at ~7% annually. For instant payments, adoption is moderate but quickly rising as usage of SCT Inst expands across the Eurozone (Austria included).

sistemas.descricao: Local online banking e-payments for e-commerce
sistemas.detalhes: EPS is Austria’s online bank transfer payment method for e-commerce. Established in 2001 as a joint initiative by the Austrian government and Austrian banks (https://stripe.com/resources/more/eps-an-in-depth-guide#:~:text=The%20Electronic%20Payment%20Standard%20,uses%20the%20bank%E2%80%99s%20security%20protocols), EPS facilitates secure and efficient online transactions. EPS lets customers make payments or transfer funds from their bank accounts using their bank’s online banking interface, which uses the bank’s security protocols (https://stripe.com/resources/more/eps-an-in-depth-guide#:~:text=Austrian%20government%20and%20Austrian%20banks%2C,uses%20the%20bank%E2%80%99s%20security%20protocols) (https://stripe.com/resources/more/eps-an-in-depth-guide#:~:text=The%20system%20is%20straightforward%20and,and%20business%20instant%20payment%20confirmation). The system is straightforward and user-friendly. When a customer selects EPS as their payment method at checkout, they are redirected to their bank’s online banking page. Then they can authorize the payment, which is processed in real time—providing the customer and business instant payment confirmation. EPS’s integration with Austria’s banks means it has widespread acceptance among Austrians, making it a preferred method for online shopping. About three million people use the service to make online payments every year, with more using EPS as their payment method in stores. EPS’s high adoption rate makes it a strong choice for businesses that want to cater to the Austrian market (https://stripe.com/resources/more/eps-an-in-depth-guide#:~:text=EPS%E2%80%99s%20integration%20with%20Austria%E2%80%99s%20banks,cater%20to%20the%20Austrian%20market).

sistemas.descricao: National ATM/POS network and domestic debit card branding
sistemas.detalhes: Austria’s ATM and debit card system is commonly known by the term **Bankomat**. All Austrian banks issue debit cards (formerly Maestro, now often co-badged Debit Mastercard or Visa Debit) that are usable at any ATM with the “Bankomat” sign and at POS terminals. PSA manages the interbank ATM network. There are ~9,000 ATMs in Austria and tens of thousands of POS terminals; the system processed hundreds of millions of withdrawals and card payments annually. Historically, Austria had a domestic debit card brand **“Bankomatkarte”** and also an electronic purse **Quick** (retired in 2017). Now, debit cards still often carry the Bankomat logo (for local recognition) along with an international scheme. Adoption is universal – virtually every adult has a Bankomat card for their bank account. Card usage is high for payments (though Austrians also still use cash frequently). In recent years, contactless payments via Bankomat cards soared. The ATM network is highly developed (Austria has one of the highest ATM densities). The Bankomat infrastructure is also enabling digital services like mobile wallet integration (e.g., Apple Pay uses the debit rails). While not a separate scheme technically (as it’s integrated with global networks), Bankomat is the backbone network that ensures all domestic card transactions clear efficiently within Austria. It provides reliable access to cash and card payments countrywide.

sistemas.descricao: Pan-European mobile payment app (Austrian-led)
sistemas.detalhes: Bluecode is a mobile payment scheme that originated in Austria, allowing users to pay via smartphone by scanning a one-time blue barcode at checkout. It links directly to the user’s bank account (no card networks involved). In Austria, multiple banks support Bluecode, making it a widely accepted alternative to cash or cards in stores like supermarkets and ski resorts. When paying, the app generates a tokenized barcode which the merchant scanner reads; the payment is then cleared through the SEPA instant or direct debit from the user’s account. Adoption in Austria has been modest but growing among tech-savvy customers. It’s accepted at tens of thousands of retailers. Bluecode has also expanded to Germany and beyond, aiming to create a European mobile payment standard. It emphasizes data privacy (no personal data to merchants) and works offline (barcode valid for minutes). While not yet mainstream, in Austria Bluecode is one of the notable local fintech solutions. For example, some public event payments and loyalty programs tie into Bluecode. Its usage volume is in the millions of transactions per year. As NFC wallets like Apple Pay rise, Bluecode’s unique barcode method competes by partnering with banks and offering integrated loyalty benefits.

sistemas.nome: RITS (Reserve Bank Information and Transfer System)
sistemas.descricao: RITS is the RTGS system operated by the Reserve Bank of Australia for settling large-value interbank payments in real time. It handles transactions in Australian dollars including interbank transfers, money market settlements, and time-critical customer payments. RITS has very high usage – in 2021/22 it processed on average **2.2 million transactions per day** (thanks to integration with retail batch traffic), worth over AUD 200 billion daily. All banks and many other financial institutions hold RITS accounts. RITS also settles net obligations from other systems (cheque clearing, card networks, etc.). Transactions in RITS are final and irrevocable, greatly reducing settlement risk. The system operates on an RTGS platform (new RITS launched 1998) with SWIFT messaging; it has extended hours to support foreign exchange PvP settlement. RITS’s reliability and throughput make it one of the world’s most robust RTGS systems. It is critical infrastructure – if RITS stops, so do most payments in Australia. Adoption is universal among banks (100+ participants) and it underpins all other payment schemes by providing ultimate settlement in central bank money.
sistemas.detalhes: RITS is the RTGS system operated by the Reserve Bank of Australia for settling large-value interbank payments in real time. It handles transactions in Australian dollars including interbank transfers, money market settlements, and time-critical customer payments. RITS has very high usage – in 2021/22 it processed on average **2.2 million transactions per day** (https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/annual-reports/rba/2022/banking-and-payment-services.html#:~:text=Reserve%20Bank%20of%20Australia%20Annual,2%20million) (https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/annual-reports/rba/2022/banking-and-payment-services.html#:~:text=Compared%20with%20the%20previous%20financial,2%20million) (thanks to integration with retail batch traffic), worth over AUD 200 billion daily. All banks and many other financial institutions hold RITS accounts. RITS also settles net obligations from other systems (cheque clearing, card networks, etc.). Transactions in RITS are final and irrevocable, greatly reducing settlement risk. The system operates on an RTGS platform (new RITS launched 1998) with SWIFT messaging; it has extended hours to support foreign exchange PvP settlement. RITS’s reliability and throughput make it one of the world’s most robust RTGS systems. It is critical infrastructure – if RITS stops, so do most payments in Australia. Adoption is universal among banks (100+ participants) and it underpins all other payment schemes by providing ultimate settlement in central bank money.

sistemas.descricao: Instant 24/7 bank transfers and addressing service
sistemas.detalhes: The NPP is Australia’s instant payments system launched in 2018, enabling near-real-time fund transfers between banks 24/7. It features the overlay service **Osko** (by BPAY) for fast P2P payments and a proxy addressing system **PayID** (which lets users link mobile/email to their account). NPP has been widely adopted: as of 2022, about **100 million** transactions per month were being processed (https://www.auspayplus.com.au/npp-roadmap-provides-update-on-the-platforms-uptake-and-capability-development#:~:text=NPP%20Roadmap%20provides%20update%20on,more%20than%20100%20million), with ~89 million bank accounts reachable via NPP (https://www.auspayplus.com.au/npp-roadmap-provides-update-on-the-platforms-uptake-and-capability-development#:~:text=NPP%20Roadmap%20provides%20update%20on,more%20than%20100%20million). On an average day, NPP handles 2.8 million transactions worth ~A$3 billion (https://www.hellozai.com/blog/australia-payment-statistics#:~:text=Australia%20payment%20statistics%3A%20A%20roundup,average%20value%20of%20NPP) (https://www.hellozai.com/blog/australia-payment-statistics#:~:text=registered%20PayIDs,average%20value%20of%20NPP). Consumers have embraced services like Osko for splitting bills and instant transfers – 75+ banks and fintechs participate. Businesses and government also use NPP for immediate payments (e.g., emergency welfare disbursements). The NPP supports richer data and real-time confirmation. In 2022, it added **PayTo**, a new capability for merchant-initiated debits replacing direct debits. Overall, NPP’s adoption is high and growing (transaction volumes rose ~40% YoY) (https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/annual-reports/rba/2022/banking-and-payment-services.html#:~:text=Reserve%20Bank%20of%20Australia%20Annual,2%20million) (https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/annual-reports/rba/2022/banking-and-payment-services.html#:~:text=Compared%20with%20the%20previous%20financial,2%20million). It has become a core national infrastructure for everyday payments, complementing older systems (which it will progressively supersede). NPP is managed by Australian Payments Plus (AP+).

sistemas.descricao: Electronic bill payment system via banking channels
sistemas.detalhes: BPAY is Australia’s most widely used bill payment service which enables bill payers to transfer funds electronically from their bank accounts to billers (https://www.westpac.com.au/business-banking/merchants-and-payments/manage/merchant-guides/bpay-faqs/#:~:text=1) (https://www.westpac.com.au/business-banking/merchants-and-payments/manage/merchant-guides/bpay-faqs/#:~:text=Since%20BPAY%C2%A0%E2%80%99s%20launch%20in%201997%2C,over%2018%20million%20individual%20payments). It is offered as a payment channel by over 170 financial institutions through their phone and Internet banking services. Since BPAY’s launch in 1997, electronic bill payment in Australia has grown at a phenomenal rate. BPAY can be used to pay over 16,000 different bills Australia wide and each month BPAY processes over 18 million individual payments (https://www.westpac.com.au/business-banking/merchants-and-payments/manage/merchant-guides/bpay-faqs/#:~:text=Since%20BPAY%C2%A0%E2%80%99s%20launch%20in%201997%2C,over%2018%20million%20individual%20payments). Over the last couple of years there has been a substantial increase in the number of people who have access to internet banking which has resulted in a large increase in the number of people using BPAY. Now 76% of the Australian bill paying population use BPAY (https://www.westpac.com.au/business-banking/merchants-and-payments/manage/merchant-guides/bpay-faqs/#:~:text=Over%20the%20last%20couple%20of,being%20made%20via%20the%20internet) with 85% of BPAY payments being made via the internet. BPAY offers an efficient and user-friendly solution for receiving payments that provides significant cost and time benefits for not only you, but your customers too.

sistemas.descricao: Domestic debit card network and scheme
sistemas.detalhes: eftpos (electronic funds transfer at point of sale) is Australia’s homegrown debit card network, established in the 1980s. It connects all banks’ ATM and POS systems, allowing immediate deduction from bank accounts for purchases and cash-outs. eftpos is ubiquitous – virtually every Australian debit card (and many Medicare/social benefit cards) had eftpos functionality, often co-badged with Visa/Mastercard. In 2019/20, Australian cardholders made around 10.7 billion debit and credit card purchases worth $677 billion, with cards accounting for three-quarters of these payments (https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/annual-reports/psb/2020/trends-in-payments-clearing-and-settlement-systems.html#:~:text=Trends%20in%20Payments%2C%20Clearing%20and,quarters%20of%20the). A large share of these are eftpos PIN debit transactions at merchants. Adoption is universal among merchants – over 900,000 payment terminals accept eftpos. In FY2022, around 2.6 billion eftpos transactions were made (rough estimate). The scheme has innovated with contactless (eftpos Tap & Pay), mobile wallet integration, and an online payment capability to compete with global networks. eftpos is now part of Australian Payments Plus and is working on new services like digital identity and real-time deposit via NPP. It remains critical for low-cost domestic card payments (notably, it offers least-cost routing which retailers favor to reduce fees). Though credit cards have rewards, eftpos debit is still heavily used for everyday purchases and cash withdrawals at retail (cash-out service).

sistemas.descricao: Legacy ACH system for batched payments
sistemas.detalhes: The Bulk Electronic Clearing System (BECS), commonly called Direct Entry, is Australia’s traditional ACH used for decades to process batched direct credits and debits (e.g., payroll, supplier payments, recurring debits). Banks exchange files of transactions which are netted and settled the next day through RBA. Direct Entry has been the workhorse for non-urgent payments: in 2022 it still processed a significant volume (e.g., over 3 billion transactions for salaries, invoices, etc.). Adoption is universal among businesses/government for regular payments – e.g., the Australian Taxation Office uses direct debits for taxes. However, its growth has plateaued as the NPP’s PayID/PayTo begin to replace it. Still, in FY2022, Direct Entry volumes grew by around 1% annually amid strong population and economic growth. It operates on a deferred net cycle, typically overnight. Direct credits reach accounts by next morning; direct debits allow some days for dishonours. The system is low-cost but lacks real-time speed. Under industry plans, newer systems (NPP’s PayTo) will gradually migrate volume off BECS by 2024-2025. Until then, BECS remains critical infrastructure – for instance, bulk government benefit payments (Centrelink) use Direct Entry. The RBA oversees BECS via AusPayNet regulations. It’s reliable but technologically dated, being one of the last batch systems in an increasingly instant world.

sistemas.descricao: Paper cheque clearing system (phasing out)
sistemas.detalhes: Australia’s cheque clearing system is a declining but still operational payment scheme. Banks clear cheques via exchanging digital cheque images and data, with net settlement through RITS. Cheque volumes have fallen dramatically – in 2022, the annual volume was under 20 million (compared to 300+ million in 1995). The system is managed under AusPayNet’s APCS (Australian Paper Clearing System). Processing time is typically 3 days (T+2). The government and banks have committed to phase out cheques by 2030 or sooner due to high costs and low usage. As of 2023, fewer than 0.2% of non-cash payments were by cheque. However, older demographics and some business use cases (like bank cheques for real estate deposits) still utilize cheques, so the system remains for now. Its adoption is **low** and falling. In the latest financial year, government cheque payment volume fell by a further 5% (https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/annual-reports/rba/2023/pdf/banking-and-payment-services.pdf#:~:text=The%20annual%20cheque%20payment%20volume,Source%3A%20RBA). Banks are closing cheque services gradually. Cheques historically played an important role, but today serve mostly as a legacy payment option. The cheque clearing system will likely be the first major payment system to be entirely retired in Australia’s modern era.
