sistemas.detalhes: AZIPS is Azerbaijan’s RTGS, processing large-value and urgent interbank payments in real time (https://www.cbar.az/page-477/real-time-gross-settlement-system-azips#:~:text=match%20at%20L464%20Real%20Vaxt,a%20kimi). It supports transactions in the national currency (AZN) and foreign currencies (https://www.cbar.az/page-477/real-time-gross-settlement-system-azips#:~:text=Real%20Vaxt%20Rejimind%C9%99%20Hesabla%C5%9Fmalar%20Sistemi,a%20kimi). Banks exchange payment instructions via SWIFT and a local secure network, with operating hours 9:20–17:00 on business days (https://www.cbar.az/page-477/real-time-gross-settlement-system-azips#:~:text=Real%20Vaxt%20Rejimind%C9%99%20Hesabla%C5%9Fmalar%20Sistemi,a%20kimi). AZIPS is systemically important, settling high-value transfers and final net positions of other systems in central bank money.

sistemas.nome: Low-Value Payments Clearing and Settlement System (XÖHKS)
sistemas.descricao: Batched ACH for small and recurring payments
sistemas.detalhes: The XÖHKS is Azerbaijan’s automated clearing house for low-value payments, handling bulk electronic transfers such as payroll, utilities, and other non-urgent transactions (https://uploads.cbar.az/assets/semiannual%20report%20-%2003.08%20last_FO_03_eng.cleaned_01_v02_PSD_FIN1.pdf#:~:text=large%20and%20instant%20payments%20was,and%20the%20value) (https://uploads.cbar.az/assets/semiannual%20report%20-%2003.08%20last_FO_03_eng.cleaned_01_v02_PSD_FIN1.pdf#:~:text=period%2C%20while%20the%20number%20of,respectively). Payments are netted in clearing cycles and settled via the central bank. It operates on a deferred net settlement basis, improving efficiency for high-volume low-value payments. In 2023 it processed around 145 million payments (e.g. salaries, direct debits) with an estimated value of ~AZN 49 billion (https://uploads.cbar.az/assets/PS%20annual%20report%20ENG.pdf#:~:text=Settlement%20System%20%28AZIPS%29%20was%202,1B). XÖHKS provides next-day or same-day settlement, reducing reliance on paper cheques.

sistemas.descricao: 24/7 instant retail payment platform
sistemas.detalhes: Launched in 2020, the IPS enables instant fund transfers between banks and payment service providers 24×7×365 (https://www.cbar.az/page-479/instant-payments-system-ips?language=en#:~:text=Image) (https://www.cbar.az/page-479/instant-payments-system-ips?language=en#:~:text=The%20key%20challenge%20of%20the,format%20in%20a%20real%20time). It allows individuals and businesses to pay and receive in seconds (5–20s per transaction) at any time (https://www.cbar.az/page-479/instant-payments-system-ips?language=en#:~:text=The%20key%20challenge%20of%20the,format%20in%20a%20real%20time). IPS uses a central addressing module for alias-based transfers (e.g. phone or ID linked to accounts) (https://www.cbar.az/page-479/instant-payments-system-ips?language=en#:~:text=e,the%20GPP%20through%20the%20IPS). Settlements occur in real-time, with liquidity prefunded from participants’ accounts in AZIPS (https://www.cbar.az/page-479/instant-payments-system-ips?language=en#:~:text=Settlements%20in%20the%20IPS%20are,the%20payment%20has%20not%20been). A transaction limit of AZN 40,000 applies (higher for government payments) (https://www.cbar.az/page-479/instant-payments-system-ips?language=en#:~:text=Settlements%20in%20the%20IPS%20are,the%20payment%20has%20not%20been). IPS is integrated with the Government Payment Portal, letting users pay over 1,000 services (taxes, utilities, fines) instantly (https://www.cbar.az/page-479/instant-payments-system-ips?language=en#:~:text=e,the%20GPP%20through%20the%20IPS). It supports QR code payments for merchants (https://www.cbar.az/page-479/instant-payments-system-ips?language=en#:~:text=platform%2C%20has%20also%20been%20integrated,the%20GPP%20through%20the%20IPS).

sistemas.descricao: National card switching network interfacing processors
sistemas.detalhes: The BKM links all card-processing organizations in Azerbaijan to ensure interoperability of ATMs/POS for domestic card transactions (https://www.cbar.az/page-480/the-interbank-card-center-icc#:~:text=match%20at%20L464%20Banklararas%C4%B1%20Kart,il%C9%99%20%C3%B6lk%C9%99%20daxilind%C9%99%20apar%C4%B1lan%20kart) (https://www.cbar.az/page-480/the-interbank-card-center-icc#:~:text=Banklararas%C4%B1%20Kart%20M%C9%99rk%C9%99zi%20,il%C9%99%20%C3%B6lk%C9%99%20daxilind%C9%99%20apar%C4%B1lan%20kart). It interfaces processors (e.g. AzeriCard, MilliKart) and in-house bank systems, routing transactions between issuing and acquiring banks (https://www.cbar.az/page-480/the-interbank-card-center-icc#:~:text=Banklararas%C4%B1%20Kart%20M%C9%99rk%C9%99zi%20,il%C9%99%20%C3%B6lk%C9%99%20daxilind%C9%99%20apar%C4%B1lan%20kart). BKM operates 24/7/365, instantly switching card authorization requests in AZN and foreign currencies (https://www.cbar.az/page-480/the-interbank-card-center-icc#:~:text=BKM,m%C3%BCbadil%C9%99si%20klasterizasiya%20edilmi%C5%9F%20telekommunikasiya%20x%C9%99tl%C9%99ri). Settlements of card transactions switched via BKM are completed on the next business day in participants’ accounts (https://www.cbar.az/page-480/the-interbank-card-center-icc#:~:text=BKM,m%C3%BCbadil%C9%99si%20klasterizasiya%20edilmi%C5%9F%20telekommunikasiya%20x%C9%99tl%C9%99ri). By integrating all banks’ card networks, BKM has unified the national card payments landscape, supporting multi-currency card use domestically and connectivity to international schemes.

sistemas.descricao: One-stop portal for public service payments
sistemas.detalhes: The Government Payment Portal (HÖP) is an integrated platform for paying government and utility bills. It is linked to IPS, allowing citizens and businesses to make instant payments to over a thousand government and service organizations (taxes, fees, utilities, fines, insurance, etc.) from a single interface (https://www.cbar.az/page-479/instant-payments-system-ips?language=en#:~:text=e,the%20GPP%20through%20the%20IPS). Users can access GPP via online banking or the AniPay mobile app and complete payments in real-time (https://www.cbar.az/page-479/instant-payments-system-ips?language=en#:~:text=e,the%20GPP%20through%20the%20IPS). By centralizing bill presentment and collection, HÖP has significantly digitized government collections. In 2024, the portal processed about AZN 8.1 billion (mostly cashless payments) as citizens increasingly use electronic methods (https://en.trend.az/business/4053545.html#:~:text=In%202024%2C%20Azerbaijan%E2%80%99s%20National%20Payment,Cashless%20card).

sistemas.descricao: Launched 2021 as part of Azerbaijan’s Digital Payment Strategy to support QR retail payments, P2P and government collections. 19 banks plus Azerpost connected; integrates to state treasury portal and e-ID.
Clears small-value, non-instant payments three times per day; net positions settle in AZIPS.

Operated by the Central Bank of Azerbaijan (CBA) since 2001 to settle large-value payments, government securities legs and clearing positions from other systems. Works alongside LVPCSS for retail and IPS for instant payments.
Handles >560 public services; integrated to municipalities, customs and treasury.
Interbank payment system
Dominant payment method

Real-Time Gross Settlement system for BAM, operated by Central Bank of BiH (https://cbbh.ba/press/readfaq/7#:~:text=System%20of%20interbanking%20clearing%20and,real%20time%20gross%20settlement%20system) (https://cbbh.ba/press/readfaq/7#:~:text=Real%20time%20gross%20settlement%2C%20RTGS%2C,them%20at%20the%20settlement%20account)
sistemas.detalhes: The high-value payments system for interbank transfers in Bosnian Convertible Mark (BAM). RTGS processes transactions above BAM 10,000 (and optionally smaller ones) individually and immediately in real time (https://cbbh.ba/press/readfaq/7#:~:text=Gyro%20clearing%20is%20system%20of,performed%20in%20four%20daily%20cycles). Run by the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina (CBBH) since 2001 as part of payment system reform (https://cbbh.ba/press/readfaq/7#:~:text=The%20Central%20Bank%20of%20Bosnia,International%20Bank%20Account%20Number), it provides final, irrevocable settlement for urgent and large payments between banks. Type: RTGS (wholesale, 8×5 operating hours). CBBH is operator and settlement agent (https://cbbh.ba/press/readfaq/7#:~:text=System%20of%20interbanking%20clearing%20and,real%20time%20gross%20settlement%20system) (https://cbbh.ba/press/readfaq/7#:~:text=for%20transactions%20above%2010%2C000,them%20at%20the%20settlement%20account).

sistemas.descricao: BAM-denominated automated clearing house for low-value transfers (up to BAM 10k) (https://cbbh.ba/press/readfaq/7#:~:text=Gyro%20clearing%20is%20system%20of,performed%20in%20four%20daily%20cycles) (https://cbbh.ba/press/readfaq/7#:~:text=Gyro%20clearing%20is%20system%20of,performed%20in%20four%20daily%20cycles)
sistemas.detalhes: The deferred net settlement system operated by CBBH for retail payments. Gyro Clearing processes interbank transactions ≤ BAM 10,000 in four daily clearing cycles (https://cbbh.ba/press/readfaq/7#:~:text=Gyro%20clearing%20is%20system%20of,performed%20in%20four%20daily%20cycles) (https://cbbh.ba/press/readfaq/7#:~:text=Gyro%20clearing%20is%20system%20of,performed%20in%20four%20daily%20cycles). It clears bulk electronic credit transfers, direct debits, and payment orders among all banks, netting multilateral positions which are then settled in RTGS at day-end. Introduced in 2001 and upgraded in 2019 to ISO 20022/SEPA standards (https://cbbh.ba/press/readfaq/7#:~:text=European%20Union%20%28EU%29), GC enables same-day clearing of intraday payments. Type: ACH (batched multilateral clearing).

sistemas.descricao: Domestic card payment and mobile instant transfer platform by Bamcard processor (https://empsa.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/EMPSA_New-Member_BAMCARD_Press-Release_100920.pdf#:~:text=Bamcard%20is%20a%20joint%20stock,ATMs%3B%20KVIKO%20instant%20%E2%80%93%20P2P) (https://empsa.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/EMPSA_New-Member_BAMCARD_Press-Release_100920.pdf#:~:text=2017%20Bamcard%20operates%20a%20Mobile,solution%2C%20is%20currently%20being%20implemented)
sistemas.detalhes: BAMCard is the national card switching and processing network in BiH, connecting ATMs and POS for all banks (https://www.verisofteurope.com/projects/bamcard/#:~:text=Bamcard%20,center%20for%20all%20BiH%20banks). It also launched “KVIKO” in 2017 – the country’s first mobile payment system (https://empsa.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/EMPSA_New-Member_BAMCARD_Press-Release_100920.pdf#:~:text=Bamcard%20is%20a%20joint%20stock,ATMs%3B%20KVIKO%20instant%20%E2%80%93%20P2P). KVIKO enables instant P2P transfers by phone number (KVIKO Instant), cardless ATM withdrawals (KVIKO Cash), mobile top-ups, and QR code payments (KVIKO Pay) across participating banks (https://empsa.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/EMPSA_New-Member_BAMCARD_Press-Release_100920.pdf#:~:text=2017%20Bamcard%20operates%20a%20Mobile,solution%2C%20is%20currently%20being%20implemented) (https://empsa.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/EMPSA_New-Member_BAMCARD_Press-Release_100920.pdf#:~:text=have%20clients%20and%20branches%20throughout,As%20it%20adaptable%20to%20be). Currently used by 3 banks (ASA, Union Banka, BBI) (https://bamcard.ba/bamcard-became-a-member-of-the-european-mobile-payment-systems-association-empsa-with-the-kviko-application/#:~:text=BAMCARD%20became%20a%20member%20of,banks%2C%20ASA%2C%20Union%2C%20and), KVIKO transactions are processed in real-time by Bamcard, with settlement via the banking system. Type: Card & instant mobile scheme (private sector operated).

sistemas.descricao: Integration with European instant payment infrastructure for EUR transactions (https://evroto.bg/en/media/178-bta-mr-petar-chobanov-deputy-governor-of-bnb-in-charge-of-the-banking-departm#:~:text=One%20of%20these%20projects%20was,BISERA%20to%20the%20Eurosystem%27s) (https://fintech.global/2024/12/20/bulgarian-national-bank-connects-to-ecbs-tips-platform/#:~:text=Bulgarian%20National%20Bank%20connects%20to,any%20other%20TIPS%20participant%2C)
sistemas.detalhes: Bosnia’s banks are preparing to join the SEPA instant credit transfer scheme via the ECB’s TIPS platform. The central bank (CBBH) connected the domestic euro clearing system (BISERA7-EUR) to TIPS in 2023 (https://evroto.bg/en/media/178-bta-mr-petar-chobanov-deputy-governor-of-bnb-in-charge-of-the-banking-departm#:~:text=BTA%3A%20Petar%20Chobanov%3A%20We%20are,BISERA%20to%20the%20Eurosystem%27s) (https://fintech.global/2024/12/20/bulgarian-national-bank-connects-to-ecbs-tips-platform/#:~:text=Bulgarian%20National%20Bank%20connects%20to,any%20other%20TIPS%20participant%2C). This allows instant euro payments to/from EU area banks, anticipating Bosnia’s eurozone accession. Currently, standard SEPA credit transfers in EUR are processed through BISERA7 on a next-day basis. With TIPS connectivity, euro transfers can be settled in seconds across borders. Type: Instant payments in EUR (cross-border). Operated by CBBH via BORICA’s module for TIPS (https://www.borica.bg/en/latest/novini/borica-advances-bulgaria-s-cross-border-instant-payments-interoperability-with-montran-s-tips-connectivity-module#:~:text=BORICA%2C%20the%20Bulgarian%20national%20payment,connectivity%20module%20developed%20by%20Montran).

sistemas.descricao: BAMCard d.d. is Bosnia’s national card payment processor and the operator of the sole domestic card scheme, Bamcard. Founded in 1999 as a joint project of banks [oai_citation:40‡bamcard.ba], it provides ATM/POS switching and card issuance services. Only a couple of banks issue Bamcard-branded debit cards (the rest use Visa/Mastercard) [oai_citation:41‡ubbih.ba]. The network enables interbank ATM withdrawals and POS payments in local currency. Bamcard has also enabled interoperability of mobile wallets (e.g., its KVIKO app) and joined the European Mobile Payment Association in recent years [oai_citation:42‡bamcard.ba].

The RTGS in Bosnia (operated by the Central Bank of BiH) settles interbank payments above BAM 10,000 in real-time gross, final and irrevocable [oai_citation:30‡cbbh.ba]. Introduced in 2001 as part of post-war payments reform, it significantly increased speed and reliability of high-value transfers [oai_citation:31‡cbbh.ba]. By design, transactions are processed immediately if funds are sufficient. About 40 million transactions per year (worth over BAM 100 billion) are conducted via CBBH payment systems, including RTGS [oai_citation:32‡cbbh.ba].

The Gyro Clearing system processes interbank payments of BAM 10,000 or below in four daily clearing cycles [oai_citation:37‡cbbh.ba]. It is operated by the central bank and nets bilateral and multilateral positions among banks. A new upgraded Gyro Clearing aligned with SEPA and ISO 20022 standards went live in 2019 [oai_citation:38‡cbbh.ba], improving efficiency and speed. Settlement of the net positions from Gyro occurs via RTGS accounts at the central bank by end of day.
Online payments

sistemas.nome: Central Bank Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS)
sistemas.descricao: Large-value real-time payment system
sistemas.detalhes: The Central Bank of Barbados operates an RTGS system (launched ~2007) for interbank settlements of large-value and urgent payments (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=system%2C%20directly%20facilitated%2055%20percent,system%20and%20the%20Central%20Bank). It processes high-value credit transfers in real time between commercial banks and the central bank, ensuring immediate finality in Barbados dollars. The RTGS also settles the net positions from other systems (like ACH and ATM networks) at end of day (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=system%2C%20directly%20facilitated%2055%20percent,system%20and%20the%20Central%20Bank). Government payments (salaries, pensions, debt obligations) are made through the RTGS, and the system runs during business hours. In 2018, RTGS transaction volumes and values spiked in H1 due to government securities trades, then fell post-debt restructuring, ending the year with 2% more transactions but ~37% lower value than 2017 (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=For%20the%20first%20six%20months,2018%20when%20compared%20to%202017). Regardless, the RTGS remains central to Barbados’ payments, handling about half of all non-cash payment value (more than any other single payment type) (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=Transactional%20platforms%2C%20namely%20the%20Caribbean,transactions%20are%20ultimately%20settled%20through). It provides safe, irrevocable settlement for Barbados’ financial institutions.

sistemas.nome: Barbados Automated Clearing House Services Inc. (BACHSI)
sistemas.descricao: ACH for cheque and electronic retail payments
sistemas.detalhes: BACHSI is Barbados’ ACH operator for low-value payments (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=Transactional%20platforms%2C%20namely%20the%20Caribbean,transactions%20are%20ultimately%20settled%20through). It clears electronic direct credits (like payroll, supplier payments) and also processes paper cheques via an image-based clearing system. Cheques and ACH credits/debits are exchanged and multilateral net settlement positions are computed daily. These net positions are then settled through the RTGS (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=system%2C%20directly%20facilitated%2055%20percent,system%20and%20the%20Central%20Bank). Cheques remain the second-largest form of domestic non-cash payments by value (after RTGS) in recent years (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=The%20number%20and%20volume%20of,based%20payments%20towards%20electronic%20payments), though their usage is slowly declining (~3% drop in volume in 2018) as electronic payments grow (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=The%20number%20and%20volume%20of,based%20payments%20towards%20electronic%20payments). BACHSI has helped streamline payments – prior to automation, intra-island cheque clearing took days, whereas now items clear generally by next business day. The ACH also processes recurring direct debits and bill payments. BACHSI’s role in direct payment processing and cheque truncation makes it pivotal for retail transactions in Barbados’ payment ecosystem.

sistemas.descricao: Domestic ATM/POS switching network
sistemas.detalhes: CARIFS is Barbados’ domestic debit card network, operational since the 1980s. It links the ATMs of all commercial banks and many credit unions to a shared network, and also connects to point-of-sale terminals at merchants (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=Incorporated%20,system%20and%20the%20Central%20Bank) (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=system%2C%20directly%20facilitated%2055%20percent,transactions%20are%20ultimately%20settled%20through). CARIFS enables 24/7 access to bank accounts via ATMs and POS countrywide, allowing customers to withdraw cash or pay with their bank card regardless of the issuing bank (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=Incorporated%20,system%20and%20the%20Central%20Bank). It essentially provides interoperability so that any Barbadian debit card (e.g. from Visa Debit or local bank networks) works at any ATM or card-accepting merchant in Barbados. CARIFS transactions (ATM withdrawals, POS purchases) are aggregated and ultimately settled through the RTGS system daily (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=system%2C%20directly%20facilitated%2055%20percent,system%20and%20the%20Central%20Bank). As of 2018, debit card usage through CARIFS continued to grow – about 9.7 million debit transactions totaling BBD 1.2 billion were made that year (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=Debit%20and%20Credit%20Card%20Transactions). CARIFS has been fundamental in the nation’s card infrastructure, driving electronic payment growth while complementing international networks like Visa/Mastercard.

sistemas.descricao: New interbank instant transfer service via ACH
sistemas.detalhes: Barbados has recently introduced a Real-Time Payments (RTP) feature within its Automated Clearing House framework to enable near-instant fund transfers between local banks. Using the RTP system, customers can send money between banks in minutes (target ~3 minutes or less) at any time during banking hours, typically via online or mobile banking apps (https://bb.scotiabank.com/personal/real-time-payments.html#:~:text=Real,Can%20I). The RTP transactions are cleared through the ACH infrastructure but processed continuously rather than in batches. In effect, RTP is a faster mode for ACH credit transfers, often used for person-to-person or small business payments that need quick settlement. By January 2024, the Central Bank mandated that no fees be charged on RTP (or any ACH) transfers to encourage adoption (https://jamaica-gleaner.com/article/caribbean/20240103/barbados-central-bank-halts-fees-charged-banks-electronic-transactions#:~:text=BRIDGETOWN%2C%20Barbados%2C%20CMC%20%E2%80%93%20The,time%20payments%20%28RTP%29%20transfers) (https://jamaica-gleaner.com/article/caribbean/20240103/barbados-central-bank-halts-fees-charged-banks-electronic-transactions#:~:text=fees%20and%20information%20requirements%20for,%E2%80%9D). Banks like Scotiabank and RBC support RTP for their customers’ interbank transfers. The service is relatively new and usage is growing as customers become aware of the convenience of instant local transfers compared to traditional next-day ACH. It marks a significant step in modernizing Barbados’ retail payments.

sistemas.descricao: Mandatory participation for all commercial banks and top credit unions by Mar-2026; will overlay QR and proxy services.
Live since Aug-2024; all commercial banks must image and exchange under new rules.
Phase-1 live; shift to ‘real-time ACH’ under Barbados Payments System Modernisation Project, with mandatory instant payments by Mar-2026.
In service since 2002; supports government, corporate and interbank transfers; links to ACH and securities settlement.
Dominant mobile money
State-backed wallet
Instant interbank settlement system for large payments
sistemas.detalhes: BD-RTGS is the real-time gross settlement system introduced by Bangladesh Bank in 2015 (https://www.bb.org.bd/en/index.php/financialactivity/paysystems#:~:text=,the%20number%20is%20increasing%20gradually). It enables high-value and time-critical transfers between banks to settle individually and immediately in central bank money. Over 10,800 bank branches are connected to BD-RTGS (https://www.bb.org.bd/en/index.php/financialactivity/paysystems#:~:text=To%20facilitate%20real%20time%20settlement,the%20number%20is%20increasing%20gradually). The system handles primarily transactions >= BDT 100,000 (threshold for customer transfers) and supports both customer and interbank transfers in real time. It has significantly sped up corporate payments and urgent transfers that previously took longer via manual processes. As of 2021, all scheduled banks were participating, and RTGS throughput was increasing (initial growth driven by government securities transactions) (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=For%20the%20first%20six%20months,percent%20lower%20in%202018%20when). BD-RTGS has become integral for large-value taka payments, ensuring finality within seconds during operating hours.

sistemas.descricao: Automated Clearing House for bulk low-value transactions
sistemas.detalhes: BEFTN is the national ACH system launched in 2011 to process bulk low-value electronic payments. It handles batched credit transfers like payroll, vendor payments, government disbursements, and debit collections (utility bills, etc.) on a next-day settlement cycle (https://iconsolutions.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Belize-White-Paper-LJ.pdf#:~:text=electronic%20payment%20mechanisms%20are%3A%20POS%2FATM,no%20interbank%20system%20for%20Direct) (https://iconsolutions.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Belize-White-Paper-LJ.pdf#:~:text=can%20be%20reduced%20to%20the,its%20own%20clearing%20and%20settlement). Banks submit files of transactions to BEFTN, which nets them and clears through Bangladesh Bank. BEFTN has greatly modernized payments – daily ACH + cheque volumes are around BDT 13,000 crore (USD ~$1.3B) in value (https://idlc.com/mbr/images/public/UHUlt40NvBb23Yq94xMVj5.pdf#:~:text=%5BPDF%5D%20CASHLESS%20ECONOMY%20,The). It has reduced transaction times (electronic credits settle by T+1 instead of multi-day paper processing (https://iconsolutions.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Belize-White-Paper-LJ.pdf#:~:text=cheques%20are%20the%20primary%20non,and%20beneficiary%20have%20accounts%20at)). BEFTN operates alongside the cheque truncation system (BACPS) under the Automated Payment System (APS) umbrella. The system has seen increasing use as organizations shift from cash/cheques to electronic transfers for routine payments.

sistemas.descricao: Digital cheque imaging and clearing system
sistemas.detalhes: BACPS is the electronic cheque clearing system (in operation since 2010s) that truncates paper cheques for digital clearing. Instead of physical movement, banks scan cheques and send images to BACPS, which clears them in an automated multilateral net settlement. With BACPS, cheque clearing times dropped from 3–7 days (manual) to next-day for local cheques (https://iconsolutions.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Belize-White-Paper-LJ.pdf#:~:text=cheques%20are%20the%20primary%20non,and%20beneficiary%20have%20accounts%20at) (https://iconsolutions.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Belize-White-Paper-LJ.pdf#:~:text=taking%20three%20days%20for%20in,accounts%20at%20the%20same%20bank). Cheques remain a significant payment instrument – in 2014 they were the primary non-cash method by value and volume in Bangladesh (https://iconsolutions.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Belize-White-Paper-LJ.pdf#:~:text=electronic%20payment%20mechanisms%20are%3A%20POS%2FATM,and%20Direct%20Debits%20for%20recurring). BACPS, operated by the central bank through the Bangladesh Bankers’ Clearing House, processes hundreds of thousands of cheques daily. While electronic payments are rising, BACPS provides efficiency for legacy paper payments and works in tandem with BEFTN. The goal is to gradually reduce reliance on cheques, but keep BACPS for those not yet fully using digital channels (https://iconsolutions.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Belize-White-Paper-LJ.pdf#:~:text=According%20to%20Marilyn%20Gardner,%E2%80%99).

sistemas.descricao: Interoperable ATM/POS and fund transfer network
sistemas.detalhes: NPSB is an interoperable switch launched in 2012 to connect banks for card-based and account-based transactions (https://www.bb.org.bd/en/index.php/financialactivity/paysystems#:~:text=,of%20October%202021%2C%2053%20banks). It links 53 banks’ ATM networks, enabling customers of any bank to use any other bank’s ATM for withdrawals, balance inquiries, fund transfers, etc. (with four types of ATM transactions supported) (https://www.bb.org.bd/en/index.php/financialactivity/paysystems#:~:text=Services%20interoperability%20is%20under%20active,set%20on%20each%20transaction%20as). NPSB also facilitates domestic POS transactions – as of 2021, 53 banks were interconnected for POS switching (https://www.bb.org.bd/en/index.php/financialactivity/paysystems#:~:text=interbank%20ATM%20transaction%20%28i,banks%20to%20ensure%20Two%20Factor) – and an internet banking fund transfer (IBFT) service that allows instant interbank account transfers via online banking (30 banks live on IBFT by 2021) (https://www.bb.org.bd/en/index.php/financialactivity/paysystems#:~:text=interbank%20ATM%20transaction%20%28i,banks%20to%20ensure%20Two%20Factor). Transaction limits (e.g. BDT 300k per transfer for individuals) apply to IBFT (https://www.bb.org.bd/en/index.php/financialactivity/paysystems#:~:text=are%20interoperable%20for%20POS%20transactions,commerce%2Finterbanking%2Fcard%20not%20present). NPSB has effectively created a unified national network for retail payments, ensuring customers can transact across banks seamlessly. It has also adopted BanglaQR standards for QR payments across providers (https://www.bb.org.bd/en/index.php/financialactivity/paysystems#:~:text=,Certified%20Institutes%20for%20BanglaQR%20Transactions). Settlement of NPSB transactions occurs via participants’ accounts at Bangladesh Bank (often through RTGS next day).

sistemas.descricao: Leading mobile money wallet with nationwide reach
sistemas.detalhes: bKash is a mobile financial service (e-wallet) launched in 2011 that has become Bangladesh’s dominant digital payments platform. It offers a wallet account (accessible via mobile app or USSD) for the unbanked and banked alike, enabling cash-in/cash-out at agents, P2P transfers, merchant payments, mobile recharges, and more. bKash’s agent network of ~330,000 agents spans urban and rural areas (https://paymentscmi.com/insights/fintech-landscape-bangladesh/#:~:text=Bangladesh%20Fintech%20and%20Payments%20Market,and%20facilitating%20millions%20of), turning cash into digital money and vice versa. With over 70 million registered users (https://paymentscmi.com/insights/fintech-landscape-bangladesh/#:~:text=Bangladesh%20Fintech%20and%20Payments%20Market,and%20facilitating%20millions%20of), bKash processes millions of transactions per day and was Bangladesh’s first fintech “unicorn”. In 2022, bKash (with Rocket and Nagad) helped digitize wage payments for many garment workers (https://btca-production-site.s3.amazonaws.com/document_files/8/document_files/Bangladesh_Country_Diagnostic.pdf#:~:text=,payments%20give%20workers%20more). bKash supports interoperability via bank links (add-money from bank accounts, etc.). It has revolutionized payments by offering instant, 24/7 transfers by phone. As of 2023, bKash and its peers facilitated 57,289 crore BDT (~$6.7B) in mobile money transactions in a single month (Jan 2021) and continue robust growth (https://www.tbsnews.net/economy/banking/mobile-banking-transactions-see-28-rise-january-yoy-388302#:~:text=Mobile%20banking%20transactions%20see%2028,at%20Tk73%2C393%20crore%20in). It remains the most widely used mobile wallet in the country, significantly advancing financial inclusion.

sistemas.descricao: Fast-growing mobile money service by Bangladesh Post
sistemas.detalhes: Nagad is a digital wallet service launched in 2019 through Bangladesh Post Office in partnership with the private sector, and it has grown extremely rapidly. It functions similarly to bKash, offering P2P transfers, merchant payments, bill pay, and cash-in/out via agents or post offices. Nagad’s rise was fueled by innovative onboarding (eKYC via mobile) and aggressive promotions. By mid-2023 Nagad reached ~80 million registered users (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/nagad-leads-the-digital-payments-revolution-in-bangladesh-301905235.html#:~:text=Having%20reached%20the%20milestone%20of,year%20in%20June%202023) (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/nagad-leads-the-digital-payments-revolution-in-bangladesh-301905235.html#:~:text=With%20Nagad%2C%20cashless%20transactions%20have,rise%20in%20digital%20payments), rivaling bKash. Daily transaction value on Nagad exceeds BDT 100 crore (~$11+ million) on average (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/nagad-leads-the-digital-payments-revolution-in-bangladesh-301905235.html#:~:text=fiscal%202022,rise%20in%20digital%20payments) (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/nagad-leads-the-digital-payments-revolution-in-bangladesh-301905235.html#:~:text=Having%20reached%20the%20milestone%20of,year%20in%20June%202023), with record single-day transactions of BDT 1,500 crore ($150 M) in March 2025 (https://www.tbsnews.net/economy/corporates/nagad-records-highest-ever-monthly-transactions-march-2025-1110261#:~:text=Nagad%20records%20highest,9%20January%2C%20Nagad%20crossed). The platform posted 240% growth in digital payment value in FY2022-23 (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/nagad-leads-the-digital-payments-revolution-in-bangladesh-301905235.html#:~:text=With%20Nagad%2C%20cashless%20transactions%20have,rise%20in%20digital%20payments). Nagad is known for integrating government payments – disbursing social allowances and education stipends digitally (over $1.85 B disbursed) (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/nagad-leads-the-digital-payments-revolution-in-bangladesh-301905235.html#:~:text=strategic%20collaborations%20with%20the%20Bangladesh,85%20billion%20among%20beneficiaries). It has also innovated with savings products and stamped itself as a key driver of cashless transactions in Bangladesh, including in rural areas via its 370k+ “Uddokta” agents. In 2023 Nagad even received a digital banking license. Its rapid adoption underscores the demand for convenient mobile money services.

sistemas.descricao: Pioneering mobile banking service by Dutch-Bangla Bank
sistemas.detalhes: Rocket (formerly **DBBL Mobile Banking**) was one of Bangladesh’s first mobile financial services, launched by Dutch-Bangla Bank in 2011. It provides mobile wallet accounts through which users can deposit/withdraw cash at agents, transfer funds, pay bills, and make purchases. Rocket initially gained substantial usage, especially among rural and low-income customers via DBBL’s nationwide agent/ATM network. It allowed basic phone (USSD) access to banking and became popular for domestic remittances. However, with the rise of bKash and Nagad, Rocket’s market share has declined. It reportedly has over 20 million registered accounts, though active user rates are lower. Rocket is still used for certain G2P payments and by customers of Dutch-Bangla Bank. It highlights the early adoption of mobile money in Bangladesh’s banking sector and continues to operate as a bank-led wallet service. In recent years Rocket’s growth has stagnated relative to its telecom-led competitors, but it remains an important player historically and for a segment of users.

sistemas.descricao: Links 58 banks for shared ATM/POS; supports Visa, Mastercard and domestic routing.
bKash leads with >70 m users; Nagad 74 m; wallets linked to Binimoy interoperability hub launched 2022.
BACPS truncates cheques (HV same-day, RV T+1); BEFTN handles ACH credits/debits for payroll, government G2P and direct debits.
Launched 2015; upgraded 2025 with ISO 20022 and 24×7 capability; settles DNS batches of BACPS, BEFTN and NPSB.
National debit system
Mobile payments
Belgian component of the Eurosystem RTGS for high-value payments
sistemas.detalhes: Belgium participates in **TARGET2**, the pan-European RTGS, through its national component TARGET2-BE. This system settles large-value euro transactions in real time, in central bank money, and is used by banks for interbank transfers, securities settlement cash legs, and urgent corporate payments. TARGET2-BE replaced Belgium’s legacy ELLIPS RTGS in 2007. All major Belgian banks connect to TARGET2; cross-border euro transfers within the network are seamless. It operates on TARGET operating days and hours (weekdays, generally 7:00–18:00 CET for customer payments). By value, TARGET2 processes the vast majority of Belgian payment flows (including final settlement of retail nets). For example, in 2022 TARGET2-BE processed transactions equivalent to several times Belgium’s GDP. It ensures immediate finality for high-value payments and is integral to Eurosystem monetary operations. The system’s adoption is universal among banks (it’s the only route for high-value euro clearing). Transactions are typically SWIFT-based messages (ISO 20022 migration ongoing).

sistemas.descricao: Domestic retail payment clearing system (ACH)
sistemas.detalhes: The CEC is Belgium’s automated clearing house for retail euro payments. It processes domestic bulk payments – SEPA credit transfers and direct debits – exchanged between Belgian banks. Retail transactions submitted during the day are cleared through multilateral netting, and the net balances are settled in TARGET2 at the end of the cycle. The CEC has been adapted to SEPA standards (it uses IBANs and SEPA file formats) while still serving as a local clearing infrastructure for intra-Belgium payments. It operates multiple clearing cycles per day. For consumers and businesses, an electronic transfer (or direct debit) sent to another Belgian bank is typically processed by the CEC and credited to the beneficiary on the same day or next day. The CEC handles a high volume of payments (hundreds of millions of transactions annually), though some large banks have gradually migrated to pan-European SEPA clearinghouses. Still, the CEC remains important for domestic efficiency. It is owned/operated by the Belgian financial sector (managed by Febelfin) under oversight of the National Bank. As of the mid-2020s, the CEC continues to clear the majority of local low-value payments that are not processed by EBA or other SEPA platforms.

sistemas.descricao: National debit card network used for POS and online payments
sistemas.detalhes: Bancontact is Belgium’s own debit card scheme, in existence since the 1980s (formerly Bancontact/Mister Cash). It is the most ubiquitous payment method for in-store payments in Belgium – nearly every Belgian with a bank account has a Bancontact card. Bancontact transactions are PIN-based (or contactless) and are authorized online against cardholder funds. The scheme is managed by Bancontact Payconiq Company and is interoperable with all Belgian banks. Bancontact is accepted at virtually all merchants, and also used for e-commerce via the Bancontact online payment button. In 2022, Belgians made roughly 2.3 billion electronic payments with Bancontact/Payconiq combined (https://www.bancontact.com/en/news/payments-with-bancontact-and-payconiq-increase-by-54-5-in-five-years#:~:text=Payments%20increase%20by%2054.5,pay%20with%20Bancontact%20or%20Payconiq), double the volume of a decade earlier. Bancontact’s share of retail payments is significant – in fact, 2022 was the first time electronic payments (largely Bancontact) exceeded cash payments in Belgium (https://www.bancontact.com/en/news/payments-with-bancontact-and-payconiq-increase-by-54-5-in-five-years#:~:text=Payments%20increase%20by%2054.5,pay%20with%20Bancontact%20or%20Payconiq). The scheme has also enabled mobile usage by linking with Payconiq. With Maestro being phased out in EU, Bancontact now co-badges with Mastercard Debit for international acceptance. Bancontact’s reliability and ubiquity make it a cornerstone of Belgium’s payment landscape.

sistemas.descricao: Mobile payment app and QR code platform
sistemas.detalhes: Payconiq is a mobile payments ecosystem that merged with Bancontact in Belgium. Via the Payconiq by Bancontact smartphone app, users can link their bank accounts and make instant payments peer-to-peer or to merchants. It uses QR code scanning or contact lists to transfer funds, with the underlying transfer executed as a SEPA Instant Credit Transfer between banks. Payconiq is widely integrated: many shops and restaurants display Payconiq QR codes for quick checkout. It’s also used for online payments (scan QR on e-commerce checkout). Belgian banks collectively support Payconiq, making it a multi-bank platform. Mobile payment usage has surged – in 2023 Belgians used mobile (Payconiq or Bancontact in app) 368 million times, 34% more than 2022 (https://assets-eu-01.kc-usercontent.com/331a0185-e26c-01d0-41e9-c42bc79a1d2c/6bf42db6-6363-4041-b9d3-54c6548f8e14/Press%20Release-22Feb2024.pdf#:~:text=,to%20be). Payconiq is especially popular for P2P (splitting bills, etc.) and for small merchants due to low fees. Together with Bancontact cards, Payconiq has driven Belgium’s digital payment volume to new heights, and the average Belgian now has the app as a common payment method. It exemplifies the shift from card-only to smartphone-based payments in the country.

sistemas.descricao: Provides QR and phone-number payments interoperable with SCT Inst.
24 banks issue co-branded cards; supports contactless, e-commerce and wearable payments; will converge into European wallet Wero.
All Belgian banks must receive instant by Jan-2025 and send by Oct-2025 under EU Regulation; currently 24 banks covering 97 % of accounts support it.
Operated by National Bank of Belgium; settles interbank, ECB monetary operations and ancillary system positions.

Regional real-time gross settlement system for West African CFA franc (https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099755005052330771/pdf/SECBOS05b2c92b0ac0b3ea004562a26270c.pdf#:~:text=STAR,in%20STAR%20in%20central) (https://cb-umoa.org/fr/glossaire/s#:~:text=STAR,r%C3%A9el%20des%20transactions%20d)
sistemas.detalhes: STAR-UEMOA is the RTGS that serves all eight countries of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU), including Burkina Faso. Operated by the Central Bank (BCEAO) since 2005, it settles high-value and urgent FCFA (CFA franc) payments in real time with finality (https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099755005052330771/pdf/SECBOS05b2c92b0ac0b3ea004562a26270c.pdf#:~:text=STAR,in%20STAR%20in%20central). All banks and treasuries in Burkina have accounts in STAR for interbank transfers, large client payments, and government transactions. It processes gross payments continuously throughout the day, and is the backbone for settling net positions from other systems (SICA, bank card switch). Type: Regional RTGS (wholesale). Operator: BCEAO.

sistemas.descricao: Automated clearing system for low-value payments in WAEMU (ACH for CFA franc) (https://www.bceao.int/en/content/payment-systems-management#:~:text=Payment%20Systems%20Management%20,less%20than%2050%20million) (https://cb-umoa.org/fr/glossaire/s#:~:text=STAR,r%C3%A9el%20des%20transactions%20d)
sistemas.detalhes: SICA-UEMOA is the regional interbank clearing house for retail payments in the CFA franc zone (https://www.bceao.int/en/content/payment-systems-management#:~:text=Payment%20Systems%20Management%20,less%20than%2050%20million). It clears batched transactions like cheques, direct debits, and small credit transfers under FCFA 100 million. Banks in Burkina send payment files to SICA, which automatically exchanges and nets them multilaterally each day. Net balances are then settled through STAR-UEMOA RTGS (https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099755005052330771/pdf/SECBOS05b2c92b0ac0b3ea004562a26270c.pdf#:~:text=STAR,in%20STAR%20in%20central). SICA has drastically sped up clearing – e.g. cheques now clear in T+1 across WAEMU. Operated by BCEAO. Type: ACH (multilateral netting for WAEMU).

sistemas.descricao: Interbank card payment and ATM/POS network for the WAEMU zone (https://blogs.worldbank.org/en/africacan/burkina-faso-public-treasury-enters-age-digital-payments#:~:text=,West%20African%20Economic%20and)
sistemas.detalhes: GIM-UEMOA (Groupement Interbancaire Monétique de l’UEMOA) is a regional switch connecting ATMs and POS terminals across the 8-country union (https://blogs.worldbank.org/en/africacan/burkina-faso-public-treasury-enters-age-digital-payments#:~:text=,West%20African%20Economic%20and). It issues a unified card scheme (branded "GIM") that all member bank cards carry, enabling withdrawals and payments region-wide on any bank’s machines. GIM-UEMOA also partners with international schemes (Mastercard partnership to co-brand cards) (https://www.mastercard.com/news/eemea/en/newsroom/press-releases/en/2024/july-1/gim-uemoa-and-mastercard-formalize-a-strategic-partnership-to-accelerate-innovation-and-promote-financial-inclusion-in-the-uemoa-region/#:~:text=GIM,inclusion%20in%20the%20UEMOA%20region). In Burkina, all major banks are members, so customers can use their bank card nationwide and in neighboring WAEMU countries seamlessly. The switch clears card transactions and net settles through BCEAO. Type: Card scheme & switch. Operator: GIM-UEMOA (a BCEAO subsidiary).

sistemas.descricao: Telecom-led mobile money services allowing instant P2P transfers and payments
sistemas.detalhes: Mobile money has become a key payment rail in Burkina Faso, led by telecom operators. Orange Money (by Orange) is the largest service, alongside MOOV Money (MOOV Africa) and YUP (Societe Generale’s mobile wallet) (https://www.bceao.int/sites/default/files/2024-04/List%20of%20electronic%20money%20issuing%20institutions%20as%20of%20march%2014%2C%202024%20%20-%20Table%20of%20issuing%20institutions_0.pdf#:~:text=MTN%20MOBILE%20MONEY%2F,UBA%20BURKINA) (https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/442841556641027805/txt/Burkina-Faso-Financial-Inclusion-Support-Project.txt#:~:text=Burkina,agent%20network%20of%2016%2C700). These services let users deposit cash at agents, then send money domestically via USSD/phone apps, pay bills, and withdraw cash. They operate on a telco platform but are regulated by BCEAO as e-money issuers. Transactions are instant within the same network; interoperability between providers is limited (though efforts exist via bilateral corridors). Type: Mobile money (wallet-based, USSD/app).

sistemas.descricao: Digital payment portals for government services and treasury operations
sistemas.detalhes: The Burkina Faso government, via the Public Treasury, has integrated with the national payments infrastructure to enable digital collection of taxes and fees (https://www.capmad.com/technology-en/burkina-faso-treasury-embraces-the-digital-payment-era/#:~:text=Burkina%20Faso%20%3A%20Treasury%20embraces,UEMOA). For example, a platform allows citizens to pay taxes, utility bills, or school fees using either mobile money, GIM-UEMOA cards, or bank transfers. The Treasury is a participant in STAR-UEMOA and SICA-UEMOA (https://www.capmad.com/technology-en/burkina-faso-treasury-embraces-the-digital-payment-era/#:~:text=Burkina%20Faso%20%3A%20Treasury%20embraces,UEMOA), meaning government receipts and disbursements settle electronically. Additionally, systems like SIGTAS (for taxes) and the Bill Payment Portal provide online payment options. Type: Government-backed payment portals (utilizing existing rails).

sistemas.descricao: Burkina Faso, as part of WAEMU, uses the BCEAO’s regional RTGS called STAR-UEMOA [oai_citation:90‡bceao.int]. STAR-UEMOA settles high-value and time-critical payments in real time across the eight member countries using the common currency (FCFA). Commercial banks in Burkina have accounts at BCEAO and send large-value fund transfers (interbank, government, FX, etc.) through STAR, which provides immediate finality. STAR-UEMOA significantly reduced settlement risk region-wide when introduced in 2004, and processes thousands of transactions daily for all WAEMU states.

Mobile money has grown significantly in Burkina Faso. Operators like Orange Money and Moov provide e-wallets that allow customers to deposit cash with agents, then send money, pay bills, and make purchases via mobile phone. While not centrally run, BCEAO oversees these services through e-money issuer licenses. Interoperability between mobile money and banks is improving (some integration via APIs for bank-wallet transfers). In 2020, mobile money in Burkina saw tens of millions of transactions, helping boost financial inclusion in rural areas. Efforts are underway at the regional level to connect mobile money to the banking network more seamlessly.

SICA-UEMOA is the regional ACH for Burkina Faso and other WAEMU countries [oai_citation:92‡bceao.int]. It clears bulk payment instruments: smaller electronic credit transfers, direct debits, cheques, and bills of exchange, on a multilateral net settlement basis. Each country has a local clearing subsystem within SICA, and BCEAO manages the overall platform. Payments under FCFA 50 million are typically funneled through SICA [oai_citation:93‡bceao.int]. At end of cycle (usually daily), net positions are settled through STAR (the RTGS). Implemented in the mid-2000s, SICA greatly improved efficiency of retail payments across the region, replacing manual clearinghouses.

GIM-UEMOA is a regional interbank card switching network that connects ATMs and POS terminals across the WAEMU countries (including Burkina). Banks issue cards with the GIM logo, which can be used at any member bank’s ATMs/POS. GIM processes card authorization and clearing, then net settles between banks via BCEAO. The scheme also integrates mobile money operators to some extent, moving toward full interoperability [oai_citation:96‡africanenda.org]. In recent years, GIM-UEMOA has rolled out contactless cards and is exploring instant payments and QR code solutions. In Burkina Faso, virtually all ATMs are part of GIM, enabling nationwide card access to cash and payments.

Real-time gross settlement system in Bulgarian lev, operated by BNB since 2003 (https://sarajevotimes.com/bosnias-central-bank-marks-20-years-since-the-establishment-of-the-payment-systems/#:~:text=Reliability%C2%A0%E2%80%93%20since%2005%20January%202001%2C,without%20any%20delays%20or%20problems) (https://sarajevotimes.com/bosnias-central-bank-marks-20-years-since-the-establishment-of-the-payment-systems/#:~:text=Since%20the%20first%20business%20day%2C,the%20payment%20systems%20of%20the)
sistemas.detalhes: RINGS (Real-time Interbank Gross Settlement) is Bulgaria’s high-value payment system. It settles payments in BGN in real time with finality, and is operated by the Bulgarian National Bank. Launched in 2003 as part of EU integration, it runs on TARGET2-like principles. Banks use RINGS for large or urgent leva transactions (e.g. interbank transfers, securities settlement) with no upper limit. It also settles net positions from BISERA clearing. Availability is intraday on business days. Type: RTGS. Operator: BNB.

sistemas.descricao: Automated clearing house for BGN retail payments (bulk transfers, <BGN 100k) (https://evroto.bg/en/media/178-bta-mr-petar-chobanov-deputy-governor-of-bnb-in-charge-of-the-banking-departm#:~:text=BTA%3A%20Petar%20Chobanov%3A%20We%20are,BISERA%20to%20the%20Eurosystem%27s)
sistemas.detalhes: BISERA6 is the electronic clearing system for lev-denominated customer payments. Operated by BORICA AD under BNB oversight, it processes credit transfers and direct debits in BGN up to a high threshold (effectively covering most retail payments) (https://evroto.bg/en/media/178-bta-mr-petar-chobanov-deputy-governor-of-bnb-in-charge-of-the-banking-departm#:~:text=BTA%3A%20Petar%20Chobanov%3A%20We%20are,BISERA%20to%20the%20Eurosystem%27s). Payments are exchanged and netted in multiple cycles per day, with two clearing sessions on business days. Net results settle in RINGS at end-of-day. BISERA6 handles salaries, bill payments, internet banking transfers, etc. Type: ACH (deferred net settlement).

sistemas.descricao: Domestic instant payment program for Lev transfers within seconds, 24/7 (https://www.ccbank.bg/en/natural-persons/internet-bank/instant-payments-blink#:~:text=INSTANT%20PAYMENTS%20BLINK%20,only%20between%20payment%20service) (https://www.unicreditbulbank.bg/en/corporate-clients/instant-payments-blink/#:~:text=Send%20and%20receive%20money%20within,regardless%20of%20holidays%20and%20weekends)
sistemas.detalhes: Blink is the new instant payment scheme under the National Card and Payment Scheme (NCPS) of Bulgaria, operated by BORICA. Launched in 2022–2023, Blink enables interbank transfers in Bulgarian lev up to BGN 30,000 to be completed within seconds, any time. Participating banks integrate Blink into their online and mobile banking, allowing customers to send money instantly to accounts at other banks (initially 24/7 availability). Blink payments clear through BORICA’s platform and settle immediately via dedicated liquidity in RINGS. Type: Instant retail payment (24/7). Operator: BORICA (NCPS).

sistemas.descricao: Clearing system for SEPA credit transfers in EUR, with TIPS instant extension (https://evroto.bg/en/media/178-bta-mr-petar-chobanov-deputy-governor-of-bnb-in-charge-of-the-banking-departm#:~:text=BTA%3A%20Petar%20Chobanov%3A%20We%20are,BISERA%20to%20the%20Eurosystem%27s) (https://fintech.global/2024/12/20/bulgarian-national-bank-connects-to-ecbs-tips-platform/#:~:text=Bulgarian%20National%20Bank%20connects%20to,any%20other%20TIPS%20participant%2C)
sistemas.detalhes: BISERA7 is the interbank clearing system for euro-denominated payments within Bulgaria (and a gateway to pan-European SEPA). Operated by BORICA, it processes SEPA credit transfers, both domestic and cross-border, including standing orders and SEPA Direct Debits. Bulgaria’s planned euro adoption has driven integration: in 2023 BISERA7 was linked to the ECB’s TARGET Instant Payment Settlement (TIPS) service (https://evroto.bg/en/media/178-bta-mr-petar-chobanov-deputy-governor-of-bnb-in-charge-of-the-banking-departm#:~:text=One%20of%20these%20projects%20was,BISERA%20to%20the%20Eurosystem%27s) (https://fintech.global/2024/12/20/bulgarian-national-bank-connects-to-ecbs-tips-platform/#:~:text=Bulgarian%20National%20Bank%20connects%20to,any%20other%20TIPS%20participant%2C). This allows Bulgarian banks to send/receive SEPA Instant payments in EUR to any TIPS participant in seconds. Type: ACH + Instant hybrid (deferred net for regular SEPA; real-time via TIPS for SEPA Instant).

sistemas.descricao: Domestic card scheme and ATM/POS network operated by BORICA
sistemas.detalhes: Bulgaria’s NCPS, run by BORICA AD, includes a national card brand called „Борика“ (Bcard) and the unified ATM/POS switching infrastructure. All banks are connected to the BORICA switch, which ensures any Bulgarian bank card can transact at any ATM or POS in the country. The Bcard debit card was introduced to offer a local low-cost alternative to Visa/Mastercard, and can be co-badged with Discover for international acceptance. NCPS sets common standards (EMV chip, contactless) and handles card transaction clearing and settlement (netted and settled via RINGS). Type: Card scheme & switch. Operator: BORICA.

sistemas.descricao: BISERA is Bulgaria’s system for clearing retail (low-value) payments. BISERA6 processes BGN-denominated transfers among banks, while BISERA7 handles EUR-denominated SEPA payments. Operated by BORICA AD under BNB oversight, BISERA clears credit transfers, direct debits, and other non-urgent payments in batches, with net positions settled in RINGS or TARGET2. In 2021, BISERA6 was upgraded to ISO 20022 XML format for credit transfers [oai_citation:79‡cashmanagement.bnpparibas.com], and Bulgaria also joined SEPA Instant via BISERA7 and TIPS in 2022 [oai_citation:80‡ecb.europa.eu]. These systems ensure efficient next-day (and now instant for EUR) clearing of consumer and business payments.

RINGS is Bulgaria’s RTGS system for payments in Bulgarian Lev, operated by BNB. It handles high-value and urgent transfers among banks and was launched in 2003. RINGS processes large-value customer payments, interbank money market settlements, and other critical transactions in real time. By 2024, RINGS availability and stability is ~100%, ensuring continuous operation. For euro payments, Bulgarian banks use TARGET2-BNB for real-time settlement. RINGS is crucial domestically until Bulgaria joins the euro, carrying the bulk of value (in 2022, RINGS transactions equaled several times GDP in value).

Bcard is Bulgaria’s national card and payment scheme, officially started in 2016 as an initiative of BNB and BORICA [oai_citation:85‡bcard.bg] [oai_citation:86‡bg.linkedin.com]. The first Bcard debit cards were issued in 2018 [oai_citation:87‡bg.linkedin.com]. Bcard aims to provide a domestic alternative for card payments, with all processing done in-country. BORICA partnered with Discover to ensure Bcard’s acceptance abroad and to allow Discover/Diners acceptance at Bcard terminals [oai_citation:88‡investorrelations.discover.com] [oai_citation:89‡borica.bg]. Bcard cards can be used at ATMs and POS of all banks in Bulgaria through the BORICA switching network. Adoption is still growing, as banks gradually add Bcard alongside Visa/Mastercard.

Banque de la République du Burundi’s real-time gross settlement system (https://migrantmoney.uncdf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Payment-Infrastructure-Assessment-Burundi-April2025.pdf#:~:text=,RTGS%29%20system%2C%20the)
sistemas.detalhes: The central bank (BRB) operates an Automated Transfer System (ATS) that includes a Real-Time Gross Settlement component for large-value payments (https://migrantmoney.uncdf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Payment-Infrastructure-Assessment-Burundi-April2025.pdf#:~:text=,RTGS%29%20system%2C%20the). Implemented in the 2010s with donor support, it allows banks to settle interbank transfers, government payments, and other high-value transactions instantly in Burundi francs. Participants hold accounts at BRB and send SWIFT-based payment instructions for immediate settlement if funds are sufficient. The RTGS ensures finality for critical payments and also settles net positions from the retail clearing. Type: RTGS (wholesale). Operated by BRB.

sistemas.descricao: Deferred net settlement system for low-value and paper-based payments
sistemas.detalhes: Burundi’s ATS also includes an Automated Clearing House for retail electronic transfers and cheque image clearing. Banks submit batches of low-value credit transfers (salaries, person-to-person bank payments) and scanned cheque data to the ACH, which nets obligations at end of cycle and forwards them to RTGS for settlement. Cheques historically were a main cashless instrument, but processing time has reduced to ~T+1 with cheque truncation. Type: ACH (multilateral netting). Operated by BRB in collaboration with the Bankers’ Association.

sistemas.descricao: Mobile money has emerged as a vital payment channel in Burundi, driven by telecom operators. Lumicash (by Lumitel) and EcoCash (formerly by Econet/Leo) allow users to send money peer-to-peer via mobile phone, pay utilities, and withdraw/deposit through agent networks . Given low bank access, these wallets serve as quasi-bank accounts for many, supporting instant transfers via USSD or app. They are denominated in BIF and regulated by BRB as e-money issuers. Some level of interoperability with banks exists (e.g., linking bank accounts to wallets), but direct wallet-to-wallet inter-network transfers are not yet in place. Type: Mobile money services.
sistemas.detalhes: Mobile money has emerged as a vital payment channel in Burundi, driven by telecom operators. Lumicash (by Lumitel) and EcoCash (formerly by Econet/Leo) allow users to send money peer-to-peer via mobile phone, pay utilities, and withdraw/deposit through agent networks (https://publication.aercafricalibrary.org/bitstreams/5ea82984-99ee-4dc9-8dc9-b8b46270b567/download#:~:text=,becoming%20an%20important%20solution). Given low bank access, these wallets serve as quasi-bank accounts for many, supporting instant transfers via USSD or app. They are denominated in BIF and regulated by BRB as e-money issuers. Some level of interoperability with banks exists (e.g., linking bank accounts to wallets), but direct wallet-to-wallet inter-network transfers are not yet in place. Type: Mobile money services.

sistemas.descricao: Cross-border payment links with East African and COMESA systems
sistemas.detalhes: As a member of the East African Community and COMESA, Burundi is connected to certain regional payment networks. The EAC’s East African Payment System (EAPS) links member central banks’ RTGS systems, enabling cross-border shilling payments (Burundi joined in 2018). COMESA’s REPSS (Regional Payment and Settlement System) allows USD/EUR transfers among trade partners through central banks. These systems let Burundian banks make relatively faster and cheaper international payments within Africa by leveraging central bank networks. Type: Regional RTGS integration (for cross-border). Operated by EAC and COMESA central banks.

sistemas.descricao: The Bank of the Republic of Burundi (BRB) implemented an ATS in 2018 that combines RTGS (real-time gross settlement) for high-value payments and an ACH module for retail payments [oai_citation:98‡cma.se]. This modern system (supplied by CMA Small Systems) replaced older processes and connects with regional networks like the COMESA REPSS and the East African Payments System (EAPS) [oai_citation:99‡cma.se]. The RTGS part handles large-value and urgent Burundi franc transfers in real time, while the ACH part clears batched low-value transactions (e.g., payroll, utility payments) on a deferred net basis. The ATS has improved efficiency and enabled interoperability with neighboring countries’ systems.

Regional payment system
Regional real-time gross settlement system in West Africa
sistemas.detalhes: Benin, as part of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU/UEMOA), uses the regional RTGS called **STAR-UEMOA** (Système de Transfert Automatique et de Règlement). Operated by the BCEAO (common central bank), STAR-UEMOA settles high-value and time-critical CFA franc payments across the eight member countries (including Benin) in real time. It processes interbank transfers, central bank operations, and settles the net positions of other systems (ACH, card switch) in central bank money. STAR-UEMOA has participants from all commercial banks and the BCEAO agencies in Benin. It has greatly sped up large-value flows – e.g. cross-border payments within WAEMU that once took days are now same-day via STAR. The system handles significant value: transactions processed region-wide amount to a substantial percentage of WAEMU’s GDP annually (https://smartafrica.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/31758-e-payments-blueprint_eng.pdf#:~:text=%5BPDF%5D%20Blueprint%20for%20e,RTGS). Benin’s banks account for a portion of that (Benin’s economy ~5% of WAEMU’s output). Adoption is universal for large payments, and STAR runs daily, closing with final multilateral net settlements. It’s a key pillar of the integrated regional payment infrastructure supporting trade and finance in Benin and neighbors.

sistemas.descricao: Regional ACH for CFA franc retail payments
sistemas.detalhes: SICA-UEMOA is the automated clearing house system that processes low-value interbank payments (cheques, EFT credits, direct debits) within WAEMU countries, including Benin. Banks send retail payment files to SICA, which computes multilateral net settlement positions for each country. It handles the clearing of cheques and SEPA-like credit transfers under standardized rules (transfers below 50 million CFA are typically via SICA) (https://www.bceao.int/en/content/payment-systems-management#:~:text=Payment%20Systems%20Management%20,less%20than%2050%20million). For Benin, this means that domestic transactions between banks – payroll, vendor payments, utility payments, etc. – are cleared in cycles through SICA-Benin, with the BCEAO’s national branch overseeing it. The net results are then settled in STAR RTGS. SICA has significantly improved efficiency, reducing cheque clearing float and enabling electronic salary payments. In 2021, SICA-UEMOA processed tens of millions of transactions regionally. Benin’s portion by volume is moderate (population ~12M). SICA is well-adopted: the majority of non-cash retail payments (except card or mobile money) go through it. It has contributed to harmonizing payments across UEMOA. In Benin, all banks participate in SICA; it has enabled innovations like check image clearing and faster funds availability.

sistemas.descricao: Regional card payment network for West Africa
sistemas.detalhes: GIM-UEMOA (Groupement Interbancaire Monétique) is the regional card switching and settlement system covering Benin and other WAEMU states. It connects banks and switches ATM and POS transactions made with domestically issued cards. GIM-UEMOA also issues a regional debit card (the **GIM card**) that can be used across all member countries’ ATMs/POS. In Benin, banks either issue GIM-branded cards or co-badge them with international schemes, and all their ATMs are part of the GIM network, enabling customers to withdraw cash or pay with cards beyond their own bank. GIM processes card authorizations in real time and nets the interbank positions for settlement via the BCEAO. In December 2011, GIM launched “GIM Mobile” to link cards to mobile accounts for mobile-based payments (https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/ng/pdf/dealadvisory/ng-KPMG-Payment-Developments-in-Africa-Volume-2.pdf#:~:text=,cards%20to%20the%20GIM) (https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/ng/pdf/dealadvisory/ng-KPMG-Payment-Developments-in-Africa-Volume-2.pdf#:~:text=services%20assets,cards%20to%20the%20GIM). Adoption has been growing as card usage slowly rises – by 2022, electronic card payments in UEMOA increased significantly, though from a low base. Benin’s card usage is modest relative to some neighbors; it accounted for ~5.2% of UEMOA’s mobile money accounts by some metrics (https://bceao.int/sites/default/files/inline-files/3etat_des_services_financiers_uemoa_2016_anglais_.pdf#:~:text=OVERVIEW%20OF%20MOBILE%20FINANCIAL%20SERVICES,GUINEA%20BISSAU%200%2C04), which suggests card adoption similarly is a fraction of region totals. Still, GIM-UEMOA has been crucial in providing a local switching alternative and reducing reliance on foreign card networks for intra-regional transactions. It continues expanding merchant acceptance and ATM interoperability in Benin.

sistemas.nome: Mobile Money Services (MTN Mobile Money, Moov Money)
sistemas.descricao: Telecom-led e-wallets for instant payments and transfers
sistemas.detalhes: Mobile money has become a dominant payment method in Benin, driven by telecom operators. **MTN Mobile Money** (MoMo) and **Moov Money** are the two primary services. These let users (even without bank accounts) store funds on their phone SIM wallet and make instant transfers, pay bills, purchase airtime, and withdraw cash via agent networks. With nearly 100% mobile penetration and a previously underbanked population, mobile money has skyrocketed – by 2021, Benin had over 10 million registered mobile money accounts, with active usage growing fast (https://www.cgap.org/sites/default/files/CGAP-Technology-Program-Country-Note-West-African-Economic-and-Monetary-Union-Jun-2011.pdf#:~:text=,Airtel%20Money%20has%20launched). Mobile money handles the bulk of person-to-person remittances and many utility payments. For example, government digital payment initiatives (like e-tax) integrate mobile money for ease of payment. According to BCEAO, in 2021 Benin’s share of WAEMU mobile money transactions was about 5.2% (https://bceao.int/sites/default/files/inline-files/3etat_des_services_financiers_uemoa_2016_anglais_.pdf#:~:text=OVERVIEW%20OF%20MOBILE%20FINANCIAL%20SERVICES,GUINEA%20BISSAU%200%2C04) (Ivory Coast, Mali being larger), but usage is expanding. Adoption is high among individuals and micro-businesses due to convenience and agent reach. Mobile money transactions are settled over the operators’ trust accounts in banks, and the BCEAO oversees interoperability initiatives. In WAEMU, regulations now allow transfers between mobile wallets of different networks, improving utility. Mobile money is arguably the most widely used non-cash payment method in Benin by volume of transactions, significantly advancing financial inclusion.

sistemas.descricao: Supports 24×7 transfers and QR payments between any account; includes alias directory; Benin banks in first and second pilot cohorts.
Operated by BCEAO; Benin banks participate through Cotonou branch; supports intraday credit and DvP for securities.
Three daily clearing sessions, net positions settle in STAR-UEMOA; cheques truncated via image.

Brunei’s first instant fund transfer system via phone number aliases (https://thescoop.co/2025/03/12/tarus-to-enable-instant-payments-using-just-a-phone-number/#:~:text=BANDAR%20SERI%20BEGAWAN%20%E2%80%93%20Brunei,instantly%20via%20their%20phone%20number) (https://thescoop.co/2025/03/12/tarus-to-enable-instant-payments-using-just-a-phone-number/#:~:text=payments)
sistemas.detalhes: tarus is a new digital payment hub (launched 2025) that enables immediate money transfers between banks and e-wallets by using mobile phone numbers as proxies (https://thescoop.co/2025/03/12/tarus-to-enable-instant-payments-using-just-a-phone-number/#:~:text=BANDAR%20SERI%20BEGAWAN%20%E2%80%93%20Brunei,instantly%20via%20their%20phone%20number) (https://thescoop.co/2025/03/12/tarus-to-enable-instant-payments-using-just-a-phone-number/#:~:text=payments). Operated by National Digital Payments Network (ndpx) – a JV of government and banks – tarus provides the backend infrastructure for 24/7 instant credits within Brunei’s financial system (https://thescoop.co/2025/03/12/tarus-to-enable-instant-payments-using-just-a-phone-number/#:~:text=their%20phone%20number) (https://thescoop.co/2025/03/12/tarus-to-enable-instant-payments-using-just-a-phone-number/#:~:text=Launched%20by%20the%20National%20Digital,wallets). Users will access tarus through their existing banking or wallet apps (it’s not a standalone app) (https://thescoop.co/2025/03/12/tarus-to-enable-instant-payments-using-just-a-phone-number/#:~:text=How%20tarus%20works) (https://thescoop.co/2025/03/12/tarus-to-enable-instant-payments-using-just-a-phone-number/#:~:text=tarus%20into%20their%20systems%2C%20allowing,platform%20transfers). By linking accounts to a phone, customers can send/receive funds across different banks or mobile wallets in seconds. Type: Instant retail payment system (24/7). Overseen by Brunei Darussalam Central Bank (BDCB), operated by ndpx.

sistemas.descricao: High-value payment system for instant interbank settlements (since 2014) (https://www.bdcb.gov.bn/consumer/financial-education/digital-payments/leap-of-faith#:~:text=for%20the%20benefit%20of%20the,on%2012th%20May%202017) (https://www.bdcb.gov.bn/consumer/financial-education/digital-payments/leap-of-faith#:~:text=,Secure)
sistemas.detalhes: Brunei’s RTGS was introduced on 7 Nov 2014 as part of the National Payment Settlement System (NPSS) project (https://www.bdcb.gov.bn/consumer/financial-education/digital-payments/leap-of-faith#:~:text=for%20the%20benefit%20of%20the,on%2012th%20May%202017). It enables immediate gross settlement of large-value or urgent transfers between banks through BDCB. Participants (banks and BDCB) send single payment instructions that are settled one by one in real time, eliminating interbank credit risk (https://www.bdcb.gov.bn/consumer/financial-education/digital-payments/leap-of-faith#:~:text=,Secure) (https://www.bdcb.gov.bn/consumer/financial-education/digital-payments/leap-of-faith#:~:text=%3E%20,liquidity%20to%20the%20financial%20system). RTGS also settles the net positions from other systems (ACH, CSD). It operates during business hours. Type: RTGS (wholesale). Operated by Brunei Darussalam Central Bank.

sistemas.descricao: Automated Clearing House for retail batched payments and cheque clearing (https://www.bdcb.gov.bn/consumer/financial-education/digital-payments/leap-of-faith#:~:text=for%20the%20benefit%20of%20the,on%2012th%20May%202017) (https://www.bdcb.gov.bn/consumer/financial-education/digital-payments/leap-of-faith#:~:text=)
sistemas.detalhes: The ACH system (launched 26 May 2016) clears high-volume, low-value transactions in Brunei’s NPSS (https://www.bdcb.gov.bn/consumer/financial-education/digital-payments/leap-of-faith#:~:text=for%20the%20benefit%20of%20the,on%2012th%20May%202017) (https://www.bdcb.gov.bn/consumer/financial-education/digital-payments/leap-of-faith#:~:text=). It processes batched files of direct credit transfers (e.g. payroll, vendor payments) and truncates cheques electronically. Batches are exchanged and processed at intervals, with final net settlement occurring in RTGS the same day. The ACH drastically reduced cheque clearing time from T+4 to T+2 (https://www.bdcb.gov.bn/consumer/financial-education/digital-payments/leap-of-faith#:~:text=). It also handles recurring payments like utility or loan payments. Type: Multilateral ACH clearing. Operated by BDCB in collaboration with banks.

sistemas.nome: Digital Wallets & E-Money (Pocket, BIBD NEXGEN, etc.)
sistemas.descricao: Mobile e-wallet apps offered by banks/telcos for QR payments, top-ups, transfers
sistemas.detalhes: Several e-money wallets operate in Brunei’s market: e.g. BIBD NEXGEN wallet (by Bank Islam Brunei Darussalam), Baiduri’s i-Banking app, Progresif’s “Dart” and “DING” apps, and Pocket (by startup ThreeG Media). These apps let users store funds, pay merchants (often via QR code or scanned in-app), and send P2P transfers within the same platform. Until tarus, they were not interoperable across providers, so each wallet formed its own ecosystem. With tarus integration, they will be able to do cross-platform instant payments (https://thescoop.co/2025/03/12/tarus-to-enable-instant-payments-using-just-a-phone-number/#:~:text=In%20the%20next%20phase%2C%20Baiduri,to%20join%20the%20tarus%20network). Type: Mobile wallet services (closed-loop, now shifting to interoperable via tarus).

sistemas.descricao: Brunei’s RTGS was implemented in November 2014 by Autoriti Monetari Brunei Darussalam (AMBD) [oai_citation:67‡cms.bdcb.gov.bn] [oai_citation:68‡cms.bdcb.gov.bn]. It is the central infrastructure for interbank fund transfers in Brunei dollars, handling large-value and urgent payments in real-time. Notably, Brunei’s RTGS was the first in ASEAN to adopt the SWIFT ISO 20022 MX standard from inception [oai_citation:69‡cms.bdcb.gov.bn], enhancing regional interoperability. All licensed banks participate. The RTGS drastically reduced settlement risk and paved the way for modern ACH and digital payments in Brunei.

Brunei is developing a centralized Digital Payment Hub to facilitate instant, low-cost payments among banks, fintech e-wallets, and merchants [oai_citation:75‡thescoop.co] [oai_citation:76‡thescoop.co]. This platform (expected ~2025) will allow real-time retail payments (P2P, P2B) by interconnecting different payment channels on a 24/7 basis. It aims to overcome current limitations: RTGS is bank-only and costly, POS networks settle next-day, and existing payment gateways are fragmented [oai_citation:77‡thescoop.co]. The Hub will use open APIs to let banks and non-banks connect, enabling interoperability of e-wallets and possibly linking to regional networks for cross-border instant payments.

Brunei’s ACH was introduced in 2015 following the RTGS launch [oai_citation:72‡cms.bdcb.gov.bn]. It facilitates electronic clearing of retail payments such as salaries, GIRO credits, direct debits, and other low-value interbank transfers. The ACH replaced the manual cheque clearing house (which was absorbed by AMBD in 2014) [oai_citation:73‡cms.bdcb.gov.bn]. It operates on a multilateral net settlement model: transactions are exchanged among banks and netted, with the final net positions settled each day via the RTGS. The ACH has greatly increased efficiency in Brunei’s payment system, enabling same-day or next-day fund transfers instead of paper-based instruments.
