Launched by the central bank in 2022, QR BCB Bolivia is a national instant payment scheme based on standardized QR codes [oai_citation:12‡iupana.com]. It enables any bank or e-wallet user to transfer funds by scanning a QR, with interoperability across all financial institutions [oai_citation:13‡bcb.gob.bo] [oai_citation:14‡bcb.gob.bo]. Initially rolled out with one bank (Banco Unión), it is gradually expanding to all banks by 2024 [oai_citation:15‡iupana.com]. Transactions are processed in real-time and available 24/7, aiming to promote cashless payments in stores, P2P, bill payments, and government disbursements.
sistemas.detalhes: A fast payment scheme launched by Banco Central de Bolivia in 2022 that uses QR codes for real-time transfers. It links banks and mobile wallets to enable 24/7 instant payments via QR scanning (https://www.bis.org/publ/bppdf/bispap153.pdf#:~:text=In%20Bolivia%2C%20the%20private%20sector,with%20QR%20codes%20in%202019) (https://www.bis.org/publ/bppdf/bispap153.pdf#:~:text=2023,or%20using%20mobile%20phone%20numbers). Operated by the central bank as part of Bolivia’s interoperable payment network, it is a retail instant payment system designed to boost financial inclusion. Adoption surged after standardization – QR payments rose from 2% of electronic transfers in 2021 to 39% by 2023 (https://www.bis.org/publ/bppdf/bispap153.pdf#:~:text=use%20skyrocketed%20with%20the%20standardisation,These%20wallets%2C%20operated%20by%20different) (https://www.bis.org/publ/bppdf/bispap153.pdf#:~:text=skyrocketed%20with%20the%20standardisation%20of,operated%20by%20different%20consortia%20of). All banks and e-money providers participate, and users can pay merchants or peers instantly by scanning codes. Type: Instant retail payment (24/7). Operated by BCB.

sistemas.descricao: Bolivia’s high-value interbank Real-Time Gross Settlement system (https://www.bcb.gob.bo/?q=sistema-de-pagos#:~:text=SISTEMA%20DE%20PAGOS%20%C2%B7%20Liquidaci%C3%B3n,recibida%20la%20instrucci%C3%B3n%20de%20pago)
sistemas.detalhes: The RTGS system operated by the Central Bank of Bolivia for large-value payments. It settles interbank transfers in real time and in central bank money (Bolivianos) (https://www.bcb.gob.bo/?q=sistema-de-pagos#:~:text=SISTEMA%20DE%20PAGOS%20%C2%B7%20Liquidaci%C3%B3n,recibida%20la%20instrucci%C3%B3n%20de%20pago). Banks and licensed financial institutions use LBTR to immediately settle urgent or high-value transactions, such as interbank loans, government payments, and securities settlements. Type: RTGS (wholesale payments). Operated by BCB under the Sistema de Pagos Nacional. Ensures final, irrevocable settlement of each transfer.

sistemas.descricao: Automated Clearing House for batched low-value payments and checks (https://www.bcrp.gob.pe/docs/Publicaciones/reporte-de-sistema-de-pagos-de-sudamerica/2024/reporte-sistemas-de-pagos-de-sudamerica-2024.pdf#:~:text=2%2C7%2054%20ACH%2061%20millones,operaci%C3%B3n%20Unilink%201%20902%20operaciones) (https://www.bcrp.gob.pe/docs/Publicaciones/reporte-de-sistema-de-pagos-de-sudamerica/2024/reporte-sistemas-de-pagos-de-sudamerica-2024.pdf#:~:text=61%20millones%20de%20operaciones%20988,ticket%20promedio%20por%20operaci%C3%B3n%20QR)
sistemas.detalhes: A deferred net settlement system handling bulk electronic transfers, such as payroll, ACH credit transfers, and cheque clearing. Operated by the Administradora de Cámaras de Compensación y Liquidación (ACCL) under oversight of BCB (https://www.bcb.gob.bo/webdocs/publicacionesbcb/2024/03/07/SISTEMA%20DE%20PAGOS%202023vf.pdf#:~:text=Las%20CCL%20que%20operan%20en,%28ACCL) (https://www.bcb.gob.bo/webdocs/publicacionesbcb/2024/03/07/SISTEMA%20DE%20PAGOS%202023vf.pdf#:~:text=nacional%20son%20UNILINK%20S,y%20la%20C%C3%A1mara%20de). Transactions are accumulated and cleared in daily cycles, with net positions settled in central bank money via the RTGS. Supports cheques and electronic credit orders under a value threshold. Type: Batched clearing (multilateral net settlement).

sistemas.descricao: Domestic mobile wallets enabling P2P and QR payments, linked to banks (https://www.muralpay.com/blog/how-to-receive-payments-from-overseas-clients-in-bolivia#:~:text=Digital%20wallets%20for%20Bolivian%20companies%E2%80%94VPay%2C,for%20B2B%20and%20B2C%20transactions) (https://www.muralpay.com/blog/how-to-receive-payments-from-overseas-clients-in-bolivia#:~:text=wages%2C%20and%20a%20shortage%20of,Bolivian%20Thoughts%2C%202024)
sistemas.detalhes: A variety of digital wallet apps (such as $imple and Vpayment) that integrate with the national QR system to facilitate instant person-to-person and person-to-merchant payments via smartphones (https://www.muralpay.com/blog/how-to-receive-payments-from-overseas-clients-in-bolivia#:~:text=Digital%20wallets%20for%20Bolivian%20companies%E2%80%94VPay%2C,for%20B2B%20and%20B2C%20transactions). These wallets allow users to link bank accounts or prepaid balances and pay by scanning QR codes or selecting contacts. Many were developed by banks or fintechs and made interoperable through the QR BCB Bolivia standard. Type: Mobile wallet services riding on instant payment infrastructure. Operated by private banks/fintech (e.g. $imple by BCB, Vpayment by bancos) under BCB’s interoperability rules.

sistemas.descricao: Newly-authorized use of cryptocurrency for payments and remittances via exchanges (https://cryptorank.io/news/feed/de9b3-crypto-payments-soar-630-in-bolivia-central-bank-reports-430m-since-lifting-ban#:~:text=Oversight%20strategy) (https://cryptorank.io/news/feed/de9b3-crypto-payments-soar-630-in-bolivia-central-bank-reports-430m-since-lifting-ban#:~:text=The%20Banco%20Central%20de%20Bolivia,31%2C%202025%2C%20approximately%20%2488%20million)
sistemas.detalhes: Following regulatory changes in 2024, Bolivian banks can route customer orders to cryptocurrency exchanges for payments (https://cryptorank.io/news/feed/de9b3-crypto-payments-soar-630-in-bolivia-central-bank-reports-430m-since-lifting-ban#:~:text=Oversight%20strategy). This has enabled the use of stablecoins and other digital assets for cross-border transfers and domestic transactions through supervised channels. While not a formal payment system, the central bank monitors crypto flows and requires daily reporting by banks (https://cryptorank.io/news/feed/de9b3-crypto-payments-soar-630-in-bolivia-central-bank-reports-430m-since-lifting-ban#:~:text=The%20BCB%20stated%20that%20it,added%20tax%20records). The national oil company was even permitted to pay imports with crypto amid dollar shortages (https://cryptorank.io/news/feed/de9b3-crypto-payments-soar-630-in-bolivia-central-bank-reports-430m-since-lifting-ban#:~:text=exchanges). Type: Crypto rails (via exchanges) under central bank oversight.

sistemas.nome: Sistema de Liquidación Integrada de Pagos (LIP)
sistemas.descricao: LIP is Bolivia’s central RTGS system operated by the Banco Central de Bolivia (BCB). It settles large-value interbank transfers in real-time gross or deferred modes, providing an integrated platform for high-value and retail payments [oai_citation:0‡bcb.gob.bo] [oai_citation:1‡bcb.gob.bo]. It replaced the earlier SIPAV RTGS around 2015 and includes a Hybrid Settlement Module (for RTGS) and a Deferred Net Settlement module for low-value transactions [oai_citation:2‡bcb.gob.bo].

Red Enlace is Bolivia’s interbank card network administered by ATC S.A. (Administradora de Tarjetas de Crédito) [oai_citation:24‡bcb.gob.bo]. It connects banks’ ATMs and POS terminals nationwide, enabling debit and credit card transactions across banks. Established in the 1990s, it is the largest electronic payment network in Bolivia, supporting local and international card brands. In 2021, ATC (Red Enlace) obtained ISO 9001 certification for its payment processing services [oai_citation:25‡eldeber.com.bo], reflecting its leading role in electronic payments.

Linkser S.A. operates Red BANCO, another interbank payment switch in Bolivia [oai_citation:28‡bcb.gob.bo]. It provides services for ATM/POS connectivity and payment processing to banks and merchants, competing with Red Enlace. Linkser also offers e-commerce payment gateways and has partnered internationally (for example, enabling acceptance of Brazil’s Pix QR payments on Linkser POS terminals in Bolivia [oai_citation:29‡publiagro.com.bo]). It plays a growing role as a fintech-oriented processor in the Bolivian payments ecosystem.

Operated by the private clearinghouse Administradora de Cámaras de Compensación y Liquidación S.A. (ACCL) – owned by the banks’ association (ASOBAN) – this system processes retail payment orders (electronic fund transfers under a threshold) and checks. It provides multilateral net clearing of low-value credits, direct debits, and cheque images, with final settlement in central bank money via the RTGS [oai_citation:7‡bcb.gob.bo] [oai_citation:8‡bcb.gob.bo].

Billetera Móvil refers to Bolivia’s regulated mobile money services operated by non-banks. The main provider is E-FECTIVO S.A. under the brand Tigo Money [oai_citation:18‡bcb.gob.bo]. Launched in 2013, it allows users (even unbanked) to store funds, send money domestically, receive remittances, pay bills, and cash-out via agents [oai_citation:19‡bcb.gob.bo]. By 2018 it saw explosive growth, reaching ~72 million transactions and 1.257 billion bolivianos in value for the year [oai_citation:20‡bcb.gob.bo], reflecting broad adoption in urban and rural areas for low-value payments.

Central bank’s instant payment system, free and available 24/7, massively adopted (https://www.bis.org/publ/bppdf/bispap152_b_rh.pdf#:~:text=examples%29,M%C3%B3vil%2C%20which%20was%20implemented%20in) (https://www.bis.org/publ/bppdf/bispap152_b_rh.pdf#:~:text=of%20a%20central,M%C3%B3vil%2C%20which%20was%20implemented%20in)
sistemas.detalhes: Launched by Banco Central do Brasil in Nov 2020, Pix enables immediate transfers between individuals, businesses, and government in real time, 24/7 (https://www.bis.org/publ/bppdf/bispap152_b_rh.pdf#:~:text=of%20fast%20payments%20,Costa) (https://www.bis.org/publ/bppdf/bispap152_b_rh.pdf#:~:text=of%20a%20central,M%C3%B3vil%2C%20which%20was%20implemented%20in). Users can send money via mobile app using aliases (phone, email, tax ID) or QR codes (https://www.bis.org/publ/bppdf/bispap153.pdf#:~:text=Lobo%20and%20Brandt%20,on) (https://www.bis.org/publ/bppdf/bispap153.pdf#:~:text=mobile%20devices%20,Pix%20transactions%20made%20by%20individuals). Funds are credited within seconds at any time. Pix is operated by BCB’s Instant Payments System (SPI) and has open participation for banks, fintechs, and e-wallets (https://www.bis.org/publ/bppdf/bispap152_b_rh.pdf#:~:text=examples%29,M%C3%B3vil%2C%20which%20was%20implemented%20in). It has become Brazil’s dominant retail payment method, overtaking cards in transaction count. Type: Instant retail payment (24/7). Owned and operated by BCB.

sistemas.descricao: The Boleto is a unique Brazilian payment instrument: a printed or electronic voucher with a barcode that represents an invoice or bill. It can be paid at any bank or authorized outlet, with funds going to the issuer’s account. The Boleto system is managed by the interbank clearing via CIP. Each boleto carries a numeric line with bank code, amount, due date, and a “Nosso Número” identifier. Banks exchange boleto payment information through the clearing system (formerly a clearinghouse called COMPE) for net settlement. Boletos are widely used for e-commerce, utility bills, and B2B invoices, especially among the unbanked (who can pay in cash at banks).
sistemas.detalhes: The Boleto is a nationwide payment scheme where a payee issues a standardized barcode slip (boleto) that can be paid by the customer at banks, ATMs, lottery agents, or online. Funds are then transferred to the issuer’s bank. It’s often used for e-commerce, utility bills, and B2B invoices – essentially a cash equivalent paper/electronic invoice guaranteed by the banking system. The clearing is handled by CIP (clearinghouse) with net settlement in STR. Type: Deferred payment voucher/collection system. Regulated by BCB; operated collectively by banks via FEBRABAN standards.

sistemas.descricao: Domestic card network
Dominant digital wallet

Brazil’s RTGS system for high-value payments in central bank money (part of SPB) (https://www.bis.org/publ/bppdf/bispap152_b_rh.pdf#:~:text=money%2C%20%E2%80%9CDiMo%E2%80%9D,3) (https://www.bis.org/publ/bppdf/bispap152_b_rh.pdf#:~:text=Brazil%20received%20or%20initiated%20a,M%C3%B3vil%2C%20which%20was%20implemented%20in)
sistemas.detalhes: STR is the Banco Central do Brasil’s real-time gross settlement system, the core of the Brazilian Payment System (SPB) for large-value transactions. It processes interbank transfers (TEDs), bank reserve movements, and other high-value operations in real time during banking hours. All financial institutions hold reserve accounts at BCB and settle obligations via STR. In operation since 2002, STR handles both BRL transactions and provides final settlement for net positions from other clearing systems. Type: RTGS (wholesale). Operated by BCB.

sistemas.descricao: Legacy electronic funds transfer systems (TED immediate, DOC next-day) between bank accounts
sistemas.detalhes: Before Pix, Brazil used TED (Transferência Eletrônica Disponível) and DOC (Documento de Crédito) for interbank account transfers. TED payments settle on the same day (near real-time through the STR RTGS or CIP clearing), while DOC transactions clear overnight or next business day via an ACH process. TED, introduced in early 2000s, has no upper limit and became popular for high-value transfers; DOC is limited to BRL 4,999 and mainly legacy. Type: Electronic credit transfers (TED – quasi-real-time during business hours; DOC – deferred net settlement). Operated by banking network (TED via CIP/SITRAF clearing to STR).

sistemas.descricao: Brazilian domestic card network (Elo) and other card payment systems
sistemas.detalhes: Elo is a local card scheme launched by Brazilian banks (Bradesco, Banco do Brasil, CAIXA) offering credit, debit, and prepaid cards that run on a domestic network. It competes with international brands (Visa, Mastercard) and is widely accepted in Brazil. Additionally, Hipercard (Itaú) is another domestic credit card brand. These schemes are processed through card switches and integrated with the Brazilian card payments infrastructure. Type: Card payment networks. Operated by consortia of banks (Elo) or merchants (Hipercard), with clearing via CIP and settlement at BCB. They support chip-and-PIN, contactless, and online payments.

sistemas.descricao: Central Bank Digital Currency prototype for Brazil (tokenized digital real platform)
sistemas.detalhes: Drex is the codename for Brazil’s CBDC project, launched in pilot in 2023. It envisions a permissioned blockchain platform where tokenized Brazilian Real (issued by BCB) can be used for wholesale interbank settlements and eventually retail use cases. Pilot tests involve digital ledgers for government bonds and retail tokenized deposits among invited banks. It is not yet in public circulation. Type: CBDC (pilot stage, wholesale focus initially). Operated by BCB with selected financial institutions testing integration.

sistemas.descricao: Pix is Brazil’s instant payment ecosystem launched in Nov 2020 by Banco Central do Brasil [oai_citation:56‡iupana.com]. It enables real-time transfers between any bank or fintech, 24/7, typically via mobile app using simple aliases (phone, email, etc.). Pix reached massive adoption – by Jan 2023 over 135 million Brazilians (over 90% of adults) had used it [oai_citation:57‡iupana.com] [oai_citation:58‡iupana.com]. It is used for P2P, merchant payments (including Pix QR codes), bill payments, and even government disbursements. Pix transactions settle in seconds through the central bank’s SPI (Instant Payments System) using ISO 20022 messages.

STR is the central bank’s RTGS system, live since 2002 [oai_citation:63‡fastpayments.worldbank.org]. It processes large-value interbank transfers and critical payments (e.g., money market, FX settlements) in real time. All banks hold reserve accounts at Banco Central do Brasil and use STR for final settlement in Brazilian Real. STR operates on the national financial network (RSFN) and has extended hours (was 06:30–18:30, now longer) to support financial markets. It uses SWIFT and local messages. Many high-value customer transfers (TEDs) also clear through STR, especially outside SITRAF hours or above certain thresholds [oai_citation:64‡imf.org].

SITRAF is a hybrid low-value payment system operated by CIP (Interbank Payments Clearinghouse). It processes electronic credit transfers (TED – Transferências Eletrônicas Disponíveis) in near-real-time via continuous batch clearing every few minutes [oai_citation:65‡rba.gov.au]. Introduced in 2002, SITRAF allows faster retail payments during business hours, with final net settlement in central bank money multiple times a day. It handles most interbank customer transfers below certain values, complementing the RTGS. Funds are typically credited to recipients within minutes of initiation.
Issued by CBOB nation-wide since Oct-2020; wallets provided by licensed PSPs and commercial banks; supports offline P2P, merchant QR, and government disbursements.
Dominant payment method
RTGS for large-value bank transfers
sistemas.detalhes: BISS is the Bahamas’ real-time gross settlement system for interbank payments (https://www.centralbankbahamas.com/viewPDF/documents/2019-12-25-02-18-11-Project-Sanddollar.pdf#:~:text=payments%20settlements%20process%20among%20the,value%20retail%20payments.8). Implemented in 2004, it settles high-value and time-critical transactions in Bahamian dollars instantly between clearing banks (https://www.centralbankbahamas.com/viewPDF/documents/2019-12-25-02-18-11-Project-Sanddollar.pdf#:~:text=payments%20settlements%20process%20among%20the,value%20retail%20payments.8). BISS is operated by the Central Bank and handles final settlement for other payment systems as well. Transactions above a threshold (e.g. B$150,000) are typically processed via BISS (https://www.centralbankbahamas.com/viewPDF/documents/2019-12-25-02-18-11-Project-Sanddollar.pdf#:~:text=Once%20the). It provides irrevocable, real-time settlement in central bank money, enhancing payment finality and reducing systemic risk. All commercial banks maintain accounts at the Central Bank for BISS settlements. BISS has become the backbone for large-value transfers and supports the efficiency of Bahamas’ financial market infrastructure (https://www.centralbankbahamas.com/viewPDF/documents/2019-12-25-02-18-11-Project-Sanddollar.pdf#:~:text=Once%20the).

sistemas.descricao: Electronic clearing for low-value payments
sistemas.detalhes: BACH is the national ACH for batched low-value transactions. Launched in 2010, it clears cheques and electronic fund transfers (direct credits, etc.) among banks on a deferred net settlement basis (https://www.centralbankbahamas.com/viewPDF/documents/2019-12-25-02-18-11-Project-Sanddollar.pdf#:~:text=settlement%20,value%20retail%20payments.8) (https://www.centralbankbahamas.com/viewPDF/documents/2019-12-25-02-18-11-Project-Sanddollar.pdf#:~:text=Once%20the). BACH processes retail payments (salaries, bill payments, checks) with multilateral netting and next-day settlement in BISS (https://www.centralbankbahamas.com/viewPDF/documents/2019-12-25-02-18-11-Project-Sanddollar.pdf#:~:text=match%20at%20L413%20All%20lower,Settlements%20clear%20though) (https://www.centralbankbahamas.com/viewPDF/documents/2019-12-25-02-18-11-Project-Sanddollar.pdf#:~:text=Once%20the). It has significantly sped up and modernized payments – reducing cheque clearing from multiple days to 1–2 days (https://www.tribune242.com/news/2013/apr/24/clearing-house-targets-2m-transactions-in-2013/#:~:text=Electronic%20transactions%20facilitated%20by%20the,companies%20using%20this%20for%20payroll) (https://www.tribune242.com/news/2013/apr/24/clearing-house-targets-2m-transactions-in-2013/#:~:text=Mr%20Smith%20said%20the%20BACH,two%20million%20mark%20for%202013). By 2013, BACH handled close to 2 million transactions annually (around B$8 billion per year) as electronic payrolls and transfers grew rapidly (https://www.tribune242.com/news/2013/apr/24/clearing-house-targets-2m-transactions-in-2013/#:~:text=Electronic%20transactions%20facilitated%20by%20the,companies%20using%20this%20for%20payroll) (https://www.tribune242.com/news/2013/apr/24/clearing-house-targets-2m-transactions-in-2013/#:~:text=transactions%20coming%20on%20later%20this,%E2%80%9D). BACH has paved the way for the decline of paper cheques and the rise of electronic payments in the Bahamas.

sistemas.descricao: Digital version of the Bahamian Dollar for retail use
sistemas.detalhes: The Sand Dollar is the Bahamas’ central bank digital currency (CBDC), launched nationwide in October 2020 as the world’s first retail CBDC (https://cointelegraph.com/learn/articles/sand-dollar-bahamas-digital-currency-a-beginners-guide#:~:text=digital%20form%2C%20is%20an%20effort,payment%20in%20the%20digital%20economy) (https://cointelegraph.com/learn/articles/sand-dollar-bahamas-digital-currency-a-beginners-guide#:~:text=digital%20payment%20systems,was%20introduced%20in%20October%202020). It is a digital Bahamian dollar (par 1:1 to the BSD) issued and backed by the Central Bank (https://cointelegraph.com/learn/articles/sand-dollar-bahamas-digital-currency-a-beginners-guide#:~:text=The%20Bahamian%20dollar%2C%20the%20national,a%20wholesale%20and%20retail%20CBDC). Citizens access Sand Dollars through digital wallets provided by authorized financial institutions (AFIs) – including mobile apps like Kanoo, SunCash, MobileAssist – or the bank’s own wallet interface (https://www.centralbankbahamas.com/news/press-releases/press-release-public-update-on-the-bahamas-digital-currency-sanddollar-1#:~:text=Public%20Update%20on%20The%20Bahamas,The%20exercise%20resulted) (https://cointelegraph.com/learn/articles/sand-dollar-bahamas-digital-currency-a-beginners-guide#:~:text=guide%20cointelegraph,enabled). The Sand Dollar enables instant, 24/7 P2P transfers, merchant payments via QR code or cards linked to wallets, and government disbursements, even offline during connectivity outages (https://cointelegraph.com/learn/articles/sand-dollar-bahamas-digital-currency-a-beginners-guide#:~:text=Bahamian%20consumers%20require%20a%20prepaid,payment%20card%20or%20mobile%20application) (https://cointelegraph.com/learn/articles/sand-dollar-bahamas-digital-currency-a-beginners-guide#:~:text=customer,transaction%20limits%20are%20also%20available). Tiered wallets impose transaction and balance limits (e.g. $500/day for basic, higher for KYC’d tiers) (https://cointelegraph.com/learn/articles/sand-dollar-bahamas-digital-currency-a-beginners-guide#:~:text=Bahamian%20consumers%20require%20a%20prepaid,payment%20card%20or%20mobile%20application). The Sand Dollar aims to improve financial inclusion across the islands and provide a resilient digital cash alternative (https://cointelegraph.com/learn/articles/sand-dollar-bahamas-digital-currency-a-beginners-guide#:~:text=digital%20payment%20systems,was%20introduced%20in%20October%202020). Adoption has grown gradually – by end of 2022, Sand Dollar usage averaged ~85,000 B$ in transactions per month (still <1% of cash in circulation) (https://www.intereconomics.eu/contents/year/2023/number/4/article/the-evolution-of-sanddollar.html#:~:text=match%20at%20L272%20increasing%20by,over%20the%20previous%20year) (https://www.intereconomics.eu/contents/year/2023/number/4/article/the-evolution-of-sanddollar.html#:~:text=match%20at%20L278%20circulation,see%20Figure%203) – and the central bank continues to promote it via wallet upgrades and incentives.

sistemas.descricao: National network for ATM and card payments (Benefit)
sistemas.detalhes: Benefit is the interbank switch that connects all ATMs and point-of-sale terminals across Bahrain (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Benefit_Company#:~:text=Websitewww) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Benefit_Company#:~:text=The%20Benefit%20Company%20,its%20kind%20in%20the%20country). Established in 1997, it links local banks’ networks, enabling any debit/credit card issued in Bahrain to be used at any ATM or merchant in the country (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Benefit_Company#:~:text=Websitewww) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Benefit_Company#:~:text=Benefit%27s%20initial%20services%20included%20connecting,local%20issuers%20in%20the%20Kingdom). Benefit provides 24/7 real-time routing of ATM withdrawals, balance inquiries, fund transfers, and POS payments between issuing and acquiring banks (https://www.cbb.gov.bh/payment-settlement/#:~:text=Payment%20%26%20Settlement%20,processes%20all%20the%20ATM) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Benefit_Company#:~:text=The%20Benefit%20Company%20,POS%20transactions%20among%20other%20services). It also connects to the regional GCCNET, allowing cross-GCC ATM/POS access (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Benefit_Company#:~:text=GCCNET). Benefit operates the national cheque image clearing system as well (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Benefit_Company#:~:text=Electronic%20check%20clearing). By integrating all banks and payment cards, the Benefit switch has been instrumental in Bahrain’s cashless infrastructure – in 2018 it handled millions of ATM and POS transactions, with debit card payments via POS reaching BHD 1.2 billion (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=Debit%20and%20Credit%20Card%20Transactions). All interbank ATM/POS transactions settled through Benefit ultimately clear in the RTGS (https://www.centralbank.org.bb/news/general-press-release/overview-of-payment-systems-in-barbados#:~:text=system%2C%20directly%20facilitated%2055%20percent,system%20and%20the%20Central%20Bank).

sistemas.nome: Electronic Funds Transfer System (EFTS: Fawri, Fawri+, Fawateer)
sistemas.descricao: Nationwide retail payment platform (ACH and instant payments)
sistemas.detalhes: Bahrain’s EFTS (launched ~2015) is a unified national retail payment scheme offering three services (https://www.transfi.com/blog/popular-local-payment-methods-and-solutions-in-bahrain#:~:text=Fawri%2B%3A%20Instant%20payment%20up%20to,of%20EFTS%20transactions): **Fawri**, the deferred ACH service for batch electronic credits (e.g. next-day transfers for salaries, bulk payments) (https://www.transfi.com/blog/popular-local-payment-methods-and-solutions-in-bahrain#:~:text=Fawri%3A%20Payment%20is%20credited%20to,within%20Bahrain%2C%20during%20business%20hours); **Fawri+**, the instant payment service up to BHD 1,000 that executes transfers within seconds, 24/7 (https://www.transfi.com/blog/popular-local-payment-methods-and-solutions-in-bahrain#:~:text=Fawri%2B%3A%20Instant%20payment%20up%20to,of%20EFTS%20transactions); and **Fawateer**, an electronic bill presentment and payment service allowing instant bill payments via banks or the BenefitPay app (https://www.transfi.com/blog/popular-local-payment-methods-and-solutions-in-bahrain#:~:text=during%20business%20hours). These services connect all retail banks in Bahrain and have greatly improved convenience and speed of fund transfers (https://www.cbb.gov.bh/payment-settlement/#:~:text=The%20CBB%20operates%20a%20Real,line%20mode) (https://www.transfi.com/blog/popular-local-payment-methods-and-solutions-in-bahrain#:~:text=These%20have%20played%20a%20huge,less%20dependent%20on%20physical%20banks). Fawri+ in particular has seen massive uptake, powering real-time P2P and small business payments (it now accounts for ~85% of all EFTS transactions by volume) (https://www.transfi.com/blog/popular-local-payment-methods-and-solutions-in-bahrain#:~:text=match%20at%20L345%20BenefitPay%20backend,of%20EFTS%20transactions). EFTS transactions settle either immediately (Fawri+) or via same-day net settlement through the RTGS. The introduction of EFTS has significantly increased digital payment usage and financial inclusion in Bahrain.

sistemas.descricao: Dominant mobile payments app linked to bank accounts
sistemas.detalhes: BenefitPay is Bahrain’s most popular digital wallet and mobile payment application (https://www.transfi.com/blog/popular-local-payment-methods-and-solutions-in-bahrain#:~:text=follows%3A). Launched in 2017 by The BENEFIT Company, it links users’ bank accounts and debit cards to enable a range of cashless payments: instant P2P transfers by mobile number, QR code payments at merchants, bill payments, and e-commerce checkout (https://www.transfi.com/blog/popular-local-payment-methods-and-solutions-in-bahrain#:~:text=BenefitPay%3A%20The%20most%20used%20wallet,peer%29%20transfers%20and%20online%20shopping). BenefitPay leverages the Fawri+ instant payment rails on the backend, and as of 2023 it handles roughly 85% of all Electronic Funds Transfer System (EFTS) transactions in Bahrain (https://www.transfi.com/blog/popular-local-payment-methods-and-solutions-in-bahrain#:~:text=match%20at%20L345%20BenefitPay%20backend,of%20EFTS%20transactions). The app has seen rapid adoption – in 2023, mobile payments via BenefitPay (and Bancontact Payconiq) reached 368 million transactions, 34% higher than the previous year (https://www.bancontact.com/en/news/mobile-payments-with-bancontact-and-payconiq-increase-tenfold-in-five-years#:~:text=The%20number%20of%20mobile%20payments,mobile%20payments%20continue%20to%20boom) (https://assets-eu-01.kc-usercontent.com/331a0185-e26c-01d0-41e9-c42bc79a1d2c/6bf42db6-6363-4041-b9d3-54c6548f8e14/Press%20Release-22Feb2024.pdf#:~:text=,to%20be). BenefitPay’s ubiquity (accepted by all local banks and many merchants) and ease of use have made it a cornerstone of Bahrain’s move toward a cashless society.

sistemas.descricao: Telecom-based digital wallet and remittance app
sistemas.detalhes: stcPay is a mobile wallet launched by telecom operator STC in Bahrain as an extension of its fintech services (following success in Saudi Arabia) (https://www.transfi.com/blog/popular-local-payment-methods-and-solutions-in-bahrain#:~:text=stcPay%3A%20The%20product%20of%20the,integrations%20such%20as%20Samsung%20Wallet). The stcPay app allows users (including non-STC subscribers) to store money, pay bills, transfer funds domestically, and perform international remittances easily from their smartphones (https://www.transfi.com/blog/popular-local-payment-methods-and-solutions-in-bahrain#:~:text=stcPay%3A%20The%20product%20of%20the,integrations%20such%20as%20Samsung%20Wallet). It integrates features like Samsung Wallet for contactless payments and supports secure transfers, catering especially to expatriates for sending money abroad (https://www.transfi.com/blog/popular-local-payment-methods-and-solutions-in-bahrain#:~:text=stcPay%3A%20The%20product%20of%20the,integrations%20such%20as%20Samsung%20Wallet). stcPay’s entry has provided competition in the digital wallet space, and while its user base is smaller than BenefitPay’s, it appeals with telecom convenience and has been growing among STC customers. It operates under Central Bank regulations for Payment Service Providers. stcPay represents the diversification of mobile financial services in Bahrain beyond bank-centric solutions.

sistemas.descricao: Jointly owned by retail banks; three daily clearing windows; higher fees for cheques to encourage electronic alternatives.
Owned and operated by the Central Bank of The Bahamas (CBOB); settles interbank, treasury and ACH net positions in BSD and USD.
Mobile banking
National standard
Bank-agnostic wallet launched 2018 by Bank of Bhutan; linked to BIPS alias scheme; tourists can pay via cards.

sistemas.nome: GIFT RTGS (Global Interchange for Financial Transactions)
sistemas.descricao: Operated by Royal Monetary Authority (RMA); offers RTGS for ≥ Nu 1 m, BITS half-hour batch ≤ Nu 1 m and BULK for payroll; interfaces with e-PEMS treasury system.
Digitalises all treasury disbursements; agencies initiate payment batches that settle same day in GIFT.
National payment switch
Mobile payment platform

Botswana’s RTGS for high-value interbank fund transfers (https://www.bankofbotswana.bw/content/botswana-interbank-settlement-system#:~:text=The%20Botswana%20Interbank%20Settlement%20System,at%20the%20Bank%20of%20Botswana) (https://www.bankofbotswana.bw/content/botswana-interbank-settlement-system#:~:text=BISS%20is%20managed%20and%20operated,as%20the%20Bank%20of%20Botswana)
sistemas.detalhes: Electronic Real-Time Gross Settlement system operated by the Bank of Botswana for instant settlement of interbank payments in pula. BISS settles payment instructions individually and irrevocably in real time, provided sending banks have sufficient balance at the central bank (https://www.bankofbotswana.bw/content/botswana-interbank-settlement-system#:~:text=The%20Botswana%20Interbank%20Settlement%20System,at%20the%20Bank%20of%20Botswana) (https://www.bankofbotswana.bw/content/botswana-interbank-settlement-system#:~:text=institutions%20on%20an%20irrevocable%20and,at%20the%20Bank%20of%20Botswana). All clearing banks hold settlement accounts at BoB and use BISS for large-value and urgent transfers (e.g. securities, corporate payments). Launched in 2006, upgraded in 2016 (https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/ng/pdf/advisory/payment-system-africa.pdf#:~:text=2006%3A%20Introduction%20of%20the%20Botswana,2008%3A%20Introduction%20of%20the%20Central) (https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/ng/pdf/advisory/payment-system-africa.pdf#:~:text=Operators%202011%3A%20Introduction%20of%20Mobile,BACH). Type: RTGS (wholesale). Operated by BoB under NCSS Act.

sistemas.descricao: Electronic clearing house for low-value payments (EFT, bulk transfers, cheques) (https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/ng/pdf/advisory/payment-system-africa.pdf#:~:text=A%20closer%20look%3A%20Botswana%E2%80%99s%20payments,which%20essentially%20relieves%20the%20Central) (https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/ng/pdf/advisory/payment-system-africa.pdf#:~:text=Electronic%20Clearing%20House%20Botswana%20,for%20the%20Central%20Bank%2C%20it)
sistemas.detalhes: Botswana’s national retail payments clearing infrastructure. The Electronic Clearing House Botswana (ECHB), operated by a private-sector entity, processes batched interbank transactions such as EFT credits, direct debits, and cheque truncation in near-real-time cycles (https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/ng/pdf/advisory/payment-system-africa.pdf#:~:text=A%20closer%20look%3A%20Botswana%E2%80%99s%20payments,which%20essentially%20relieves%20the%20Central) (https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/ng/pdf/advisory/payment-system-africa.pdf#:~:text=transfers%20and%20other%20payment%20orders,the%20implementation%20of%20corrective%20measures). It was modernized in 2015 as BACH for greater efficiency. Banks submit bulk files (salaries, bill payments) to BACH, which nets obligations and forwards the net positions to BISS for settlement. Type: ACH (multilateral net clearing). Overseen by BoB, operated jointly with banks.

sistemas.descricao: Telecom-led mobile wallet services for instant P2P transfers, bill pay, airtime (https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/ng/pdf/advisory/payment-system-africa.pdf#:~:text=of%20Mobile%20Money%20services%20%E2%80%93,live%20on%20the%20SADC%20Integrated) (https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099113023113526062/pdf/P1790340f765cc07c0b967022a091caa813.pdf#:~:text=retail%20payments%20infrastructure%20that%20supports,while%20maintaining%20competition%20amongst%20all)
sistemas.detalhes: Non-bank e-money platforms offered by mobile operators enabling users to send and receive money via phone. Launched since 2011 (Orange Money) (https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/ng/pdf/advisory/payment-system-africa.pdf#:~:text=Operators%202011%3A%20Introduction%20of%20Mobile,BACH), mobile money wallets allow instant domestic remittances, merchant payments, and cash-in/cash-out at agent kiosks. They operate outside the traditional banking rails, but are interoperable to some extent (though full inter-platform instant interoperability is still lacking in Botswana (https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099113023113526062/pdf/P1790340f765cc07c0b967022a091caa813.pdf#:~:text=%5BPDF%5D%20republic%20of%20botswana%20,realization%20is%20critical%20for)). Popular services include Orange Money and Mascom’s MyZaka, each tied to a mobile network. Type: Mobile money (stored-value wallets). Regulated by BoB via EMI licenses.

sistemas.descricao: Regional cross-border RTGS for Southern African Development Community payments (https://www.resbank.co.za/content/dam/sarb/what-we-do/payments-and-settlements/sadc-rtgs-/SADC-RTGS%20PFMIs%20Disclosure%20Framework%202024%20Final%2031Mar2025.pdf#:~:text=%5BPDF%5D%20SADC,the%20purposes%20of%20this%20publication) (https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/ng/pdf/advisory/payment-system-africa.pdf#:~:text=enhanced%20Botswana%20Automated%20Clearing%20House,SIRESS)
sistemas.detalhes: An international payment system allowing banks in Botswana to settle cross-border payments within SADC in near-real time. SIRESS (now operating through the SARB’s TIPS) settles transactions in multiple currencies (primarily ZAR) among member central banks and commercial banks (https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/ng/pdf/advisory/payment-system-africa.pdf#:~:text=enhanced%20Botswana%20Automated%20Clearing%20House,SIRESS). Botswana joined SADC-RTGS in 2016, enabling efficient regional transfers (e.g. between Botswana, South Africa, Namibia, etc.) in central bank money. Type: Regional RTGS (cross-border large-value). Operated by SADC Banking Association via South African Reserve Bank platform.

sistemas.descricao: Private electronic payment network for unbanked, using smart cards and agents (https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/ng/pdf/advisory/payment-system-africa.pdf#:~:text=Botswana%20Interbank%20Settlement%20System%20,Central%20Securities%20Depository%20Company%20of) (https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/ng/pdf/advisory/payment-system-africa.pdf#:~:text=2006%3A%20Introduction%20of%20SmartSwitch%2C%20a,money)
sistemas.detalhes: A universal electronic payment system (UEPS) introduced in 2006 by SmartSwitch Botswana (joint venture with Net1) to reach unbanked communities (https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/ng/pdf/advisory/payment-system-africa.pdf#:~:text=2006%3A%20Introduction%20of%20the%20Botswana,2008%3A%20Introduction%20of%20the%20Central). It provides biometric smart cards and a merchant/agent network for cash withdrawals, money transfers, and government grant disbursements in remote areas. Transactions can be done offline and later synchronized, suitable for villages with intermittent connectivity. SmartSwitch allows users to receive salaries or benefits on a card and spend or cash out at local stores equipped with point-of-sale devices. Type: Proprietary card-based network for financial inclusion. Operated by SmartSwitch (private).

sistemas.descricao: BISS is Botswana’s RTGS, launched in 2006 to settle large-value and time-critical payments in real time [oai_citation:45‡bankofbotswana.bw]. Operated by the Bank of Botswana, it provides irrevocable settlement between banks via their accounts at the central bank. BISS operates during business hours and is credited with reducing systemic risk and modernizing Botswana’s financial infrastructure [oai_citation:46‡bankofbotswana.bw] [oai_citation:47‡bankofbotswana.bw]. Only licensed banks (and the central bank) participate. Transactions are processed individually, and high-value customer transfers also flow through BISS for same-day clearing.

SmartSwitch Botswana is a fintech platform (subsidiary of Lesaka) that implements the Universal Electronic Payment System (UEPS) to distribute government food aid via biometric smart cards [oai_citation:51‡fintechnews.africa] [oai_citation:52‡fintechnews.africa]. Launched in 2006, it provides unbanked beneficiaries with chip cards secured by fingerprint verification, allowing them to receive monthly allowances and spend at authorized local merchants. Transactions can even be done offline and are later synchronized, with settlement to merchants within 48 hours [oai_citation:53‡fintechnews.africa]. The system serves over 75,000 recipients, improving efficiency and transparency in social payments.

Mobile money in Botswana is offered by mobile operators, notably Orange Money and Mascom’s MyZaka. These services allow users to store value in e-wallets linked to phone numbers and to transfer funds, pay bills, and make purchases via USSD or mobile apps. Orange Money, launched in 2011, has seen growing adoption especially among the unbanked. While not a formal national clearing system, the central bank oversees these services under e-money regulations, and is working toward interoperability. As of 2020, mobile money usage was rising with tens of thousands of active users, partly accelerated by COVID-19 shifts.

BACH (formerly ECH Botswana) is the national retail payments clearing system. It processes bulk low-value transactions (ACH credit transfers like salaries, debit orders, and also truncated cheque images) in batch cycles [oai_citation:49‡bankofbotswana.bw] [oai_citation:50‡bankofbotswana.bw]. Established mid-2000s alongside BISS, BACH is operated under the Botswana Payments and Settlement Association. It uses a Cheque Image Truncation System (CITS) so that physical cheques are imaged and cleared electronically. Net positions from BACH are settled in BISS at end-of-day, ensuring finality in central bank money.
National payment system
Domestic card scheme
RTGS core of national payment infrastructure
sistemas.detalhes: BISS is the RTGS in Belarus, launched in 1995 and upgraded over time, serving as the central platform for large-value interbank settlements (https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2006/177/article-A001-en.xml#:~:text=,transactions%20in%20Belarusian%20rubel) (https://www.bis.org/cpmi/publ/d45.pdf#:~:text=,The). It processes high-value payments and urgent credit transfers in Belarusian rubles in real time, providing immediate finality. BISS is operated by the National Bank (NBRB) and is the backbone of the Automated System of Interbank Settlements (ASIS) (https://www.bis.org/cpmi/publ/d45.pdf#:~:text=D,and%20domestic%20financial%20transactions). It settles not only interbank transfers but also the net positions from retail clearing systems. By design, about 90% of total payment value flows through BISS (with only non-urgent small payments going via clearing) (https://www.bis.org/cpmi/publ/d45.pdf#:~:text=Glossary%20) (https://www.bis.org/cpmi/publ/d45.pdf#:~:text=D,and%20domestic%20financial%20transactions). Participants maintain accounts at NBRB; liquidity and queue management tools are in place. BISS drastically reduced settlement times, moving Belarus from previously using correspondent accounts to a modern RTGS. It remains mission-critical for monetary operations and large corporate payments in Belarus.

sistemas.descricao: Nationwide bill payment and retail payment system
sistemas.detalhes: ERIP (also called the "Raschet" system) is Belarus’s largest payment system, launched in 2008 by the NBRB (https://dab.by/en/works/erip-logo-identity/#:~:text=Image%3A%20img). It is an interoperable platform that consolidates virtually all bill payments and many retail payments under one network. Through ERIP, individuals can pay for a very wide range of services – utilities, taxes, fines, telecom, insurance, e-commerce, etc. – using any participating bank or payment channel (https://dab.by/en/works/erip-logo-identity/#:~:text=The%20system%20was%20launched%20in,%D0%9A%D0%B0%D1%81%D1%81%D0%B0%29%20joined%20ERIP). It connects 23 banks and Belarus’ postal network (Belpochta) so that payments can be made at over 13,000 service points in cash or via electronic means (https://docs.bepaid.by/en/payment_methods/apms/erip/#:~:text=Accepting%20payments%20via%20ERIP%20,via%20the%20Internet%20and) (https://dab.by/en/works/erip-logo-identity/#:~:text=The%20system%20was%20launched%20in,%D0%9A%D0%B0%D1%81%D1%81%D0%B0%29%20joined%20ERIP), as well as through internet banking and mobile apps. ERIP also supports person-to-person transfers and QR code payments in stores via its "Address Book" and QR infrastructure (https://myuniver.org/en/articles/kak-rasplachivatsya-v-belarusi#:~:text=How%20to%20pay%20in%20Belarus%3F,as%20well%20as%20instantly) (https://eor.by/payment-systems-vs-eor-in-belarus/#:~:text=The%20Belarusian%20national%20electronic%20payment,pay%20for%20goods%20and). All transactions are routed through ERIP for instant or same-day posting to billers. It operates as a hub, greatly simplifying the billing and payment process: payers can use one interface to pay any biller listed in the system. ERIP has been enormously successful in digitizing payments – for example, in 2020 the system was rebranded and unified services under one brand, and it continues to add new service providers constantly (https://dab.by/en/works/erip-logo-identity/#:~:text=Image%3A%20img). It has become the default way Belarusians pay routine obligations.

sistemas.descricao: National payment card network and e-wallet
sistemas.detalhes: Belkart is Belarus’s domestic payment card scheme, introduced in 1994 to provide a local alternative to Visa/Mastercard. Belkart debit cards are issued by all major Belarusian banks and can be used at ATMs and POS terminals nationwide. The scheme is now managed by the national processing center ("Belkart" company) and has been made interoperable – many Belkart cards are co-badged with MIR (Russia) for international acceptance (https://spex.by/eng/news/how-to-work-with-mir-cards#:~:text=How%20to%20work%20with%20MIR,Making%20a%20card). Belkart transactions are switched and settled locally (often via the Belarusian Card Switch system). In recent years, Belkart also launched a digital wallet app (Belkart Pay) for contactless mobile payments, and supports linking cards to smartphone NFC wallets. As of 2025, electronic money solutions popular in Belarus include "Belkart wallets" among others (https://spex.by/eng/news/electronic-money-in-belarus#:~:text=Only%20banks%20that%20are%20residents,and%20mobile%20applications%20from%20banks). Belkart has significant market share in debit cards; when international card networks withdrew due to sanctions, Belkart/MIR became even more vital for card payments. The scheme ensures Belarusian consumers can perform cashless payments inside the country reliably, and it underpins many e-commerce payments via local gateways like WebPay (https://akurateco.com/payment-methods/webpay#:~:text=WebPay%20,as%20well%20as%20installment). Its acceptance network covers practically all merchants that take cards in Belarus.

sistemas.descricao: Private e-wallets and online payment gateways
sistemas.detalhes: Belarus has a number of electronic money platforms licensed as Payment Service Providers by NBRB. These include **WebPay** (an online payment gateway enabling merchants to accept cards including Belkart, Visa, etc.), **iPay**, **EasyPay**, and others (https://spex.by/eng/news/electronic-money-in-belarus#:~:text=Only%20banks%20that%20are%20residents,and%20mobile%20applications%20from%20banks). These systems allow individuals to open e-wallets (prepaid accounts) and pay for goods and services online, transfer funds among users, and top-up via banks or ERIP (https://spex.by/eng/news/electronic-money-in-belarus#:~:text=Forms%20of%20presentation) (https://spex.by/eng/news/electronic-money-in-belarus#:~:text=Only%20banks%20that%20are%20residents,and%20mobile%20applications%20from%20banks). The e-money is issued by banks or authorized operators and is fully backed by fiat deposits. For example, users can load an EasyPay wallet via internet banking or cash, then use it for e-commerce or P2P without needing a bank account (https://spex.by/eng/news/electronic-money-in-belarus#:~:text=Forms%20of%20presentation). WebPay in particular serves as a common gateway for online stores in Belarus to process card payments securely (https://akurateco.com/payment-methods/webpay#:~:text=WebPay%20,as%20well%20as%20installment). Mobile apps from banks (like Belarusbank’s M-Belarusbank or Priorbank’s app) also integrate e-money features such as QR code payments using the ERIP system (https://spex.by/eng/news/electronic-money-in-belarus#:~:text=%2A%20E,codes%20or%20using%20NFC%20technology). Adoption of e-wallets is moderate – popular mainly for certain online transactions and among tech-savvy users – but growing as digital commerce expands. They complement the broader payment ecosystem by providing additional cashless options outside traditional cards.

sistemas.descricao: Rules approved Sept-2022; banks began joining 2023-24; mobile alias and QR features.
Connects 24 banks; net positions settle in BISS.
Net positions settle in BISS; supports cheques, direct debits, credit transfers.
Operated by National Bank of the Republic of Belarus (NBRB); supports collateralised intraday credit and settles clearing balances from the national clearing system and Belcard.
