sistemas.nome: Automated Payment and Securities Settlement System (APSSS – RTGS module)
sistemas.descricao: Modern real-time gross settlement for interbank payments
sistemas.detalhes: Belize’s APSSS, implemented in 2017, includes an RTGS component that allows banks to settle large-value and urgent interbank transfers in real time through the Central Bank. This RTGS replaced manual settlement processes and greatly increased efficiency and safety for big transactions. It is used for high-value customer payments, interbank money market transactions, and for settling net obligations from the retail systems. The central bank and five commercial banks participate. Before APSSS, large transfers were slower and relied on correspondent accounts – now they are immediate. For example, government payments and treasury settlements now use RTGS. The RTGS operating hours align with local business hours. While cash is still heavily used in Belize, the RTGS has become key for wholesale payments and underpins the other payment subsystems. It also allowed Belize to connect more easily with regional payment initiatives. With APSSS’s launch, Belize signaled commitment to a robust, electronic payment infrastructure (https://iconsolutions.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Belize-White-Paper-LJ.pdf#:~:text=Belize%E2%80%99s%20payment%20system%20is%20largely,Whilst%20Belize) (https://iconsolutions.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Belize-White-Paper-LJ.pdf#:~:text=Significant%20challenges%20with%20AML%20and,well%20as%208%20special%20recommendations).

sistemas.nome: Automated Clearing House (ACH – Belize Bankers Association)
sistemas.descricao: Electronic clearing for retail payments and cheques
sistemas.detalhes: Belize’s ACH (launched as part of APSSS around 2016) processes low-value payments in batch, replacing the old manual clearing house. It clears cheques (via truncation) and electronic fund transfers like payroll credits and automatic debits. Prior to automation, cheque clearing took 3 days within city (and 7 days across districts) (https://iconsolutions.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Belize-White-Paper-LJ.pdf#:~:text=electronic%20payment%20mechanisms%20are%3A%20POS%2FATM,no%20interbank%20system%20for%20Direct). Now, with electronic clearing, most cheques and ACH credits settle by next business day (https://iconsolutions.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Belize-White-Paper-LJ.pdf#:~:text=cheques%20are%20the%20primary%20non,and%20beneficiary%20have%20accounts%20at). The Belize Bankers’ Clearing House (run by the Bankers Association in coordination with Central Bank) manages this system. Cheques remain a very common payment form by volume, even post-APSSS, though declining gradually as electronic transfers grow (https://iconsolutions.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Belize-White-Paper-LJ.pdf#:~:text=electronic%20payment%20mechanisms%20are%3A%20POS%2FATM,and%20Direct%20Debits%20for%20recurring) (https://iconsolutions.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Belize-White-Paper-LJ.pdf#:~:text=Belize%E2%80%99s%20payment%20system%20is%20largely,Whilst%20Belize). The ACH also allows direct credit transfers between banks (e.g. salary payments and supplier payments) with next-day settlement. However, one limitation historically was lack of an interbank direct debit system – recurring debits could only occur within the same bank (https://iconsolutions.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Belize-White-Paper-LJ.pdf#:~:text=can%20be%20reduced%20to%20the,its%20own%20clearing%20and%20settlement), something the new ACH may address. The ACH’s introduction has reduced float times and improved confidence in non-cash payments. It’s now the backbone for retail transactions, working alongside the RTGS for final settlement.

sistemas.descricao: Mobile wallet for consumers and merchants (Belize’s first)
sistemas.detalhes: e-kyash is a digital wallet launched in 2021 by Belize Bank (in partnership with Wallet Factory) as the country’s first mobile payment wallet (https://www.e-kyash.com/#:~:text=E,a%20registered%20Belize%20Phone%20number). It aims to advance financial inclusion by enabling easy, instant payments via mobile phone. Users download the E-kyash app, register with a Belize phone number and ID, and can then load funds from bank accounts or agents. The wallet allows person-to-person transfers by phone number, merchant payments via QR code, bill payments, mobile recharges, and even international remittances. It’s accepted at many stores and online sites across Belize (wherever the “E-kyash accepted” sign is displayed) (https://www.e-kyash.com/#:~:text=E,a%20registered%20Belize%20Phone%20number). For merchants, E-kyash offers a lower-cost alternative to card POS, and for consumers it provides 24/7 cashless convenience without needing a bank account. The Central Bank granted Belize Bank a PSP license for E-kyash, ensuring regulatory oversight. Adoption is growing, especially among young and unbanked users. The wallet had tens of thousands of sign-ups within its first year. As of 2024, E-kyash remains a leading mobile money solution in Belize, with other institutions considering joining the digital wallet space. It represents a shift towards smartphone-based payments in an economy historically reliant on cash and cheques.

sistemas.descricao: Launched Jul-2017; speeds cheque clearing from up to seven days to next-day.
Accessible in branch, Internet and mobile banking; funds delivered in minutes; supports alias (mobile) lookup.
Launched 2021; interoperable with APSSS; tourists and unbanked users can pay via smartphone.
Live since Oct-2016 under Central Bank of Belize; provides RTGS for large-value, ACH for low-value (EFT), instant funds transfer 24×7, and government securities depository.
Real-time gross settlement
Upcoming 24/7 instant payments system under development by Payments Canada
sistemas.detalhes: The Real-Time Rail is a new instant payment system being developed as part of Canada’s payments modernization. Planned to enable Canadians to send and receive funds in real time, 24/7/365, using ISO 20022 data-rich messages (https://www.blakes.com/insights/canadian-payments-update-significant-developments-anticipated-in-2025/#:~:text=Among%20Payments%20Canada%E2%80%99s%20top%20priorities,and%20365%20days%20a%20year) (https://www.blakes.com/insights/canadian-payments-update-significant-developments-anticipated-in-2025/#:~:text=in%202016%2C%20the%20RTR%20was,and%20365%20days%20a%20year). Interac Corp. was selected to build the exchange infrastructure, and as of June 2023 the core exchange platform was completed (https://www.blakes.com/insights/canadian-payments-update-significant-developments-anticipated-in-2025/#:~:text=funds%20through%20real,and%20365%20days%20a%20year). The next phase focuses on the clearing and settlement component and industry testing through 2024-25 (https://www.blakes.com/insights/canadian-payments-update-significant-developments-anticipated-in-2025/#:~:text=In%20June%202023%2C%20Payments%20Canada,law%20in%202025). RTR will support real-time low-value payments with immediate finality and integrated fraud controls, addressing rising fraud risks observed in other countries’ fast payment systems (https://www.blakes.com/insights/canadian-payments-update-significant-developments-anticipated-in-2025/#:~:text=Payments%20Canada%20has%20also%20made,explored%20a%20range%20of%20possible) (https://www.blakes.com/insights/canadian-payments-update-significant-developments-anticipated-in-2025/#:~:text=methods). Operated by Payments Canada, it will likely leverage Interac as a service provider. Adoption is currently in pilot/testing (Pilot), with launch expected once development and regulatory approvals conclude. No production transaction volume exists yet as of 2024. RTR is anticipated to significantly improve payment speed and innovation once live.

sistemas.descricao: Interac e-Transfer is a popular electronic funds transfer service that lets individuals and businesses send money using email or mobile phone numbers. Funds are transferred in near real-time between deposit accounts at Canadian banks and credit unions via the Interac network. Operated by Interac Corp. and established in 2002, it has become a ubiquitous method for P2P payments, bill split, and small business invoicing. The service uses a good funds model (debiting sender and crediting recipient, with notifications by email/SMS). Adoption is Very High – by 2022 over one billion e-Transfers were sent annually . In 2024, Interac reported 1.4 billion e-Transfer transactions for the year . Nearly every Canadian online banking user has access to e-Transfers, making it a core payment rail for instant person-to-person payments. The latest known annual transaction volume exceeded $300 billion (e.g. over $350 billion was sent in the first year of the pandemic) . Interac e-Transfer will be integrated into the forthcoming RTR for real-time settlement .
sistemas.detalhes: Interac e-Transfer is a popular electronic funds transfer service that lets individuals and businesses send money using email or mobile phone numbers. Funds are transferred in near real-time between deposit accounts at Canadian banks and credit unions via the Interac network. Operated by Interac Corp. and established in 2002, it has become a ubiquitous method for P2P payments, bill split, and small business invoicing. The service uses a good funds model (debiting sender and crediting recipient, with notifications by email/SMS). Adoption is Very High – by 2022 over one billion e-Transfers were sent annually (https://www.payments.ca/insights/research/canada-reaches-117-trillion-payment-transactions-2022-seven-cent-value-2021#:~:text=2022%20www,BNPL%29). In 2024, Interac reported 1.4 billion e-Transfer transactions for the year (https://www.interac.ca/en/company/about/corporate-year-in-review/#:~:text=,transactions). Nearly every Canadian online banking user has access to e-Transfers, making it a core payment rail for instant person-to-person payments. The latest known annual transaction volume exceeded $300 billion (e.g. over $350 billion was sent in the first year of the pandemic) (https://blog.vopay.com/payment-rails-everything-canadian-businesses-need-to-know/#:~:text=Since%20the%20beginning%20of%20the,billion%20in%20total%E2%80%94have%20taken). Interac e-Transfer will be integrated into the forthcoming RTR for real-time settlement (https://www.bankofcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/annual-oversight-report-2024.pdf#:~:text=,Payments%20Canada%27s%20RTR%20payment) (https://www.blakes.com/insights/canadian-payments-update-significant-developments-anticipated-in-2025/#:~:text=In%20June%202023%2C%20Payments%20Canada,law%20in%202025).

sistemas.descricao: National debit card network

ACSS is Canada’s core clearing system for retail payments such as cheques, direct deposits, pre-authorized debits, and electronic fund transfers [oai_citation:7‡en.wikipedia.org]. Operated by Payments Canada since 1984 [oai_citation:8‡en.wikipedia.org], it aggregates and nets low-value transactions among financial institutions. Settlement occurs via the Bank of Canada, typically at end-of-day. ACSS uses batch file exchanges following Payments Canada rules for standardized payment items.
Canada's RTGS high-value payment system for irrevocable large-value fund transfers
sistemas.detalhes: Lynx is Canada's high-value electronic wire payment system, launched in August 2021 to replace the legacy LVTS. It uses real-time gross settlement, meaning payments are settled immediately in central bank money, eliminating intraday credit risk (https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2023/10/staff-analytical-note-2023-14/#:~:text=Payments%20Canada%20achieved%20a%20key,Bank%20of%20Canada%C2%A02021) (https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2023/10/staff-analytical-note-2023-14/#:~:text=In%20an%20RTGS%20system%2C%20there,settlement%20speed%20and%20liquidity%20efficiency). Operated by Payments Canada and overseen by the Bank of Canada, Lynx processes large-value and time-critical interbank transactions, including those from financial market infrastructures (https://www.finextra.com/the-long-read/662/introducing-iso-20022-to-lynx-canadas-high-value-payment-system#:~:text=Leveraging%20Swift%E2%80%99s%20secure%20financial%20messaging,amounts%20owed%20between%20their%20customers) (https://www.finextra.com/the-long-read/662/introducing-iso-20022-to-lynx-canadas-high-value-payment-system#:~:text=The%20%20launch%20of%20Lynx,valued%20at%20approximately%20%24115%20trillion). It employs liquidity-saving mechanisms like queued payment offsetting to reduce liquidity needs while maintaining speedy settlement (https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2023/10/staff-analytical-note-2023-14/#:~:text=Suppose%20two%20financial%20institutions%20each,delay%20in%20settling%20the%20payments) (https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2023/10/staff-analytical-note-2023-14/#:~:text=,liquidity%20efficiency%20in%20payment%20settlement). Lynx is designated a systemically important payment system. In its first year of operation, it cleared and settled over 12 million payments worth about $115 trillion (https://www.finextra.com/the-long-read/662/introducing-iso-20022-to-lynx-canadas-high-value-payment-system#:~:text=The%20%20launch%20of%20Lynx,valued%20at%20approximately%20%24115%20trillion) (roughly $450 billion daily). Adoption is universal among Canadian banks (Very High), as Lynx is the backbone for large-value payments, including securities and FX settlements (https://www.finextra.com/the-long-read/662/introducing-iso-20022-to-lynx-canadas-high-value-payment-system#:~:text=Leveraging%20Swift%E2%80%99s%20secure%20financial%20messaging,amounts%20owed%20between%20their%20customers) (https://www.finextra.com/the-long-read/662/introducing-iso-20022-to-lynx-canadas-high-value-payment-system#:~:text=the%20Bank%20of%20Canada%2C%20and,valued%20at%20approximately%20%24115%20trillion).

sistemas.descricao: Automated Clearing Settlement System for low-value payments (batch netting of cheques & electronic items)
sistemas.detalhes: The ACSS is Canada’s national retail payments clearing system, operated by Payments Canada for the deferred net settlement of low-value transactions. It clears cheques, pre-authorized debits, ATM payments, and electronic fund transfers in batches, with net balances settled in Lynx at end-of-day (https://www.bcentral.cl/en/areas/payment-system#:~:text=While%20in%20the%20first%20system,Time%20Gross%20Settlement%20system) (https://www.bcentral.cl/en/areas/payment-system#:~:text=While%20in%20the%20first%20system,Time%20Gross%20Settlement%20system). ACSS thus handles the high volume of consumer and business payments that are not processed in real-time. All Payments Canada member financial institutions participate. Adoption is high, as virtually all paper items and many electronic payments flow through ACSS. In 2023, the Lynx and ACSS systems together cleared over $112 trillion (https://www.payments.ca/insights/research/canada-reaches-119-trillion-retail-payment-transactions-217-billion-transactions#:~:text=Canada%20reaches%20%2411,Some%20of%20the%20transactions), with ACSS representing the retail portion. The ACSS processes billions of payment items annually, though average transaction values are low. It is a key national infrastructure ensuring ubiquitous interoperability for everyday payments.

sistemas.descricao: Interac Debit is Canada’s national PIN-based debit card network, used for point-of-sale payments and ATM withdrawals. Operated by Interac Corp., it links virtually all Canadian deposit-taking institutions and merchants. Consumers use Interac debit cards to pay from their bank accounts at retail terminals or to withdraw cash from ATMs. The network offers secure online and contactless (Interac Flash) payments as well. Adoption is Very High – Interac Debit is accepted at over 500,000 merchant locations and widely used for everyday purchases. In 2024, Interac reported 6.6 billion Interac Debit transactions (including mobile/contactless) , reflecting Canadians’ heavy reliance on debit. The network clears transactions multilaterally, with net settlement occurring via ACSS daily. Interac ensures broad interoperability of debit cards across all banks, credit unions, ATMs and point-of-sale devices nationwide . It has near-ubiquitous penetration, making it a fundamental retail payment scheme in Canada.
sistemas.detalhes: Interac Debit is Canada’s national PIN-based debit card network, used for point-of-sale payments and ATM withdrawals. Operated by Interac Corp., it links virtually all Canadian deposit-taking institutions and merchants. Consumers use Interac debit cards to pay from their bank accounts at retail terminals or to withdraw cash from ATMs. The network offers secure online and contactless (Interac Flash) payments as well. Adoption is Very High – Interac Debit is accepted at over 500,000 merchant locations and widely used for everyday purchases. In 2024, Interac reported 6.6 billion Interac Debit transactions (including mobile/contactless) (https://www.interac.ca/en/company/about/corporate-year-in-review/#:~:text=,transactions), reflecting Canadians’ heavy reliance on debit. The network clears transactions multilaterally, with net settlement occurring via ACSS daily. Interac ensures broad interoperability of debit cards across all banks, credit unions, ATMs and point-of-sale devices nationwide (https://www.interac.ca/en/company/about/corporate-year-in-review/#:~:text=,transactions). It has near-ubiquitous penetration, making it a fundamental retail payment scheme in Canada.

sistemas.descricao: Central bank digital currency initiative (research phase)
sistemas.detalhes: The Bank of Canada is researching and preparing for a potential central bank digital currency (CBDC) as a contingency for the future digital economy. Often referred to as a "digital Canadian dollar," this CBDC would be a legal tender fiat currency issued in digital form by the central bank. As of 2024, Canada has not launched a CBDC; the project remains in the Research phase. The Bank of Canada has undertaken pilot studies (e.g., Project Jasper) in collaboration with industry to explore wholesale and retail CBDC designs, but no public issuance has occurred (https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2023/10/staff-analytical-note-2023-14/#:~:text=Every%20day%2C%20households%20and%20businesses,with%20financial%20institutions%20and%20authorities) (https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2023/10/staff-analytical-note-2023-14/#:~:text=modernization%20includes%20replacing%20the%20electronic,with%20financial%20institutions%20and%20authorities). The BoC’s work focuses on ensuring readiness to issue a CBDC if needed (for example, if cash usage declines significantly or private e-money threatens monetary sovereignty). Adoption is currently N/A (research only). Transaction volume is zero since it is not launched. The CBDC initiative is essentially a policy and technology exploration to future-proof Canada’s payment systems.

sistemas.descricao: Lynx is an electronic wire transfer system operated by Payments Canada for real-time gross settlement of high-value interbank payments in Canadian dollars. It launched in 2021, replacing the LVTS system [oai_citation:1‡en.wikipedia.org]. Lynx initially used SWIFT MT messages and later adopted the ISO 20022 standard (MX messages) to carry richer data [oai_citation:2‡bankofcanada.ca]. It processes urgent wire transfers between financial institutions with finality and central bank settlement.
Airtel Money, Orange Money
Primary payment method
Real-time gross settlement system of Banque Centrale du Congo for CDF/USD
sistemas.detalhes: The Democratic Republic of Congo’s central bank (BCC) operates an RTGS system to settle high-value and urgent interbank payments. Implemented around 2015 as part of payment reforms, the RTGS can handle transactions in both Congolese francs (CDF) and U.S. dollars, reflecting DRC’s partially dollarized economy (https://deskeco.com/2021/07/06/rdc-loperationnalisation-du-switch-monetique-national-une-des-realisations-majeures-leguees-par#:~:text=De%20la%20premi%C3%A8re%20interop%C3%A9rabilit%C3%A9%20mon%C3%A9tique,secteur%20financier%20dans%20le%20pays) (https://deskeco.com/2021/07/06/rdc-loperationnalisation-du-switch-monetique-national-une-des-realisations-majeures-leguees-par#:~:text=passant%20par%20le%20syst%C3%A8me%20de,secteur%20financier%20dans%20le%20pays). The system (often referred just as the "RTGS" or SYGBTS) provides immediate finality for transfers between banks, the government treasury, and the central bank. Adoption is Medium-High: all 18+ commercial banks are connected, and it’s used for large corporate payments, government expenditures, and settlement of net positions from clearing processes. However, DRC’s formal financial sector is small, so volumes are not large compared to other countries – perhaps a few hundred payments per day, but these include critical transactions (mining revenues, etc.). The RTGS runs on modern software (the BCC worked with partners like World Bank to install it). It has significantly reduced interbank settlement delays and risk, which previously could take days. Now, for example, a transfer from Bank A to Bank B for CDF 1 billion is processed within minutes if sent through RTGS. It also links with the national securities depository for DvP of government securities. Overall, the RTGS in DRC is a cornerstone for financial stability, handling virtually all wholesale payments and ensuring liquidity moves efficiently in a challenging environment.

sistemas.descricao: Interoperable national card and mobile payment switch integrating banks and e-money
sistemas.detalhes: The Switch Monétique National, branded “Mosolo” (meaning “money” in Lingala), is an electronic payment switch launched in Dec 2020 by the BCC to interconnect all digital payment channels in DRC (https://deskeco.com/2021/07/06/rdc-loperationnalisation-du-switch-monetique-national-une-des-realisations-majeures-leguees-par#:~:text=Focus%20sur%20le%C2%A0) (https://deskeco.com/2021/07/06/rdc-loperationnalisation-du-switch-monetique-national-une-des-realisations-majeures-leguees-par#:~:text=De%20la%20premi%C3%A8re%20interop%C3%A9rabilit%C3%A9%20mon%C3%A9tique,secteur%20financier%20dans%20le%20pays). It facilitates interoperability of ATM/POS card transactions and mobile money across the country. With this switch, cards or e-wallets issued by any participant (banks, microfinance, mobile operators) can be used on any other participant’s infrastructure. Upon launch, Mosolo enabled customers of four pilot banks to perform ATM withdrawals, POS payments, and balance inquiries across each other’s ATMs/POS terminals (https://deskeco.com/2021/07/06/rdc-loperationnalisation-du-switch-monetique-national-une-des-realisations-majeures-leguees-par#:~:text=L%E2%80%99interop%C3%A9rabilit%C3%A9%20des%20paiements%20d%C3%A9sormais%20un,acquis) (https://deskeco.com/2021/07/06/rdc-loperationnalisation-du-switch-monetique-national-une-des-realisations-majeures-leguees-par#:~:text=A%20son%20inauguration%20en%20d%C3%A9cembre,la%20possibilit%C3%A9%20d%E2%80%99imprimer%20le%20ticket). All other banks are following to interface their systems. Importantly, mobile money providers (Vodacom M-Pesa, Orange Money, Airtel Money, Africell’s Afrimoney) are also connecting (https://deskeco.com/2021/07/06/rdc-loperationnalisation-du-switch-monetique-national-une-des-realisations-majeures-leguees-par#:~:text=Quant%20aux%20autres%20banques%20commerciales%2C,la%20BCC%2C%20ce%20processus%20se) (https://deskeco.com/2021/07/06/rdc-loperationnalisation-du-switch-monetique-national-une-des-realisations-majeures-leguees-par#:~:text=Switch%2C%20suivant%20un%20calendrier%20approuv%C3%A9,la%20BCC%2C%20ce%20processus%20se), meaning a user can transfer funds between mobile wallets of different telecoms or between a mobile wallet and a bank account seamlessly. The Mosolo switch thus creates “one network” for all electronic payments in DRC. Adoption is Growing: initially only limited users in pilot, but by 2023 most major banks and e-money issuers are joining. A domestic card scheme under Mosolo is being issued as well – a national debit card that all institutions will accept (https://deskeco.com/2021/07/06/rdc-loperationnalisation-du-switch-monetique-national-une-des-realisations-majeures-leguees-par#:~:text=Il%20sied%20d%E2%80%99indiquer%20que%20cette,TPE%2C%20DAB%2C%20GAB) (https://deskeco.com/2021/07/06/rdc-loperationnalisation-du-switch-monetique-national-une-des-realisations-majeures-leguees-par#:~:text=destin%C3%A9%20%C3%A0%20la%20production%20locale,TPE%2C%20DAB%2C%20GAB). The switch handles clearing in real-time, with final settlement in BCC money via RTGS. While cash is still king, Mosolo provides the backbone for expanding digital payments by dramatically increasing interoperability and convenience. Early usage is modest but ramping up as more ATMs, POS, and wallets become interoperable. The switch is a milestone in modernizing DRC’s payment infrastructure and should lead to cost reductions (one shared network instead of siloed ones) and broader acceptance of cashless payments over time.

sistemas.nome: Mobile Money (M-Pesa, Orange Money, Airtel Money)
sistemas.descricao: Telecom-led mobile wallets widely used for P2P transfers, dominating retail payments
sistemas.detalhes: Mobile money is a cornerstone of DRC’s payment landscape, far surpassing traditional banking in reach. Services like Vodacom M-Pesa (launched 2012), Orange Money, Airtel Money, and Africell Money allow people to send and receive money, pay bills, and purchase goods using their phone. Customers deposit or withdraw cash through extensive agent networks. Adoption is Very High: by Q1 2024, DRC had over 23.1 million mobile money users (40% of mobile subscribers) (https://bankable.africa/en/business-climate/0310-350-mobile-money-drc-had-23-1m-users-in-q1-2024-up-from-18-2m-in-q1-2023#:~:text=Date%3A%20%2003%20October%202024,06%3A25) (https://bankable.africa/en/business-climate/0310-350-mobile-money-drc-had-23-1m-users-in-q1-2024-up-from-18-2m-in-q1-2023#:~:text=The%20Democratic%20Republic%20of%20Congo,Vodacom%2C%20Orange%2C%20Airtel%2C%20and%20Africell), up from 8 million in 2020 (https://bankable.africa/en/business-climate/0310-350-mobile-money-drc-had-23-1m-users-in-q1-2024-up-from-18-2m-in-q1-2023#:~:text=The%20Democratic%20Republic%20of%20Congo,Vodacom%2C%20Orange%2C%20Airtel%2C%20and%20Africell) (https://bankable.africa/en/business-climate/0310-350-mobile-money-drc-had-23-1m-users-in-q1-2024-up-from-18-2m-in-q1-2023#:~:text=2024%20had%20a%20Mobile%20Money,Vodacom%2C%20Orange%2C%20Airtel%2C%20and%20Africell). This explosive growth has made mobile wallets the primary non-cash payment method. In 2022, DRC’s mobile money transaction value was several billion USD per month. Mobile money is used for domestic remittances (vital in such a large country with poor roads), salaries by some NGOs/companies, and everyday person-to-person transfers. Orange Money and Airtel Money also offer merchant payment solutions in urban areas. With the national switch integration, interoperability between these previously siloed wallets is being achieved, further boosting usage. While there are still challenges (fraud, agent liquidity, telecom outages), mobile money has greatly improved financial inclusion – around 26% of adults have a mobile money account vs 15% with a bank account (https://www.elibrary.imf.org/downloadpdf/view/journals/002/2022/211/article-A002-en.pdf#:~:text=,Saharan) (https://www.elibrary.imf.org/downloadpdf/view/journals/002/2022/211/article-A002-en.pdf#:~:text=Approximately%2016%20percent%20of%20adults,Saharan). In sum, mobile money rails in DRC carry enormous volume and are critical for the population to transact, effectively functioning as the country’s retail payment system in practice.

sistemas.descricao: DRC’s participation in SADC’s mobile-based cross-border instant payment scheme
sistemas.detalhes: DRC, as a member of the Southern African Development Community (SADC), is part of the SADC initiative called Transactions Cleared on an Immediate Basis (TCIB). TCIB is a regional platform enabling instant low-value cross-border payments, focusing on interoperability between mobile money and bank accounts across SADC countries (https://www.paymentcomponents.com/all-about-payments-in-africa/#:~:text=) (https://www.paymentcomponents.com/all-about-payments-in-africa/#:~:text=%E2%80%98Transactions%20Cleared%20on%20an%20Immediate,South%20Africa%2C%20Tanzania%2C%20Zambia%2C%20Zimbabwe). It allows, for example, someone in DRC to send money in real-time to a recipient’s mobile wallet or bank in Zambia or Malawi (converted via forex at backend). TCIB was launched in 2021 by BankservAfrica and has several SADC countries piloting, including DRC. Adoption is currently Pilot in DRC: one or two operators (possibly Airtel or Orange) have started testing TCIB transfers to neighboring countries, but volumes are extremely low since the service is new and not widely publicized. Over time, as awareness and participation grow, TCIB could capture a share of the substantial informal remittance flows between DRC and bordering countries. It offers a cheaper, faster alternative to Western Union or carrying cash over borders. DRC’s central bank supports it as part of regional integration. In summary, TCIB is an emerging scheme linking DRC’s domestic mobile money to the region. Still in early rollout, its adoption in DRC remains limited for now but has significant future potential to streamline cross-border small value payments for trade and remittances in Central/Southern Africa.

sistemas.descricao: The Democratic Republic of Congo’s RTGS was modernized under a World Bank project and launched in September 2017 [oai_citation:61‡documents1.worldbank.org]. Operated by the Central Bank (BCC), it settles high-value interbank payments in real time. Uniquely, it supports multi-currency: both Congolese Franc (CDF) and USD transactions were settled (USD capability was briefly active in 2019) [oai_citation:62‡documents1.worldbank.org] [oai_citation:63‡documents1.worldbank.org]. The RTGS provides final, irrevocable settlement and has significantly improved efficiency (electronic payments that once took days are now same-day or immediate [oai_citation:64‡documents1.worldbank.org]). All major banks in DRC participate. The system handles government payments, large corporate transfers, and net settlements from other clearing systems.

sistemas.nome: Mobile Money Services (M-Pesa, Airtel Money, Orange Money)
sistemas.descricao: Mobile money has become a cornerstone of everyday payments in the DRC, where traditional banking reaches only a small fraction of the population. Services like Vodacom’s M-Pesa (launched 2013), Airtel Money, and Orange Money allow millions of Congolese to send money, pay bills, and buy prepaid credits using just a mobile phone. Users cash-in at agents to fund their wallet, then transfer value via USSD or app instantly to other users of the same network. Mobile money transactions are typically low-value but high-volume, and have grown rapidly alongside the expansion of cellular networks. While the platforms are proprietary and siloed by provider, there are initiatives to interconnect them and link to banks. These wallets have greatly improved financial inclusion and domestic remittances, even though most transactions ultimately settle outside the banking system.

The DRC’s Automated Clearing House system was introduced alongside the RTGS in 2017 to process low-value payments electronically. It clears batched transactions like payroll direct credits, interbank ATM withdrawals, and cheque images. The ACH drastically reduced clearing times – for example, cheque clearing shortened from about a week to next-day (T+1) [oai_citation:66‡documents1.worldbank.org]. It operates in both CDF and (formerly) USD. By 2019, the ACH processed over 4.6 million transactions, of which 4.5 million in local currency (990% of target) [oai_citation:67‡documents1.worldbank.org]. Net positions from the ACH are settled each day in the RTGS. The ACH uses a multilateral netting software (often called ATS+ in BCC reports), providing more efficient retail payments.

Mosolo is the DRC’s interbank card scheme and switching platform, launched in 2020 to facilitate nationwide card transactions. It allows bank-issued debit cards to be used interoperably at any ATM or point-of-sale terminal connected to the network. Operated initially by the central bank, Mosolo is branded for domestic cards and aims to reduce reliance on international card networks. As of 2021, 11 banks had connected (5 actively transacting, others onboarding) [oai_citation:70‡documents1.worldbank.org]. Some larger banks, which used a private switch (Multipay), have started integrating into Mosolo [oai_citation:71‡documents1.worldbank.org]. Mosolo handles authorization routing and clearing of card transactions, with final settlement occurring via the RTGS. The system is still scaling up, but it is expected to expand card acceptance and usage in the DRC.

Regional real-time gross settlement system for Central African states (XAF currency)
sistemas.detalhes: SYGMA (Système de Gros Montants Automatisé) is the RTGS system serving all six CEMAC countries (including Central African Republic). Operated by the regional central bank BEAC, it provides instantaneous settlement of high-value interbank transfers in the CFA franc (XAF) (https://www.businessincameroon.com/finance/0207-5523-beac-launches-the-regional-committee-for-method-of-payment-monitoring-in-the-cemac-zone#:~:text=BEAC%20launches%20the%20Regional%20Committee,involving%20over%20100%20million%20FCFA) (https://www.businessincameroon.com/finance/0207-5523-beac-launches-the-regional-committee-for-method-of-payment-monitoring-in-the-cemac-zone#:~:text=It%20involves%20the%20automated%20gross,involving%20over%20100%20million%20FCFA). SYGMA handles urgent and large-value payments (over 100 million XAF per BEAC definition (https://www.businessincameroon.com/finance/0207-5523-beac-launches-the-regional-committee-for-method-of-payment-monitoring-in-the-cemac-zone#:~:text=BEAC%20launches%20the%20Regional%20Committee,involving%20over%20100%20million%20FCFA) (https://www.businessincameroon.com/finance/0207-5523-beac-launches-the-regional-committee-for-method-of-payment-monitoring-in-the-cemac-zone#:~:text=It%20involves%20the%20automated%20gross,involving%20over%20100%20million%20FCFA)), including central bank operations, treasury payments, and bank-to-bank transfers. Adoption is High among banks: all licensed banks in CAR and the region must use SYGMA for large transactions and final net settlements. As of 2020, SYGMA processed 67 thousand transactions region-wide (https://cenfri.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/Payment-systems-in-SSA-Note-2.pdf#:~:text=%5BPDF%5D%20Payment%20systems%20in%20sub,SYSTAC%29%20that) (https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/321341524231758456/txt/BEAC-CEMAC-PAD-PAD2558-04092018.txt#:~:text=These%20systems%20which%20are%20operated,bulk%20payments%20at%20a) (increasing as financial activity grows). In value terms, traditional bank transfers via SYGMA dominate – e.g., in 2022 conventional transfers made up 44% of total transaction value in CEMAC (CFA 48,573 billion) (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=The%20document%20indicated%20that%20over,totaling%20CFA48%2C573%20billion%2C%20followed%20by) (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=be%20noted%20that%20mobile%20money,transaction%20value%20in%20the%20zone). For CAR, SYGMA is crucial for government and international payments. It operates in real-time through BEAC’s platform and ensures settlement finality for the region’s shared currency.

sistemas.descricao: Regional automated clearing house for retail payments in Central Africa
sistemas.detalhes: SYSTAC (Système de Télécompensation en Afrique Centrale) is the CEMAC region’s automated clearing system for low-value, bulk payments (https://cenfri.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/Payment-systems-in-SSA-Note-2.pdf#:~:text=%5BPDF%5D%20Payment%20systems%20in%20sub,SYSTAC%29%20that) (https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/321341524231758456/txt/BEAC-CEMAC-PAD-PAD2558-04092018.txt#:~:text=These%20systems%20which%20are%20operated,bulk%20payments%20at%20a). Also run by BEAC, SYSTAC clears batched transactions like cheques, direct debits, and electronic transfers among banks across Central African Republic, Chad, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Republic of Congo, and Cameroon. Payments are netted within each national zone and settled via SYGMA at end-of-cycle. Adoption is Medium: banks and MFIs use SYSTAC for everyday retail payments, but mobile money has eroded some usage. Still, SYSTAC handled ~2% of the region’s payment volume in 2022 (48.3 million transactions) (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=The%20document%20indicated%20that%20over,totaling%20CFA48%2C573%20billion%2C%20followed%20by) and a significant share of value (especially corporate and salary payments). It operates on a deferred net settlement model. In CAR, given a small banking sector, SYSTAC volume is modest but it remains the backbone for clearing paper instruments and interbank transfers like payroll. The system helps ensure interoperability of traditional payment methods within the region’s banking system.

sistemas.descricao: Regional interbank switch integrating card and mobile payments across CEMAC
sistemas.detalhes: GIMAC (Groupement Interbancaire Monétique de l'Afrique Centrale) is the interoperable payment switch for the CEMAC region, linking banks, card networks, and mobile money operators (https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/SIIPS2023_CaseStudy_CEMAC.pdf#:~:text=The%20objective%20of%20forming%20GIMAC,MFIs%29%2C%20and) (https://africa-on-air.com/en/economy-en/2022/11/la-carte-gimac-bouscule-le-marche-digital-bancaire-en-afrique-centrale/#:~:text=GIMAC%20card%20shakes%20up%20the,within%20the%20six%20member%20countries). 99% owned by BEAC, GIMAC’s mission is to promote electronic payments and financial inclusion (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=institutions%2C%2011%20Mobile%20Money%20operators%2C,one%20Treasury%2C%20and%2014%20aggregators) (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=With%20a%20capital%20of%20CFA3,in%202022%20according%20to%20BEAC). It operates GIMACPAY, an ecosystem launched in 2020 that converges ATM/POS card transactions with mobile money transfers across different providers (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=backed) (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=The%20rise%20in%20transaction%20volume,December%2031%2C%202022%2C%20the%20GimacPay). Through GIMAC, a common "GIMAC Card" has been issued allowing cardholders to transact in all six countries (https://www.mfw4a.org/news/gimac-payment-card-now-available-across-cemac#:~:text=GIMAC%20payment%20card%20now%20available,Chad%2C%20Equatorial%20Guinea%20and%20CAR) (https://www.mfw4a.org/news/gimac-payment-card-now-available-across-cemac#:~:text=This%20card%20allows%20users%20to,Chad%2C%20Equatorial%20Guinea%20and%20CAR), and mobile wallets of various telcos are now interoperable regionally. Adoption is Growing: by end-2022, GIMACPAY connected 89 participants (53 banks, 11 mobile money operators, etc.) (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=card%20transactions%20and%20merging%20Mobile,one%20Treasury%2C%20and%2014%20aggregators) (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=mobile%20wallet%20connected%20to%20bank,one%20Treasury%2C%20and%2014%20aggregators). It still processed only about 1% of electronic money transactions in 2022 (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=With%20a%20capital%20of%20CFA3,in%202022%20according%20to%20BEAC), but volumes are rising rapidly. In 2022, GIMAC handled over 7.3 million mobile money interoperability transactions (CFA 224 billion) (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=The%20Interbank%20Monetary%20Group%20of,BEAC) (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=operations%20amounting%20to%20CFA21,BEAC), a tenfold increase since 2020. In CAR, GIMAC enables, for example, an Orange Money user to send funds to an MTN Mobile Money user, or to withdraw cash at any GIMAC ATM. As the regional payment hub, GIMAC is increasingly vital for integrating CAR’s digital payments with its neighbors.

sistemas.descricao: Telecom-led e-money wallets widely used for domestic payments
sistemas.detalhes: Mobile money services have become the dominant retail payment method in CAR given low bank access. Operators like Orange Money and Telecel (MOOV) Money allow users to store value in a phone-based wallet and send money via mobile phone, pay merchants, and buy goods. Adoption is Very High: mobile wallets account for the vast majority of payment transactions in the economy. In 2022, across CEMAC, over 96% of payment transactions (2.3 billion operations) were via mobile money (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=The%20document%20indicated%20that%20over,totaling%20CFA48%2C573%20billion%2C%20followed%20by). In CAR, even before interoperability, citizens heavily relied on mobile money for P2P transfers and purchases due to insecurity and limited banking. However, mobile money transactions are mostly small in value. By value, they made up ~21% of total in 2022 (CFA 23,332 billion in instant mobile transfers regionally) (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=be%20noted%20that%20mobile%20money,transaction%20value%20in%20the%20zone) (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=be%20dominated%20by%20traditional%20banks,transaction%20value%20in%20the%20zone). With GIMAC integration, CAR’s mobile money providers can now interconnect with other countries. Adoption continues to grow as mobile coverage expands. Mobile money has substantially increased financial inclusion in CAR, though cash still circulates for many informal transactions.

sistemas.descricao: Controversial adoption of Bitcoin as official currency (since repealed)
sistemas.detalhes: In April 2022, the Central African Republic passed a law declaring Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies legal tender alongside the CFA franc (https://www.centralbanking.com/central-banks/currency/digital-currencies/7956294/car-to-drop-crypto-as-legal-tender#:~:text=The%20Central%20African%20Republic%E2%80%99s%20parliament,Monetary%20Community%20of%20Central%20Africa). This move made CAR the first African nation to adopt Bitcoin as an official currency, aiming to attract investors and circumvent banking constraints. A government project called "Sango" was launched to promote crypto usage and even sell citizenship and land via crypto tokens. However, adoption has been extremely Low. Due to limited internet (around 10% penetration) and electricity access, very few in CAR actually transact in Bitcoin. The initiative faced criticism from regional partners (BEAC and IMF) and was largely symbolic. By late 2022, CAR halted the implementation amid pressure, and in March 2023 the legal tender law for crypto was unanimously repealed by parliament (https://www.centralbanking.com/central-banks/currency/digital-currencies/7956294/car-to-drop-crypto-as-legal-tender#:~:text=The%20Central%20African%20Republic%E2%80%99s%20parliament,Monetary%20Community%20of%20Central%20Africa) (https://www.centralbanking.com/central-banks/currency/digital-currencies/7956294/car-to-drop-crypto-as-legal-tender#:~:text=bitcoin%20and%20other%20cryptocurrencies%20legal,Monetary%20Community%20of%20Central%20Africa). As of 2024, Bitcoin is no longer official currency, and crypto usage remains negligible in the local economy. CAR’s brief crypto experiment thus had virtually no transaction volume or real adoption on the ground.

sistemas.descricao: GIMACPAY is the interbank electronic payment platform in Central Africa, covering card transactions (ATM/POS) and emerging digital payments across CEMAC. It is administered by GIMAC (the regional card switching network, Groupement Interbancaire Monétique de l'Afrique Centrale) [oai_citation:43‡beac.int]. GIMACPAY connects banks and microfinance institutions for interoperable card withdrawals, purchases, and increasingly mobile wallet payments. In CAR, local banks and mobile money operators link into GIMAC to enable, for example, a customer of one bank to use their card in another bank’s ATM. The system operates continuously, with settlement of net positions via BEAC. GIMACPAY is being upgraded to adopt the ISO 20022 standard for more advanced digital transactions [oai_citation:44‡paymentcomponents.com].

Orange Money is a telecom-operated mobile money platform that allows users in CAR to send and receive money, pay bills, and purchase services via mobile phone. It operates on USSD and mobile app channels, enabling the unbanked population to access basic financial services. In the Central African Republic, where traditional banking is limited, Orange Money has gained a majority share of the mobile payments market (over 90% of mobile money users) [oai_citation:52‡wholesale.orange.com]. Customers deposit cash with Orange agents to fund their wallets and can cash-out similarly. Transfers occur instantly between wallets. While popular for P2P transfers and merchant payments, transactions remain outside the formal banking system, with interoperability only through agent cash handling or planned integrations with banks.

Sango Coin is a cryptocurrency launched by the Central African Republic government in 2022 as a so-called “national digital currency.” It was introduced after CAR made Bitcoin legal tender in April 2022, becoming the first African nation to do so [oai_citation:49‡reuters.com]. The Sango project aimed to attract foreign investment and tokenise the country’s resources. Investors can purchase Sango Coins (initially priced at $0.10) using Bitcoin or Ethereum [oai_citation:50‡reuters.com]. Technical specifics (blockchain protocol, etc.) have not been fully disclosed, and uptake has been extremely limited due to low internet penetration and skepticism. The initiative is more of a strategic experiment in crypto-based infrastructure than a mainstream payment system at this stage.

sistemas.nome: SYSTAC (Système de Télécompensation en Afrique Centrale)
sistemas.descricao: SYSTAC is the CEMAC regional automated clearing house for low-value (mass) payments in CFA francs. Launched alongside SYGMA in 2007 [oai_citation:39‡beac.int], SYSTAC handles the net clearing of cheques, direct debits, and electronic transfers among banks in Central African Republic and neighboring states. Banks transmit payment files to BEAC’s processing center, which calculates multilateral net settlement positions daily. The net positions are then settled through SYGMA (the RTGS) at BEAC [oai_citation:40‡beac.int]. SYSTAC significantly reduced float and delays for intraregional retail payments, though the clearing cycle for cheques remains T+2 days [oai_citation:41‡beac.int].

SYGMA is the real-time gross settlement system used by Central African Republic and other CEMAC countries (Cameroon, Chad, Congo-Brazzaville, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea) for large-value fund transfers in the CFA franc (XAF). Implemented by the BEAC (regional central bank) in 2007 [oai_citation:34‡beac.int] [oai_citation:35‡cma.se], SYGMA provides instantaneous settlement of interbank transfers above certain thresholds (e.g., >100 million XAF) [oai_citation:36‡businessincameroon.com] with finality in central bank money. It operates via a single shared platform for the region, ensuring that transactions between banks across CEMAC settle securely and in real time.
Primary payment method
Limited services
Regional RTGS for high-value payments in CFA Franc (see CAR/Chad)
sistemas.detalhes: The Republic of the Congo (Congo-Brazzaville) uses the CEMAC-wide SYGMA system for large-value payments in the CFA franc. Operated by BEAC, SYGMA processes Brazzaville’s interbank transfers, central government payments, and oil revenue transactions in real time (https://cenfri.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/Payment-systems-in-SSA-Note-2.pdf#:~:text=%5BPDF%5D%20Payment%20systems%20in%20sub,SYSTAC%29%20that) (https://cenfri.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/Payment-systems-in-SSA-Note-2.pdf#:~:text=These%20systems%2C%20which%20are%20operated,SYSTAC%29%20that). Adoption is High among the country’s banks and treasury: it’s mandatory for transactions above the threshold (100 million XAF) and for settling net positions from other systems. For instance, when the treasury in Brazzaville transfers funds to a contractor’s bank, that likely goes via SYGMA to ensure immediate finality. While the number of banks is small (~10 in country), SYGMA volume reflects major economic flows, particularly oil sector payments which are typically large. In 2022, traditional bank transfers in CEMAC (via SYGMA) dominated value terms (44% of total value) (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=be%20noted%20that%20mobile%20money,transaction%20value%20in%20the%20zone). In Congo’s context, that includes transfers related to oil exports, government spending, etc. SYGMA’s availability has markedly improved payment speed: before, some large transfers might have been done by paper or correspondents causing delays. Now they settle same-day within the region. The RTGS is thus critical for Brazzaville’s financial system stability and integration in regional monetary operations. Overall, SYGMA is fully adopted by Congo’s formal financial sector and underpins essentially all high-value payments in the economy.

sistemas.descricao: Regional clearing system for cheques and retail payments (see CAR/Chad)
sistemas.detalhes: Congo-Brazzaville’s low-value interbank payments are cleared through SYSTAC, the Central African regional ACH. SYSTAC aggregates and nets retail transactions – e.g., cheques, direct debit for utility bills, interbank small credit transfers – for all banks in Congo, then sends the net results to BEAC for settlement. Adoption is Moderate: the use of cheques and traditional bank transfers is limited to the small banked population and businesses (many retail payments, especially outside cities, still happen in cash). Still, SYSTAC serves important functions: e.g., Brazzaville’s clearing house handles cheque exchanges; salaries of civil servants paid by cheque or transfer are cleared in SYSTAC. Regionally, SYSTAC processed ~48.3 million transactions in 2022 (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=The%20document%20indicated%20that%20over,totaling%20CFA48%2C573%20billion%2C%20followed%20by) – Congo’s portion of that might be a few million. The system operates on daily cycles. As mobile money grows (which bypasses banks), SYSTAC’s share of volume may decline, but for now it remains a backbone for bank-mediated payments. All Congo’s banks participate via BEAC’s local branch. SYSTAC ensures interoperability – e.g., a cheque drawn on Bank A Pointe-Noire and deposited at Bank B Brazzaville will clear through SYSTAC. With the regional nature, cross-border low-value payments (like an electronic transfer from a bank in Congo to Cameroon) also clear via SYSTAC. In summary, SYSTAC is used by banks in Congo for clearing their retail instruments, with decent adoption in formal sectors, though overall transaction counts are limited by heavy reliance on cash and emerging mobile money alternatives.

sistemas.descricao: Regional interbank network enabling card usage and mobile money interoperability
sistemas.detalhes: Congo Republic is part of the GIMAC interbank network covering Central Africa. Through GIMAC, banks in Brazzaville issue the GIMAC interbank card which is accepted at ATMs/POS throughout CEMAC (https://www.mfw4a.org/news/gimac-payment-card-now-available-across-cemac#:~:text=GIMAC%20payment%20card%20now%20available,Chad%2C%20Equatorial%20Guinea%20and%20CAR) (https://www.mfw4a.org/news/gimac-payment-card-now-available-across-cemac#:~:text=This%20card%20allows%20users%20to,Chad%2C%20Equatorial%20Guinea%20and%20CAR), and local mobile money providers (e.g., MTN Mobile Money) are linked into a shared platform (GIMACPAY) for interoperability (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=backed) (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=The%20rise%20in%20transaction%20volume,December%2031%2C%202022%2C%20the%20GimacPay). Adoption in Congo is Emerging: as of 2022, GIMAC had members including the Congo Treasury, all major banks and at least one mobile operator (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=card%20transactions%20and%20merging%20Mobile,one%20Treasury%2C%20and%2014%20aggregators). For cards, this means a Congolese bank customer can withdraw cash at any ATM in Cameroon, Chad, etc., and vice versa. For mobile money, users are starting to be able to transact across networks/countries. GIMAC processed 7.3 million interoperable transactions regionally in 2022 (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=The%20Interbank%20Monetary%20Group%20of,BEAC), likely a small fraction in Congo itself but expected to grow as awareness increases. MTN Congo and Airtel Congo have large mobile money user bases, and their connection to GIMACPAY will allow, say, an Airtel user to send funds to an MTN user seamlessly (which previously was impossible). Additionally, GIMAC facilitates cross-border remittances in the region (like a worker in Gabon sending money home to Congo through mobile). For now, GIMAC’s services in Congo are being rolled out – adoption is so far Low but trending upward. The central bank and GIMAC are actively promoting these services to reduce cash dependence and encourage electronic transactions. Over the next few years, usage of GIMAC’s unified card/mobile network in Congo is anticipated to expand, improving convenience and financial integration for Congolese consumers.

sistemas.descricao: Telecom-operated e-money wallets becoming key for domestic transfers and payments
sistemas.detalhes: In the Republic of Congo, mobile money services offered by telecom companies have rapidly gained traction as accessible financial tools. MTN Mobile Money and Airtel Money are the primary services, allowing individuals to use their mobile phones to store money, send and receive funds, pay utilities, and even withdraw cash via agent networks. Adoption is Medium and rising: by 2022, an estimated 1.5 million people (roughly 30% of adults) had mobile money accounts, up from practically none a few years prior. This growth is fuelled by the limited banking network and a need for remittance services. Mobile money is used especially for P2P domestic remittances (e.g., urban workers sending money to family in villages) and bill payments (electricity, TV subscriptions). With GIMAC integration, these wallets will also be interoperable with bank accounts and across borders, further enhancing utility. Despite this progress, cash still dominates overall transactions in Congo; mobile money usage, while significant in urban centers, has not yet penetrated all rural areas. Still, the trend is toward greater reliance on mobile wallets due to their convenience and the ubiquity of mobile phones. The central bank (BEAC) regulates these as e-money, requiring telcos to partner with banks for float holding. As the network of agents and merchant acceptance expands, mobile money could become a leading payment rail in Congo-Brazzaville for everyday transactions, gradually reducing cash’s prominence. Currently, its share of transaction volume is growing but from a low base, so in 2023 it’s best characterized as a high-growth segment of the payment system.

sistemas.nome: SYSTAC (Système de Télécompensation en Afrique Centrale)
sistemas.descricao: SYSTAC is the shared low-value clearing system for Republic of Congo and its CEMAC peers. (See CAR’s SYSTAC.) It nets cheque payments, electronic credits, and other retail transactions within the day and sends net results to the RTGS for settlement. This provides an efficient multicountry ACH framework for the CFA franc zone.

MTN Mobile Money is a prominent mobile payment wallet in the Republic of Congo, provided by the MTN telecom network. It allows users to load cash at MTN agents, then send money, pay bills, and purchase services through their mobile phones. With MTN MoMo being widely available, it has achieved significant reach; about 25% of the population were using mobile money by late 2010s [oai_citation:58‡facebook.com]. MTN’s platform is similar to others in that transactions are executed via USSD menus or the MTN app, and balances are stored in an electronic wallet linked to the user’s phone number. MTN MoMo has helped reduce reliance on physical cash, especially for domestic remittances and everyday payments, although interoperability with bank systems is still limited.

SYGMA is the RTGS for high-value transfers in the Central African CFA franc, shared by Republic of Congo and other CEMAC members. (Refer to Central African Republic’s SYGMA description.) It enables instant, irrevocable settlement of large-value interbank payments via BEAC’s centralized platform.

GIMACPAY serves Republic of Congo as the platform for interbank card transactions and emerging instant payments in the CEMAC region. (See CAR’s GIMACPAY entry.) It allows, for example, a Congolese bank’s customer to use ATMs or POS terminals in any member country. It also lays the foundation for connecting mobile money with bank accounts under a unified switch.
Mobile payment app
Interbank clearing

SIC is Switzerland’s central payment system, launched in 1987, operated by SIX on behalf of the Swiss National Bank [oai_citation:18‡snb.ch]. It processes both large-value and retail CHF transactions among banks and financial institutions. SIC follows real-time gross settlement principles and is overseen by the SNB.
Leading mobile wallet
Competing mobile wallet
Leading online gateway
Real-time transfers
Chile’s high-value real-time gross settlement system operated by the central bank
sistemas.detalhes: The Sistema de Liquidación Bruta en Tiempo Real (LBTR) is Chile’s interbank RTGS system for settling high-value payments in Chilean pesos. Run by the Central Bank of Chile, LBTR is the backbone for large-value transfers – including interbank loans, corporate payments, and settlement of other systems’ net positions (https://www.bcentral.cl/en/areas/payment-system#:~:text=Large%20value%20payment%20systems%20provide,a%20Bank%20Draft%20Support%20Company) (https://www.bcentral.cl/en/areas/payment-system#:~:text=and%20importance%20to%20the%20economy,a%20Bank%20Draft%20Support%20Company). It provides immediate, irrevocable settlement in central bank money. LBTR operates during business hours, processing both proprietary bank payments and customer payments that require urgent clearing. Adoption is Very High among financial institutions: all banks and relevant financial intermediaries maintain accounts at the central bank and use LBTR for wholesale payments. On average, LBTR processes thousands of transactions daily totaling trillions of pesos. For instance, the daily average value settled in LBTR often exceeds CLP 5–6 trillion (over USD 6 billion). LBTR also settles the net obligations from the Combanc clearing house at day-end (https://www.bcentral.cl/en/areas/payment-system#:~:text=While%20in%20the%20first%20system,Time%20Gross%20Settlement%20system) (https://www.bcentral.cl/en/areas/payment-system#:~:text=While%20in%20the%20first%20system,Time%20Gross%20Settlement%20system). The system is crucial for monetary policy operations and for final settlement of stock exchange and CCP (CCLV) transactions. With a USD RTGS module as well, LBTR ensures both CLP and USD high-value transfers settle safely. As Chile’s only LVPS, LBTR’s adoption is universal and critical for financial stability.

sistemas.descricao: Deferred net settlement system for large-value interbank payments in Chile
sistemas.detalhes: Alongside LBTR, Chile has a complementary high-value clearing system known as the Cámara de Compensación de Pagos de Alto Valor (CCAV), managed by Combanc S.A. (https://www.bcentral.cl/en/areas/payment-system#:~:text=Large%20value%20payment%20systems%20provide,a%20Bank%20Draft%20Support%20Company) (https://www.bcentral.cl/en/areas/payment-system#:~:text=and%20importance%20to%20the%20economy,a%20Bank%20Draft%20Support%20Company). In this system, participating banks send large-value payment orders throughout the day which are queued and netted rather than settled individually. At the end of the cycle, a single multilateral net position per bank is calculated and then settled in central bank money via the LBTR RTGS (https://www.bcentral.cl/en/areas/payment-system#:~:text=While%20in%20the%20first%20system,Time%20Gross%20Settlement%20system) (https://www.bcentral.cl/en/areas/payment-system#:~:text=While%20in%20the%20first%20system,Time%20Gross%20Settlement%20system). This netting mechanism improves liquidity efficiency by offsetting payments among banks. CCAV is particularly used for high-volume, high-value client payments and certain market transactions where slight delays are acceptable. Adoption is High: all major banks in Chile participate in Combanc’s clearing house for peso transactions, benefiting from reduced intraday liquidity needs. The system processed an annual value of CLP ~226 trillion (approx. USD 300 billion) in recent years. It also has a dollar-clearing segment. While LBTR can handle all large payments, CCAV offers an alternative route that optimizes liquidity usage. It is tightly integrated with LBTR (for final settlement) and with the central securities depository for DvP of OTC trades. In practice, around half of large-value payments by number might flow through CCAV. The system is overseen by the central bank and considered systemically important. It provides robustness via a loss-sharing agreement and collateral requirements for participants to cover net debit positions, ensuring settlement finality each day.

sistemas.descricao: Shared nationwide ATM network interconnecting banks in Chile
sistemas.detalhes: Redbanc is an interbank network that links the ATMs of all major Chilean banks, enabling customers to withdraw cash or inquire balances at any ATM regardless of the issuing bank. Formed in 1987, Redbanc acts as a switch and clearing house for ATM transactions (cash withdrawals, balance lookups, etc.). Adoption is Very High – it connects over 7,000 ATMs across Chile and virtually every bank participates, meaning bank customers have broad ATM access countrywide. Redbanc ATM withdrawals are cleared via a specialized clearinghouse (with net positions settled in LBTR each day) (https://www.bcentral.cl/en/areas/payment-system#:~:text=In%20Chile%2C%20payments%20of%20this,determined%20in%20specialized%20clearing%20houses) (https://www.bcentral.cl/en/areas/payment-system#:~:text=as%20cash%2C%20checks%2C%20credit%20and,determined%20in%20specialized%20clearing%20houses). The network handles millions of withdrawal transactions per month. As of 2023, the number of ATM transactions has been stable or declining slightly due to increased digital payments, but it remains a critical payment service especially for cash access. Redbanc also supports some utility payments and credit card cash advances at ATMs. By pooling ATMs, Redbanc increases efficiency (customers are not limited to their own bank’s machines) and lowers costs. It is jointly owned by banks and overseen by the CMF. The system ensures interoperability and high availability of cash distribution, forming an important part of Chile’s payment infrastructure especially for those reliant on cash.

sistemas.descricao: Domestic card payment scheme & processor (credit/debit acquiring network)
sistemas.detalhes: Transbank is Chile’s main card payments processor and network for retail payments, historically a bank-owned monopoly that acquires and processes all major credit and debit card transactions in the country. It operates the RedCompra debit scheme – Chile’s domestic debit card brand – which works via the global networks (often co-branded with Visa/Mastercard) but is processed locally by Transbank (https://www.globaldata.com/store/report/chile-cards-and-payments-market-analysis/#:~:text=Chile%20Cards%20and%20Payments%20%E2%80%93,a%20CAGR%20of%20more). Transbank connects over 200,000 merchants through POS terminals and online gateways (WebPay). Adoption is Very High: virtually all point-of-sale card payments in Chile (whether Visa, MasterCard, or RedCompra debit) are funneled through Transbank’s platform. In 2022, card payments value in Chile was about USD 84 billion, up 16% YoY (https://www.electronicpaymentsinternational.com/marketdata/chile-card-payments-value-cagr-2025-2/#:~:text=Chile%27s%20card%20payments%20value%20to,7tn) (https://www.electronicpaymentsinternational.com/marketdata/chile-card-payments-value-cagr-2025-2/#:~:text=2025%20www,7tn), reflecting heavy usage. Debit cards are especially prevalent (over 27 million debit cards active (https://rankingslatam.com/blogs/industry-news/credit-and-debit-cards-market-in-chile-2023-12-rankings#:~:text=Rankings%20rankingslatam,to%20the%20end%20of%202022)). Transbank operates in online mode with authorization and guarantee of payments; net settlements between issuers and acquirers occur via the central bank at end of day. With regulatory changes, new acquirers are entering, but Transbank remains dominant. It ensures nationwide merchant acceptance, fraud prevention, and switching of transactions. RedCompra debit transactions are PIN-based and accounted for a large share of the 3+ billion card transactions annually. Transbank’s network is thus crucial for everyday consumer spending in Chile, from supermarkets to e-commerce, and its reliability and coverage have made card payments nearly ubiquitous.

sistemas.descricao: Fintech mobile wallets and prepaid accounts for fast retail payments
sistemas.detalhes: In recent years, Chile has seen rapid growth of non-bank digital wallets offered by fintechs and banks. Notable examples include Mach (a prepaid Visa card app launched by Banco Bci) and Tenpo (a standalone fintech wallet). These services provide users with an app-based account, a virtual or physical card, and the ability to quickly transfer money or pay online. Mach and Tenpo target younger consumers and the underbanked with low fees and easy onboarding (https://krealo.pe/en/portfolio/tenpo/#:~:text=Tenpo%20is%20a%20Fintech%20that,to%20bringing%20democracy%20to%20finance) (https://www.nuvei.com/apm/mach#:~:text=Mach%20,management%2C%20payments%2C%20and%20financial%20services). Adoption is Medium but rising fast: by 2023, Mach had ~5 million users and Tenpo over 2 million, contributing to Chile’s ~55 million digital wallet transactions annually (https://coinscrapfinance.com/fintech-news/best-neobanks-colombia/#:~:text=Top%2010%20neobanks%20in%20Colombia,in%20Colombia%27s%20neobank%20market) (https://coinscrapfinance.com/fintech-news/best-neobanks-colombia/#:~:text=By%202023%2C%20access%20to%20financial,in%20Colombia%27s%20neobank%20market). These wallets allow instant P2P transfers (often via simplified bank transfer systems like using phone contacts or QR codes) and integration with the traditional card networks for merchant payments. They benefit from Chile’s interoperable bank transfer infrastructure – for example, services like Khipu and CuentaRUT (BancoEstado’s widely held basic account) are used alongside. Mach and Tenpo store value in prepaid accounts and are regulated as non-bank payment service providers. As of 2024, digital wallets have over 60% population reach in Chile (https://coinscrapfinance.com/fintech-news/best-neobanks-colombia/#:~:text=Top%2010%20neobanks%20in%20Colombia,in%20Colombia%27s%20neobank%20market) (https://coinscrapfinance.com/fintech-news/best-neobanks-colombia/#:~:text=By%202023%2C%20access%20to%20financial,in%20Colombia%27s%20neobank%20market). They are especially popular for e-commerce and contactless payments via smartphone. Volume, while still a fraction of traditional banking transactions, is growing double-digits yearly. These fintech wallets complement Chile’s payment ecosystem by providing user-friendly, 24/7 instant payment options outside of conventional bank channels, and they represent the future trajectory of retail payments (highly digital and mobile).

sistemas.nome: Sistema LBTR (Liquidación Bruta en Tiempo Real)
sistemas.descricao: LBTR is the RTGS operated by the Central Bank of Chile (BCCh) to settle large-value interbank payments in Chilean pesos (and since 2021, it also supports USD settlements) [oai_citation:83‡bis.org]. Payments are processed immediately and individually, providing finality in central bank money. LBTR has been in operation since 2004, handling high-value transfers including those from financial markets and urgent customer transactions. In recent years BCCh has been upgrading LBTR’s technology and aligning it with international standards (e.g., migrating to ISO 20022 messaging). The system settles the majority of wholesale payments in Chile and serves as the core of the financial plumbing for the economy.

Transbank is Chile’s dominant payment processing network for card transactions, operating since 1989. It serves as a unified platform connecting merchants, banks, and card issuers for both credit and debit card payments. Transbank runs the RedCompra debit card system and processes Visa, MasterCard, and domestic cards at point-of-sale and online [oai_citation:100‡norbr.com]. Merchants use Transbank-provided POS terminals or e-commerce gateways to accept card payments. Transbank handles authorization routing, ensures funds are captured from the card-issuing bank, and guarantees settlement to merchants. It effectively acts as the main card acquirer and switch in Chile’s market, though competition has begun to emerge in recent years. Card usage via Transbank is widespread – payment card transactions account for about an entire year’s worth of GDP in value, similar to TEF’s scale [oai_citation:101‡bis.org]. Transbank’s infrastructure supports high volumes securely and underpins Chile’s shift towards cashless payments.

sistemas.nome: CCAV (Cámara de Compensación de Pagos de Alto Valor)
sistemas.descricao: The CCAV is a deferred net settlement system for large-value payments in Chile, administered by ComBanc S.A., a bank-owned service company. In CCAV, participating banks send high-value payment orders throughout the day, which are netted multilaterally. At end-of-day, each bank has a single net position which is then settled in the LBTR RTGS [oai_citation:88‡bcentral.cl]. This allows liquidity savings by offsetting payments. CCAV handles many of the same transaction types as LBTR (interbank transfers, OTC securities payments, etc.), but through a netting mechanism. It has been operational since the mid-2000s. CCAV is subject to central bank oversight and has continuity arrangements to ensure final settlement via LBTR even if any participant fails to pay in.

TEF is Chile’s fast payment scheme enabling immediate bank-to-bank credit transfers for retail users. Launched in the late 2000s by a private automated clearinghouse, TEF was a pioneering near-instant payment system [oai_citation:91‡bis.org]. When a person makes an electronic funds transfer via online banking, the funds become available to the recipient instantly, 24/7, through TEF. The system is operated by a private company owned by major banks and now includes some non-bank payment service providers [oai_citation:92‡bis.org]. TEF has extremely high usage – in 2023 it processed roughly 2 billion transactions (about 7.5 transactions per person per month) [oai_citation:93‡bis.org], equivalent to around one times Chile’s GDP in value annually [oai_citation:94‡bis.org]. It has greatly facilitated P2P, P2B, and B2B payments by providing a quick, convenient alternative to cash and cheques.
MTN Mobile Money and Orange Money
Regional card payment system

Automated gross settlement system for the Central African CFA franc zone (https://entreprises.societegenerale.cm/fileadmin/user_upload/Cameroun/PDF/2024/CLICOM_T2_2024_VA.pdf#:~:text=%5BPDF%5D%20EXE%20CLICOM%2060X80VA%20,to%20a%20business%20outside%20CEMAC)
sistemas.detalhes: SYGMA (Système de Gros Montants Automatisé) is the real-time gross settlement system operated by BEAC (Central Bank of Central African States) for CEMAC countries, including Cameroon. Established in 2015 to replace a paper-based system (https://entreprises.societegenerale.cm/fileadmin/user_upload/Cameroun/PDF/2024/CLICOM_T2_2024_VA.pdf#:~:text=Cameroun%20entreprises,to%20a%20business%20outside%20CEMAC), SYGMA processes high-value transfers (typically ≥ XAF 100 million) (https://entreprises.societegenerale.cm/fileadmin/user_upload/Cameroun/PDF/2024/CLICOM_T2_2024_VA.pdf#:~:text=%5BPDF%5D%20EXE%20CLICOM%2060X80VA%20,to%20a%20business%20outside%20CEMAC) between banks and BEAC in real time. It ensures immediate settlement in central bank money for interbank transfers, central bank operations, and other urgent payments across Cameroon, Gabon, Chad, etc. All participant institutions maintain accounts at BEAC. Type: RTGS (wholesale, regional). Operated by BEAC.

sistemas.descricao: Automated clearing system for CEMAC retail payments (cheques, EFT)
sistemas.detalhes: SYSTAC (Système de Télécompensation Automatisé en Cemac) is the clearing house for low-value payments in Central Africa. It electronically exchanges and nets interbank transactions like cheques, LVP (low-value payments), and direct debits among banks in each CEMAC country. In Cameroon, banks submit daily files of cheques and transfers to BEAC’s SYSTAC, which then calculates multilateral net positions to settle through SYGMA at day’s end. It significantly sped up clearing – local cheques clear in 2 days. SYSTAC is implemented per country but connected regionally. Type: ACH (multilateral net). Operated by BEAC.

sistemas.descricao: GIMAC (Groupement Interbancaire Monétique de l'Afrique Centrale) is the central African interbank card network analogous to GIM-UEMOA in West Africa. GIMAC interconnects banks and switches in Cameroon and neighbors to allow cross-bank ATM/POS usage. It also launched GIMACPAY, a digital platform for retail payments and mobile money interoperability across CEMAC . GIMACPAY enables instant transfers between member banks and also between different mobile money providers, aiming for region-wide interoperability . Cameroon, being the largest member, has led adoption of GIMAC’s services. Type: Card & instant payment network. Operated by GIMAC (with BEAC oversight).
sistemas.detalhes: GIMAC (Groupement Interbancaire Monétique de l'Afrique Centrale) is the central African interbank card network analogous to GIM-UEMOA in West Africa. GIMAC interconnects banks and switches in Cameroon and neighbors to allow cross-bank ATM/POS usage. It also launched GIMACPAY, a digital platform for retail payments and mobile money interoperability across CEMAC (https://www.paymentcomponents.com/all-about-payments-in-africa/#:~:text=Components%20www,Economic%20and) (https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/SIIPS2023_CaseStudy_CEMAC.pdf#:~:text=,border%20within%20the). GIMACPAY enables instant transfers between member banks and also between different mobile money providers, aiming for region-wide interoperability (https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/SIIPS2023_CaseStudy_CEMAC.pdf#:~:text=,border%20within%20the). Cameroon, being the largest member, has led adoption of GIMAC’s services. Type: Card & instant payment network. Operated by GIMAC (with BEAC oversight).

sistemas.nome: Mobile Money (MTN Mobile Money, Orange Money)
sistemas.descricao: Telco-run mobile wallets for instant P2P transfers, dominant in retail payments
sistemas.detalhes: Cameroon’s two leading mobile operators, MTN and Orange, offer mobile money services that have revolutionized payments. Users can deposit cash at an agent and send money via phone to any other user of the same network instantly, as well as pay bills or buy airtime. These services are fast (SMS/USSD-based) and available to anyone with a mobile phone, no bank account needed. They operate on a closed-loop but are beginning to integrate with banks and the GIMACPAY switch for interoperability. By value, mobile money transactions now rival or exceed bank non-cash transactions. Type: Mobile money (proprietary networks).

sistemas.descricao: Digital portals for paying taxes, utilities, and other bills electronically
sistemas.detalhes: Cameroon’s government and utility companies have introduced e-payment platforms to let citizens pay online or via mobile. For example, the Ministry of Finance’s eTax platform allows businesses to pay taxes through bank transfer or mobile money. Utility firms (electricity, water) partner with mobile money and banks so customers can pay bills digitally. These payments often funnel through aggregators and then through GIMAC or SYSTAC for final settlement to the biller’s bank. Type: Government/utility payment schemes (using existing rails).

sistemas.nome: SYSTAC (Système de Télécompensation de l’Afrique Centrale)
sistemas.descricao: SYSTAC is the ACH system for countries in the CEMAC monetary union (including Cameroon) [oai_citation:114‡paymentcomponents.com]. It provides electronic clearing (télécompensation) of low-value instruments: cheques, interbank electronic transfers, direct debits, etc. Each member country has a national clearing center under SYSTAC, and BEAC oversees the entire system. Payment files are exchanged daily among banks via SYSTAC; net positions are calculated and then settled via SYGMA RTGS at end of cycle. SYSTAC has dramatically sped up retail payment processing in Central Africa since its introduction in the late 2000s, though occasional technical incidents have been noted [oai_citation:115‡beac.int].

SYGMA is the RTGS system operated by BEAC (Bank of Central African States) for Cameroon and five other CEMAC countries [oai_citation:110‡cma.se]. Launched in 2007 as part of a modernization project [oai_citation:111‡cma.se], SYGMA settles high-value transactions (FCFA currency) in real time. All commercial banks in Cameroon connect to SYGMA via BEAC’s network in Yaoundé, and transfers are final and irrevocable. It processes interbank transfers, central bank operations, and time-critical payments across the region.
