SYGMA has significantly reduced the systemic risk in the region; any liquidity issues are addressed via intraday credit from BEAC if needed. The system runs on SWIFT-based infrastructure provided by CMA Small Systems.
Dominant mobile payment platform integrated with e-commerce and lifestyle services
sistemas.detalhes: Operated by Ant Group (Alibaba affiliate), Alipay processes transactions through QR code scanning, NFC, and in-app payments. It supports P2P transfers, bill payments, investments, and international transactions. The system operates as a digital wallet linked to bank accounts or stored value, with real-time processing through China's CNAPS infrastructure. Features include credit scoring (Sesame Credit), mini-programs, and cross-border functionality through partnerships with 250+ global institutions .

sistemas.descricao: Socially integrated payment service within WeChat ecosystem
sistemas.detalhes: Operated by Tencent, this wallet integrates payments into messaging (red envelopes), social sharing, and mini-programs. It processes instant P2P/P2M transactions via QR codes or in-app payments, settling through China's interbank systems. Supports 20+ currencies for international users and links with services like DiDi and JD.com. Operates 24/7 with biometric security and AI-driven fraud detection .

sistemas.descricao: Central bank digital currency for retail payments
sistemas.detalhes: Issued by People's Bank of China (PBOC), e-CNY operates on a two-tier structure: PBOC distributes to commercial banks, which deliver to users via digital wallets. Features programmable smart contracts, offline payments, and tokenization. Integrated into Alipay/WeChat Pay wallets and accepted across 29 cities for transport, healthcare, and government services. Uses controlled anonymity with transaction monitoring .

sistemas.descricao: National backbone for high-value and retail payments
sistemas.detalhes: Operated by PBOC, integrates: 1) HVPS for real-time gross settlement of large-value interbank transfers, 2) BEPS for batched retail payments, and 3) IBPS for instant retail payments supporting mobile wallets. Processes 80% of domestic payments with final settlement in central bank money. Connects to CIPS for cross-border RMB clearing .

sistemas.descricao: Dominant domestic card scheme with global acceptance
sistemas.detalhes: State-owned network processing debit/credit transactions through 8.7 million+ POS terminals. Uses tokenization for mobile payments (UnionPay QuickPass) and integrates with Huawei Pay/Xiaomi Pay. Operates on a four-party model with net daily settlement through CNAPS. Expanding through partnerships with international schemes for dual-branded cards .

sistemas.descricao: Integrated digital prepaid instruments

The e-CNY is a digital version of the renminbi issued by the People’s Bank of China. It is a tokenized currency stored in digital wallets and intended for retail payments. Since pilot launch around 2020-2021, the e-CNY has been tested in dozens of cities. Users can download an official e-CNY wallet or use integrated bank apps to receive and spend digital yuan, even offline. The e-CNY transactions are authorized by PBoC and settle instantly in central bank money. Despite significant infrastructure rollout, adoption remains modest relative to private platforms – by end of 2021, about 261 million individual users had activated wallets, and cumulative transactions were only around ¥87.6 billion (~$13.8 billion) [oai_citation:115‡cbdctracker.hrf.org]. The CBDC aims to complement cash and existing electronic payments, improve financial inclusion, and provide a secure, sovereign digital payment method. Technically, it uses a two-tier architecture: PBoC issues e-CNY to selected commercial banks, which distribute it to users. Transactions use cryptographic protocols but are not anonymous (the central bank can trace balances to prevent illicit use). The e-CNY supports programmability and has features like controlled anonymity for users.

CNAPS (China National Advanced Payment System) is the backbone domestic payment infrastructure run by the People’s Bank of China. The second generation CNAPS (CNAPS2), launched in 2013, integrates both real-time gross settlement for high-value payments and deferred net settlement for low-value/bulk transactions [oai_citation:104‡fintechfutures.com]. It uses the ISO 20022 messaging standard, allowing rich data and Chinese character support. CNAPS2 processes large-value interbank transfers, corporate payments, as well as the clearing of retail payments like checks and electronic credits. It operates on a nationwide basis with hundreds of direct participant banks. CNAPS provides final RMB fund transfers and serves as the settlement backbone for China’s economy.

The IBPS is a real-time retail payment network launched by PBoC to facilitate rapid account-to-account transfers. It enables citizens and businesses to make instant RMB payments through online banking or mobile banking channels, typically for smaller values. IBPS is ISO 20022-based and over 200 banks participate [oai_citation:109‡fintechfutures.com]. It has seen broad adoption as it powers many “fast payment” services in China (such as 24/7 instant bank transfers via smartphone apps). IBPS transactions settle within seconds through centralized clearing at PBoC, making funds immediately available. It complements CNAPS by handling the high-volume, low-value segment in real time.

China UnionPay (CUP) is the country’s dominant card payment scheme, integrating ATM and POS networks of all banks. Founded in 2002, UnionPay issues bank cards (debit, credit, prepaid) through member banks and provides the interbank transaction switching and clearing infrastructure. It’s now the world’s largest card network by total cards and transaction count. Adoption is Very High: virtually every bank account in China comes with a UnionPay-enabled card (over 8 billion UnionPay cards in circulation ). UnionPay cards are accepted at almost all merchants domestically and increasingly abroad (UnionPay is accepted in 180+ countries ). In 2022, UnionPay processed over 247 billion transactions totaling ~¥252 trillion (≈$35 trillion) , underlining the massive scale of card spending in China. UnionPay also offers mobile and QR payments via its QuickPass wallet and integrates with mobile wallets. It operates the clearing of transactions and settlement between merchant acquirers and issuers, typically next-day net settlement through PBOC. UnionPay’s role is systemically important given it handles most domestic retail card payments (though Visa/MasterCard are also present for some international cards, they are minor by comparison). In summary, UnionPay is a backbone scheme enabling cashless payments nationwide, with near-universal adoption by consumers, merchants, and banks, and transaction volumes among the highest globally .

sistemas.nome: Alipay and WeChat Pay (Mobile Wallet Ecosystem)
sistemas.descricao: Alipay (by Ant Group/Alibaba) and WeChat Pay (by Tencent) are ubiquitous mobile wallet services in China, used for a vast array of daily transactions from peer-to-peer transfers to retail purchases. These apps link users’ bank accounts or prepaid balances and generate QR codes to send/receive money instantly. With each platform exceeding 1 billion users and combined transaction value around $40 trillion annually [oai_citation:113‡fintechfutures.com], they form a critical pillar of China’s payment landscape. Technically, Alipay and WeChat Pay operate as closed-loop systems: payments between users or to merchants on the same platform settle within that platform’s accounts, with periodic net settlements to partner banks via clearinghouses like NetsUnion (a PBoC-supervised switch for non-bank payment institutions). Both wallets offer open APIs and have extended into offline POS payments, online e-commerce, and even government services. They rely on tokenized payment credentials and strong user authentication (app PIN or biometric). Though not operated by the central bank, they are regulated and deeply integrated with the banking system.
Online banking payments
Neobank platform
Sistema de Cuentas de Depósito – RTGS system operated by Banco de la República
sistemas.detalhes: The CUD (Cuenta de Depósito) is Colombia’s high-value payments system, providing real-time gross settlement of interbank transfers in Colombian pesos. Managed by the central bank (Banco de la República), CUD is the backbone for large-value and time-critical payments such as interbank loans, government securities settlement, and large corporate payments (https://www.banrep.gov.co/es/sistemas-pago/sistema-cuentas-deposito-cud#:~:text=Rep%C3%BAblica%20www,que%20provee%20a%20las). It settles transactions individually and immediately, eliminating credit risk. Adoption is Very High: all banks and key financial institutions participate and use CUD daily for wholesale transfers and as the final settlement layer for other payment systems. It operates RTGS during business hours and also has an overnight component for multilateral settlement. In 2022, the CUD system processed significant values: for example, it might settle COP 4,000+ trillion annually (including monetary policy operations). It also settles the results of the retail ACH and cheque clearing (CEDEC) each day. CUD’s reliability and continuous operation are crucial; any disruption can affect the entire financial system. The system is fully electronic and has been upgraded to ISO 20022 messaging recently. As of end-2022, Colombia’s RTGS has shown growth in volume aligned with economic activity. For instance, a 2019 figure noted ~2 million CUD transfers that year. In summary, CUD’s adoption by banks is total and it processes essentially all high-value payments in the economy, making it indispensable for financial stability.

sistemas.descricao: Automated clearing house for electronic credits/debits and online payments (PSE)
sistemas.detalhes: ACH Colombia is the national ACH network that processes bulk low-value payments among banks. It clears electronic credit transfers (e.g., payroll, supplier payments), direct debits (automated bill payments), and powers the PSE (Pagos Seguros en Línea) system which is an online bank transfer payment gateway for e-commerce. ACH Colombia is a private company owned by financial institutions, and it operates the interbank clearing and settlement of these transactions, with final settlement at the central bank. Adoption is High: it handles the majority of non-cash retail payments outside of cards. In 2022, ACH Colombia processed 323 million transactions (credits + debits) totaling COP 1671 trillion (https://repositorio.banrep.gov.co/bitstream/handle/20.500.12134/10741/financial-infrastructure-report-2023.pdf#:~:text=During%202022%2C%20ACH,in%20real%20terms%29%20in) – a substantial portion of GDP (https://repositorio.banrep.gov.co/bitstream/handle/20.500.12134/10741/financial-infrastructure-report-2023.pdf#:~:text=During%202022%2C%20ACH,in%20real%20terms%29%20in). This reflects widespread use for salaries, government disbursements, utility payments, and online purchases via PSE. PSE in particular is widely accepted by merchants for e-commerce, allowing customers to pay directly from their bank accounts. ACH volumes have been growing near 10% annually. The ACH operates on a deferred net settlement model, with multiple intraday clearing cycles for electronic transfers, and next-day settlement for PSE transactions. It has extended service to 7x24 for some instant products like Transfiya. Overall, ACH Colombia’s network is critical to the country’s payments, enabling interoperability among 35+ banks and fintechs for everyday transactions, and helping move the economy toward more electronic payments.

sistemas.descricao: Real-time 24/7 mobile payments service by ACH Colombia for interbank transfers
sistemas.detalhes: Transfiya is an immediate funds transfer service launched in 2020 that allows people to send money between bank accounts instantly using a mobile phone number or alias. Operated by ACH Colombia, it’s essentially Colombia’s fast payment scheme, providing 24/7, low-value credit transfers that complete in seconds (https://repositorio.banrep.gov.co/bitstream/handle/20.500.12134/10270/payment-systems-report-2021.pdf#:~:text=Banrep%20repositorio,to%20transfer%20or%20receive). Transfiya is accessible via participating banks’ mobile apps or digital wallets; users can send up to a certain limit (initially COP 2 million per transaction) any time. Adoption is Growing rapidly: by 2024, over 15 million Colombians had registered their phone for Transfiya, reaching about 44% of the banked population (https://www.thisweekinfintech.com/transfiya/#:~:text=) (https://www.thisweekinfintech.com/transfiya/#:~:text=Over%2015%20million%20Colombians%20have,%28Source). Over 30 banks and fintechs have joined the network, including neobanks. Monthly transaction counts are climbing quickly (millions per month). Transfiya significantly enhances financial inclusion and convenience – for example, it’s used for splitting bills, P2P payments, and micro-merchant sales, replacing cash. Settlement occurs through ACH Colombia’s infrastructure in real time, with finality assured by participating institutions’ prefunded accounts. As of 2023, Transfiya was moving relatively small values (average transaction under COP 100k), but its share in total payment volume is expanding. It competes with private wallet networks (like Daviplata/Nequi) but also interlinks with them (many wallets connect to Transfiya rails). In summary, Transfiya is Colombia’s equivalent of an instant payment rail, with fast-growing adoption making it a key component of the retail payment ecosystem going forward.

sistemas.descricao: Pagos Seguros en Línea – national online bank transfer payment gateway
sistemas.detalhes: PSE is an online payment platform developed by ACH Colombia that enables customers to pay merchants directly from their bank accounts. Acting as an intermediary between e-commerce sites and banks, PSE allows real-time debit of a buyer’s bank account and credit to a merchant, with the transaction cleared via ACH. Adoption is High among e-commerce and service providers – over 17,000 merchants accept PSE (https://docs.v3.localpayment.com/request-a-payment/payins/bank-transfer/apms/pse-colombia#:~:text=PSE%20%28Colombia%29%20,make%20a%20transaction%2C%20the) (https://www.yapstone.com/assets/files/YS_Colombia_CG.pdf#:~:text=%5BPDF%5D%20Country%20Guide%20,roughly%20sees%20around%20%245), and it’s accessible to practically all online banking users (~1.8 million active users as of mid-2020s (https://repositorio.banrep.gov.co/bitstream/handle/20.500.12134/10741/financial-infrastructure-report-2023.pdf#:~:text=1.1.2%20ACH,and%20debit%20operations%2C%20for) (https://docs.v3.localpayment.com/request-a-payment/payins/bank-transfer/apms/pse-colombia#:~:text=PSE%20%28Colombia%29%20,make%20a%20transaction%2C%20the)). PSE transactions have grown with Colombia’s digital commerce: as of 2023, PSE volume was around US$14.6 billion annually (https://www.emerchantpay.com/insights/apms-in-focus-pse-colombias-widely-used-bank-transfer-payment-solution/#:~:text=Solution%20www,10%20billion%20in%202022) (https://www.emerchantpay.com/insights/apms-in-focus-pse-colombias-widely-used-bank-transfer-payment-solution/#:~:text=Developed%20by%20ACH%2C%20which%20controls,10%20billion%20in%202022). It’s commonly used for things like airline tickets, utility bill pay on company websites, and government fees. The user experience involves being redirected to one’s bank login to authorize payment (similar to iDEAL in Netherlands). Funds move via ACH net settlement, typically same-day. PSE has contributed to reducing card usage barriers in e-commerce and brings those without credit cards into online shopping. It is secure (using banking credentials, no card data needed) and cost-effective for merchants (lower fees than cards). In Colombia’s payment landscape, PSE is a crucial scheme bridging banks and merchants in the digital economy, complementing card networks and now instant transfers like Transfiya in providing comprehensive electronic payment options.

sistemas.descricao: Popular bank-led mobile wallets offering simplified accounts
sistemas.detalhes: Nequi (owned by Bancolombia) and Daviplata (by Davivienda) are the two largest digital wallet platforms in Colombia. They provide app-based, zero-fee accounts that are easy to open and use, targeting young and unbanked customers. These wallets function as simplified bank accounts with deposit and withdrawal via agents/ATMs, P2P transfers, bill payments, and integration with card networks (Nequi issues a Visa virtual card). Adoption is Very High: together Nequi and Daviplata have over 30 million users (https://www.latamrepublic.com/top-5-neobanks-in-colombia-in-2023/#:~:text=Top%205%20Neobanks%20in%20Colombia,30%20million%20users%20in) (https://www.latamrepublic.com/top-5-neobanks-in-colombia-in-2023/#:~:text=Some%20of%20the%20entities%20that,30%20million%20users%20in), which is a massive portion of the adult population (Colombia’s total adult pop ~36 million). By 2023, Nequi had 13+ million active users (https://iupana.com/2023/08/28/zero-cac-an-inside-look-at-the-success-of-nequi-in-colombia/?lang=en#:~:text=Bancolombia%20spin,7%20million%20total) and Daviplata around 17 million (https://www.muralpay.com/blog/checklist-is-your-colombian-business-ready-for-global-payments#:~:text=Mano%2C%20DaviPlata%20now%20reach%2061,with%20growth%20driven%20by) (https://www.americaeconomia.com/en/business-industries/digital-payments-when-wallet-rules#:~:text=Digital%20payments%3A%20when%20the%20wallet,million%20clients%20with%20balances). These wallets were instrumental in distributing government subsidies during the pandemic, boosting usage. They allow instant transfers between users and also interoperate with the banking system (e.g., via Transfiya). Daviplata and Nequi are among the main drivers of Colombia’s financial inclusion rising to 88%. In terms of volume, each processes tens of millions of transactions monthly, though mostly small values. They are regulated as deposit accounts and covered by deposit insurance up to certain limits. The convenience of opening an account with just a phone and ID has made them extremely popular. Their user base and transaction counts continue to grow, making them a cornerstone of Colombia’s retail payments, especially for low-value everyday transactions and P2P payments, further diminishing reliance on cash.

sistemas.descricao: Cash remains significant; crypto use is niche but growing
sistemas.detalhes: Despite modern digital systems, cash is still widely used in Colombia, particularly for informal and small-value transactions. Over 85% of Colombians made cash payments in the past year, and cash in circulation is around 6% of GDP. However, its share is gradually declining as digital options (cards, transfers, wallets) grow (https://www.nuvei.com/apm/transfiya#:~:text=TransFiYa%20,instant%20payments%20via%20mobile%20devices). The government and fintechs continue efforts to promote digital payments over cash for efficiency and tax purposes. On the other hand, cryptocurrencies have a presence in Colombia but primarily as speculative investment, not mainstream payment rails. No cryptocurrency is legal tender or officially integrated into payment systems. That said, Colombia ranks relatively high in Latin America for crypto adoption (with thousands of merchants accepting Bitcoin via payment processors). The financial regulator has run a sandbox pilot allowing some banks to connect customers to crypto exchanges. Still, crypto’s use in day-to-day commerce is Low. Stablecoins see limited use for cross-border remittances by tech-savvy users. The central bank is in early Research stages of a potential CBDC (as of 2023, considering a digital peso to address tax evasion and money laundering concerns). In summary, cash remains a key payment method especially in rural/informal settings, while crypto rails are nascent and marginal. Both are notable in the context of inclusion: cash for those outside the digital economy, and crypto as an emerging alternative for a small segment.

sistemas.descricao: CEDEC (Compensación Electrónica de Cheques) is the national clearing house for checks in Colombia. Although check usage has declined over the years, CEDEC allows banks to exchange digital images of checks and calculate net balances to settle through the central bank [oai_citation:129‡iconsolutions.com]. Physical cheques are truncated and imaged for clearing. CEDEC operates with daily clearing cycles, and funds from local cheques are usually available within 1-2 business days. The net positions from CEDEC are settled in the CUD at end-of-day. As electronic payments grow, the volume of cheques in CEDEC continues to decrease, but it remains an important service for businesses and individuals who still utilize checks for certain payments.

CUD is the country’s main high-value payment system, providing real-time gross settlement of interbank transfers in Colombian pesos. Operated by Banco de la República, CUD processes urgent and large-value credit transfers (alto valor) and settles the obligations arising from other clearinghouses in Colombia [oai_citation:118‡iconsolutions.com]. Transactions are settled one by one with immediate finality. As of mid-2010s, it had around 140 direct participants including banks and key financial institutions [oai_citation:119‡iconsolutions.com]. CUD also has a USD transaction capability (for certain dollar-settled operations through the central bank). The system is critical for Colombia’s financial stability, handling all major interbank payments and ensuring net settlements from retail systems are completed in central bank money. Currently, CUD operates during business hours, though plans exist to extend operating times. The messaging format is based on SWIFT standards (MT messages) with plans to migrate to ISO 20022 in line with global trends.

Colombia’s card payment infrastructure is served mainly by two networks: Credibanco and Redeban. These are bank-owned companies that act as switches and acquirers for card transactions (Visa through Credibanco, and MasterCard through Redeban, among others). They connect merchants’ point-of-sale terminals with card issuers, enabling authorization and processing of card payments. The networks use international standards (EMV for chip, ISO 8583 for messaging) and settle transactions in COP through the banking system. As of mid-2010s, payment cards have grown substantially; there were ~41 credit cards per 100 adults and even more debit cards [oai_citation:130‡iconsolutions.com]. Card payments (both credit and debit) are common for retail purchases and e-commerce, comprising a significant share of non-cash payments in Colombia. Credibanco and Redeban also provide ATMs switching services. While historically each network handled separate sets of banks, they both offer nationwide coverage and have increasingly overlapping services. In recent years, they have worked on innovations like contactless payments and mobile payment integration. Merchant settlement from card transactions flows via the networks to issuing banks, with net interbank positions settled through the central bank.

ACH Colombia is a privately operated clearinghouse owned by Colombian banks that processes low-value, non-urgent electronic payments. It handles batched credit transfers (e.g., payroll, supplier payments, person-to-person transfers) and direct debits (for bill payments) between financial institutions [oai_citation:122‡iconsolutions.com] [oai_citation:123‡iconsolutions.com]. Transactions are accumulated and cleared in cycles, with final net settlement occurring in the CUD RTGS at the end of each cycle [oai_citation:124‡iconsolutions.com]. ACH Colombia typically offers same-day or next-day availability of funds to beneficiaries (T+0 or T+1) depending on submission time [oai_citation:125‡iconsolutions.com]. It uses a format originally based on NACHA (the US ACH standard) adapted to local needs [oai_citation:126‡iconsolutions.com]. In addition to traditional ACH transfers, ACH Colombia powers online payment services like PSE (Pagos Seguros en Línea), which allows real-time e-commerce payments through bank accounts. More recently, it also introduced an instant payments service called Transfiya that leverages the ACH network for immediate transfers via mobile number aliasing. ACH Colombia is a key component of Colombia’s retail payments, gradually reducing reliance on cash and checks.
Electronic payment system

SINPE Móvil is Costa Rica’s fast payment scheme launched in 2015, allowing 24/7 instant transfers via mobile phone number aliases . It gained traction during COVID-19, now handling about 80% of interbank transfers by volume . By mid-2024 it reached ~3 million users (76% of adults) actively sending small-value payments . In 2023, it processed over 500 million transactions, with CRC 8.6 trillion (~USD 16.5 billion) transferred . The service is free for transfers up to ₡100,000 and has spurred financial inclusion .
sistemas.detalhes: SINPE Móvil is Costa Rica’s fast payment scheme launched in 2015, allowing 24/7 instant transfers via mobile phone number aliases (https://fintechnews.am/costa-rica/52549/fast-payment-system-sinpe-movil-driving-financial-inclusion-efficiency-in-costa-rica/#:~:text=SINPE%20M%C3%B3vil%20is%20a%20FPS,mobile%20phone%20numbers%20as%20aliases) (https://fintechnews.am/costa-rica/52549/fast-payment-system-sinpe-movil-driving-financial-inclusion-efficiency-in-costa-rica/#:~:text=Adoption%20of%20SINPE%20M%C3%B3vil). It gained traction during COVID-19, now handling about 80% of interbank transfers by volume (https://fintechnews.am/costa-rica/52549/fast-payment-system-sinpe-movil-driving-financial-inclusion-efficiency-in-costa-rica/#:~:text=Though%20adoption%20of%20SINPE%20M%C3%B3vil,of%20all%20interbank%20transfers). By mid-2024 it reached ~3 million users (76% of adults) actively sending small-value payments (https://fintechnews.am/costa-rica/52549/fast-payment-system-sinpe-movil-driving-financial-inclusion-efficiency-in-costa-rica/#:~:text=transfers). In 2023, it processed over 500 million transactions, with CRC 8.6 trillion (~USD 16.5 billion) transferred (https://fintechnews.am/costa-rica/52549/fast-payment-system-sinpe-movil-driving-financial-inclusion-efficiency-in-costa-rica/#:~:text=Globally%2C%20SINPE%20M%C3%B3vil%20ranks%20fourth,focused%20transactions). The service is free for transfers up to ₡100,000 and has spurred financial inclusion (https://fintechnews.am/costa-rica/52549/fast-payment-system-sinpe-movil-driving-financial-inclusion-efficiency-in-costa-rica/#:~:text=In%20Costa%20Rica%2C%20SINPE%20M%C3%B3vil,active%20user%20in%20SINPE%20M%C3%B3vil).

sistemas.descricao: Costa Rica’s central electronic payment system connecting all banks
sistemas.detalhes: SINPE is a centralized digital payments platform operated by the Central Bank of Costa Rica, launched in 1997. It links financial institutions and enables real-time interbank transfers, check clearing, direct debits, and other services (https://www.bccr.fi.cr/en/payments-system/general-information#:~:text=National%20System%20of%20Electronic%20Payments) (https://www.bccr.fi.cr/en/payments-system/general-information#:~:text=This%20technological%20platform%20was%20launched,significant%20means%20of%20money%20movements). Over 90% of Costa Rica’s adult population uses SINPE for electronic payments (https://www.imfconnect.org/content/imf/en/annual-meetings/calendar/open/2024/10/23/188896.html?calendarCategory=UHJlc3M=#:~:text=climate,iv%29%20foster%20financial), reflecting very high adoption. It has over 30 integrated services, helping reduce cash usage and transaction costs in the economy (https://www.imfconnect.org/content/imf/en/annual-meetings/calendar/open/2024/10/23/188896.html?calendarCategory=UHJlc3M=#:~:text=,payments%20due%20to%20inoperability%20challenges).

sistemas.descricao: Contactless open-loop fare payment system for public transport
sistemas.detalhes: SINPE-TP is an electronic fare collection system initiated in 2022 by the central bank for buses and trains (https://littlepay.com/resource-hub/blog/articles/littlepay-announces-its-participation-in-costa-ricas-national-electronic-payment-system-for-public-transportation-sinpe-tp/#:~:text=Today%2C%20Littlepay%20has%20announced%20it,Payment%20System%20for%20Public%20Transportation) (https://littlepay.com/resource-hub/blog/articles/littlepay-announces-its-participation-in-costa-ricas-national-electronic-payment-system-for-public-transportation-sinpe-tp/#:~:text=SINPE,matter%20the%20route%20or%20operator). It enables riders to pay fares directly with contactless bank cards or mobile wallets, using an interoperable, multimodal platform. The system is being rolled out nationwide (targeting 5,000 buses) and is projected to handle up to 600 million fare payments per year at full deployment (https://littlepay.com/resource-hub/blog/articles/littlepay-announces-its-participation-in-costa-ricas-national-electronic-payment-system-for-public-transportation-sinpe-tp/#:~:text=their%20fares%2C%20no%20matter%20the,route%20or%20operator). This initiative leverages Costa Rica’s high contactless card penetration (98% of cards) to reduce cash in transit and improve efficiency (https://littlepay.com/resource-hub/blog/articles/littlepay-announces-its-participation-in-costa-ricas-national-electronic-payment-system-for-public-transportation-sinpe-tp/#:~:text=Since%202015%2C%20the%20BCCR%2C%20card,all%20card%20transactions%20were%20contactless).

sistemas.descricao: Widely used debit and credit cards with high contactless adoption
sistemas.detalhes: International card schemes like Visa, Mastercard and American Express are extensively used in Costa Rica for retail payments. There are around 8.4 million payment cards in circulation (6.0 m debit, 2.4 m credit) in a population of ~5 million (https://one.oecd.org/document/DAF/COMP/LACF(2021)8/en/pdf#:~:text=country%20was%208,5%20debit). Nearly all cards (98%) are contactless-enabled, and by 2021 about 77% of card transactions were contactless (https://littlepay.com/resource-hub/blog/articles/littlepay-announces-its-participation-in-costa-ricas-national-electronic-payment-system-for-public-transportation-sinpe-tp/#:~:text=Since%202015%2C%20the%20BCCR%2C%20card,all%20card%20transactions%20were%20contactless), making Costa Rica a Latin American leader in tap-to-pay adoption. Card payments are processed via banks and international networks, and accounted for significant payment volume alongside bank transfers (https://www.bccr.fi.cr/en/payments-system/sinpe-service-statistics#:~:text=In%202012%C2%A0%20the%20amount%20of,according%20to%20the%20following%20criteria) (https://littlepay.com/resource-hub/blog/articles/littlepay-announces-its-participation-in-costa-ricas-national-electronic-payment-system-for-public-transportation-sinpe-tp/#:~:text=Since%202015%2C%20the%20BCCR%2C%20card,all%20card%20transactions%20were%20contactless).

sistemas.descricao: Pagos Inmediatos is an instant payment service that allows bank customers to transfer funds in real-time to any other bank account within Costa Rica [oai_citation:7‡bccr.fi.cr]. Introduced in March 2000, it provides 24/7 availability (subject to each bank’s channels) and credits the beneficiary within seconds after initiation [oai_citation:8‡bccr.fi.cr] [oai_citation:9‡bccr.fi.cr]. This service is used for urgent payments where speed is critical, complementing the scheduled direct credit (ACH) system [oai_citation:10‡bccr.fi.cr]. Transactions are processed individually and settled immediately through SINPE, with the Central Bank ensuring finality. PIN transactions have a transaction limit (often for retail transfers) and may incur fees set by each bank [oai_citation:11‡bccr.fi.cr].

Launched in 1997 by the Central Bank of Costa Rica, SINPE processes high-value and low-value payments either in real time or deferred net batches [oai_citation:1‡bis.org]. It began with nationwide cheque clearing, and expanded to interbank transfers, direct debits/credits, and other services [oai_citation:2‡bis.org] [oai_citation:3‡bccr.fi.cr]. SINPE links banks, financial institutions and public entities via a private network, enabling customers to transfer funds between accounts at different institutions. It supports all payment use cases (P2P, P2B, B2B, government payments, etc.) under a single infrastructure [oai_citation:4‡bis.org]. The Central Bank operates SINPE and provides final settlement for participating institutions.

Transfermóvil is a mobile application launched by ETECSA (the state telecom) in partnership with Cuban banks to enable a range of digital financial services. Via Transfermóvil, users can perform bank transactions such as transferring funds between their own accounts or to others within the same bank, paying utility bills, recharging mobile phones, and paying for government services – all from a smartphone. The app, introduced in 2018, works by securely connecting to the user’s bank (using their credentials) and issuing payment instructions. While initially limited to on-net (intrabank) transfers, it has expanded to support interbank transfers as well. In 2023, new features like QR code payments were added [oai_citation:46‡periodicocubano.com] to simplify merchant transactions. Transfermóvil has been key to Cuba’s “bancarización” push (reducing cash usage), and as of 2023, it offered incentives (like fee discounts and tax benefits) to encourage online payments [oai_citation:47‡horizontecubano.law.columbia.edu]. The platform is tied to the centralized national switch, so transactions ultimately clear through the banking system’s networks (e.g., Red or interbank arrangements) after being initiated on the app.
sistemas.detalhes: Transfermóvil is a mobile money application launched in 2015 by Cuba’s telecom company (ETECSA) in partnership with state banks. It uses USSD/SMS to allow users to pay utility bills, transfer funds between bank accounts, top-up mobile phones, and more from a basic cellphone. By mid-2023, Transfermóvil had about 4.3 million active users – roughly 75% of Cuban adults – and processed 785 million transactions in 2022 (https://www.granma.cu/cuba/2023-08-14/transfermovil-y-enzona-un-camino-seguro-en-la-bancarizacion-14-08-2023-18-08-11#:~:text=Ambos%20mecanismos%20agrupan%20a%20m%C3%A1s,Xetid%29%2C%20respectivamente) (https://www.granma.cu/cuba/2023-08-14/transfermovil-y-enzona-un-camino-seguro-en-la-bancarizacion-14-08-2023-18-08-11#:~:text=Alrededor%20de%204%2C3%20millones%20de,de%2060%20servicios%20y%20funcionalidades). The service operates 24/7 with near 100% uptime (https://www.granma.cu/cuba/2023-08-14/transfermovil-y-enzona-un-camino-seguro-en-la-bancarizacion-14-08-2023-18-08-11#:~:text=Alrededor%20de%204%2C3%20millones%20de,de%2060%20servicios%20y%20funcionalidades). It was pivotal during the pandemic, driving a huge shift away from cash. With Transfermóvil, Cubans can conduct banking remotely, although usage is limited to those with bank accounts and mobile access.

sistemas.descricao: Prepaid FX cards
Real-time gross settlement system for interbank transfers in CUP
sistemas.detalhes: Cuba’s central bank has developed a **Liquidación Bruta en Tiempo Real (LBTR)** system to modernize interbank settlements (https://www.bc.gob.cu/sistema-de-pago#:~:text=Los%20principios%20fundamentales%20de%20este,sistema%20son%20los%20siguientes). Implemented in the early 2000s, it allows real-time electronic fund transfers between banks in Cuban pesos (and US dollars for certain operations) (https://www.bc.gob.cu/sistema-de-pago#:~:text=los%20subsistemas%20que%20se%20requieran,nacional%20y%20en%20d%C3%B3lares%20estadounidenses). All commercial banks hold accounts at the central bank for this RTGS. The system ensures immediate, irrevocable settlement of payments, improving efficiency and reducing systemic risk. However, Cuba’s telecom infrastructure has constrained full deployment, and as of late 2010s the RTGS was still being gradually introduced (there was historically no full RTGS in operation) (https://www.agpaytech.co.uk/pdf/rtgs.pdf#:~:text=%5BPDF%5D%20RTGS%20IN%20AFRICA%20,and%20National%20Bank%20of). The LBTR is central to Cuba’s National Payment System strategy.

sistemas.descricao: Domestic debit card network and ATM switching system
sistemas.detalhes: Servicios de Pago RED S.A. is the Cuban entity managing the national ATM and debit card network (the RED system) (https://www.bc.gob.cu/institucion/nobancaria/12#:~:text=El%20Banco%20Central%20de%20Cuba%2C,espec%C3%ADfica%20mediante%20la%20Resoluci%C3%B3n%2069%2F2011) (https://www.bc.gob.cu/institucion/nobancaria/12#:~:text=REDSA%20est%C3%A1%20facultada%20a%20ejercer,las%20siguientes%20actividades). Established in 2010 under the central bank’s authorization, RED S.A. operates all ATMs in Cuba and processes **Tarjeta RED** debit card transactions, as well as international card transactions at Cuban ATMs (https://www.bc.gob.cu/institucion/nobancaria/12#:~:text=El%20Banco%20Central%20de%20Cuba%2C,espec%C3%ADfica%20mediante%20la%20Resoluci%C3%B3n%2069%2F2011) (https://www.bc.gob.cu/institucion/nobancaria/12#:~:text=,RED%20a%20los%20bancos%20emisores). It handles interbank settlement of ATM withdrawals and purchases, and personalizes cards for member banks (https://www.bc.gob.cu/institucion/nobancaria/12#:~:text=REDSA%20est%C3%A1%20facultada%20a%20ejercer,las%20siguientes%20actividades) (https://www.bc.gob.cu/institucion/nobancaria/12#:~:text=nacionales.%20,emisores%2C%20con%20sus%20respectivos%20pines). The RED debit card is used for salary payments, pensions, and cash withdrawals. Adoption is high – as of 2021 Cuban banks had issued over 15 million magnetic cards (https://www.granma.cu/cuba/2023-08-14/transfermovil-y-enzona-un-camino-seguro-en-la-bancarizacion-14-08-2023-18-08-11#:~:text=%C2%BFCu%C3%A1nto%20pueden%20aportar%20las%20pasarelas,15%20millones%20de%20tarjetas%20bancarias). However, due to U.S. sanctions, global cards (Visa/Mastercard) issued outside Cuba generally do not work, though Cuba has started accepting UnionPay and MIR cards for foreign visitors.

sistemas.descricao: EnZona is a fintech platform developed by the Cuban company Xetid that functions as a digital wallet, allowing users to make peer-to-peer transfers, online purchases, and pay merchants electronically [oai_citation:48‡directoriocubano.info]. Launched in 2019, EnZona links to users’ bank accounts or cards and enables payments via a mobile app or web portal. It supports QR code payments in stores, e-commerce transactions, and person-to-person payments without cash. The platform experienced explosive early growth – operations via EnZona grew by 2,399% from 2019 to 2020 [oai_citation:49‡cashessentials.org] – as it filled gaps in e-commerce and provided an alternative to cash amid economic reforms. EnZona transactions are processed through Cuba’s banking network (it acts as an overlay service), and it requires users to have accounts at participating banks. The government has been promoting EnZona as part of its digital payments initiative, and many state agencies and retailers now accept EnZona payments. Security is handled through encryption and user authentication in the app.
sistemas.detalhes: EnZona is a Cuban electronic payments platform (launched in 2019) that functions as a wallet and marketplace. Developed by Xetid (a state IT company), EnZona allows individuals and businesses to make and accept payments via mobile app or web – including peer-to-peer transfers, online purchases, bill payments, and even government fee payments. By mid-2023, EnZona had about 0.8 million registered users and handled ~40 million transactions annually (https://www.granma.cu/cuba/2023-08-14/transfermovil-y-enzona-un-camino-seguro-en-la-bancarizacion-14-08-2023-18-08-11#:~:text=Ambos%20mecanismos%20agrupan%20a%20m%C3%A1s,Xetid%29%2C%20respectivamente) (https://www.granma.cu/cuba/2023-08-14/transfermovil-y-enzona-un-camino-seguro-en-la-bancarizacion-14-08-2023-18-08-11#:~:text=,102%20862%20pagos%20a%20servicios). Users can link their bank accounts or Tarjeta RED cards to the app. While smaller in scale than Transfermóvil, EnZona has been growing as Cuba pushes for digital commerce and aims to reduce reliance on cash.

sistemas.descricao: “Red” is the domestic interbank card switch and ATM network in Cuba. Expanded in the early 2000s as part of payments modernization, by end-2001 Cuba had over 100 ATMs under the Red brand and ~550,000 magnetic stripe cards issued [oai_citation:44‡bc.gob.cu]. The network links ATMs and POS terminals across the country, allowing holders of cards issued by Cuban banks (e.g., debit cards tied to CUP accounts) to withdraw cash, check balances, and make payments at retailers. Red provides interbank clearing of card transactions and routes authorization requests to the issuing bank. Given Cuba’s limited connectivity to international card schemes, Red serves as a critical domestic card processing infrastructure. It is operated centrally (reporting to the central bank) and ensures that transactions between different banks’ cards and merchants are settled securely through the central bank. In recent years, Red also supports chip cards and has been adding support for new use cases like payroll and social security disbursements via cards [oai_citation:45‡bc.gob.cu].

sistemas.nome: SLBTR (Sistema de Liquidación Bruta en Tiempo Real)
sistemas.descricao: The SLBTR is an RTGS operated by the Central Bank of Cuba, providing instant final settlement for large-value and urgent payments. After years of planning, it was implemented around 2010 to modernize Cuba’s payment infrastructure [oai_citation:38‡bc.gob.cu]. The system processes high-value transfers between banks in real time, in both Cuban pesos (CUP) and convertible currency (USD) [oai_citation:39‡bc.gob.cu] [oai_citation:40‡bc.gob.cu]. Communications run over a private interbank network; each participant bank connects via a secure node. Transactions are sent as standardized electronic messages and are cryptographically signed for authenticity and integrity. Upon receipt at the central processor, funds are debited and credited across the banks’ settlement accounts instantly (if sufficient balance) with immediate irrevocability. Unfunded payments queue until funds are available, then execute, otherwise they are rejected by end-of-day. The SLBTR greatly reduced payment delays and settlement risk in Cuba’s banking system.
National payment network
Mobile money service
High-value real-time gross settlement system of Banco de Cabo Verde
sistemas.detalhes: The Sistema de Gestão de Depósitos e Liquidação (SGDL) is Cape Verde’s RTGS system for large-value interbank payments in escudos. Operated by the central bank (Banco de Cabo Verde), it provides immediate gross settlement of transfers between banks in central bank money (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=smooth%20functioning%20of%20clearing%20and,in%20central%20bank%20money%2C%20it) (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=amount%20%280.1,of). SGDL settles high-value and time-critical payments, including money market and government securities transactions. It also settles the net results of retail clearing systems (ACH and card networks) at day-end (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=respectively%29%20and%20value%20%2812.4,systems%2C%20as%20well%20as%20the) (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=having%20settled%20a%20total%20of,365%20days%20in%20both%20years). Adoption is High among the banking sector, as all banks use SGDL for wholesale transfers and final settlement. While it accounts for only ~0.1% of transaction volume, it carries ~97% of the total value exchanged in the national payments system (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=of%20settled%20transactions,of) (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=amount%20%280.1,of). For example, in 2019 SGDL processed a daily average of CVE 37 billion in gross settlements (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=volume%20%2812.1,7%20transactions%2C%20worth) (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=from%2099%2C548,in%20volume%20and). SGDL is a core infrastructure ensuring financial stability in Cape Verde’s economy.

sistemas.descricao: Integrated interbank clearing house for retail payments (cheques, EFT, etc.)
sistemas.detalhes: Cape Verde’s Sistema Integrado de Compensação e Liquidação Interbancária (SICIL) is the integrated clearing house for retail payment instruments. Under SICIL, the central bank and SISP (Sociedade Interbancária e Sistemas de Pagamentos) operate several subsystems: (i) Cheque Clearing for paper checks, (ii) Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) clearing for credit transfers and direct debits, and (iii) others (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=financial%20settlement%20of%20all%20transactions,ii%29%20Electronic%20Funds%20Transfer) (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=in%20the%20interbank%20transfer%20and,prominent%20position%20in%20terms%20of). These systems aggregate low-value transactions from all banks and compute multilateral net positions, which are settled in SGDL at end of day (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=respectively%29%20and%20value%20%2812.4,systems%2C%20as%20well%20as%20the) (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=having%20settled%20a%20total%20of,365%20days%20in%20both%20years). Adoption is High among banks for retail payments – in 2019, the check+EFT clearing systems processed 80.6% of total payment value in the country (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=match%20at%20L2291%20Systems%20that,and%2012.3) (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=As%20for%20the%20amounts%20processed%2C,Note%20that%2C%20in%20terms%20of). However, in terms of number of transactions, electronic payments dominate: nearly all non-cash consumer payments (salaries, bill payments, etc.) flow through SICIL. For example, the interbank EFT subsystem cleared CVE 158.7717 billion in 2019 (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=having%20settled%20a%20total%20of,365%20days%20in%20both%20years) (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=processed%2C%20the%20interbank%20transfer%20clearing,of%20the%20total%20value). The SICIL infrastructure is vital for efficient batched clearing of everyday transactions in Cape Verde.

sistemas.descricao: National interbank debit card network and ATM/POS system (managed by SISP)
sistemas.detalhes: Vinti4 ("24" in Cape Verdean Creole) is Cape Verde’s national card payment network, operated by SISP (Interbank and Payment Systems Company). It links banks, ATMs, and point-of-sale terminals, allowing debit/ATM cards issued by any Cape Verdean bank to be used across all ATMs and merchants domestically (https://gfrid.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/2022-09-27_Diagnostic_CaboVerde_W_FINAL.pdf#:~:text=%28SISP%29%20is%20a%20shared%20inter,by%20banks%20that%20ensures) (https://www.bcv.cv/en/SistemadePagamentos/CompensacaoInterbancaria/Paginas/CompensacaoInterbancariaeLiquidacaoSICIL.aspx#:~:text=,SISP). Vinti4 provides 24/7 card authorization and clearing services. It is the primary non-cash retail payment scheme in the country, widely used for withdrawals and in-store payments. Adoption is Medium-High among the banked population: in 2019, the Vinti4 network handled ~27 million transactions (96% of all payment transaction volume) (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=In%202019%2C%20the%20vinti4%20network,systems%2C%20as%20well%20as%20the) (https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2021/Cabo%20Verde%27s%20Payment%20System%20Report%202019.pdf#:~:text=having%20settled%20a%20total%20of,365%20days%20in%20both%20years), though cash still remains prevalent for small vendors (https://www.transfi.com/blog/popular-local-payment-methods-and-solutions-in-cape-verde#:~:text=match%20at%20L325%20Cash%20is,you%20use%20the%20local%20currency) (https://www.transfi.com/blog/popular-local-payment-methods-and-solutions-in-cape-verde#:~:text=Cash%20is%20the%20majority%20choice,you%20use%20the%20local%20currency). The network supports debit cards (often co-branded with Visa/Mastercard for international use) and has deployed over 10,000 POS terminals and many ATMs (https://www.caixa.cv/financial-education/20?l=en#:~:text=POS%20System%20in%20business%3A%20Is,branches%20of%20activity%2C%20with). Vinti4 transactions are cleared by SISP and settled in central bank money daily. The network’s introduction has greatly modernized Cape Verde’s retail payments, providing convenient electronic access to funds nationwide.

sistemas.descricao: Digital wallet and remittance app (first mobile money service in Cabo Verde)
sistemas.detalhes: Makeba is a fintech mobile money platform launched in 2018 as Cape Verde’s first digital wallet service. Available via smartphone app, Makeba allows users to hold an e-wallet, send and receive money domestically or internationally (targeting remittances), pay merchants, and pay bills all electronically (https://insidetelecom.com/the-new-african-fintech-startup-makeba-secures-200000-through-a-crowdfunding-campaign/#:~:text=Until%20September%201%2C%202020%2C%2095,9%20million%20subscribers%20and%20%241) (https://insidetelecom.com/the-new-african-fintech-startup-makeba-secures-200000-through-a-crowdfunding-campaign/#:~:text=the%20Wefunder%20platform,%E2%80%9CHaving%20no%20costly%20payment). It operates in partnership with the government (used for university fee payments and pension disbursements) (https://www.paymentsdive.com/ex/mpt/news/african-fintech-startup-makeba-exceeds-crowdfunding-goal/#:~:text=ahead%20to%20deploy%20in%20its,market%20of%20Cape%20Verde%2C%20Africa) (https://www.paymentsdive.com/ex/mpt/news/african-fintech-startup-makeba-exceeds-crowdfunding-goal/#:~:text=Makeba%20has%20also%20entered%20into,the%20Cape%20Verdean%20Public%20University). Makeba accounts are tied to users’ phones and can be topped up from bank accounts or cash-in points. Adoption is Low but growing – as of 2020 Makeba had about 3,200 users in Cape Verde (https://insidetelecom.com/the-new-african-fintech-startup-makeba-secures-200000-through-a-crowdfunding-campaign/#:~:text=Until%20September%201%2C%202020%2C%2095,9%20million%20subscribers%20and%20%241) (https://insidetelecom.com/the-new-african-fintech-startup-makeba-secures-200000-through-a-crowdfunding-campaign/#:~:text=the%20Wefunder%20platform,%E2%80%9CHaving%20no%20costly%20payment), a small share of the population. It is in a growth phase, aiming to drive financial inclusion and cheaper remittances for the unbanked. While volumes are currently modest, Makeba represents a new digital payment rail in Cape Verde, pioneering mobile wallet usage where previously most transactions were via cash or cards. It is effectively in a pilot/early growth stage, supported by crowdfunding and partnerships.

sistemas.nome: SICIL (Sistema Integrado de Compensação Interbancária e Liquidação)
sistemas.descricao: SICIL is Cape Verde’s integrated interbank clearing system for retail payments. Established in 1995 [oai_citation:25‡bcv.cv], it includes three subsystems: one for cheque clearing, one for electronic credit transfers, and one for transactions via the “vinti4” card network [oai_citation:26‡bcv.cv]. The central bank (BCV) manages SICIL and delegates daily operations to SISP (Sociedade Interbancária e Sistemas de Pagamento). Throughout the day, banks send payment transaction files over SISP’s network; at scheduled intervals, SICIL computes multilateral net positions. The net balances are then settled in the SGDL RTGS at BCV [oai_citation:27‡bcv.cv]. SICIL greatly sped up retail payment clearing, reducing systemic risk for low-value transactions.

Vinti4 is Cape Verde’s national interbank card network, launched in 1999 to facilitate electronic payments by card [oai_citation:30‡bcv.cv]. Managed by SISP, the Vinti4 network links all banks’ ATMs and point-of-sale terminals, enabling holders of a Vinti4 debit card to withdraw cash or make purchases throughout the country. It operates 24/7, handling card authorization and switching domestically. The network has grown to hundreds of ATMs and thousands of POS devices, and has issued hundreds of thousands of cards. It significantly modernized retail payments by reducing reliance on cash.

sistemas.nome: SGDL (Sistema de Gestão de Depósitos e Liquidação)
sistemas.descricao: The SGDL is the RTGS in Cape Verde’s national payment system, operated by the central bank (BCV). It settles high-value payments and the net positions from retail clearing in real time on the books of the BCV. SGDL ensures final, irrevocable settlement of interbank transfers in Cabo Verdean escudos. It interfaces with clearing subsystems to credit or debit banks’ accounts for large-value and time-critical transactions.
Payment gateway
Neobank adoption
Real-time gross settlement system for large-value euro payments
sistemas.detalhes: As a Eurosystem member, Cyprus conducts large-value interbank settlements via TARGET2-CY, the national component of TARGET2 (now consolidated into T2). This RTGS system settles euro transactions in central bank money, providing real-time, irrevocable settlement for high-value transfers and securities settlement payments. TARGET2-CY replaced Cyprus’s legacy RTGS upon euro adoption in 2008. The Central Bank of Cyprus operates TARGET2-CY and designates it as systemically important (https://www.centralbank.cy/en/financial-market-infrastructures-payments/financial-market-infrastructures-policy-oversight/classification-of-payment-systems#:~:text=The%20CBC%2C%20acting%20as%20the,ESMA). All Cypriot banks participate (often through ECB infrastructure), so adoption is total. It processes thousands of transactions daily, forming the backbone of wholesale payments.

sistemas.descricao: Cheque clearing system operated by the Central Bank of Cyprus
sistemas.detalhes: The Cyprus Clearing House handles the clearing of paper cheques and other deferred transfers between banks. Despite declining cheque usage, CCH remains an important retail payment mechanism by value – cheques made up about 8% of payment value in Cyprus as of H2 2023 (https://cyprus-mail.com/2024/08/02/cyprus-sees-e129-billion-in-cashless-transactions-in-second-half-of-2023#:~:text=The%20CBC%20also%20reported%20that,popular%20payment%20method%20in%20Cyprus) (https://cyprus-mail.com/2024/08/02/cyprus-sees-e129-billion-in-cashless-transactions-in-second-half-of-2023#:~:text=Cheques%20were%20the%20second%20most,presence%20in%20the%20domestic%20market). Banks exchange cheque images and settlement positions through the Clearing House for next-day settlement in central bank money. The system is classified as an "Other Retail Payment System" under oversight (non-systemically important) (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/paym/pol/systems/html/index.da.html#:~:text=JCC%20Payment%20Card%20System%20) (https://www.centralbank.cy/en/financial-market-infrastructures-payments/financial-market-infrastructures-policy-oversight/classification-of-payment-systems#:~:text=Framework%20for%20Retail%20Payment%20Systems,eu%20%20%28OFRPS). Adoption among businesses and consumers is moderate and gradually decreasing as digital alternatives grow, but the infrastructure ensures efficient nationwide cheque processing.

sistemas.descricao: The CY-SDD system is a retail payment system dedicated to direct debit collections in euro, launched in 2014 to facilitate migration to the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) [oai_citation:57‡centralbank.cy]. It allows creditors (billers) to pull payments from customers’ accounts via SEPA Core Direct Debits. Banks submit direct debit files which are cleared multilaterally. Settlement of the net results occurs in TARGET2-CY on the same day [oai_citation:58‡centralbank.cy]. The CY-SDD Payment System is interoperable with Deutsche Bundesbank’s RPS SEPA Clearer for facilitating cross-border SDDs [oai_citation:59‡centralbank.cy]. This interoperability ensures that Cyprus-originating direct debits can reach banks across SEPA. The system follows the SEPA Rulebook standards and formats (ISO 20022 pain messages for initiation, pacs for interbank). The Central Bank of Cyprus oversees CY-SDD operations. The system has enabled utilities, telecoms, and other recurring billers in Cyprus to collect payments efficiently under SEPA.
sistemas.detalhes: The Cyprus SEPA Direct Debit system allows automated recurring payments in euro – such as utility bills, subscriptions, and loan payments – to be pulled from customers’ bank accounts with consent. It operates under the SEPA Core Direct Debit rules and is overseen by the Central Bank as an "Other Retail Payment System" (https://www.centralbank.cy/en/financial-market-infrastructures-payments/financial-market-infrastructures-policy-oversight/classification-of-payment-systems#:~:text=Framework%20for%20Retail%20Payment%20Systems,eu%20%20%28OFRPS). Launched after Cyprus joined SEPA, CY-SDD enables both domestic and cross-border euro direct debits. While not heavily used by consumers historically, adoption is increasing as more companies offer SEPA direct debit for bill payment convenience. All banks in Cyprus participate, and transactions clear via European clearinghouses connected to this scheme.

sistemas.descricao: Domestic card payment processing network (debit/credit)
sistemas.detalhes: JCC Payment Systems is the primary card payments processor in Cyprus. It serves as a national card switch and acquirer, processing transactions for Visa, Mastercard, and local debit cards across merchants and ATMs. JCC connects all banks and handles clearing and settlement of card payments. The system is considered a prominently important retail payment system by the central bank (https://www.centralbank.cy/en/financial-market-infrastructures-payments/financial-market-infrastructures-policy-oversight/classification-of-payment-systems#:~:text=Framework%20for%20Retail%20Payment%20Systems,eu%20%20%28OFRPS). Card usage in Cyprus is high – on average, every Dane makes more than one card payment a day, and we shop on the Internet to a much larger extent than most other Europeans. (https://www.nationalbanken.dk/en/what-we-do/safe-and-efficient-payments/payment-habits-in-denmark#:~:text=recent%20survey%20by%20Danmarks%20Nationalbank,extent%20than%20most%20other%20Europeans). In H2 2023, there were 111 million card payment transactions in Cyprus (18% higher than the previous year) (https://cyprus-mail.com/2024/08/02/cyprus-sees-e129-billion-in-cashless-transactions-in-second-half-of-2023#:~:text=4%20per%20cent%20to%208,the%20same%20period%20in%202022), with values around €7 billion (https://cyprus-mail.com/2024/08/02/cyprus-sees-e129-billion-in-cashless-transactions-in-second-half-of-2023#:~:text=Moreover%2C%20the%20value%20of%20card,remained%20unchanged%20at%20%E2%82%AC11%20billion). Nearly all POS terminals support EMV and contactless payments, and JCC also provides the “JCCSmart” online bill-pay portal.

sistemas.descricao: JCC Payment Systems Ltd operates the country’s main card payments processing system [oai_citation:60‡centralbank.cy]. Established in 1989 as a consortium of major banks [oai_citation:61‡talentteam.com.cy], JCC acts as the card acquirer and processor for domestic debit/credit card transactions. It authorizes, clears, and settles transactions made with cards issued under international schemes (Visa, Mastercard, Diners, etc.) at local merchants [oai_citation:62‡centralbank.cy]. JCC routes authorization requests to issuing banks and performs end-of-day net settlement of card transactions between acquiring and issuing banks. Settlement obligations in euro are settled via the central bank. JCC also provides ATMs and point-of-sale connectivity and services like the JCCSmart online bill pay portal. The system enforces EMV standards (since mid-2010s) and complies with PCI security standards. By centralizing card clearing, JCC has enabled widespread card acceptance in Cyprus and efficient processing of millions of card payments annually.

The Cyprus Clearing House (CCH) processes domestic cheques in euro. In operation since 1964 [oai_citation:53‡centralbank.cy], it provides an interbank clearing mechanism for paper cheques. Banks exchange digital cheque images and data through an Electronic Cheque Clearing System (ECCS), which conducts daily clearing sessions [oai_citation:54‡centralbank.cy]. All banks in Cyprus participate via a Plenary governance structure [oai_citation:55‡centralbank.cy]. During each clearing cycle, cheques deposited at banks are imaged, data is transmitted electronically, and net positions for each bank are calculated. Final settlement of the net debit/credit positions takes place in TARGET2-CY at end-of-day [oai_citation:56‡centralbank.cy]. The CCH is the sole local cheque clearing arrangement in Cyprus and is governed by the Bills of Exchange law. Usage of cheques has been declining, but the system remains in place for legacy and consumer preference reasons. The Central Bank chairs the CCH committee and ensures smooth operation.

Since adopting the euro in 2008, Cyprus uses the pan-European TARGET2 system for large-value and urgent interbank payments. The Central Bank of Cyprus operates a national component (TARGET2-CY) that connects Cypriot banks to TARGET2’s single shared platform [oai_citation:51‡centralbank.cy]. TARGET2-CY settles euro transactions in real time with immediate finality, primarily handling interbank transfers, corporate treasury payments, and settlement of other systems (like cheque clearing net totals). In March 2023, TARGET2 was upgraded to a new T2 system with ISO 20022 messaging [oai_citation:52‡centralbank.cy]. Cypriot banks maintain accounts on TARGET2-CY for central bank money settlement. The system is available on all TARGET operating days and observes the standard Eurosystem schedule and holidays. Oversight is by the ECB/Eurosystem. TARGET2-CY ensures that high-value payments in Cyprus (now in euro) are processed securely and efficiently alongside other Eurozone countries.
Real-time settlement
BNPL service
Central Electronic Register for Interbank Settlements – RTGS system
sistemas.detalhes: CERTIS is the Czech National Bank’s RTGS system that processes all interbank payments in Czech Koruna (https://www.bis.org/publ/bppdf/bispap123_g.pdf#:~:text=The%20only%20system%20for%20interbank,stems%20from%20the%20fact). Operating since 1992, CERTIS settles high-value and retail payments in real-time on a gross basis (https://www.cnb.cz/en/payments/certis/certis-the-interbank-payment-system-description/#:~:text=Directive%20on%C2%A0settlement%20finality%20in%20payment,the%20Central%20Securities%20Depository%20Prague) (https://rutlandfx.com/what-is-certis/#:~:text=CERTIS%2C%20short%20for%20the%20Czech,The). It handles an enormous volume (about 3.6 million transactions daily, ~910 million in 2023) with values around CZK 329 trillion annually (https://rutlandfx.com/what-is-certis/#:~:text=CERTIS%2C%20short%20for%20the%20Czech,value%20of%20CZK%201%2C318%20billion). All banks and credit unions in Czechia participate directly, making adoption universal. CERTIS also provides intraday liquidity via collateralized credit and queues payments if funds are insufficient (https://www.cnb.cz/en/payments/certis/certis-the-interbank-payment-system-description/#:~:text=,functioning%20of%20the%20payment%20system) (https://www.cnb.cz/en/payments/certis/certis-the-interbank-payment-system-description/#:~:text=,and%20then%20serve%20as%20collateral). It has high throughput (up to 1.5 million tx/hour) and has proven extremely reliable in processing both large and small CZK payments.

sistemas.descricao: 24/7 instant payment service integrated into CERTIS
sistemas.detalhes: In 2019, the CNB introduced instant payments in CZK as an extension of CERTIS (https://www.cnb.cz/en/payments/certis/certis-the-interbank-payment-system-description/#:~:text=Within%20the%20CERTIS%20system%2C%20it,is%20also%20operated). This service allows bank customers to send transfers up to CZK 400,000 (later increased to CZK 2.5 million) that are credited within seconds, anytime 24/7 (https://cashmanagement.bnpparibas.com/print/pdf/node/115#:~:text=,day%2C%20seven%20days%20a%20week). By 2022, most major Czech banks supported instant payments, and usage has grown rapidly (the number of instant transactions has multiplied since 2016) (https://www.nationalbanken.dk/en/what-we-do/safe-and-efficient-payments/payment-habits-in-denmark#:~:text=Since%202014%2C%20citizens%20in%20Denmark,widespread%20popularity%20among%20Danish%20consumers). These payments settle individually in real-time through CERTIS’s instant processing module, giving finality immediately. Adoption is rising as more consumers and businesses opt for the convenience of near-instant money transfers, although not all banks offer it on all accounts yet.

sistemas.descricao: Centralized household bill payment scheme operated by Czech Post
sistemas.detalhes: SIPO is a long-standing Czech payment scheme for aggregating and paying multiple bills through a single transaction. Run by Česká Pošta (Czech Post), SIPO lets households consolidate utilities, rent, insurance, etc., into one monthly payment, which is then direct-debited from the customer’s bank via CERTIS. It has been a popular method especially for those who prefer not to manage individual bill payments. While SIPO usage has declined somewhat with online banking rise, it still serves a significant segment for convenient bill pay. Adoption is moderate – millions of bills are paid via SIPO each month – and it remains an integral part of the payment landscape for older and rural customers.

sistemas.descricao: Widespread use of debit and credit cards (Visa, Mastercard) with contactless tech
sistemas.detalhes: Card payments are ubiquitous in the Czech Republic. All major banks issue debit cards (often Visa or Mastercard), and credit cards are also common. By 2017, Czechs averaged ~172 non-cash transactions per capita, among the highest in Europe (https://www.europeanpaymentscouncil.eu/sites/default/files/infographic/2019-04/Czech%20payment%20landscape.pdf#:~:text=In%202017%2C%20the%20Czech%20Republic,of%20koruna%20banknotes%20and%20coins), reflecting heavy card usage. Contactless payments have been standard since the 2010s – virtually all payment terminals accept tap-and-go cards or mobile wallets. The country has no domestic card scheme, but international schemes are well-integrated. Card transactions are cleared via processors and ultimately settled in CERTIS (card clearing houses participate as ancillary systems) (https://www.cnb.cz/en/payments/certis/certis-the-interbank-payment-system-description/#:~:text=Ancillary%20systems%20%28so%20called%20,parties). With over 12 million payment cards in circulation, adoption is very high, and cards are used daily for retail, e-commerce, and services.

sistemas.descricao: CERTIS is the sole interbank payment system in the Czech Republic, operated by the Czech National Bank (CNB) [oai_citation:65‡europeanpaymentscouncil.eu]. Introduced in the mid-1990s, CERTIS processes every domestic payment in Czech koruna – handling high-value urgent transfers and high-volume retail payments alike. It functions primarily as an RTGS: payments are processed individually throughout the day with immediate finality in participants’ accounts at CNB. However, it efficiently handles large volumes (nearly a billion transactions annually in recent years) by also supporting queued processing and multiple intraday settlement cycles for retail payments. All banks and credit unions in Czechia are participants. Operating hours are extended (CERTIS runs virtually 24x7, except brief maintenance) [oai_citation:66‡cashmanagement.bnpparibas.com] [oai_citation:67‡cashmanagement.bnpparibas.com]. Initially based on proprietary formats, CERTIS has been upgraded to support instant payments and modern messaging. The system has proven robust – in 2017, Czechia had Europe’s highest per-capita credit transfer count, thanks to CERTIS’s efficiency [oai_citation:68‡europeanpaymentscouncil.eu]. CERTIS significantly contributes to financial stability by providing immediate, irrevocable settlement finality for CZK transactions.

The CNB introduced instant payments in 2019 as an extension of CERTIS. This service allows customers of participating banks to send CZK payments up to a set limit (in the order of hundreds of thousands CZK) that are credited to the beneficiary within seconds, 24/7. The instant payments follow the European SCT Inst scheme standards so that they can be processed quickly and potentially interoperable. By mid-2022, most major Czech banks offered instant payments, but customer uptake was gradual. The transactions clear through CERTIS (or a dedicated module of it) continuously, with final settlement in central bank money. As an example of adoption, within the first year about 10–15% of eligible transfers were being sent as instant. The introduction of this service put Czechia on par with fast payment trends, albeit volumes are still growing. Technically, the service uses ISO 20022 messages and a timeout of seconds for response. This new feature did not require a separate system, leveraging CERTIS’s infrastructure.

SEPA Instant Credit Transfer is the euro-denominated instant payments scheme. Initiated by the EPC, it enables sending up to €15,000 in under 10 seconds, 24/7. German banks have joined SCT Inst, and usage has grown rapidly. For example, nearly 97 million instant transfers were executed in Germany in 2023 [oai_citation:27‡bundesbank.de]. These settle in real time via TIPS.
sistemas.detalhes: Operated by Eurosystem through TIPS infrastructure, enables euro transfers <10 seconds 24/7. Integrated with German online banking apps (e.g., Sparkasse, Deutsche Bank) and emerging digital wallets. Supports end-to-end data fields for invoices and reconciliation. Adopted by 60%+ German banks but merchant acceptance lags .

sistemas.descricao: ECB-operated system processing large-value interbank transfers with individual settlement in central bank money. Critical for monetary policy operations, interbank lending, and securities settlements. Integrated with T2S securities platform and provides liquidity for SEPA Instant .
Deferred payment solution for retail
sistemas.detalhes: Led by Klarna, PayPal, and Ratepay, offers installment plans at online/offline checkouts. Uses soft credit checks for approvals with repayment terms from 30 days to 24 months. Expanding into healthcare (elective procedures) and sustainable financing (solar panels). Regulated under EU consumer credit directives since 2024 .

sistemas.descricao: CBDC for retail payments under development
sistemas.detalhes: ECB-led initiative to complement cash with offline functionality and cash-like privacy. Features include programmable conditional payments (e.g., release funds upon delivery) and integration with existing banking apps. In testing phase with 70+ European partners including Deutsche Bank and Commerzbank .

sistemas.descricao: Direct debit authorization system

SEPA Credit Transfer is a Europe-wide ACH operated under the Single Euro Payments Area. German banks exchange retail credit transfer orders (e.g., salaries, invoicing) usually in multiple daily clearing batches settled via TARGET. Nearly all euro accounts in Germany can send and receive SCT payments under EPC rules.

TARGET2 (and its successor T2 launched 2023) is the Eurozone-wide RTGS system run by the Eurosystem. German banks (via Bundesbank) use T2 to settle high-value interbank payments in euro in real time. According to the Bundesbank, T2 processes transaction sums approaching the entire eurozone GDP every five days [oai_citation:24‡bundesbank.de], reflecting its central role in cross-border euro settlement.

SEPA Direct Debit (Core/Business) allows customers to authorize organizations to collect funds from their accounts. German consumers use SDD for utilities, subscriptions, and invoices. Like SCT, SDD is processed in clearing batches via TARGET.

Girocard is the domestic debit card network in Germany, co-branded with Maestro/V PAY internationally. It is owned by the German banking industry. Over 100 million Girocards have been issued [oai_citation:30‡girocard.eu], and they are accepted at virtually all German ATMs (~53,000) and POS terminals (~1.2 million) [oai_citation:31‡girocard.eu]. Transactions clear through interbank nets, but funds settle via central bank accounts (TARGET2).
Primary payment method
Limited services
Planned Automated Transfer System (RTGS/ACH) under central bank
sistemas.detalhes: Djibouti is in the process of establishing a modern National Payment System. The central bank (BCD), with World Bank support, has been implementing an **Automated Transfer System (ATS+)** that will include an RTGS for high-value payments and an Automated Clearing House for retail transfers (https://www.agpaytech.co.uk/pdf/rtgs.pdf#:~:text=%5BPDF%5D%20RTGS%20IN%20AFRICA%20,and%20National%20Bank%20of) (https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/331131646420868726/txt/Djibouti-Governance-for-Private-Sector-Development-and-Finance-Project.txt#:~:text=,an%20automated%20National%20Payment). As of the late 2010s, Djibouti had no live RTGS and relied on manual or correspondent arrangements (https://www.agpaytech.co.uk/pdf/rtgs.pdf#:~:text=%5BPDF%5D%20RTGS%20IN%20AFRICA%20,and%20National%20Bank%20of). The new ATS aims to digitize interbank settlements in real time and batch, improving efficiency and financial sector development. Adoption is currently in pilot/testing stages (with key banks onboarding). Once operational, it will handle all large-value DJF payments and interbank transfers, marking a significant upgrade in Djibouti’s payment infrastructure.

sistemas.descricao: Mobile money wallet by Djibouti Telecom for person-to-person transfers
sistemas.detalhes: D-Money is a mobile money service launched by the state telecom (Djibouti Telecom) in June 2020 (https://migrantmoney.uncdf.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Djibouti-Diagnostic-Report-ENG.pdf#:~:text=,new%20innovative%20service%20allows). It provides unbanked and banked users with the ability to store money in a mobile wallet and perform transfers, merchant payments, and airtime top-ups through their phone. Users can cash-in and cash-out via telecom agents. D-Money aims to emulate the success of mobile money in neighboring East African countries. Adoption is growing especially among individuals without bank accounts, though overall mobile money penetration remains modest. D-Money transactions are in Djiboutian Francs and provide a domestic digital alternative to cash for everyday payments.

sistemas.descricao: All-in-one mobile wallet app (private fintech)
sistemas.detalhes: Waafi is a mobile wallet and financial app operated by a private fintech (Safarifone) in Djibouti. It offers services like person-to-person money transfers, merchant payments, bill payments, and airtime purchase via a smartphone app (https://waafipay.net/#:~:text=Welcome%20To%20WaafiPay%20Mobile%20Money,Credit%20Cards). Waafi functions as an e-wallet where users can deposit funds and transact digitally. It is marketed as a lifestyle app combining communication and payments (https://waafi.com/#:~:text=WAAFI%20is%20your%20new%20life,productivity%20in%20a%20unified%20app). Waafi has been expanding in Djibouti and the Horn of Africa region, targeting both banked and unbanked populations. While exact user numbers are not public, it has gained users due to features like cross-border remittances. The FATF describes Waafi as providing a range of mobile financial services in Djibouti (https://www.fatf-gafi.org/content/dam/fatf-gafi/fsrb-mer/Republic%20of%20Djibouti%20MER_En.pdf#:~:text=,A%20Waafi). Adoption is moderate but increasing, especially among younger, tech-savvy customers.

sistemas.descricao: Traditional debit/credit cards (limited usage, mostly international cards)
sistemas.detalhes: Djibouti’s usage of payment cards is relatively low. A few banks issue Visa or Mastercard debit cards, and there is a small network of ATMs in the capital. Most local card transactions route via international networks or require foreign currency (USD/EUR) accounts. Due to the economy’s dollarization and cash-oriented nature, cards have not been a primary payment method domestically. However, expatriates and some urban residents use cards for ATM withdrawals or at hotels. Djibouti has no domestic card scheme; it relies on international card systems. The adoption is limited: only a minority of the population holds payment cards, and acceptance is confined to certain merchants catering to international customers.

sistemas.nome: SYRAD (Automated Settlement System of Djibouti, ATS+)
sistemas.descricao: SYRAD (Système de Règlement Automatisé de Djibouti) is the integrated national payments platform implemented by the Central Bank of Djibouti. Going live on 15 July 2021 [oai_citation:102‡economie.gouv.dj], it combines Real-Time Gross Settlement for large-value payments, an Automated Clearing House for batched retail payments, and an Instant Funds Transfer component [oai_citation:103‡lanation.dj]. Built on Montran’s ATS+ solution [oai_citation:104‡lanation.dj] [oai_citation:105‡lanation.dj], SYRAD allows banks to send high-value interbank transfers that settle immediately in central bank money, and also exchange bulk files for low-value transactions (like salary credits and direct debits) that net and settle in scheduled cycles. Additionally, it supports instant retail transfers (TFI – Transferts de Fonds Instantanés) enabling real-time bank-to-bank customer payments without going through net clearing [oai_citation:106‡lanation.dj]. SYRAD operates on modern infrastructure with participants connected via fiber optic and secure wireless links [oai_citation:107‡lanation.dj]. It adheres to international standards (BIS principles) and has significantly upgraded Djibouti’s payment capacity, moving it from manual processes to electronic, and positioning the country as a potential regional hub. Settlement in SYRAD occurs in both Djiboutian franc (DJF) and possibly USD (for certain operations), with full central bank oversight.
