D-Money ("Djibouti Money") is a digital wallet and mobile payment service launched by Djibouti Telecom in late 2019 [oai_citation:108‡developingtelecoms.com]. It allows users (including unbanked populations) to store monetary value on their mobile phone and perform transfers, bill payments, and merchant purchases through a mobile app/USSD. D-Money essentially acts as an electronic wallet: customers cash-in and cash-out via agents or partner banks, and can send money P2P by using phone numbers. It also facilitates salary disbursements and payments at participating retailers (often via QR codes or merchant codes). In the port of Djibouti, for example, D-Money has been used to pay workers digitally [oai_citation:109‡developingtelecoms.com]. The service is secured via PINs and runs on a platform developed by an international provider. D-Money transactions are recorded in a central ledger at Djibouti Telecom and net settlements with banks (to manage liquidity backing) likely occur through the central bank. D-Money is part of Djibouti’s strategy to increase financial inclusion. Adoption is gradually expanding as more merchants and government services come onboard. The currency handled is Djiboutian Franc; the system is regulated by the central bank under e-money guidelines.

sistemas.nome: SYRAD (Système de Règlement Automatisé de Djibouti)

sistemas.descricao: MobilePay is a mobile payment service launched by Danske Bank in 2013 that has become the most popular payment app in Denmark. It allows users to send money instantly to others using just the recipient’s phone number, as well as to pay merchants via QR code or online checkout. MobilePay links to the user’s bank account or card for funding, but the transfer between users is executed as a Straksclearing instant payment on the backend when different banks are involved. The app offers a very user-friendly interface, which led to explosive adoption – within two years over 2 million Danes had MobilePay, and by 2020 about 90% of smartphone owners had installed it [oai_citation:97‡ergomania.eu]. In 2020, MobilePay processed transactions worth over €18 billion [oai_citation:98‡ergomania.eu]. It supports features like splitting bills (WeShare), integrating loyalty programs, and invoicing for businesses. MobilePay has also been adopted in Finland and some other countries. In 2022, MobilePay announced a merger with Norway’s Vipps. Technically, MobilePay transactions that stay within the same bank may be internal book transfers; interbank transactions are sent through instant clearing. The success of MobilePay has significantly reduced the use of cash in Denmark.
sistemas.detalhes: MobilePay is a mobile payment app launched in 2013 by Danske Bank that has become Denmark’s most popular payment method for peer-to-peer and point-of-sale payments. It allows users to instantly send money to friends or merchants using just the recipient’s phone number or a QR code, with the transfers clearing through Straksclearing. By 2023, MobilePay had ~4.5 million users in Denmark (out of 5.9 million population) (https://www.nationalbanken.dk/en/what-we-do/safe-and-efficient-payments/payment-habits-in-denmark#:~:text=In%20Denmark%2C%20it%20became%20possible,5%20million%20users%20in%20Denmark) and an average user makes 124 payments per year (https://www.telecompaper.com/news/mobilepay-denmark-says-transactions-rise-11-in-2023--1486901#:~:text=MobilePay%20Denmark%20says%20transactions%20rise,times%2C%20with%20per%20capita). MobilePay is used for everything from splitting restaurant bills to paying in shops and online. Its near-universal adoption (over 90% of young adults use it) has helped Denmark reach a point where ~33% of in-store payments are via mobile (https://www.nationalbanken.dk/en/what-we-do/safe-and-efficient-payments/payment-habits-in-denmark#:~:text=Danes%20are%20increasingly%20using%20their,contactless%20card%20payments%20in%20stores). In 2022 MobilePay merged with Norwegian Vipps, ensuring continued innovation.

sistemas.descricao: Dankort is Denmark’s national debit card system, introduced in 1983. It is a card scheme owned by Nets (formerly PBS) and Danish banks. Dankort cards (often co-badged with Visa) are issued by banks to consumers and widely accepted by merchants. The Dankort system operates a central switch for authorizations and a clearing system for card transactions in DKK. When a Dankort transaction is made, the merchant’s acquirer routes the transaction to the Dankort network, which then either authorizes it against the issuer or uses offline limits. Transactions are aggregated and cleared among banks typically next day (via Nets’ clearing which ultimately settles in Kronos). Dankort’s ubiquity made it the preferred payment method in Denmark for decades (it has extremely high acceptance, including for online payments with a CPR-based security code). With the rise of international cards and MobilePay, Dankort usage growth has leveled off, but it remains a critical component of the payment landscape, especially for domestic retail payments (no currency exchange and low fees).
sistemas.detalhes: Dankort is Denmark’s domestic debit card network, originally introduced in 1983. It is the most widely held payment card in Denmark and often co-issued with Visa (Visa/Dankort). Dankort transactions route through Nets (formerly PBS) for clearing. The scheme is known for low merchant fees and has extremely high usage – it accounts for the largest number of card transactions in Denmark (https://dankort.dk/en-GB/dankort#:~:text=Fast%20and%20secure%20payments,of%20card%20transactions%20in%20Denmark). In 2024, total card spending in Denmark was DKK 661 billion (https://www.nationalbanken.dk/en/news-and-knowledge/data-and-statistics/payments/20250203-the-turnover-from-card-payments-continued-to-increase-in-2024#:~:text=The%20turnover%20from%20card%20payments,640%20billion%20in%202023), much of it on Dankort. Almost all merchants accept Dankort, and the card supports contactless and mobile wallets. Adoption is very high (over 5 million Dankort cards for ~6 million people) and it remains a cornerstone of Danish payments, though international cards are also used.

sistemas.descricao: Danmarks Nationalbank’s real-time gross settlement system for DKK
sistemas.detalhes: Kronos2 is the core large-value payment system in Denmark, settling interbank transfers, monetary policy operations, and the net positions of clearing houses in real time (https://www.nationalbanken.dk/en/what-we-do/stable-financial-system/oversight-of-payments-infrastructure#:~:text=Kronos2%20is%20Danmarks%20Nationalbank%E2%80%99s%20system,critical%20payments%20in%20Danish%20kroner). It processes high-value DKK payments individually and instantly, providing immediate finality. Kronos2 operates on TARGET infrastructure and in 2025 is being linked to the Eurosystem’s T2 for cross-currency settlements (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2024/html/ecb.pr24321~4d598cf1fe.en.html#:~:text=Denmark%20joins%20T2%20and%20TIPS,payments%20in%20Danish%20kroner%2C%E2%80%9D). All banks hold accounts in Kronos2, so adoption is universal. It functions 07:00–18:00 CET for RTGS; after Easter 2025, Kronos2 will settle 24/7 via TIPS for instant DKK payments (https://finansdanmark.dk/media/0gml2whw/technical-changes-to-instant-payments-information-meeting-2023-09-20-presentation.pdf#:~:text=Finance%20Denmark%20will%20close%20at,From%20Easter%202025%2C). Kronos2’s safe and efficient operations are critical – it handled about DKK 1.3 trillion per day on average in 2023.

sistemas.descricao: Straksclearing (also called Express Clearing) is Denmark’s instant payment solution, operational since November 2014 [oai_citation:89‡data.ecb.europa.eu]. It allows bank customers to send DKK payments up to DKK 500,000 that are received within seconds at any time. The service is available 24/7/365, with payments pre-funded and settled continuously via a special account structure at the central bank [oai_citation:90‡nationalbanken.dk] [oai_citation:91‡nationalbanken.dk]. Nets (now Mastercard Payment Services) operates the instant clearing hub: it receives instant payment instructions from sending banks and immediately forwards them to receiving banks, while holding reserved liquidity from each bank in a central bank account to guarantee settlement [oai_citation:92‡nationalbanken.dk]. Formal settlement of accumulated instant transfers happens in Kronos periodically (multiple times per day) by moving liquidity to/from these dedicated accounts [oai_citation:93‡nationalbanken.dk] [oai_citation:94‡nationalbanken.dk]. From the user perspective, payments are irrevocable and final within seconds. Straksclearing has been widely adopted – most person-to-person mobile payments (like MobilePay transactions between different banks) utilize this system. It has effectively replaced cash for many small transactions in Denmark.
sistemas.detalhes: Straksclearing is Denmark’s domestic instant payment system launched in 2014, allowing near-real-time transfers between banks 24/7. Operated by Finance Denmark/Mastercard, it enabled popular services like MobilePay to instantly move money. All major Danish banks connected to Straksclearing, and it could process payments within seconds, with a typical limit of DKK 500,000 per transaction. By 2023, around 10%+ of all Danish electronic payments were instant (https://www.numeral.io/guide-article/instant-payments-european-countries#:~:text=The%20State%20of%20Instant%20Payments,). However, Denmark is migrating to a new setup: as of April 2025, local instant payments will settle via **TIPS-DKK** (Eurosystem’s platform) and Straksclearing will be phased out (https://finansdanmark.dk/media/0gml2whw/technical-changes-to-instant-payments-information-meeting-2023-09-20-presentation.pdf#:~:text=Danmark%20finansdanmark,From%20Easter%202025%2C) (https://www.riksbank.se/globalassets/media/rapporter/staff-memo/svenska/2025/fast-payments-offer-economic-benefits-but-pose-new-challenges.pdf#:~:text=,which%20was%20operated%20by%20Mastercard). Adoption of instant payments is very high, with millions of transactions daily, driven by mobile app usage.

sistemas.descricao: Deferred net clearing of low-value payments (batched systems)
sistemas.detalhes: Denmark’s retail payments are cleared through two main batch systems: **Sumclearing** (overnight clearing of bulk payments, e.g. salary and vendor payments) and **Intradagclearing** (multiple intra-day clearings for same-day payments). These systems, operated by Finance Denmark, aggregate credit transfers and other low-value transactions and net the obligations among banks. The net results are settled in Kronos2 at designated times (https://www.nationalbanken.dk/en/what-we-do/stable-financial-system/oversight-of-payments-infrastructure#:~:text=Kronos2%20is%20used%2C%20among%20other,CPH%20settlement%20and%20CLS) (https://www.nationalbanken.dk/en/what-we-do/stable-financial-system/oversight-of-payments-infrastructure#:~:text=The%20Sumclearing%2C%20the%20Intradagclearing%20and,retail%20payments%20in%20Danish%20kroner). These clearing houses handle high volumes of transactions (hundreds of thousands daily), albeit non-urgent ones. They are overseen to ensure efficiency and security. Adoption is high as they underlie regular bank transfers, but their role is gradually shrinking as Danes shift to instant payments for many uses.

sistemas.descricao: Automated direct debit service for recurring bills
sistemas.detalhes: Betalingsservice is Denmark’s nationwide direct debit scheme operated by Nets. It allows consumers and companies to authorize automatic payment of recurring bills (utilities, rent, subscriptions, etc.) on due dates. Over 95% of Danish adults use Betalingsservice at least annually (https://www.atlar.com/guides/bank-payments-in-denmark#:~:text=Betalingsservice%20is%20the%20main%20direct,make%20recurring%20payments%20for), making it a highly trusted bill-pay method. Each year more than 200 million payments are processed through Betalingsservice (https://www.nationalbanken.dk/media/5lpnsrfv/report-assessment-of-betalingsservice.pdf#:~:text=Danish%20citizens%20and%20firms%20execute,Betalings%02service%20according%20to%20the%20European), with funds pulled from payers’ accounts and transferred to billers via the clearing system. It significantly reduces late payments and manual handling. Adoption is very high; most households have several agreements. The central bank oversees Betalingsservice as a key retail payment instrument and found it broadly compliant with standards (https://www.nationalbanken.dk/media/5lpnsrfv/report-assessment-of-betalingsservice.pdf#:~:text=Central%20Bank%20,standards%2C%20Nets%20is%20the%20governance) (https://www.nationalbanken.dk/media/5lpnsrfv/report-assessment-of-betalingsservice.pdf#:~:text=In%20August%202019%2C%20Nets%20and,to%20be%20carried%20on%20by).

sistemas.descricao: Kronos is Danmarks Nationalbank’s real-time gross settlement system for Danish kroner. It settles interbank payments, high-value customer payments, and provides final settlement for ancillary systems (clearing houses) in central bank money [oai_citation:72‡nationalbanken.dk]. Kronos has been operational since 2001 (upgraded to Kronos2 in 2018) and processes time-critical payments continuously during business hours. It uses a SWIFT-based platform and provides features like liquidity reservation, queue management and intraday credit via automatic collateralization [oai_citation:73‡nationalbanken.dk] [oai_citation:74‡nationalbanken.dk]. Kronos also settles the net outputs of the retail systems (Sumclearing, Intraday, and Straksclearing) at designated times [oai_citation:75‡nationalbanken.dk] [oai_citation:76‡nationalbanken.dk]. In 2021, Kronos2 introduced extended operating hours and modernized technical infrastructure. As of 2025, Kronos (with Kronos2) remains the core of Danish payments, ensuring safe and immediate settlement of large payments and supporting Denmark’s financial stability.

The Sumclearing (Sum Clearing) is the traditional ACH in Denmark for retail payments like credit transfers, salaries, and bulk direct debits. Operated by Finance Denmark (the bank association) and Mastercard Payment Services (formerly Nets) [oai_citation:78‡nationalbanken.dk], Sumclearing compiles payment instructions from banks throughout the day and nets them for settlement in Kronos during a night cycle. It processes two main runs: one at end-of-day and one early morning after non-banking days [oai_citation:79‡nationalbanken.dk]. Payments submitted by end-of-business are available in receivers’ accounts the next morning once settled at 1:30 (and 06:00 on the first business day after a weekend/holiday) [oai_citation:80‡nationalbanken.dk]. Sumclearing has been in place for decades, ensuring efficient low-cost clearing. It uses a central infrastructure where banks send files of outgoing payments and receive their net results. With the advent of instant payments, some volume shifted away, but Sumclearing still handles high volumes of recurring and bulk transactions.

The Intradagclearing (Intraday Clearing) in Denmark provides additional clearing cycles during the day for payments that need same-day execution but are not urgent enough for RTGS. Launched in 2013 [oai_citation:83‡data.ecb.europa.eu], it runs at several times (e.g., 9:00, 12:00, 14:00) on business days [oai_citation:84‡nationalbanken.dk]. This enables e.g. same-day bill payments or batched retail transfers to be cleared and settled before end-of-day. Like Sumclearing, it is owned by Finance Denmark and operated by Mastercard/Nets, using a similar netting mechanism. Banks submit payments up to cutoff times for each cycle; positions are netted and settled in Kronos at the scheduled times (with pre-funded liquidity on dedicated accounts in Kronos) [oai_citation:85‡nationalbanken.dk] [oai_citation:86‡nationalbanken.dk]. Intraday Clearing improves efficiency by reducing payment float and giving more opportunities to settle during the day. It uses the same technical platform as Sumclearing with separate processing windows.
Dominant payment method
Regional ACH for batched electronic transfers and cheque imaging
sistemas.detalhes: Dominica, as part of the Eastern Caribbean Currency Union (ECCU), participates in the ECACH – a unified clearing house for the Eastern Caribbean dollar (XCD). ECACH, launched in 2014, connects all banks across ECCU countries to clear payments electronically (https://ecach.org/file/2024/10/ECACH-Presentation-to-Credit-Unions-Sep-25_24_Fina_240925_065712.pdf#:~:text=,2023%20Transaction%20Volumes). It initially introduced cheque image clearing (scanning cheques for faster inter-island clearing) and later enabled electronic funds transfers (EFT) in 2018 (https://ecach.org/file/2024/10/ECACH-Presentation-to-Credit-Unions-Sep-25_24_Fina_240925_065712.pdf#:~:text=,2023%20Transaction%20Volumes). Through ECACH, transactions like payroll, wire transfers, and cheque settlements are processed in batch and settled in the ECCB. Adoption is increasing as paper cheque processing is modernized and electronic credit transfers grow. By 2023, ECACH handled thousands of items daily across the region. In Dominica, all commercial banks are linked, making the system integral for non-cash payments.

sistemas.descricao: Digital Eastern Caribbean Dollar issued by ECCB
sistemas.detalhes: DCash is a central bank digital currency pilot launched by the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank in 2021 (https://www.dcashec.com/#:~:text=DCash%20is%20the%20digital%20version,ECCB%29%20in%20March%202021). Dominica is one of the pilot countries. DCash is a digital version of the EC Dollar stored in a mobile wallet. Users (after KYC) can download the DCash app to send and receive funds with others in the ECCU instantly, without fees. The system is intended to foster financial inclusion and payment efficiency across islands (https://www.eccb-centralbank.org/blogs/the-eccb-s-digital-currency-dcash-is-a-critical-step-in-the-buildout-of-a-digital-economy-in-the-eccu#:~:text=The%20ECCB%27s%20Digital%20Currency%20,DCash%20is%20the%20significant). Adoption remains in early stages (few thousand users regionally) as the pilot faced some technical outages (https://www.eccb-centralbank.org/news/dcash-service-resumes-1#:~:text=centralbank,now%20benefits%20from%20several%20upgrades). In Dominica, merchants and individuals are slowly signing up. Transaction volumes are low but growing as public awareness increases. As of 2023, DCash remains in pilot status, with the ECCB working on its reliability and expanding its features (DCash 2.0).

sistemas.descricao: International debit/credit cards in use (processed via regional networks)
sistemas.detalhes: Dominica does not have a domestic card scheme; banks issue international cards (Visa, Mastercard) often linked to XCD accounts. Card transactions in Dominica are processed by the Eastern Caribbean’s card networks, primarily the Caribbean Credit Card Corporation (4C’s) based in St. Kitts. Adoption of cards is moderate – many employed persons have debit cards for ATM withdrawals and point-of-sale, but cash is still widely used. Merchants in tourism, retail, and services accept cards, though smaller vendors may not. The number of card transactions has been rising as POS infrastructure spreads. With about 50–60% of adults owning a payment card, adoption is medium. Annual card transaction value in Dominica is in the tens of millions of XCD, a smaller share compared to ACH and cash usage.

sistemas.descricao: Emerging digital wallets and remittance platforms
sistemas.detalhes: A few mobile payment solutions have appeared in Dominica in recent years. These include apps for mobile top-ups and bill payments, often provided by telecom operators or fintech startups. For example, *Flow* (telecom) offers a digital wallet for top-ups, and regional services like *CaribePay* have piloted cashless payment apps for small businesses. Additionally, many Dominicans use international remittance apps (MoneyGram, Western Union mobile) to receive funds from abroad. While none of these are national-scale schemes yet, they represent a growing trend towards digital payments. Adoption is currently low and limited to tech-savvy users, but as smartphone penetration increases, these mobile and online payment channels are expected to gain traction.

Cash payment network

sistemas.nome: LBTR – Sistema de Liquidación Bruta en Tiempo Real
sistemas.descricao: Central Bank’s real-time gross settlement system for DOP and USD
sistemas.detalhes: The Dominican Republic’s LBTR system is a real-time gross settlement platform run by the Banco Central (BCRD) since 2008 (https://eldinero.com.do/267336/lbtr-ha-marcado-un-antes-y-un-despues-en-el-sistema-de-pagos-dominicano/#:~:text=El%20Sistema%20de%20Liquidaci%C3%B3n%20Bruta,28%20de%20abril%20de%202008). It settles high-value payments and interbank transfers in Dominican Pesos – and also supports USD transactions among local banks – with immediate finality (https://eldinero.com.do/267336/lbtr-ha-marcado-un-antes-y-un-despues-en-el-sistema-de-pagos-dominicano/#:~:text=sucursal%20u%20oficina%20bancaria). Originally used mainly for large-value and urgent payments, LBTR is now also used for instant retail transfers (“pagos al instante”) by bank customers, as it processes small transfers in real time for a fee (https://eldinero.com.do/267336/lbtr-ha-marcado-un-antes-y-un-despues-en-el-sistema-de-pagos-dominicano/#:~:text=ImageTodas%20las%20transacciones%20realizadas%20a,en%20la%20cuenta%20bancaria%20destino). Transactions via LBTR skyrocketed in recent years: from ~12,500 operations in 2014 to 21.9 million in 2023 (https://eldinero.com.do/267336/lbtr-ha-marcado-un-antes-y-un-despues-en-el-sistema-de-pagos-dominicano/#:~:text=Partiendo%20del%20volumen%20reportado%20por,de%20transacciones%20v%C3%ADa%20el%20LBTR), reflecting the shift to digital banking. The system charges a flat fee (~RD$100) per transfer (https://eldinero.com.do/267336/lbtr-ha-marcado-un-antes-y-un-despues-en-el-sistema-de-pagos-dominicano/#:~:text=ImageTodas%20las%20transacciones%20realizadas%20a,en%20la%20cuenta%20bancaria%20destino). Adoption is high among banks (all are participants) and increasingly by consumers for fast transfers. In 2023 the value settled via LBTR reached RD$2.836 trillion (https://eldinero.com.do/267336/lbtr-ha-marcado-un-antes-y-un-despues-en-el-sistema-de-pagos-dominicano/#:~:text=Partiendo%20del%20volumen%20reportado%20por,de%20transacciones%20v%C3%ADa%20el%20LBTR).

sistemas.descricao: The country’s ACH (often just called “ACH”) processes deferred net settlement of large volumes of retail payments, including payroll direct deposits, recurring credit transfers, and interbank checks. It is operated by the private company Cámara de Compensación Electrónica (CCE) under central bank oversight. Banks submit files of ACH credit transfers (e.g., salaries) and ACH debit collections (e.g., utility bills) throughout the day. Transactions are sorted and exchanged among banks, and net balances are calculated. Settlement of the net positions occurs once per day through the central bank’s LBTR at a designated time (typically end-of-day). The ACH also incorporates electronic cheque clearing: physical checks are truncated and images/data are exchanged for next-day clearing. The ACH system in the DR uses a standardized format somewhat akin to NACHA files and assigns a unique trace number to each entry for tracking. It operates only on banking days. Though BCRD’s LBTR now offers near-instant transfers, ACH remains heavily used for bulk payments due to cost-effectiveness. For instance, the local ATMs/POS network (CardNet) uses ACH for next-day settlement of some transactions, and many government payments are distributed via ACH.
sistemas.detalhes: The Dominican Republic’s ACH system processes batched electronic fund transfers (credit transfers) and direct debits between banks. It is operated by the private company CardNet (Consorcio de Tarjetas Dominicanas) on behalf of the banking sector (https://eldinero.com.do/267336/lbtr-ha-marcado-un-antes-y-un-despues-en-el-sistema-de-pagos-dominicano/#:~:text=Tambi%C3%A9n%20est%C3%A1n%20las%20transferencias%20ACH%2C,a%20sucursal%20u%20oficina%20bancaria). ACH transfers in DOP are typically used for regular, non-urgent payments (payroll, vendor payments, etc.) and settle within 24 hours. They are free to bank customers, encouraging use for everyday transfers (https://eldinero.com.do/267336/lbtr-ha-marcado-un-antes-y-un-despues-en-el-sistema-de-pagos-dominicano/#:~:text=ImageTodas%20las%20transacciones%20realizadas%20a,en%20la%20cuenta%20bancaria%20destino). The ACH handles millions of transactions annually. While slower than LBTR, it carries a significant volume of retail payments. All commercial banks connect to ACH Dominicana, making adoption universal in the banking system. The system has been upgrading to facilitate near-real-time ACH and operates in parallel with the instant LBTR for smaller payments.

sistemas.descricao: Domestic card payment acquiring networks for Visa/Mastercard
sistemas.detalhes: Card payments in the Dominican Republic are supported by two main acquiring networks: **CardNet** and **Azul**. CardNet (owned by multiple banks) and Azul (owned by Banco Popular) process transactions for Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and local proprietary cards at merchants nationwide. These networks route transactions to issuing banks and handle POS and ATM switching. The country has about 8.4 million payment cards in circulation (https://one.oecd.org/document/DAF/COMP/LACF(2021)8/en/pdf#:~:text=country%20was%208,5%20debit) and an extensive POS network. Contactless card usage is growing quickly. Adoption of cards is moderate-high: cards are commonly used in urban centers and for e-commerce, though cash still dominates small transactions. In 2020, the DR had around 191,700 POS devices and 8.4 million cards (https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4119820#:~:text=Regulating%20Payment,24%2C%202020). The card networks also power the sub-agent networks (bank agents) enabling card withdrawals in local shops. Overall card payment volume has been rising year over year as electronic payments expand.

sistemas.descricao: Mobile payments platform linking bank accounts for P2P, bills, and top-ups
sistemas.detalhes: tPago is a popular Dominican mobile payment and online banking service (USSD/app) developed by GCS International (a subsidiary of Grupo Popular) (https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/TPago#:~:text=tPago%20es%20una%20plataforma%20de,8). Launched in 2010, it allows users to link multiple bank accounts and credit cards to their phone and perform various transactions: person-to-person transfers, bill payments, mobile recharges, and merchant payments (https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/TPago#:~:text=tPago%20es%20una%20plataforma%20de,8) (https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/TPago#:~:text=Grupo%20Popular.%20,8). By 2017, tPago had over 700,000 users and had processed more than 70 million transactions totaling RD$17 billion (https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/TPago#:~:text=En%202016%2C%20tPago%20llev%C3%B3%20a,16). It has grown further since then, becoming a key platform for financial inclusion. tPago transactions are executed in real time (the service operates 24/7) and settle through the banking network. Most major banks in the DR are part of the tPago network. Adoption is high among smartphone users – it’s a convenient alternative to cash or visiting bank branches, contributing to the digitization of payments.

sistemas.descricao: The Eastern Caribbean Central Bank (ECCB) operates an RTGS that serves all member countries of the Eastern Caribbean Currency Union (including Dominica). Implemented in 2004, this common platform settles large-value Eastern Caribbean dollar (XCD) payments in real time across the eight island economies [oai_citation:111‡kansascityfed.org]. It allows instant interbank transfers, central bank operations, and settlement of net positions from other systems in final central bank money. The system uses SWIFT infrastructure for communication and was upgraded in 2009 to enable straight-through processing and improved efficiency [oai_citation:112‡elibrary.imf.org]. Participants include the ECCB and all commercial banks in the region. By pooling volume from multiple small countries, the ECCU RTGS achieves economies of scale. It operates during regional business hours. Transactions are irrevocable once settled. This RTGS underpins financial stability by eliminating settlement risk for high-value transfers within the ECCU. Its messaging initially used SWIFT MT standards; ECCB has plans to modernize towards ISO 20022 in line with global trends. The RTGS provides the backbone for initiatives like regional government securities settlement and large cross-border corporate payments.

ECACH is the shared automated clearing house for the Eastern Caribbean Currency Union, launched in the mid-2010s to streamline retail payments. It processes low-value electronic payments (like payroll transfers, utility payments, and cheque images) among banks in Dominica and other ECCU member states [oai_citation:114‡eccb-centralbank.org]. The clearing house operates in each island via a local ACH unit and is governed by common rules under the ECCB. Banks submit files of credit transfers and direct debits; the ECACH computes multilateral net positions for each bank and those positions are then settled on the ECCB RTGS at day-end. The system significantly improved efficiency by replacing manual cheque clearing and paper-based instruments with electronic processing. It uses electronic cheque presentment (cheque truncation) and ACH credit standards similar to US ACH formats (NACHA-like). The ECACH is accessible to commercial banks and large credit unions. It is regulated under the Payment System Act and rules issued by ECCB [oai_citation:115‡ecach.org]. The clearing cycle is typically overnight or same-day, and once settlement occurs, beneficiary accounts are credited accordingly. ECACH has reduced float and accelerated funds availability across the ECCU.

DCash is a blockchain-based central bank digital currency (CBDC) issued by the ECCB, the first of its kind in a currency union. The pilot went live in early 2021 in four ECCU countries (including Dominica) [oai_citation:119‡kansascityfed.org] [oai_citation:120‡kansascityfed.org], and later expanded. DCash is a digital version of the EC dollar aimed at promoting financial inclusion and payment efficiency. Users access DCash via a mobile app or through participating financial institutions; they can make person-to-person transfers, merchant payments via QR code, and other transactions instantly, without traditional intermediaries. The system operates on a distributed ledger platform managed by ECCB and its technology partner Bitt Inc. Transactions are verified by a permissioned network of nodes. DCash wallets are either held with financial institutions (if KYC’d) or as simpler value-based wallets with lower limits. While technically successful, adoption has been limited – a few thousand users and 400 merchants by March 2023 [oai_citation:121‡kansascityfed.org] – due to network outages and public caution. ECCB continues to refine the project. DCash transactions incur no fees and settle effectively in real time (the CBDC is directly a liability on ECCB). DCash is denominated 1:1 with the XCD and can be converted to physical cash or bank deposits through participating institutions.

CardNET and AZUL are the two main electronic payment networks in the Dominican Republic that process ATM withdrawals and POS card transactions. CardNET (owned by multiple banks in consortium with EVERTEC) and AZUL (owned by Banco Popular) act as switches that route card authorizations to the appropriate issuer and handle settlement of card transactions within the country. They each operate a network of ATMs and POS terminals. When a card issued by Bank A is used at an ATM or store of Bank B, the transaction goes through one of these switches to obtain authorization and later clearing. Settlement between banks for card transactions is done typically via next-day entries, either through bilateral arrangements or via the ACH. Both networks support chip (EMV) and contactless transactions, and connect to international schemes (Visa, Mastercard) for global interoperability. These networks have vastly expanded card usage in the DR. As of 2022, nearly all merchants have POS connected to either CardNET or AZUL, and the country saw over 150 million card purchase transactions. While not a single “national switch” (two competing ones exist), together they form the domestic card payment infrastructure. The central bank oversees them indirectly via banking regs.

The Banco Central de la República Dominicana (BCRD) runs an RTGS known as the LBTR system, which settles high-value and urgent electronic payments in Dominican pesos immediately and with finality. Implemented in 2008 [oai_citation:123‡analytica.com.do], LBTR initially operated only during business hours, but it has since been extended to operate 7 days a week from 7:00am to 11:00pm [oai_citation:124‡prousuario.gob.do], effectively serving also as an instant payment service. Participants include the central bank, commercial banks, and clearing houses. Through LBTR, banks can transfer funds on behalf of themselves or customers (large corporate payments, interbank loans, etc.) and receive immediate confirmation. The system also settles the results of the ACH and other deferred systems at end-of-cycle. Locally, the public associates LBTR with BCRD’s “Pagos al Instante” service because it enables near-real-time transfers across banks. By design, LBTR uses a SWIFT-based infrastructure for messaging and has multi-currency capability (it can settle USD transactions among local banks as well). It significantly reduced settlement times from days to seconds in the Dominican financial system and adheres to international risk management standards (queueing, gridlock resolution, etc.).
Domestic interbank card network for ATMs/POS
sistemas.detalhes: CIB is Algeria’s national interbank card scheme, managed by **SATIM** (the national interbank card switch). Banks issue **CIB debit cards** to account holders, which can be used across all ATMs and POS terminals in the country (https://www.aps.dz/economie/135098-e-paiement-hausse-de-20-du-nombre-des-cartes-interbancaires-en-2021#:~:text=hausse%20de%2020,cartes%20Epargne%20est%20de). CIB cards carry the “CIB” logo and allow cash withdrawals, balance inquiries, and local purchases. As of 2023 there were over **4 million** CIB cards in circulation (https://lapatrienews.dz/e-paiement-plus-de-19-millions-de-cartes-electronique-en-circulation/#:~:text=E,sont%20des%20cartes%20d%27Alg%C3%A9rie%20Poste) (https://www.horizons.dz/?p=163563#:~:text=Les%20TPE%20et%20le%20mobile,Le%20nombre). The ATM/POS network under CIB is branded **“MULTI-CIB”** or **“MULTICAISSE”** in some contexts (through GIE Monétique). Card adoption has grown ~20% annually; in 2021, 1.53 million personal CIB cards were active (plus ~83k corporate and 1.16 million savings-linked cards) (http://news.radioalgerie.dz/fr/node/4439#:~:text=Ce%20chiffre%20est%20r%C3%A9parti%20comme,suit). These cards handle tens of millions of ATM withdrawals per year and an increasing number of POS payments. However, historically Algerians used cards mostly for cash – e.g. in 2021 cardholders made 87.7 million ATM withdrawals versus only ~2.15 million POS transactions (http://news.radioalgerie.dz/fr/node/4439#:~:text=,789%20transactions%20valides%20%28%2B50%2C14) (http://news.radioalgerie.dz/fr/node/4439#:~:text=,par%20rapport%20%C3%A0%202020). The government and banks are expanding POS acceptance and incentivizing digital payments, so CIB card usage for purchases is rising. CIB is fully EMV-compliant and coexists with international card brands (Visa, MasterCard) on dual-network cards.

sistemas.descricao: Postal financial card for government and personal payments
sistemas.detalhes: **Edahabia** is a payment card issued by Algérie Poste for holders of postal accounts (CCP). It is used for withdrawing cash at postal ATMs, making POS purchases, and paying bills through Algeria Post’s network. Edahabia has massive reach: over **13.3 million** Edahabia cards were in circulation by 2023 (https://www.horizons.dz/?p=163563#:~:text=Les%20TPE%20et%20le%20mobile,Le%20nombre) – far exceeding bank-issued cards – as many government salaries, pensions, and social benefits are paid into postal accounts. Edahabia is EMV chip-enabled and can be used online and at any Algérie Poste or CIB network terminal. Algérie Poste also offers **BaridiMob**, a mobile app linked to Edahabia for digital payments. In the first 5 months of 2023, BaridiMob handled 13 million transactions (https://www.aps.dz/en/algeria/tag/Epayment#:~:text=Epayment%20,of%202023%2C%20the%20Minister) – many of these are Edahabia cardholders paying utilities, P2P transfers, etc. Edahabia’s adoption is very high, driving financial inclusion by giving millions of unbanked citizens electronic payment access. The volume of Edahabia transactions is growing rapidly, making it a key pillar of Algeria’s payments ecosystem.

sistemas.descricao: National payment card system
Growing mobile money services

Société d’Automatisation des Transactions Interbancaires et de Monétique (SATIM) links 18 banks; 3 868 ATMs and 45.9 m POS transactions Q1-2024. Instant person-to-person and QR merchant payments launched pilot June 2024.
Electronic clearing house for retail payments
sistemas.detalhes: ATCI is Algeria’s national electronic clearing system for retail payments (mass payments like checks, electronic transfers, direct debits and card payments) (https://fr.linkedin.com/posts/banque-d-alg%C3%A9rie_le-gouverneur-de-bank-of-algeria-%D8%A8%D9%86%D9%83-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AC%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%A6%D8%B1-activity-6907646881338699776-ujIY#:~:text=Post%20de%20Bank%20of%20Algeria,des%20moyens%20de%20paiement). Banks send batches of payment instructions to ATCI, which calculates multilateral net positions and forwards the net balances to the RTGS for settlement (http://droit-afrique.com/upload/doc/algerie/Algerie-Reglement-2005-06-compensation-cheques.pdf#:~:text=Alg%C3%A9rie%20Compensation%20des%20ch%C3%A8ques%20et,r%C3%A8glements%20bruts%20en%20temps) (http://droit-afrique.com/upload/doc/algerie/Algerie-Reglement-2005-06-compensation-cheques.pdf#:~:text=,r%C3%A8glements%20bruts%20en%20temps). ATCI has greatly sped up clearing of cheques and other instruments. Usage is extensive: in 2013 ATCI processed about **19.47 million** payment transactions totaling DA 12,662 billion (https://fr.scribd.com/document/705902882/Les-Moyens-de-Paiement-Et-La-Monetique-en-Algerie-Bejaya#:~:text=Le%20nombre%20d%E2%80%99op%C3%A9ration%20effectu%C3%A9%20par,de%20l%E2%80%99ann%C3%A9e%202013%2C%20est%20de). This includes settlement of check clearing, automated transfers and card network settlements. ATCI operates with daily clearing cycles. It is jointly run by the central bank and banking sector. Adoption is high – all banks use ATCI for their retail payment exchange, making it the backbone for everyday non-cash transactions in Algeria’s economy.

sistemas.descricao: Mobile payment app and QR service by Algeria Post
sistemas.detalhes: BaridiMob is Algeria Post’s mobile wallet application that allows Edahabia cardholders to conduct digital transactions from their smartphone. Via BaridiMob, users can transfer money to others, pay bills, recharge phones, and view account balances (https://www.mpt.gov.dz/strengthen-financial-inclusion-and-widespread-of-the-e-payment/#:~:text=Strengthen%20Financial%20Inclusion%20and%20Widespread,apps%20in%20Algeria%20on). It has become Algeria’s most downloaded financial app. In early 2023, BaridiMob was processing over **2.6 million transactions per month** (https://www.aps.dz/en/algeria/tag/Epayment#:~:text=Epayment%20,of%202023%2C%20the%20Minister). In parallel, Algérie Poste launched **BaridiPay**, a QR code payment service integrated into BaridiMob that enables instant retail payments without a physical card (https://www.dzair-tube.dz/en/algerie-poste-launches-baridi-pay-mobile-payment-service-a-bold-step-toward-a-cashless-card-free-economy/#:~:text=tube,the%20need%20for%20bank). This is aimed at merchants and informal markets to further promote cashless payments. Together, BaridiMob/BaridiPay form a fast-growing digital payments ecosystem leveraging Algeria’s extensive postal network. Adoption is growing quickly (13 million e-payments via BaridiMob in Jan–May 2023 (https://www.aps.dz/en/algeria/tag/Epayment#:~:text=Epayment%20,of%202023%2C%20the%20Minister), nearly double year-on-year). These services significantly enhance the utility of Edahabia and drive the migration from cash to electronic payments in everyday transactions.

sistemas.descricao: Managed by Centre de Pré-compensation Interbancaire (CPI); dematerialised clearing replacing manual houses since 2006 with daily multilateral netting to ARTS.
Live since 2006; processes interbank and BoA operations in dinars with liquidity facilities.
RTGS system for large-value payments in Algeria
sistemas.detalhes: ARTS is Algeria’s RTGS system operated by the Bank of Algeria to settle high-value interbank payments in real time. In French it is the **Règlement Brut en Temps Réel** system. All major banks and the central bank participate. ARTS has significantly reduced systemic risk and settlement times for large transactions. For example, by 2013 the RTGS processed ~290,000 payments annually (https://fr.scribd.com/document/705902882/Les-Moyens-de-Paiement-Et-La-Monetique-en-Algerie-Bejaya#:~:text=Le%20nombre%20d%E2%80%99op%C3%A9ration%20effectu%C3%A9%20par,de%20l%E2%80%99ann%C3%A9e%202013%2C%20est%20de), with a total value of DA 358,000 billion (hundreds of trillions of dinars) (https://fr.scribd.com/document/705902882/Les-Moyens-de-Paiement-Et-La-Monetique-en-Algerie-Bejaya#:~:text=Le%20nombre%20d%E2%80%99op%C3%A9ration%20effectu%C3%A9%20par,de%20l%E2%80%99ann%C3%A9e%202013%2C%20est%20de). Transactions are final and irrevocable once settled in ARTS. The system typically handles government securities trades, interbank transfers, and other urgent payments. Adoption is very high among banks – ARTS is the primary channel for wholesale payments. The central bank is also connecting to the regional SADC-RTGS to facilitate cross-border settlements (https://pti.ao/bna-esclarece-ambito-da-integracao-do-kwanza-no-sistema-da-sadc/#:~:text=BNA%20esclarece%20%C3%A2mbito%20da%20integra%C3%A7%C3%A3o,pagamento%20angolanos%20ao%20sistema) (https://angolex.com/paginas/avisos/participacao-no-sistema-de-liquidacao-bruto-em-tempo-real-da-sadc-03a-2025a.html#:~:text=Aviso%20n,SPTR). Overall, ARTS is a cornerstone of Algeria’s modern payment infrastructure.

sistemas.descricao: Interbank transfers

The SPI is the interbank clearing system for retail payments in Ecuador [oai_citation:129‡esigef.finanzas.gob.ec]. Managed by the central bank, it channels electronic fund transfers such as payroll deposits, person-to-person bank transfers (that are not immediate), and recurring payments across banks. Banks send their transfer instructions to the SPI central system, which sorts and clears them in deferred cycles. Typically, there are multiple clearing batches per day for the SPI, enabling same-day or next-day fund availability for most transactions. The SPI also encompasses a direct debit system known as SCI (Sistema de Cobros Interbancarios) for interbank debit pulls [oai_citation:130‡bce.fin.ec], and possibly check clearing integration. All banks and many cooperatives participate. Final settlement of net positions from SPI cycles occurs in SPL (the RTGS) at designated times. The message format was originally proprietary (fixed-length records for each transfer), but BCE has been migrating SPI to ISO 20022 (pain messages for submissions). SPI significantly increased efficiency and electronic payment usage in Ecuador, especially after the adoption of the US dollar, as it replaced older paper instruments. It’s the backbone for everyday transactions like utilities and intra-country remittances.
sistemas.detalhes: Ecuador’s SPI is the national interbank payment system operated by the Banco Central del Ecuador (BCE). Since Ecuador is dollarized (uses USD), SPI provides the mechanism for domestic USD transfers between banks (https://www.bce.fin.ec/sistema-de-pagos/sistema-central-de-pagos/sistema-de-pagos-interbancarios-spi/#:~:text=Ecuador%20www,a%20trav%C3%A9s%20de%20bancos%2C). It functions as a hybrid RTGS and ACH: high-value and urgent transfers settle continuously in real time, while bulk low-value transfers are cleared in batches. The SPI connects banks, public entities, and cooperatives via the central bank’s network, enabling electronic credit transfers for the public and private sector (https://www.bce.fin.ec/sistema-de-pagos/sistema-central-de-pagos/sistema-de-pagos-interbancarios-spi/#:~:text=Ecuador%20www,a%20trav%C3%A9s%20de%20bancos%2C). Adoption is high – virtually all financial institutions participate. SPI processes millions of transactions yearly, including payroll, government payments, and bank transfers, all in US dollars. It has significantly modernized payments post-dollarization, ensuring efficient in-country USD circulation without relying on correspondent banking for local settlements.

sistemas.descricao: Defunct central bank digital cash project (2014–2018)
sistemas.detalhes: Dinero Electrónico was a pioneering electronic money system launched by Ecuador’s central bank in 2014. It allowed citizens to hold and transfer USD balances via a mobile phone platform managed by the central bank – effectively a retail CBDC ahead of its time. Users could open e-money accounts linked to their ID, deposit cash at partner agents (e.g., cooperatives and telecom stores), and make P2P transfers or merchant payments by USSD/SMS. While innovative, it saw limited adoption (around 400,000 users at peak) due to mistrust and competition from banks. In 2018, the government terminated Dinero Electrónico and passed regulation transferring mobile money initiatives to the private sector. Although short-lived, it provided lessons and infrastructure that paved the way for subsequent private mobile wallet solutions in Ecuador.

sistemas.descricao: BIMO is a mobile wallet service launched in 2019 by Ecuador’s private financial institutions (through BANRED network) as the replacement for the central bank’s e-money . BIMO allows users to register their phone with a participating bank and send or receive small payments instantly using the mobile app or USSD. It’s interoperable across banks and works 24/7. The wallet is capped at modest balances (e.g., $50 limit) to target micro-payments . Early adoption was slow – by end of 2020, BIMO had about 75,000 active users – due to limited merchant acceptance and user awareness . However, the service is growing as more banks promote it for person-to-person transfers and QR code payments in shops. BIMO aims to improve financial inclusion by offering a low-cost digital payment alternative linked to the banking system.
sistemas.detalhes: BIMO is a mobile wallet service launched in 2019 by Ecuador’s private financial institutions (through BANRED network) as the replacement for the central bank’s e-money (https://www.bankingly.com/es/noticias/que-significa-bimo-para-las-instituciones-financieras-y-como-pueden-aumentar-su-impacto/#:~:text=,a%20donde%20quiera%20que). BIMO allows users to register their phone with a participating bank and send or receive small payments instantly using the mobile app or USSD. It’s interoperable across banks and works 24/7. The wallet is capped at modest balances (e.g., $50 limit) to target micro-payments (https://gk.city/2020/02/19/funciona-bimo-dinero-electronico/#:~:text=%C2%BFFunciona%20BIMO%3F%20Los%20problemas%20del,no%20es%20la%20mejor%3A). Early adoption was slow – by end of 2020, BIMO had about 75,000 active users (https://www.primicias.ec/noticias/economia/billetera-movil-75000-usuarios-ecuador/#:~:text=La%20Billetera%20M%C3%B3vil%20ya%20tiene,o%20usuarios%20de%20la%20BIMO) – due to limited merchant acceptance and user awareness (https://gk.city/2020/02/19/funciona-bimo-dinero-electronico/#:~:text=%C2%BFFunciona%20BIMO%3F%20Los%20problemas%20del,no%20es%20la%20mejor%3A). However, the service is growing as more banks promote it for person-to-person transfers and QR code payments in shops. BIMO aims to improve financial inclusion by offering a low-cost digital payment alternative linked to the banking system.

sistemas.descricao: Bank-issued Visa/Mastercard cards and ATM networks
sistemas.detalhes: Ecuador’s banks issue Visa and Mastercard debit cards (linked to savings accounts) and credit cards, which are widely used for ATM withdrawals and in-store payments. The country’s ATM/POS network is shared by processors like **Banred** and **Redbanc**. Card usage grew after dollarization – by the 2020s, card payment value and count have steadily risen each year. For example, in 2022 the number of card transactions was in the hundreds of millions, as more merchants adopted POS terminals. Diners Club is also popular in Ecuador, historically offered via Diners Club Ecuador. While cash remains common, cards play a significant role, especially in urban areas and for e-commerce. Ecuador does not have a domestic-only card scheme; all operate on international networks. Nearly all ATMs accept global cards, and contactless technology is being rolled out. Adoption is medium-high and increasing as the economy digitizes.

sistemas.descricao: The Central Bank of Ecuador (BCE) operates the Sistema de Pagos en Línea (SPL), which is the RTGS for Ecuador’s dollarized economy [oai_citation:125‡esigef.finanzas.gob.ec]. SPL handles high-value and urgent interbank transfers in US dollars (the official currency) with immediate settlement. It was introduced in the 2000s as part of payment system modernization and runs on a 24/7 basis to accommodate continuous settlement needs. Banks, cooperatives, and the government maintain accounts at the BCE for settlement. SPL processes large-value customer payments, interbank money market settlements, and time-critical public sector payments. It uses a SWIFT-based system for messaging and ensures finality upon posting to the central bank ledger. Given full dollarization, SPL plays a crucial role in circulating liquidity among banks. By design, it integrates with other subsystems: for example, the securities settlement system and ATM network settlements. The system’s availability and capacity were enhanced over time. In recent years the BCE has worked on adopting ISO 20022 for SPL messages [oai_citation:126‡cemla.org]. SPL’s reliability underpins confidence in Ecuador’s financial transactions since there is no local currency lender of last resort beyond efficient payment processing.
Mobile payments
Real-time transfers
Operated by Eesti Pank; ISO 20022 XML messages settle interbank and monetary-policy transactions.
Estonian PSPs can settle SCT Inst directly in central-bank money via TIPS.
Clears SCT Inst within seconds; settlement in TARGET2; instant payments now the majority of Estonian retail euro transfers.
Provides debit, prepaid and tokenised e-commerce acceptance nationwide; interoperable at ATMs and POS.
Electronic payment network
Egypt's high-value payment system for instantaneous interbank settlements
Handles payroll, direct debits and government payments with next-day settlement windows.
Processes large-value and urgent interbank, government and securities payments in real time via SWIFT Y-Copy.
Launched in 2022, processed $53B in 2024 (up from $3.6B in 2023). Supports 24/7 interbank transfers, remittances, and integrations with Apple/Google Pay. 11.5M+ users registered .
Nearly exclusive payment method
Eritrea lacks a dedicated national RTGS or instant-payment scheme; intrabank postings dominate and interbank transfers rely on manual batch files or correspondent banking.

Bizum is a real-time payment service launched in Spain in November 2016 by a consortium of Spanish banks (under the authority of the Bank of Spain) [oai_citation:4‡bde.es]. It allows consumers to send money via mobile phone to contacts instantly. Settlement is done as instant SEPA credit transfers through the SNCE clearing system [oai_citation:5‡bde.es].
Payment processor

SNCE is the centralized retail payment clearing system in Spain, managed by Iberpay (a consortium of banks) under oversight of the Bank of Spain. Since 2011 it processes SEPA Credit Transfers, SEPA Direct Debits, cheques and bills, settling net positions via TARGET2-Banco de España [oai_citation:3‡bde.es].

TARGET2 is the Eurosystem’s real-time gross settlement system for euro payments. The Bank of Spain participates by operating the Spanish component of TARGET2. High-value wholesale and interbank transfers are settled through TARGET2-ES (BaŃco de España) via SWIFT or local gateways.

sistemas.detalhes: Operated by Groupement des Cartes Bancaires CB, this national payment scheme processes over 95% of French card transactions. Cards are typically debit or deferred debit (single monthly withdrawal). Uses EMV chip-and-PIN technology with contactless functionality (up to €50 without PIN). STET operates the clearing infrastructure under Banque de France oversight . The system combines domestic routing for French transactions with international network capabilities via Visa/Mastercard partnerships.

sistemas.detalhes: Operated by STET (owned by major French banks) under Banque de France oversight, processes SEPA Credit Transfers, SEPA Direct Debits and domestic instruments. Uses deferred net settlement with daily multilateral clearing through T2. Processes high-volume, low-value transactions with next-day settlement. Subject to ECB oversight as a systemically important payment system .

Features include: free checkbooks for consumers, €1,000 cash payment limit, and strict penalties for bounced cheques (5-year banking ban). Retailers may refuse cheques with posted notices .

Uses advanced controls including satellite imagery for agricultural aid verification. Processes payments through banking networks to millions of beneficiaries .

Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system operated by the Central Bank of Central African States (BEAC) for large-value interbank payments.

SYSTAC (Système de Compensation Automatisé) is the regional clearing system for batch processing of payments like checks, credit transfers and commercial bills. It nets obligations among banks and settles periodically, typically at the central bank, enabling efficient processing of retail and interbank transactions across Gabon and CEMAC [oai_citation:4‡mfw4a.org].

GIMAC (Groupement Interbancaire Monétique Afrique Centrale) is a regional card-payment switch in the CEMAC zone, enabling Gabonese banks to issue and accept domestic EMV chip cards. Launched in 2016, it allows bank customers to withdraw cash and pay at merchants across CEMAC countries using the GIMAC-branded cards [oai_citation:7‡mfw4a.org]. GIMAC is co-owned by participating banks and operated by an interbank group, promoting cashless payments regionally.

Operated by the Central Bank of Central African States (BEAC), SYGMA settles high-value wholesale transfers (above defined CFA thresholds) on a real-time, transaction-by-transaction basis. It ensures immediate finality of large interbank payments across Gabon and other CEMAC countries [oai_citation:1‡mfw4a.org]. All commercial banks in the zone use SYGMA for large transfers, reducing settlement risk by settling in central bank money.

Airtel Money is a mobile wallet launched in Gabon for person-to-person transfers, bill payments and merchant purchases via USSD or app. It allows users to deposit/withdraw cash and send money via mobile phones. In CEMAC overall, mobile money is dominant – the two telecom operators have mobilized 2.4 billion transactions (≈107 trillion XAF) by 2022, accounting for ~98% of opened payment accounts [oai_citation:9‡4mlegaltax.com]. Gabonese customers can transfer funds between Airtel Money wallets and bank accounts.

Orange Money is a mobile wallet service offered by Orange in Central African countries including Gabon. It enables mobile-based transfers, bill payments and merchant payments via smartphone or feature phone. Users can cash in/out at Orange agents or bank branches. It is interoperable with other CEMAC mobile money networks and bank accounts, contributing to the high uptake of digital payments in the region [oai_citation:11‡4mlegaltax.com].

The Faster Payments Service enables near-real-time transfers (seconds) between bank accounts in the UK, 24/7. Launched in 2008 (now run by Pay.UK), it supports account-to-account and bill payments. It handled around 4.9 billion transactions in 2023 [oai_citation:17‡ukfinance.org.uk]ww.ukfinance.org.uk/system/files/2024-07/Summary%20UK%20Payment%20Markets%202024.pdf#:~:text=strongly,of%20payments%20made%20by%20consumers), making it the backbone of everyday retail payments.
sistemas.detalhes: Operated by Pay.UK, FPS enables near real-time sterling payments 24/7 with transaction completion typically under 2 seconds. It uses a bilateral net settlement model with multiple daily settlements through the Bank of England's RTGS system. Supports account-to-account (A2A) payments, mobile banking transactions, and is being enhanced for ISO 20022 messaging standards .

sistemas.descricao: CHAPS is the UK’s RTGS system (operated by the Bank of England) for sterling high-value wholesale and interbank payments. It settles transactions on the same day with finality. CHAPS handled 51.1 million payments in 2023, valued at £91.5 trillion [oai_citation:14‡ukfinance.org.uk]ww.ukfinance.org.uk/system/files/2024-07/Summary%20UK%20Payment%20Markets%202024.pdf#:~:text=51%C2%A0million%20CHAPS%20payments%20processed%20in,CHAPS), reflecting its critical role in large transactions (it accounted for ~0.1% of volume but 88% of value [oai_citation:15‡ukfinance.org.uk]ww.ukfinance.org.uk/system/files/2024-07/Summary%20UK%20Payment%20Markets%202024.pdf#:~:text=2023%20CHAPS%20accounted%20for%20just,CHAPS)).
sistemas.detalhes: Operated by the Bank of England, CHAPS processes high-value (£10k+ typically) and time-critical payments (e.g., property transactions) using real-time gross settlement (RTGS). It features 30+ direct participants and thousands of indirect participants. Payments settle individually in central bank money throughout the business day (6am-6pm) with liquidity-saving mechanisms. Governed by the RTGS/CHAPS Board with 99.8%+ operational resilience .

sistemas.detalhes: Dominant card schemes processing debit/credit transactions. Feature four-party model (cardholder, merchant, acquirer, issuer) with net settlement through RTGS. Operated by Visa Europe and Mastercard Europe respectively, both under Payment Systems Regulator (PSR) oversight. Currently under PSR market review for fee structures .

sistemas.detalhes: Open Banking-driven system for recurring account-to-account payments (e.g., subscriptions). Operated under Open Banking Limited (transitioning to FCA regulation). Uses API-based payment initiation with sweeping (same-bank) and non-sweeping (cross-bank) capabilities. Phase 2 implementation for merchant payments underway in 2025 .

Bacs is the UK’s batch clearing house. It includes Direct Credit (for salaries/pensions) and Direct Debit (for recurring payments). In 2023, Bacs Direct Credit processed about 2.2 billion payments [oai_citation:19‡vocal.media]ocal.media/trader/ap-is-and-automation-fueling-the-uk-s-real-time-payment-boom#:~:text=Resilience%20Through%20Bacs). Settlement takes a few days, and Bacs remains essential for payroll and billing cycles.

LINK is the UK’s nationwide ATM network, linking over 37,000 ATMs across banks and independents. It allows any bank’s customer to withdraw cash at any LINK ATM. In 2023, roughly 1.49 billion ATM transactions were processed [oai_citation:23‡link.co.uk]ww.link.co.uk/data-research#:~:text=2021%20%2099%2097%20114,112%20109%20114%20107%20639), making LINK central to cash access.

The Cheque and Credit Clearing Company processes interbank cheque payments in the UK using image-based clearing. Cheque usage has declined, but ~110 million cheques were written in 2023 [oai_citation:21‡ukfinance.org.uk]ww.ukfinance.org.uk/system/files/2024-07/Summary%20UK%20Payment%20Markets%202024.pdf#:~:text=The%20number%20of%20cheques%20used,Both). Cheque deposits are cleared overnight via this system.

CHAPS is the UK's high-value, same-day payment system, designed for transactions that are too large or too time-sensitive for other schemes. It has no upper limit on transaction value, and funds are guaranteed to settle on the same business day if initiated within operating hours. CHAPS payments are irrevocable upon settlement and are processed through the Bank of England's Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system. Due to its high fee per transfer and availability only during business days, CHAPS is typically reserved for critical transactions such as property completions, large corporate payments, and significant tax bills.

Handles bulk transactions like payroll and bill payments over 2-3 days. Processes Direct Debits and Direct Credits. Settled £5.62 trillion across 6.78B transactions in 2023. Transitioning to ISO 20022 under New Payments Architecture.
Card payments
Mobile wallet

As a member of the Eastern Caribbean Currency Union, Grenada uses the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank’s RTGS for large-value transactions in XCD (EC$). ECCB’s RTGS settles interbank transfers among commercial banks instantly in central bank money. It handles wholesale and time-critical payments for all ECCU members.

The Eastern Caribbean ACH processes bulk, retail payments (small-value transfers, checks, direct credits/debits) across ECCU banks. It nets participants’ obligations and settles via the ECCB. The ACH facilitates wage payments, bill payments and check clearing by batch. (The ECCB site refers to the ACH as "Eastern Caribbean Automated Clearing House.")

DCash is the ECCB’s digital EC dollar, launched in a pilot on 12 March 2019 [oai_citation:44‡eccb-centralbank.org]. It is a blockchain-based central bank digital currency used via mobile wallets. DCash is issued by the ECCB and distributed by licensed banks to allow P2P transfers and purchases on mobile devices. It remains in pilot but aims to deepen financial inclusion and efficiency [oai_citation:45‡eccb-centralbank.org].
Mobile wallet

An instant payment system is under development by the National Bank of Georgia to enable real-time retail payments with ISO 20022 messaging.

The NBG and government are piloting a new instant payment platform for retail GEL transfers. Scheduled for rollout, it will enable account-to-account payments in seconds at all hours. Once implemented, it will be a P2P/payments 24×7 service across banks, likely using ISO 20022 rails. (As of 2024 it remains in development.)
The National Bank of Georgia is developing a new RTGS system with ISO 20022 standards, aiming to enhance real-time settlement capabilities.

The National Bank of Georgia operates an RTGS for high-value interbank transfers. All banks hold settlement accounts and can send/receive high-value payments 24/7 through this system, ensuring immediate finality. It processes both large and time-critical transactions via SWIFT/ISO messaging. The NBG also uses it to settle securities, providing delivery-versus-payment by linking to the Central Securities Depository. [oai_citation:18‡nbg.gov.ge]

United Financial Corporation (UFC) is the other main card processing company in Georgia. UFC provides authorization and clearing for bank cards (both local and international brands) and supplies payment terminals. Along with Georgian Card, it ensures interoperability among banks’ ATMs and POS for card transactions [oai_citation:22‡nbg.gov.ge].

Georgian Card is a major domestic card processor in Georgia. Together with United Financial Corporation (UFC), it runs the interbank card-switching networks for debit and credit cards. Both companies handle the majority of card transactions in Georgia, processing local and international card payments (Visa/Mastercard) on behalf of member banks [oai_citation:20‡nbg.gov.ge].
Dominant mobile wallet
Competing mobile wallet

GhIPSS runs the "Gh-link" national switch integrating banks’ ATM and POS networks. Launched 2015, it connects all banks, allowing any bank’s customers to use ATMs or POS of other banks seamlessly. It also settles card-based and interbank mobile transfers. In 2015, ~1.9 million transactions (GH¢305M) passed through Gh-link [oai_citation:36‡bog.gov.gh].

GhIPSS also provides a direct debit scheme under the ACH for merchants and utilities to pull funds from payer accounts with authorization. According to BoG, about 693,000 direct-debit transactions occurred in 2015 (≈GH¢70.9M) [oai_citation:33‡bog.gov.gh], showing usage by large billers.

GIP is Ghana’s instant payment platform operated by GhIPSS, launched 2018. It allows near-instant interbank transfers between accounts via mobile apps or bank platforms, 24×7. Funds are credited within seconds. GIP leverages an ISO 20022-based switch under GhIPSS, and its uptake is growing among banks.

The Bank of Ghana operates a real-time gross settlement system for high-value interbank transactions. Interbank transfers (large or urgent payments) are settled immediately and irrevocably on this platform, ensuring final settlement of funds in central bank money. It is used by all commercial banks and government to move funds in large sums.

e-zwich is Ghana’s national biometric smart card scheme. Managed by GhIPSS, it provides debit card functionality (at ATMs/POS) and serves as an electronic wallet. Cards store user credentials and account balances, enabling withdrawals, deposits, and transfers. In 2015 there were ~1.37M e-zwich holders, with 2.25M transactions (GH¢922.9M) that year [oai_citation:39‡bog.gov.gh].

GhIPSS ACH handles batch processing of credit transfers and other retail payments. Banks submit instructions (e.g. salary payments, bills) which are netted and settled in batch cycles. It enables efficient clearing of retail transactions across Ghanaian banks.

GhIPSS MMI is a clearing service allowing users of different mobile-money networks (e.g. MTN MoMo, Vodafone Cash) to transfer funds to each other or to bank accounts seamlessly. It settles these wallet-to-wallet, wallet-to-bank, and bank-to-wallet transfers through the central switch, fostering financial inclusion.
Mobile payment service
Dominant payment method

The Central Bank runs an Automated Clearing House (ACH) for offsetting checks and bulk electronic payments (direct credits/debits). Banks submit checks and credit transfers into the system in daily batches. The ACH nets positions and settles at the central bank, replacing physical check exchange and enabling automated retail payments processing [oai_citation:15‡cbg.gm].

The Securities Settlement System (SSS) handles delivery-versus-payment of government and central bank securities. It allows banks to settle trades in government bills/bonds via book entries, ensuring synchronized transfer of securities and funds. It is integrated with the RTGS for funds finality. (No public volumes available.)

The Central Bank of The Gambia operates an RTGS platform as part of the Gambia Electronic Payment and Settlement System (GEPSS). It settles large-value and time-critical interbank transfers in real time, 8am–3:45pm on business days. The RTGS offers liquidity management tools (e.g. intraday repo facilities) and high security, ensuring large payments are transferred final and irrevocably between banks [oai_citation:13‡cbg.gm].

Q-Money is the mobile wallet service of QCell in Gambia. It allows users to deposit, withdraw and transfer money via their phone, and to pay merchants and utility bills using USSD or an app. Q-Money is interoperable with banks and other wallets, enabling seamless transfers between mobile wallets and bank accounts.

Wave is a fintech mobile money provider operating in Gambia. It offers an account accessible via phone app/USSD for P2P transfers, bill payments, and cash in/out at agents. Wave transactions interoperate with bank accounts via the national switch. As with other mobile money, it plays a major role in Gambia’s digital payments ecosystem.

GamSwitch is a public–private national payment switch launched by the Central Bank of Gambia. It links all commercial banks, enabling shared ATM and POS networks and real-time interbank transfers (P2P) across banks and mobile channels. The platform supports online clearing of all Gambian banks and billers, facilitating e-commerce and mobile payments. According to the CBG, GamSwitch provides "full online payment integration of all banks, billing systems and electronic channels such as ATMs, POS, Web and Mobile" [oai_citation:17‡cbg.gm].
Mobile payment service
Primary payment method

Banque Centrale de la République de Guinée (BCRG) operates an RTGS for final settlement of large interbank transfers in GNF. All banks maintain central bank accounts, and large-value payments (e.g. corporate transfers, government payments) are settled immediately through this platform [oai_citation:49‡imf.org].

BCRG also provides an ACH for netting and clearing bulk retail payments (e.g. payroll, bills, checks) between banks. Transactions are collected throughout the day and netted off for settlement at intervals. This ACH system supports the majority of low-value payment flows in Guinea [oai_citation:51‡imf.org].

MTN Mobile Money is a major mobile payment platform in Guinea. Users can deposit/withdraw cash at MTN agents, and send money or pay merchants via phone. It interconnects with banks for cash in/out and supports person-to-person transfers within MTN’s network.

BCRG’s securities settlement system (CSD) ensures delivery versus payment for government and central bank securities. Securities trades are settled on a DvP basis via this system, reducing settlement risk. It is integrated with the RTGS for the cash leg of securities transactions [oai_citation:53‡imf.org].
Airtel Money offers similar mobile payment services via the Airtel network. Customers can use it for transfers, bill payments and merchant purchases through Airtel’s USSD and agent network.
