KNET (Shared Electronic Banking Services) operates Kuwait’s interbank ATM and POS network [oai_citation:59‡cbk.gov.kw]. All local banks route card transactions through KNET, enabling cardholders to withdraw cash or pay merchants across banks.

GCC-Net links Kuwait’s ATM and POS network with other GCC countries (initially Bahrain/Qatar) [oai_citation:61‡cbk.gov.kw]. It allows customers from one GCC bank to use another country’s ATMs/POS seamlessly, settling transactions across borders under a common switch.

KECCS is Kuwait’s automated clearinghouse for paper KWD cheques. Introduced in 2015, it converts cheques into electronic images for processing [oai_citation:57‡cbk.gov.kw], enabling same-day collection and settlement of cheque payments via net positions in the RTGS.

This platform (developed with the Ministry of Finance) centralizes all public revenues/expenditures through a single treasury account system [oai_citation:63‡cbk.gov.kw]. It automates payments to government entities and manages cash budgeting efficiently.

KASSIP (Kuwait Automated Settlement System for Inter-Participant Payments) is the central RTGS system operated by the Central Bank of Kuwait [oai_citation:55‡cbk.gov.kw]. It provides immediate, final settlement for interbank transfers among local banks and the CBK. KASSIP uses SWIFT messaging for secure, real-time settlement.

sistemas.nome: KASSIP (Kuwait Automated Settlement System for Inter-participant Payments)

sistemas.descricao: Super-app ecosystem
National standard

The ISMT (Interbank System of Money Transfer) is Kazakhstan’s RTGS for national currency payments. Established in 2000, it processes high-value transfers on a real-time, gross basis [oai_citation:47‡is.ambis.cz]. All licensed banks participate, and payments are final and irrevocable upon settlement.

Kazakhstan’s instant payment service allows bank customers to send money to another bank account 24/7 using a mobile phone number alias [oai_citation:49‡astanatimes.com]. Operated by the NBK and National Payments Corp, it offers real-time final settlement for small-value retail transfers, with low fees to encourage adoption.
National switch

A Lao national QR code payment scheme launched in 2020. It enables instant mobile payments by scanning QR codes and supports cross-border QR payments (e.g. with Cambodia) in local currencies [oai_citation:19‡fintechnews.sg].

The Bank of Lao PDR’s real-time gross settlement (RTGS) system, introduced in June 2020 [oai_citation:11‡fintechnews.sg]. It provides 24/7 immediate settlement of interbank transfers and securities, linking Laos to SEPA/TIPS for euro transactions.

A mobile wallet and payment app by Lao Telecom (Lao Mobile Money), launched in 2020 [oai_citation:21‡thefintechtimes.com]. It allows QR-payments, peer transfers, bill payments, and remittances. It has over 30,000 merchants and 3,500+ cash agents at launch [oai_citation:22‡thefintechtimes.com].

The Bank of the Lao PDR has established a national QR payment standard to facilitate interoperable QR code payments across different banks and payment service providers. This system supports cross-border QR connectivity, particularly with Vietnam and other ASEAN countries through the Regional Payment Connectivity initiative. The standard enables instant retail payments through mobile banking applications.

Operated by BCEL, LapNet is a shared ATM network linking 14 member banks (BCEL, LVB, APB, LDB, JDB, etc.) [oai_citation:13‡bcel.com.la]. It lets customers use any member bank’s ATM for withdrawals and balance inquiries 24/7.

LaPASS (Lao Payment and Settlement System) is the integrated payment infrastructure operated by the Bank of the Lao PDR. The system combines Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) for high-value transactions and Automated Clearing House (ACH) for retail payments. Launched in July 2020, LaPASS supports ISO 20022 standards and provides comprehensive settlement services for both large-value and retail transactions. The system connects all banks in Laos and enables real-time interbank payments.

Introduced in 2015 by the central bank with China UnionPay, this system processes all domestic card transactions in Laos [oai_citation:15‡thefintechtimes.com]. Most Lao cards are UnionPay-branded, and the system connects all ATMs/POS nationwide. By 2015, UnionPay had issued ~600,000 cards (70% of Laos’s total) [oai_citation:16‡globaltimes.cn].
Primary payment method
Money transfer
A mechanism managed by BDL for government salary and social benefit payments. It ensures same-day credit of state disbursements to beneficiaries [oai_citation:36‡lana.gov.ly].

BDL-RTGS is Lebanon's real-time gross settlement system operated by the Central Bank of Lebanon (Banque du Liban). The system went live in July 2012 and supports four currencies: Lebanese Pound (LBP), US Dollar (USD), Euro (EUR), and British Pound (GBP). Each participant maintains separate settlement accounts for each currency. The system processes large-value and time-critical payments with electronic signatures and data encryption, with a minimum transaction value of 10,000 LYD.

A new fintech-issued e-wallet focused on diaspora remittances and ATM cash-out. Licensed by the central bank in 2023, it aims to provide low-cost transfers and financial inclusion [oai_citation:40‡fintechfutures.com].
A mobile/e-wallet service with a prepaid Visa card. Licensed by Banque du Liban [oai_citation:38‡suyool.com], it allows users (including unbanked) to transact and withdraw cash via the Visa network.
Global card networks (Visa, Mastercard, etc.) used by Lebanese banks. These enable debit/credit card payments and ATM withdrawals at merchants and ATMs.

BDL-CLEAR is Lebanon's automated retail payment system that went live in November 2013. The system handles the clearing and settlement of retail payment instruments including cheques, electronic funds transfers, and card transactions. BDL-CLEAR operates as part of Lebanon's National Payment System infrastructure and processes high-volume, low-value transactions with same-day or next-day settlement.
Common payment method
Same as Saint Kitts: Eastern Caribbean Central Bank’s RTGS for large-value EC dollar payments:contentReference[oaicite:30]{index=30}.

DCash is the ECCB’s digital currency pilot (launched Mar 2019) [oai_citation:35‡eccb-centralbank.org]. It is a centrally issued electronic version of the Eastern Caribbean dollar (DCash). Licensed banks and fintechs distribute DCash; consumers can send DCash to each other or pay merchants via a smartphone app or QR code [oai_citation:36‡eccb-centralbank.org]. The pilot assesses inclusion and efficiency gains of a CBDC within the ECCU.

4Cs (Caribbean Credit Card Corporation) is the regional switch that processes domestic Visa and Mastercard transactions in the ECCU. It authorizes and settles ATM and POS transactions across member states, enabling cross-border card usage within ECCU. Net settlement among banks is done through ECCB accounts.
Same as Saint Kitts: ECCB’s DCash pilot digital EC dollar for P2P and merchant payments:contentReference[oaicite:33]{index=33}.

ECACH is the Eastern Caribbean Automated Clearing House, a net-settlement system set up by ECCB and banks in 2014 [oai_citation:34‡eccb-centralbank.org]. It clears domestic cheques, direct debits and batch credit transfers. Cheque clearing uses imaging (ANSI X9.100-187) and credit transfers use a NACHA-like format. Net obligations are settled via the central RTGS.
Same as Saint Kitts: 4Cs for Visa/Mastercard processing in the ECCU:contentReference[oaicite:32]{index=32}.

The ECCB operates a RTGS (LVPS) for the Eastern Caribbean Currency Union, settling high-value interbank and government XCD payments in real time [oai_citation:33‡eccb-centralbank.org]. It provides irrevocable settlement via SWIFT messaging for all large transactions among member banks and governments.
Integration with Swiss infrastructure
Mobile banking

Liechtenstein participates in Switzerland’s instant payments platform introduced in Nov 2023 [oai_citation:64‡llb.li]. This service (SIC4 Instant) allows banks to send 24/7 real-time transfers (up to CHF/EUR20k) between accounts.
Visa and Mastercard are widely accepted for bank cards in Liechtenstein, enabling domestic and international ATM and merchant payments.

As an EEA member in the euro area, Liechtenstein banks use EU systems (TARGET2, TIPS) for euro payments. The ECB and Bank of Lithuania infrastructure provide SEPA credit transfers and instant payments.

Through Liechtenstein's currency union with Switzerland, the country has access to the Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) system for Swiss franc payments. The Swiss National Bank serves as Liechtenstein's central bank, providing access to Swiss payment infrastructure. This includes SIC5 IP (instant payments) and traditional Swiss franc clearing and settlement services.

Due to the monetary union with Switzerland, Liechtenstein banks use the Swiss SIC and RTGS systems (run by SNB/SIX) for Swiss franc transfers [oai_citation:62‡bankenverband.li]. These provide real-time settlement for CHF payments.

Liechtenstein participates fully in the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) as an EEA member, enabling seamless euro payments across Europe. The system supports SEPA Credit Transfers, SEPA Direct Debits, and SEPA Instant Payments with processing times under 10 seconds. Banks like LGT utilize advanced payment hubs to comply with EU instant payment regulations and provide 24/7 payment services.
National payment app
Super-app wallet

LANKAQR is Sri Lanka’s national QR payment standard launched in July 2019 by the Central Bank and all major banks [oai_citation:9‡lankapay.net]. It allows QR-based payments for P2P and merchant transactions. All participating banks issue interoperable static and dynamic QR codes linked to accounts for seamless fund transfers.

CEFTS is Sri Lanka’s real-time gross settlement platform operated by LankaClear (LankaPay). It was first used in 2016 (by Commercial Bank) and officially mandated by the Central Bank in 2018 [oai_citation:6‡en.wikipedia.org]. CEFTS enables instant 24/7 transfers across banks (up to LKR 5 million) between customer accounts and is integrated with central bank RTGS for settlement [oai_citation:7‡en.wikipedia.org].

LankaPay Card is a joint national debit card launched in March 2022 by a consortium of Sri Lankan banks (LankaPay) in partnership with JCB. It provides a low-cost domestic alternative to international cards, used for ATM and PoS transactions. The scheme is overseen by the Central Bank [oai_citation:8‡lankapay.net].

SLIPS is the Sri Lankan automated clearing house operated by LankaClear on behalf of the Central Bank. Introduced in 1993 (upgraded online in 2010), it provides same-day retail credit transfers (T+0) in two cycles per day. Transactions (e.g. payroll, vendor payments) are net settled via the central bank RTGS.
Primary payment method
A mobile financial service by Orange Liberia (formerly Cellcom/Tigo). It allows customers to send money, pay bills, top up airtime, and access other financial services via phone.
Visa and Mastercard networks are supported by Liberian banks for issuing debit/credit cards and accepting payments at ATMs and merchants.

Operated by the Central Bank of Liberia, this RTGS settles large-value interbank transfers and securities transactions [oai_citation:46‡cbl.org.lr]. It ensures immediate settlement for critical payments.

A unified ACH that handles checks, credit/debit transfers, card transactions and other retail instruments by batching them. All ordinary retail payments are netted through this system [oai_citation:50‡cbl.org.lr].
An electronic settlement system for government bonds and notes. It maintains custody and book-entry accounting for Liberian government securities [oai_citation:48‡cbl.org.lr].

A mobile wallet app by MTN. It offers transfers, bill pay, QR-code payments and international remittances [oai_citation:54‡lonestarcell.com]. Over 10 million transactions have been processed, making it widely used in Liberia.

The National Electronic Payment Switch (NEPS) is Liberia's retail payment infrastructure that enables interoperability between banks, mobile money operators, and other payment service providers. Developed with TPS technology solutions, NEPS includes ATM/POS switching, card management, and utility bill payment capabilities. The system supports multi-bank hosting and provides gateways to international payment schemes.
Mobile payment service
Dominant payment method
Visa and Mastercard networks supported by local banks. Used for debit/credit cards at merchants and ATM withdrawals internationally.

Lesotho Wire is the country's Real-Time Gross Settlement system operated by the Central Bank of Lesotho since August 2006. The system processes large-value and time-critical payments (transactions of M100,000 and above) using SWIFT messaging. It connects all commercial banks and enables real-time settlement in central bank money. The system also processes government payments and provides liquidity management facilities for participants.

A mobile money service launched in 2013 by Vodacom. It allows payments and transfers via a smartphone app. In 2025, Vodacom opened M-Pesa to all networks (not just Vodacom subscribers) [oai_citation:44‡developingtelecoms.com].
An ACH that batches and nets routine customer payments (salaries, transfers, bills) for settlement. It processes smaller payments on a deferred schedule.

The Lesotho Automated Clearing House (LACH) processes small-value, large-volume transactions under M100,000. Implemented in 2012 with Bankserv Africa as the service provider, LACH handles Electronic Funds Transfers (EFTs), automated cheque clearing, ATM/debit card transactions, and real-time credits. The system provides same-day clearing and settlement for retail payment instruments.

LeSwitch is Lesotho's National Payment Switch launched in 2024 by the Central Bank of Lesotho. The system enables interoperability between different payment platforms including Point-of-Sale terminals, ATMs, mobile money systems, and e-commerce platforms. LeSwitch consolidates all domestic electronic transactions into a single central hub for authorization and processing, supporting 24/7 real-time payments and promoting financial inclusion.
National payment system
Fintech wallet
Visa and Mastercard dominate card payments. Lithuanian banks issue these cards and merchants accept them widely for consumer payments.
Real-time (instant) credit transfers in euros, processed via CENTROlink/TIPS. Usage surged to 128.1 million transactions (€137.6B) in 2022 [oai_citation:69‡lb.lt], showing broad adoption.

A registry by the Bank of Lithuania that links phone numbers to bank accounts. It allows users to initiate instant transfers by entering the beneficiary’s mobile number instead of IBAN [oai_citation:72‡lb.lt]. It had ~530,000 users by end-2022.
Real-time settlement
Mobile payments
SEPA Credit Transfers and SEPA Direct Debits for euro payments. These are the main batch payment methods for businesses and consumers (settled via SWIFT/T2S) in Luxembourg.
Luxembourgian banks can use the SEPA Instant Payments infrastructure (TARGET Instant Payment Settlement or EBA RT1) for real-time transfers. It enables immediate intra-day payments at any time.
Visa, Mastercard and other global card systems are widely used in Luxembourg for debit/credit card payments at merchants and ATM withdrawals.
Luxembourg banks participate in the Eurosystem’s TARGET2 RTGS for high-value euro transactions. The Banque centrale du Luxembourg provides the gateway for local banks.
Mobile payments
Real-time transfers

The Electronic Clearing System (EKS) is Latvijas Banka's payment system for processing customer payments across the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA). EKS provides both clearing services for regular payments and instant payment services available 24/7. The system processed 37.3 million instant payments totaling 16.6 billion euros in 2022, with over 99.9 % availability. EKS was the first instant payment system in the eurozone and supports non-bank payment service providers.
Visa, Mastercard, and other international card networks are the main payment card schemes in Latvia. They support local debit/credit card issuance and merchant acceptance at ATMs and POS.

TARGET-Latvija is Latvia's component system of the European TARGET real-time gross settlement system, operated by Latvijas Banka. The system processes interbank payments and monetary policy operations in central bank money. TARGET-Latvija provides efficient, fast and secure infrastructure for real-time processing of euro payments, settling an average of 641 payments daily with a value of 1.3 billion euros.

Part of the European TARGET2 system, this RTGS platform settles large-value euro payments for Latvian banks. Operated by Latvijas Banka, it handles urgent and high-value transfers in real time [oai_citation:24‡bank.lv].

Introduced in August 2017 [oai_citation:30‡bank.lv], the nationwide instant payments system (via LB) allows bank customers to transfer euros instantly at any time. Major banks (SEB, Swedbank, Citadele, etc.) participate.
Primary payment method

Libya's National Switch system launched in September 2008 connects banks for electronic payment processing. Initially implemented with four major banks and 112 networked ATMs, the system is operated by a financial services company owned by participating banks and financial institutions. The switch handles ATM and POS transactions domestically.
Major card networks (Visa, Mastercard) are offered by local banks for debit/credit cards, enabling payments and ATM withdrawals.
Libyan banks use the SWIFT network for cross-border payments and correspondent banking. It is the global standard for international fund transfers.

Libya's RTGS system implemented by the Central Bank of Libya in April 2008. The system processes high-value, low-volume transactions with real-time settlement in central bank money. Initially launched with 6 state banks, the system has expanded to include 13 direct participants. It provides the foundation for settlement of other payment systems and handles large-value interbank payments.
A real-time retail payment system being considered by the Central Bank (discussed in 2023) [oai_citation:60‡lana.gov.ly]. If launched, it would enable immediate P2P transfers at any time.

The ACH processes bulk and low-value payments such as salary disbursements and daily retail transactions. The central bank plans to use RTGS/ACH to ensure same-day government payroll transfers [oai_citation:58‡lana.gov.ly].
A real-time gross settlement system implemented in April 2008 [oai_citation:57‡cma.se]. It handles large-value and interbank payments for banks in Libya.

LYPay is Libya's instant payment system launched by the Central Bank of Libya in 2024. The service enables instant money transfers between individuals and QR code-based merchant payments. LYPay operates 24/7/365 with real-time settlement and is free of charge until end of 2024. The system has daily transfer limits of 500 dinars and purchase limits of 1,500 dinars during the trial period.
National payment processing
Mobile payment app

In June 2023 Bank Al-Maghrib and GSIMT launched an instant interbank transfer service [oai_citation:30‡bkam.ma]. It enables customers to send payments (up to MAD 20,000) across banks in <20 seconds, 24/7, initially free for individuals [oai_citation:31‡bkam.ma]. The system, operated by GSIMT, is ISO 20022–compliant and processes real-time mobile or account-to-account transfers [oai_citation:32‡bkam.ma].

SWAM (formerly HPS Switch) is Morocco’s central switching platform for card and electronic payments. It connects banks, acquirers, mobile wallets and fintechs. In 2024, SWAM processed ~401 million card payments (plus 5.3M mobile wallet transactions):contentReference[oaicite:21]{index=21}.

Morocco’s domestic Carte Bancaire (CB) scheme and international networks (Visa, Mastercard) facilitate consumer payments. Together they handled hundreds of millions of transactions in 2024:contentReference[oaicite:22]{index=22}.

The SRBM (Système des Règlements Bruts du Maroc) is Morocco’s RTGS, launched in 2006 [oai_citation:26‡cma.se]. It is operated by Bank Al-Maghrib (with CMA’s RTS/X technology). The system settles high-value transfers in real time and has been integrated with the national securities depository (Maroclear) since 2011 [oai_citation:27‡cma.se].

Bank Al-Maghrib (Morocco’s central bank) operates SRBM, the RTGS system for high-value dirham transactions:contentReference[oaicite:19]{index=19}. It provides intraday settlement and liquidity management for participant banks.
French card system
High-end payment systems

As a euro-using non-EU state, Monaco’s high-value payments settle through the Eurosystem’s TARGET2 system operated by Banque de France. Monaco joined the euro in 2002 and participates fully in SEPA [oai_citation:13‡ecb.europa.eu]. There is no separate Monaco RTGS; domestic payments use SEPA credit transfers/direct debits and SWIFT. This aligns Monaco’s payments with EU standards [oai_citation:14‡ecb.europa.eu].

Monaco has no central bank or currency of its own. Its banks use the euro and participate in EU payment infrastructures. High-value euro transfers are settled via the Eurosystem’s TARGET2 RTGS, effectively through French/Italian central banking links:contentReference[oaicite:8]{index=8}.

Monaco participates in the EU’s SEPA framework. Euro transfers (credit transfers and, from 2025, instantaneous transfers) follow SEPA standards. This aligns Monaco with EU payment space:contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}.
Most banks in Monaco participate in France’s Carte Bancaire (CB) scheme. French-issued CB cards and domestic CB transactions are accepted in Monaco.
Western Union and MoneyGram operate in Monaco, allowing residents to send and receive remittances internationally, supplementing formal banking transfers.
Visa and Mastercard cards are accepted by merchants in Monaco. These global networks facilitate consumer and business payments alongside domestic schemes.
National payment system
Mobile wallet

Moldova’s ACH (based on CMA BCS/X) processes retail and bulk payments (credit transfers, direct debits) [oai_citation:5‡cma.se]. It operates in batch/net cycles for smaller transactions in lei, with final settlement in the RTGS system. The ACH is integrated with the RTGS and securities systems [oai_citation:6‡cma.se].

The National Bank of Moldova uses a CMA Small Systems RTS/X platform (RTGS) for high-value transfers, launched in 2006 [oai_citation:2‡cma.se]. It settles interbank payments in lei on a gross-real-time basis. The system is integrated with securities settlement (Maroclear equivalent) and uses IBAN standards [oai_citation:3‡cma.se].

MPay is Moldova’s government payment gateway (since 2013) for paying taxes, fees and other public services online:contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}. By 2023 it had processed ~37 million transactions worth MDL 22.5 billion:contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}, serving millions of citizens.

Moldova’s central bank (BNM) operates SAPI, an automated interbank system for clearing and settlement. It includes an RTGS component for large-value transfers and an ACH component (batch clearing) for retail payments. In 2021, SAPI processed ~13.8M transactions worth MDL 1083B:contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}.
Visa and Mastercard are widely used in Moldova for POS purchases and ATM withdrawals. They operate via local acquirers and issuing banks to serve customers.

MIA is an instant payment platform launched in March 2024 [oai_citation:8‡cma.se]. It allows banks’ customers to send money in <15 seconds using a recipient’s phone number (no fees for users initially) [oai_citation:9‡cma.se]. Supported by most Moldovan banks, it handled over 100,000 transactions (~MDL 100 million) in its first six weeks [oai_citation:10‡centralbanking.com], and currently covers P2P and requests-to-pay (B2B/payouts coming later [oai_citation:11‡centralbanking.com]).

Moldmediacard is a major payment processing center in Moldova, handling about 40% of local bank cards, ATMs, and POS operations:contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}. It provides acquiring and processing for Visa, Mastercard, AmEx and also supports mobile wallets (Apple/Google Pay) for participating banks.
Mobile payments
Dominant payment method

The Central Bank of Montenegro operates an interbank payment system (launched 2005) combining RTGS and bulk clearing for euro payments:contentReference[oaicite:15]{index=15}. It processes interbank transfers in real time (RTGS) and in net batches for retail payments.
Visa and Mastercard cards are widely accepted in Montenegro. Banks issue MasterCard (and some Visa) for consumer and business transactions, ensuring broad card coverage.

Euro transfers between Montenegro and EU countries use the SEPA scheme (credit transfers and, when implemented, instant transfers). Montenegro is aligning with EU payment standards as it integrates further into European systems:contentReference[oaicite:18]{index=18}.

In May 2025, CBCG introduced the RTS/X system, merging RTGS with 24/7 on-line clearing for transfers up to €1,000 [oai_citation:21‡seenews.com]. Fully ISO 20022–compliant [oai_citation:22‡seenews.com], it provides instant availability of funds (non-reversible) and aligns Montenegro with EU norms. In April 2025 Montenegro processed ~€2.37B through its NPS [oai_citation:23‡montenegrobusiness.eu]. The RTS/X marks a major upgrade from the old deferred net settlement system.

Montenegro plans to launch an instant euro payments system based on Italy’s TIPS platform. A Letter of Intent was signed in 2025, with operations expected by mid-2026:contentReference[oaicite:16]{index=16}:contentReference[oaicite:17]{index=17}.

MVola (Mobinav) is the e-money service offered by Telma, the state-owned telecom operator. Users can perform peer-to-peer transfers, pay utility bills, and make merchant payments via the MVola app or USSD. Madagascar has around 23 million mobile money accounts across Orange Money, Airtel Money and MVola [oai_citation:2‡developingtelecoms.com].

Airtel Money is the mobile payment service provided by Airtel Madagascar for peer-to-peer transfers, bill payments, and merchant transactions. It operates via USSD and a mobile app, supported by an agent network. It is one of the key mobile wallet services in Madagascar [oai_citation:1‡developingtelecoms.com].

A mobile wallet service offered by Orange Madagascar enabling users to send/receive money, pay bills, and top-up airtime. Transactions can be initiated via USSD or smartphone apps, with cash-in/out at Orange agent points. It is widely used in the country [oai_citation:0‡developingtelecoms.com].

Orange Money Madagascar and Airtel Money offer mobile wallet accounts via telecommunication networks. Users can send/receive funds via USSD/app to other wallets or cash-out through agents. By 2021, Madagascar had over 10 million registered mobile money accounts (surpassing bank accounts). These wallets are used for P2P transfers, merchant payments and bill pay, and interface with the bank-led clearing system for liquidity management.
Processes batch-settlement of retail transactions such as cheque clearings and direct credits among banks. This system typically settles on a deferred net basis daily, overseen by the central bank.
Operated by the central bank of Madagascar, linking banks for large-value transfers in real time. It uses the SWIFT network for communication and settles payments immediately upon submission.

The Marshall Islands passed a 2018 law to issue the SOV – a blockchain-based digital currency backed by the government [oai_citation:36‡centralbanking.com]. SOV will circulate alongside the US dollar. It is built on the Algorand blockchain for fast, secure transactions [oai_citation:37‡algorandtechnologies.com]. The project is managed by the Sovereign Currency Commission (Government). Implementation is pending final approval.

The Marshall Islands primarily relies on Visa and Mastercard for electronic payments at businesses and ATMs (often via US correspondent banks). There is no local payment switch; banks connect to international card networks for settlement.

The Republic of the Marshall Islands passed the Sovereign Currency Act in 2018 to create a national cryptocurrency called the Sovereign (SOV). The SOV is a blockchain-based token intended as legal tender. Its launch has been delayed amid regulatory concerns and remains at pilot/research stage [oai_citation:20‡centralbanking.com].

Given the small economy, many Marshall Islanders use international remittance services (e.g. Western Union, MoneyGram) to send/receive funds in USD. These are private services rather than national systems but are widely used.
Central bank system
Dominant payment method

KIBS (Klirinski Interbankarski Sistemi) is a multilateral deferred net settlement system handling low-value payments (e.g. salaries, utilities). Transactions up to MKD1,000,000 are netted and settled periodically:contentReference[oaicite:21]{index=21}.
MIPS, operated by NBRM...

CaSys International (operated by ICS AD Skopje) processes and clears domestic card payments (Visa/Mastercard are cleared internationally). It manages the domestic card network, settling net positions via the central bank:contentReference[oaicite:22]{index=22}.

MIPS, run by the National Bank, is North Macedonia’s real-time gross settlement system. It clears large denar transactions (monetary policy and urgent interbank transfers) in real time and irrevocably:contentReference[oaicite:19]{index=19}.

Orange Money is a mobile wallet service by Orange Mali for sending money, paying bills, and merchant purchases. It is one of two leading mobile money services (with Moov/MoMo). Mobile money has surged in Mali, with about 14.5 million accounts by 2022 [oai_citation:13‡ecofinagency.com].
Dominant payment method

Wave Money and Wizall Money are fintech-led mobile payment providers expanding in Mali, focusing on low-fee P2P and remittance transfers. They operate alongside telecom wallets, contributing to financial inclusion.

The WAEMU Automated Clearing House (SICA) processes batch payments (e.g., salaries, utility payments, cheques) for member countries on a net settlement basis. Mali’s banks use this regional ACH for low-value retail transfers.

SICA (Système Interbancaire de Compensation Automatisé) is the WAEMU regional ACH for low-value payments [oai_citation:31‡bceao.int]. Mali’s banks use SICA for bulk clearing of transfers, cheques and direct debits. Net obligations are settled via STAR. SICA handles the routine clearing of retail payments across WAEMU.

Mali participates in the BCEAO-operated GIM-UEMOA real-time gross settlement network for high-value transfers in the West African CFA franc zone. It settles interbank payments instantaneously across member states.

Orange Money Mali (Orange Finances Money Mali) is a major mobile money platform. It allows users to cash-in/out, send/receive money, pay bills and merchants via USSD or app [oai_citation:32‡thefintechtimes.com]. The service has millions of users. Funds move through the partner banks for interbank settlement. A 2024 partnership with TerraPay expanded its international remittance capabilities [oai_citation:33‡thefintechtimes.com].

Moov Money (MTN Mobile Money) is the other major mobile wallet in Mali. Users can deposit cash with agents, then pay, transfer, or cash out via phone. Competition from newcomers like Wave and Wizall is expanding options.

STAR-UEMOA is the regional real-time gross settlement system operated by BCEAO (central bank of the WAEMU) [oai_citation:30‡bceao.int]. Mali’s banks use STAR for large-value interbank transfers and urgent payments. Transactions are settled in central bank money in real time across the region.

Malian banks issue Visa and Mastercard debit/credit cards, accepted by ATMs and merchants (especially in cities and tourist venues). Usage is smaller compared to mobile money. International networks connect Mali to global payment rails.
Mobile financial service

The Myanmar QR (MMQR) is an interoperable QR code standard launched by CBM in 2022 [oai_citation:39‡gsma.com]. It enables real-time merchant payments via smartphones. All banks and MFS providers route MMQR transactions through a central switch, integrating with CBM-NET [oai_citation:40‡dfdl.com].

MPU is Myanmar’s domestic card scheme and payment switch:contentReference[oaicite:28]{index=28}. It links member banks for card issuance and acceptance, facilitating debit/credit card transactions within the country.

Major mobile money services include Wave Money (Telenor), KBZPay (KBZ Bank), and MPT Money. These allow peer-to-peer transfers, bill payments, and merchant payments. For example, Wave Money handled MMK 12 trillion (~$8.7B) in 2020:contentReference[oaicite:30]{index=30}.

MMQR is Myanmar’s standard QR code for merchant payments, launched in 2022:contentReference[oaicite:29]{index=29}. It enables real-time QR-based payments at merchants, integrated with issuing banks and digital wallets.

The Central Bank of Myanmar’s CBM-NET includes an RTGS function for high-value kyat payments:contentReference[oaicite:26]{index=26}. Large transfers (≥10M kyats) settle on this real-time system to provide finality and liquidity management.
CBM-NET also includes an ACH for lower-value retail payments:contentReference[oaicite:27]{index=27}. Transactions below 10M kyats (e.g. P2P, P2M) are processed through this clearing system.
Digital banking
Visa and Mastercard cards are issued by Mongolian banks and accepted at merchants and ATMs nationwide. They complement UnionPay and domestic card services.

The Bank of Mongolia operates an RTGS for transfers above MNT 3 million:contentReference[oaicite:10]{index=10}. It provides intraday liquidity, instant final settlement, and risk reduction for large interbank transfers.

The Bank of Mongolia operates an RTGS system for transfers above MNT 3 million [oai_citation:15‡mongolbank.mn]. Launched by CMA in 2006, it provides intraday final settlement, liquidity facilities and central monitoring [oai_citation:16‡mongolbank.mn]. This reduces settlement risk and allows banks to manage interbank liquidity in real time.

Mongolia’s ACH+ (by BoM) handles payments of MNT 3 million or less:contentReference[oaicite:11]{index=11}. It supports real-time 24/7 and batch processing for retail payments, with net settlement in the RTGS system.

UnionPay is widely used in Mongolia, especially by Chinese visitors and banks. Mongolian banks support UnionPay transactions, including UnionPay QR payments introduced in 2021:contentReference[oaicite:13]{index=13}.

In 2024, Khan Bank partnered with Alipay+ to accept 12 international e-wallets (Alipay, KakaoPay, TrueMoney, etc.) via QR codes in Mongolia:contentReference[oaicite:14]{index=14}. This system allows tourists to pay in local shops using their preferred mobile wallets.

The NETC, operated by Bank of Mongolia, clears interbank card transactions on a net basis, with final settlement via the RTGS:contentReference[oaicite:12]{index=12}. It serves as Mongolia’s centralized card transaction hub.
Mobile wallet

Primary payment method

Mauritania’s banks participate in the STAR-UEMOA RTGS, the regional settlement system of the West African Economic and Monetary Union. STAR handles large interbank transfers in real time, with final settlement in the central bank. It is operated by BCEAO and connects all WAEMU members.

HelloCash is a mobile money service in Mauritania, operated by MobiCash (Orange Money). It allows users to open wallets with an ID (no bank account needed) and perform P2P transfers, merchant payments and utility bill payments. The platform uses USSD and agent networks for cash-in/out. It is interoperable with the bank-led payment system for withdrawals.

Mauritania is a member of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU). Its banks use the BCEAO’s real-time gross settlement system (GIM-UEMOA) for interbank transfers in CFA francs, ensuring fast settlement across member states.

Visa and Mastercard debit/credit cards are accepted in urban areas of Mauritania. Some local banks issue cards, but cash remains dominant. Without a domestic switching system, card transactions are processed through international networks.

Mauritania’s telecom operators (e.g. Orange, Chinguitel/Tigo) offer mobile money wallets enabling customers to send money, pay bills, and make merchant payments via phones. Mobile money is growing as a financial inclusion tool.

SICA (Système Interbancaire de Compensation Automatisé) is the regional ACH for WAEMU, including Mauritania. It processes bulk clearing of low-value transactions (transfers, cheques) and net settlement via STAR. SICA is managed by BCEAO and covers all member banks.

The WAEMU Automated Clearing House (SICA) processes bulk transactions (salaries, transfers, cheques) on a net settlement basis among member countries, including Mauritania. It supports routine electronic transfers between Mauritanian banks.
National payment system
Neobank adoption

Mobile wallet services like Apple Pay and Google Pay are available in Malta through local banks. They allow users to pay with smartphones or wearables via NFC at contactless terminals, boosting digital payment usage.

Malta uses the SEPA framework for retail payments. SEPA Credit Transfer allows euro transfers across SEPA countries under a uniform scheme. Maltese banks send pain.001 messages, which settle via TARGET2. SEPA ensures interoperability of electronic payments throughout Europe.

MauCAS is a national QR code payment platform enabling customers to pay merchants via mobile banking by scanning a QR code. It is being rolled out to reduce cash use, but adoption is still in early stages.

Maltese banks offer SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for immediate euro transfers (up to €100,000) any time of day. These payments are settled in seconds via the TARGET Instant Payment Settlement (TIPS) system. SCT Inst uses the same ISO 20022 messaging format as SEPA Credit Transfers.

As a eurozone country, Malta participates in the TARGET2 system for real-time gross settlement in euros [oai_citation:34‡centralbankmalta.org]. TARGET2 provides central bank liquidity and immediate final settlement for interbank and customer payments. The Central Bank of Malta directs participant access to TARGET2 under ECB guidelines [oai_citation:35‡centralbankmalta.org].

MTEUROPAY is the euro retail payment system for Malta, operated by the Central Bank. It enables credit transfers and direct debits among banks and licensed institutions in Malta, complementing the European SEPA schemes.

International card schemes (Visa, Mastercard) are widely used in Malta for merchant and ATM payments. Maltese banks issue EU debit cards (Maestro) and credit cards that are accepted locally and internationally.

The Malta Clearing House handles retail payments including cheques and bulk credit transfers via net settlement. In 2024 it cleared ~1.99 million cheques (value €7.75B) [oai_citation:18‡centralbankmalta.org]. Cheque use is declining in favor of electronic methods.
Mobile payment service
National payment switch

Mauritius has several mobile payment applications (e.g., MIPS MobiPay, bank mobile apps) that allow peer-to-peer transfers and merchant payments using smartphones. These are increasingly used for small everyday payments.

MauCAS is a national QR code payment system launched by the central bank. Merchants display a MauCAS QR code; customers pay by scanning it with banking apps (linking to their accounts or wallets), enabling instant settlement.

Mauritian banks issue VISA and Mastercard debit/credit cards, widely used at POS and ATMs. Contactless cards and mobile NFC payments are growing in popularity. The domestic MauSwitch network links ATMs and merchants across banks.

MACSS is the Bank of Mauritius’s RTGS for large-value payments [oai_citation:38‡bom.mu]. Commercial banks settle interbank payments and government collections in real time via their accounts at the central bank. Settlements are final and irrevocable. MACSS also provides settlement for sub-systems like the Port Louis ACH (PLACH) and the CDS [oai_citation:39‡bom.mu].

PLACH is Mauritius’s ACH for retail clearing [oai_citation:40‡bom.mu]. It handles bulk low-value payments including cheque truncation and batch credits/debits. Net positions are settled through MACSS. PLACH streamlines cheque processing and other routine payment exchanges.

sistemas.descricao: Mobile wallet

Dhiraagu (largest operator) launched a mobile money service in 2016 for users to send/receive funds, pay bills and buy airtime via mobile phones [oai_citation:26‡unescap.org]. Transactions are facilitated over USSD/SMS and settled through participating banks. (Ooredoo Maldives offers a similar service.) These wallets have helped improve financial inclusion across islands [oai_citation:27‡unescap.org].

The Maldives ACH processes bulk low-value payments such as salary credits and cheque clearings on a deferred net basis. It includes direct credits, cheques (via imaging/truncation), and other retail transactions daily.

Favara is the Maldives Instant Payment System (MIPS) launched in 2023. It enables real-time, 24x7 account transfers among local banks. The system allows instant fund transfers using mobile or online banking, facilitating digital payments.

The MMA’s ACH is a session-based clearing system for low-value bulk payments (direct credits, cheques, etc.). It runs typically once or twice daily, netting transactions for settlement via the RTGS. Currently the ACH supports direct credits and cheque truncation. It uses SWIFT-based messaging for exchanges.

The Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA) operates MRTGS for large-value interbank transfers (above MVR100,000) [oai_citation:25‡payments.mv]. It processes transactions individually and immediately using SWIFT messaging. Settlements are final upon execution. The system typically runs during banking hours.

Major Maldivian banks offer mobile payment apps (e.g., BML Mobile Banking, Hayya by SBI, Faisa by MIB). These apps support NFC/contactless payments and QR-based transfers. Adoption is growing due to full mobile coverage and efforts to reduce cash usage.

International card networks (Visa, Mastercard) are the primary electronic payment methods in the Maldives. Non-bank acquirers handle a majority of card transactions [oai_citation:12‡payments.mv]. Without a local switch, transactions are often processed through overseas banks.

The Maldives RTGS (MRTGS) handles high-value interbank transactions in real time and is operated by the Maldives Monetary Authority. All banks use MRTGS for large transfers. In 2023 it processed about 431K transactions totaling MVR3.8T [oai_citation:10‡payments.mv].

Ooredoo Maldives introduced its mobile money platform in 2017. Similar to Dhiraagu’s service, it enables peer-to-peer transfers and payments via mobile phones. The platform uses USSD and app interfaces, linked to the banking network for interbank settlement [oai_citation:28‡unescap.org].

Airtel Money provides mobile wallet accounts enabling P2P transfers, bill payments and airtime top-ups. It is one of two major MNO-led wallets (with TNM Mpamba) and is integrated to the national switch for interbank settlements [oai_citation:9‡ifc.org]. The service operates via USSD and mobile apps. In 2023, mobile payments grew by 31% to 1.36 billion transactions, valued at MK13 trillion [oai_citation:10‡mwnation.com].

TNM Mpamba is Telekom Networks Malawi’s mobile money platform. It offers P2P transfers, merchant payments and cash-in/cash-out through agents. Mpamba is also connected to Natswitch [oai_citation:12‡ifc.org], allowing interoperability with banks. The system is accessed via USSD or mobile app.

A real-time instant payment system (launched by PawaPay) enabling immediate interbank transfers for low-value transactions. It processes peer-to-peer and merchant payments instantly using account identifiers. In 2024 it handled ~33.5M transactions (MK5T value) [oai_citation:3‡mwnation.com].

The Malawi Automated Clearing House (MACH) handles batch interbank payments like cheques and payroll via net settlement. Historically paper-based, it has modernized to process bulk transfers across banks, but its use has declined as real-time systems and mobile money have grown.

The Reserve Bank of Malawi operates an RTGS platform for high-value interbank transfers (Perago CRISPTM RTGS), enabling immediate settlement of large payments. It connects all major banks using SWIFT messaging and replaced older cheque clearing for high-value flows.

Natswitch Ltd. operates Malawi’s national payments switch (since 2015) for POS, ATM, mobile and e-wallet transactions [oai_citation:4‡africanenda.org]. It provides instant clearing of low-value transactions (P2P, P2B) among banks, MFIs and payment providers. Natswitch uses the ISO 8583 messaging standard and is in the process of adding an ISO 20022 translation layer [oai_citation:5‡africanenda.org]. It processes tens of millions of transactions annually (e.g. 11.5M in 2022) [oai_citation:6‡africanenda.org].

Visa and Mastercard debit/credit cards are accepted by many merchants and ATMs in Malawi. A local switch (MalawiSwitch) links ATMs/POS across banks. However, overall card transaction volumes remain relatively low compared to cash and mobile money.
Real-time interbank electronic payment system

CoDi is a government-backed digital payment platform (launched 2019) that uses QR/NFC codes for instant payments. Users scan a QR code to pay, triggering a SPEI transaction. CoDi had over 10.7 million registered users by 2021 [oai_citation:44‡clon.cemla.org]. Behind the scenes, it relies on ISO 20022 payment messages through the SPEI infrastructure.
Cash-based voucher system for e-commerce
Regional e-commerce integrated wallet
Visa/Mastercard dominance

CLABE is the standard 18-digit bank account numbering for Mexico. Banks and payment providers use CLABE numbers for interbank transfers via SPEI. This system underpins most retail transfers (e.g. salaries, bills) across Mexico’s banks.

Visa, Mastercard and American Express cards are widely used for payments in Mexico. These cards are accepted at the majority of retailers and ATMs. In recent years (post-2018 interchange reform) card payments have grown dramatically (hundreds of billions USD annually).

Mobile and online wallets (e.g. Mercado Pago, banking apps) are popular especially for e-commerce and person-to-person payments. These services often integrate with SPEI or CoDi to move funds. Their adoption is rising among younger, tech-savvy users.

Platforms like PayPal, as well as country-specific digital services (e.g. AeroMexico Pay), provide cross-border and domestic payment solutions. They typically fund transactions via SPEI or international card rails.

SPEI (Sistema de Pagos Electrónicos Interbancarios) is Mexico’s interbank electronic payment system [oai_citation:41‡commercegate.com]. Operated by Banco de México, SPEI enables instant transfers between bank accounts 24/7. Launched in 2004, it has become the backbone of Mexican payments. SPEI achieved peaks of over 17 million daily transactions [oai_citation:42‡clon.cemla.org].

DuitNow is Malaysia’s instant payment platform (launched 2018) [oai_citation:22‡paynet.my]. It enables 24/7 real-time transfers using account numbers or proxies (mobile/NRIC) [oai_citation:23‡paynet.my]. Payments are pushed to the recipient’s account instantly (settling via RENTAS/TIPS). The system uses ISO 20022 messaging.
Super-app wallet

RENTAS (Real-time Electronic Transfer of Funds and Securities) is the Bank Negara Malaysia’s RTGS platform for interbank, high-value fund and securities transfers. It operates during banking hours with real-time final settlement of transactions.

Visa and Mastercard debit/credit cards are extensively used in Malaysia for ATM withdrawals and retail payments. These international networks operate alongside domestic schemes and are accepted by most merchants.

eSPICK is the national cheque clearing system [oai_citation:16‡paynet.my]. Participating banks submit scanned cheque images and data through eSPICK, which automates exchange and netting. Settlement is done via RENTAS. The system replaced physical cheque clearing to speed up processing.

MyDebit is a national debit scheme for ATM-issued cards [oai_citation:17‡paynet.my]. It allows direct account payments at POS. Transactions are switched through PayNet’s infrastructure and settle in real time on RENTAS. MyDebit uses ISO 8583 messaging for card payment authorization.

DuitNow is Malaysia’s instant payment service operated by PayNet. It allows real-time interbank transfers using identifiers like mobile number, NRIC, or DuitNow QR. It has seen rapid adoption, facilitating billions of transactions annually.

RENTAS (Real-time Electronic Transfer of Funds and Securities) is Malaysia’s RTGS for wholesale interbank and securities settlement [oai_citation:13‡paynet.my]. Launched in July 1999, it provides real-time, final settlement of high-value transfers and also supports offshore CNY clearing [oai_citation:14‡paynet.my]. RENTAS adopted ISO 20022 messaging in 2022, replacing older MT formats.

JomPAY is Malaysia’s standardized bill payment system [oai_citation:19‡paynet.my]. Through internet banking, payers use a single JomPAY code per biller. The payment instruction is sent as a credit transfer via IBG. JomPAY mandates interbank interoperability (42 banks) and reduces integration costs for billers [oai_citation:20‡paynet.my].

eSPICK is the electronic cheque clearing system in Malaysia, operated by PayNet. Cheques are exchanged digitally between banks, reducing paper handling. It settles daily net obligations from cheque presentations.

The Direct Debit scheme allows merchants to collect recurring payments (with customer mandate) [oai_citation:21‡paynet.my]. Instruction files (pain.008) are sent to banks for processing. Debits are settled via the ACH. Commonly used for utility bills and subscriptions.

IBG is the ACH system for account-to-account payments (e.g., payroll, vendor payments) [oai_citation:15‡paynet.my]. Banks submit bulk credit instructions, which settle net via RENTAS. IBG operates daily and handles high volumes of low-value transfers. It currently uses proprietary formats and is transitioning to ISO 20022.

DuitNow QR is Malaysia’s universal QR code standard for payments [oai_citation:24‡paynet.my]. It allows any approved QR code (MyQR) to be accepted by participating banks and e-wallets. Scanning a DuitNow QR triggers an instant debit to the payer’s account. Settlement occurs over the existing instant payment infrastructure.

FPX (Financial Process Exchange) is an online payment gateway [oai_citation:18‡paynet.my]. It allows customers to pay merchants directly from their bank accounts via internet banking. FPX transactions are authorized in real time (ISO 8583) and settle in net via RENTAS. Widely used for e-commerce payments.

Banco de Moçambique implemented a modern RTGS system on 30 Nov 2023 [oai_citation:33‡bancomoc.mz]. This ISO20022-compliant platform provides real-time funds availability, queue management, liquidity-saving features and enhanced risk controls [oai_citation:34‡bancomoc.mz]. It replaces the older national switch for large-value transactions, improving speed and security.

Banco de Moçambique’s CEL (Clearing and Settlement Subsystem) electronically clears retail payment instruments (cheques, credit transfers) in meticais:contentReference[oaicite:24]{index=24}. Net settlements are finalized via the RTGS.

In Dec 2023, the Bank of Mozambique launched a new RTGS platform (Montran, ISO 20022) for high-value interbank transfers:contentReference[oaicite:23]{index=23}. It provides real-time final settlement and liquidity management in meticais for banks.

An ACH system was introduced concurrently with the RTGS (late 2023) to handle bulk payments. It processes net-settled low-value transfers (e.g. payrolls, vendor payments) in MZN, with final settlement in the RTGS. This modernizes the national payment infrastructure to improve efficiency.
Visa and Mastercard cards are accepted by banks and merchants in Mozambique, facilitating consumer payments and withdrawals.

Mozambique has three major mobile money wallets – Vodacom’s M-Pesa, Tmcel’s mKesh and Movitel’s e-Mola. Since 2022 these wallets are interoperable, letting customers send money across networks:contentReference[oaicite:25]{index=25}.

The Namibia Interbank Settlement System (NISS) is BoN’s RTGS, launched in 2002 [oai_citation:41‡bon.com.na].aspx#:~:text=The%20NISS%2C%20a%20real%20time,NAMSWITCH%29%20and%20the). It settles high-value single transactions gross in real time, as well as bulk retail transfers. Settlements are final and irrevocable. The NISS also connects to Namibia’s card and EFT switches [oai_citation:42‡bon.com.na].aspx#:~:text=The%20NISS%2C%20a%20real%20time,NAMSWITCH%29%20and%20the).
Namibia’s banks issue and accept Visa and Mastercard cards for POS and ATM transactions. These global schemes serve both domestic consumers and international visitors.

Namibia’s RTGS, the Namibia Interbank Settlement System (NISS), is operated by the Bank of Namibia:contentReference[oaicite:31]{index=31}. In 2024/25 it settled ~97,074 transactions (value N$1.2 trillion):contentReference[oaicite:32]{index=32}, ensuring final settlement of interbank payments.

NamPay is the national ACH (launched 2021) for low-value EFTs [oai_citation:45‡namclear.com.na]. Operated by Namclear, it processes bulk credit transfers (e.g. salaries) and other EFTs in batches. Settlement of NamPay nets is performed in NISS [oai_citation:46‡bon.com.na].aspx#:~:text=irrevocability,both%20operated%20by%20Namclear).

NamPay is a domestic EFT system launched in 2021 by the Namibian banking industry (in partnership with the Payments Association of Namibia). It standardizes credit/debit transfers across banks using ISO 20022 messaging:contentReference[oaicite:33]{index=33}.

SICA-UEMOA is the BCEAO’s automated interbank clearing system (deferred net settlement) for WAEMU member states (including Niger). It processes bulk retail payments like transfers and checks, netting and settling between banks.
STAR-UEMOA is used by Niger via BCEAO...

STAR-UEMOA is the BCEAO-operated Real-Time Gross Settlement system for the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU), used by Nigerien banks for large urgent transfers. It settles transactions instantly in regional currency (CFA franc).

Mobile network operators offer mobile money wallets (e.g. Moov Flooz, Airtel Money) under BCEAO regulations. Citizens use these for person-to-person transfers, airtime top-ups and merchant payments via mobile apps/USSD.
Mobile payment platform
Real-time interbank payment system

NIBSS Instant Payments (NIP) is Nigeria’s interbank instant funds transfer system. It processes real-time, push-based transfers between banks 24/7. NIP is among the world’s largest RTP systems, handling billions of dollars daily and serving as the backbone for P2P transfers and mobile money payouts:contentReference[oaicite:14]{index=14}.
The Central Bank of Nigeria operates an RTGS system for settlement of high-value interbank transfers. It provides immediate final settlement in central bank money for urgent transactions.

The NIBSS Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) service is used for less-urgent payments. It batches and nets payments like salaries and vendor payments, typically settling them within hours or the next day.

Verve (Interswitch) is Nigeria’s domestic card network (debit and prepaid). It issues and processes chip-and-PIN cards accepted across Nigeria (and increasingly abroad). Verve is Africa’s largest domestic card scheme:contentReference[oaicite:16]{index=16}.

Licensed mobile money services (e.g. Paga, OPay, MTN Mobile Money) allow users to store value and transfer money via phone. They support P2P transfers, merchant payments and bill payment, often using NIP rails.

Managed by the Central Bank of Nicaragua, TTS is the national RTGS for clearing large interbank payments in local currency. It settles high-value transfers immediately across banks.
SINPE is Nicaragua’s core interbank payment network...

SIP (Sistemas de Interconexión de Pagos) connects Nicaragua with other Central American countries for instant cross-border transfers. It uses shared standards (SWIFT) to enable secure low-cost intraregional payments:contentReference[oaicite:13]{index=13}.

sistemas.descricao: iDEAL is a Dutch internet payment system that lets consumers pay merchants directly from their bank accounts. It is managed by Dutch banks (Currence) and accounts for roughly 73% of e-commerce transactions:contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}.
P2P payment app

The Dutch domestic debit card network (often called PIN/Maestro) is managed by the Betaalvereniging. It handles ATM withdrawals and in-store chip-card transactions nationwide, coexisting with international Visa/Mastercard networks.

TARGET2-NL (operated by DNB) settles large-value EUR-denominated payments in real time and finality, including interbank and central bank operations. It is fully integrated into the Eurosystem’s TARGET2 network. All Dutch banks access TARGET2 through DNB, enabling cross-border euro payments with other Euro area RTGS participants. Historically (2010) it processed ~33,000 payments/day (~€294bn/day).

Tikkie is a widely-used smartphone payment app (launched by ABN AMRO in 2016) for peer-to-peer bill splitting. Users send payment requests (via WhatsApp, SMS, etc.) which recipients pay by clicking a link. By 2024 it had ~10 million users and handled 157 million requests (€7.4B):contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}.

SEPA Instant is the pan-European instant credit transfer scheme (operated by the Eurosystem’s TIPS) allowing near-immediate EUR payments any time. Dutch banks are heavy users: over 40 million instant interbank payments per month were processed nationwide by 2024:contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}.

Vipps (by DNB and partners) is a leading mobile app for peer-to-peer and merchant payments in Norway. It allows instant transfers by phone or QR. In 2022 Norwegian banks processed 259 million instant payments (via Vipps and mobile banking):contentReference[oaicite:28]{index=28}.

BankAxept is Norway’s domestic debit card scheme (co-badged with Visa/Mastercard). It is widely used in stores; in 2022 it handled about 1.8 billion card transactions at points-of-sale:contentReference[oaicite:26]{index=26}.
The Norges Bank’s settlement system (NBO)...

NBO is Norges Bank’s RTGS system for NOK. It performs final settlement of interbank payments in real time (24/7) via SWIFT. It underpins settlement for high-value and net-cleared payments:contentReference[oaicite:23]{index=23}.

NICS Real, operated by bank consortium Bits, is Norway’s real-time payment infrastructure (ISO 20022-based). It enables immediate account-to-account transfers between different banks' customers any time of day:contentReference[oaicite:24]{index=24}.

Several digital wallet platforms (e.g. eSewa, Khalti, IME Pay) are popular in Nepal for P2P transfers, bill payments and mobile top-ups. These wallets link to users’ bank accounts and integrate with NCHL infrastructure, enabling instant transfers via mobile apps or USSD.

connectIPS, operated by Nepal Clearing House (NCHL), is a faster payment system that enables real-time bank-to-bank transfers via web, mobile app and APIs. Customers link their accounts to send instant payments for e-commerce, bill payments, fund transfers and wallet top-ups:contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}.

The Central Bank (Nepal Rastra Bank) operates an RTGS system for settling large or urgent interbank transfers immediately. Payments are final and settled in central bank money, used for high-value credit, forex and public-sector payments:contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}.

The NRB RTGS (known as connectRTGS) settles large-value domestic and cross-border transfers in real time and finality (NPR, USD, EUR, GBP, JPY). It is owned and operated by Nepal Rastra Bank and used by all commercial and development banks. RTGS supports immediate settlement 24/7 for urgent credit transfers, including banks’ foreign currency settlement. High-value flows and interbank obligations are processed through this central bank system.

NCHL-IPS (Interbank Payment System) is a bulk batch clearing system used by Nepali banks for non-urgent retail payments (salaries, dividends, bills, remittances, etc.). It processes scheduled credits (direct credit) and debits (direct debit) in batch, settling net positions among banks:contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}.
Visa and Mastercard cards are accepted at Nauru’s merchants and ATMs (via the Bendigo agency). There are no local card issuers, so cards are usually foreign-issued.
Nauru has an ATM network served by the Bendigo Bank agency. Nauruans made ~40,000 ATM withdrawals per month (2019-20) totaling about A$8.3M:contentReference[oaicite:34]{index=34}.

Nauru’s only banking agency is run by Bendigo and Adelaide Bank (Australia). It provides basic deposit, ATM and payment services to residents. All electronic transfers use Australian correspondent banking rails.

ESAS is New Zealand’s RTGS system...

CECS is the consumer electronic clearing system (managed by Payments NZ) that processes net settlements for everyday payments like EFTPOS transactions and consumer-oriented transfers. Payments are accumulated and settled in scheduled clearing batches.
ESAS (Exchange Settlement Account System) is the Reserve Bank of New Zealand’s RTGS platform for large-value NZD payments. It settles payments between banks in real time (24/7).
BECS, run by Payments NZ, is an ACH system handling large volumes of bulk payments (e.g. salaries, bill payments). It processes multiple clearing runs per day and settles net positions via RTGS.

HVCS (operated by Payments NZ) is used for high-value non-reversible payments (e.g. property transactions). It nets transactions at intervals. It handles fewer, larger transactions than retail systems.
Digital wallet

The Central Bank of Oman’s RTGS (upgraded to 24/7 in 2023) settles interbank transfers instantly. It handles high-value payments in real time, improving liquidity management and linking to regional payment systems:contentReference[oaicite:30]{index=30}:contentReference[oaicite:31]{index=31}.

The ACH system (operated by CBO) processes batch payments such as salaries, pensions and recurring transfers. It enables efficient clearing of large volumes of transactions, settling net positions periodically. In 2023 it processed 21.9 million payments (OMR13.5B):contentReference[oaicite:33]{index=33}.
The CBO RTGS is the national high-value settlement infrastructure...

OmanNet is the interbank switch for ATM/POS card payments in Oman. It processed 329 million card transactions in 2023 (NOM 6.4B), as card usage grew via expanded POS deployment:contentReference[oaicite:37]{index=37}.

The Mobile Payments Clearing and Settlement System (MPCSS) enables interoperability and clearing between Oman’s mobile money wallets. It saw a surge from 4.9M transactions in 2022 to 40M in 2023, reflecting rapid growth in mobile payments:contentReference[oaicite:35]{index=35}.
Oman’s ECC system handles interbank clearing of paper cheques. Cheque usage is declining: 3.7 million cheques were processed in 2023 (slightly down from 2022):contentReference[oaicite:39]{index=39}.
Digital wallet
P2P payments

ACH Xpress is a 24/7 real-time retail payment system operated by Telered, launched in 2022. It enables customers of participating banks to send and receive instant transfers (up to $5,000) via online or mobile channels [oai_citation:5‡telered.com.pa].

"Mis Pagos Hoy" is Panama’s centralized bill and utility payments platform provided by Telered. Customers of participating banks can pay bills (electricity, water, etc.) via online banking or ATM using this system. It operates by debiting the payer’s account and crediting the biller’s account in one of the daily clearing sessions. Over 25 banks and cooperatives participate. The system enhances convenience of payments by integrating utility companies and retailers into a single platform, clearing funds via ACH Directo. Transaction data and volumes are managed by Telered with final settlement by Banco Nacional.

ACH Xpress is a real-time, low-value payment service launched by Telered in August 2022. It enables instant interbank transfers (peer-to-peer or business payments) around the clock. ACH Xpress processes small transactions (90% under US$500) immediately upon originator’s instruction. It is accessed via mobile banking and online apps of participating banks. By 2024, usage grew rapidly, with 1.9 million transactions (~B/.346 million) in 2024:contentReference[oaicite:16]{index=16}. The system is managed by Telered with settlement by Banco Nacional. It complements ACH Directo by shifting frequent small payments to instant rails. Adoption is growing as more banks connect to the service.

The Banco Nacional de Panamá operates the country’s clearing house infrastructure. It provides deferred net settlement for multilateral clearing sessions including check clearing and settlement of ACH (Telered) obligations. It can operate in real-time (RTGS) mode, but by practice uses five daily clearing cycles. All banks clear obligations through the BN clearinghouse which nets payments across systems (ACH, check imaging, card settlements) and settles via accounts at the National Bank. This centralized clearing system ensures multilateral net settlement and finality for large-value and retail transactions.

Operated by Banco Nacional de Panama, the Clearinghouse is the main settlement platform for domestic payments. It nets and settles interbank transfers and other retail transactions (cheques, credits/debits) in daily batches. The system was upgraded in 2019 to support real-time gross settlement [oai_citation:3‡superbancos.gob.pa].

ACH Directo is Panama’s main Automated Clearing House system operated by the banks’ switch company (Telered). It processes retail interbank credit and debit transfers (salary payments, bill pay, transfers) on a deferred-net settlement basis. 47 banks and cooperatives participate:contentReference[oaicite:14]{index=14}. ACH Directo handles the majority of retail payments in Panama, with settlement via the Banco Nacional de Panamá clearinghouse. It operates three daily clearing sessions and settles once per day. ACH Directo follows international file formats (NACHA, moving to ISO 20022) and links to the US ACH for pension transfers.

Sistema Clave is Panama’s national debit card scheme, operated by Telered. It provides an integrated network for ATM withdrawals and POS payments with domestic cards in local currency. Clave transactions are processed through this interbank network using EMV chip standards and ISO8583 messaging.

Clave is the national brand for interbank debit cards and ATM transactions managed by Telered. Under Clave, banks issue cards tied to the local switch, allowing ATM withdrawals and POS payments nationwide and in some neighboring countries. It links ATMs/POS of 27 banks in Panama. Clave cards work on 1LINK/MultiRed and in Panama through Clave branding. As of 2023, Panama had ~3.2 million debit cards (most co-branded Visa/Mastercard). The Clave network ensures interoperability of cards and ATMs, supporting contactless and PIN transactions. Telered owns and operates the switch; settlement is through the BNP clearinghouse.

ACH Directo is Panama’s traditional automated clearing house for credit transfers and direct debits in local currency, operated by Telered. It processes batched interbank payments (e.g. salaries, recurring bills) with multiple settlement windows each business day [oai_citation:4‡superbancos.gob.pa].

Yape is a popular smartphone wallet launched by Banco de Crédito del Perú in 2016. It allows users of participating banks to transfer funds using just phone numbers or QR codes. Yape operates via a simple app (no formal account needed) and links to bank accounts for funding/withdrawing. It enables instant person-to-person and merchant payments and has grown rapidly (over 11 million users by end-2022):contentReference[oaicite:29]{index=29}. The BCRP mandated that Yape be interoperable with other wallets (like Plin) to ensure wide reach. Yape transactions are settled over the Peru instant payments infrastructure. It significantly boosted digital inclusion and e-payments:contentReference[oaicite:30]{index=30}.

Plin is a mobile payments app developed by BBVA Bancomer (for its Peruvian branch) and linked banks, launched in 2020. It provides functionality similar to Yape, allowing instant money transfers via smartphone using phone numbers or QR. By end-2022 it had about 8 million users:contentReference[oaicite:33]{index=33}. Plin is fully interoperable with Yape and other digital payment instruments due to BCRP regulations, enabling cross-wallet transfers. Plin facilitated the surge of Peru’s fast payments; by 2023 Peru reached 157 fast payments per capita:contentReference[oaicite:34]{index=34}. The app contributes to reducing cash usage and is used for personal and merchant transactions.

The Sistema de Liquidación Bruta en Tiempo Real (LBTR) is Peru’s real-time gross settlement system, owned and operated by the Central Reserve Bank of Peru (BCRP). It processes high-value interbank transfers individually and immediately, providing final settlement for large transactions and financial market operations. LBTR is the principal high-value payment system, settling funds transfers between banks and with the central bank. It operates on business days, ensuring secure settlement of obligations among financial institutions:contentReference[oaicite:26]{index=26}.
Peru’s ACH system handles large volumes of deferred retail transfers (e.g. payroll, bills). It nets transactions and settles them in batch cycles each day.
LBTR is Peru’s RTGS system, operated by the Central Reserve Bank of Peru (BCRP). It settles large-value and time-critical interbank peso payments with finality.

Yape is a mobile wallet by Banco de Crédito del Perú enabling instant transfers via QR codes or phone numbers. It has wide adoption and interoperates with other systems. Yape, together with Plin, accounted for ~165 million monthly transactions by late 2024 [oai_citation:12‡bcrp.gob.pe].
Tunki is a mobile wallet targeted at the unbanked population, offered by Caja Rural. It allows QR-code and phone-number payments for rural users with limited bank access.

BiPay is a retail CBDC pilot launched by BCRP in 2024. It tokenizes the Peruvian sol and distributes it via a mobile wallet (in partnership with telecom Bitel). Pilot usage grew from ~54k to 91k daily transactions from Oct 2024 to Feb 2025 [oai_citation:13‡bcrp.gob.pe].

The CCE is Peru’s interbank automated clearing house, handling batch processing of retail credit transfers (e.g., salary, transfers) and direct debits (e.g., bill payments). Operated by the payments center under BCRP oversight, it nets payments from multiple banks and settles the net positions via LBTR. The CCE has historically handled checks, transfers and low-value instruments. As of 2022, the clearing house and associated retail systems settled ~4.74 billion transactions (4.9% increase over prior year):contentReference[oaicite:27]{index=27}. The CCE complements the RTGS by offering bulk settlement and interbank clearing.

Cobro con Cédula o Celular (Plin) is a 24/7 instant interbank transfer service linking accounts via phone numbers or national ID alias. It allows immediate P2P transfers and has seen explosive growth when interoperated with wallets [oai_citation:11‡bcrp.gob.pe].

KATS is the Bank of Papua New Guinea’s RTGS system for Papua New Guinea’s currency (PGK). Launched in 1999, it processes high-value interbank transfers (bank-to-bank, government payments, and securities settlements) on a real-time gross basis. In addition to large-value payments, KATS also handles batch settlement for checks and retail clearing. It enables instant settlement for large transactions and schedules check clearings (overnight). All commercial banks and some government entities have BPNG settlement accounts on KATS. The system is managed by BPNG, ensuring 24/7 availability and final settlement of obligations:contentReference[oaicite:21]{index=21}.

The Retail Electronic Payment System (REPS) is PNG’s national switch operated by the central bank. It connects ATM, EFTPOS (debit/credit card) and mobile wallet networks of member banks. REPS enables person-to-person transfers, merchant acquiring and ATM interoperability. It is used for card-present and card-not-present transactions and links mobile money. The system provides real-time switching and routes transactions between banks. REPS is run by the central bank (BPNG) with participation of all commercial banks and major mobile money providers. It supports the growth of digital payments by linking disparate payment rails at the national level.

The Bank of Papua New Guinea has expressed interest in exploring a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) as part of its national Vision 2050 and financial inclusion goals. The project, sometimes informally referred to as “Digital Kina,” is in exploratory stages (as of 2024). The BPNG is studying the potential design of a digital kina for retail use to complement physical cash and promote financial access. As of now, no pilot or official digital currency has been launched, and this remains in the research and planning phase by the central bank.

KATS is a real-time gross settlement system operated by the Bank of Papua New Guinea, enabling immediate settlement of large-value interbank transfers. It also handles direct credits and cheque clearance. KATS was implemented via SWIFT (connected in 2015) [oai_citation:6‡swift.com].

CellMoni is a mobile wallet and remittance service offered by Digicel PNG that allows users to store funds and conduct transactions (P2P transfers, bill payments, merchant payments) via USSD/app. It operates 24/7 and is especially popular in areas with limited banking access.

Launched in July 2019 by the Bank of PNG, the PNG National Switch connects ATMs and EFTPOS terminals nationwide. It standardizes domestic card transactions across banks, allowing interoperable use of cards at ATMs and merchants [oai_citation:7‡bankpng.gov.pg].
