BancNet is the primary ATM and POS switching network in the Philippines, linking member banks for cash withdrawals and POS transactions. It also operates the InstaPay infrastructure.

GCash is a licensed e-Money issuer’s mobile wallet widely used in the Philippines. Provided by Globe Telecom’s fintech arm, GCash allows users to open a virtual account, load money (via bank transfer or cash-in partners) and make P2P transfers, bill payments, QR payments, and buy goods online/offline. It is interoperable with InstaPay/PESONet for bank transfers and supports remittances. GCash has tens of millions of users and processed a large share of mobile payments. It is a private service regulated by BSP as an electronic money issuer.

BancNet is one of the Philippine interbank networks that links ATM and POS terminals of member banks. It enables ATM withdrawals, balance inquiries and debit card payments nationwide. BancNet also operates InstaPay. (Its affiliate CardNet provides merchant acquiring and e-commerce for Visa/Mastercard.) BancNet ensures interoperability of ATMs/POS and routing of card transactions across banks. The network is owned by consortium of banks, under BSP oversight. Alongside other networks (MegaLink, ExpressNet), BancNet is key to payment card acceptance and electronic banking in the Philippines.

PhilPaSSplus is the Philippines’ Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system for the peso, owned and run by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP):contentReference[oaicite:36]{index=36}. It handles large-value interbank transfers, money market settlements, and net settlements of retail clearing (checks, ATMs). As the sole high-value settlement system, PhilPaSSplus provides immediate finality of payments among banks. It also supports settlement of Peso leg of foreign exchange and government transactions. The system is active during banking hours and has advanced features for liquidity management. By centralizing interbank settlements, it underpins financial market stability:contentReference[oaicite:37]{index=37}.

QR Ph is the standardized quick-response code payment system mandated by the BSP (per Circular 1055) for banks and e-money issuers. It follows the EMV QR specification, allowing merchants to accept payments from any participating app by scanning a common QR. Launched in late 2020, it unifies fragmented QR solutions (e.g. GCash, PayMaya, bank apps) under one interoperable standard:contentReference[oaicite:43]{index=43}. QR Ph supports both person-to-person and merchant (P2M) use cases. Adoption has grown steadily, improving ease of small-value payments across different providers.

The Philippine Dollar Transfer System (PDDTS) is an RTGS platform operated by the Philippine Clearing House Corporation (PCHC) for USD payments between banks in the Philippines [oai_citation:15‡fintechnews.ph].

PhilPaSS plus is the national real-time gross settlement system managed by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. It processes large-value interbank peso transactions with finality [oai_citation:14‡fintechnews.ph].

InstaPay is the Philippines’ real-time electronic funds transfer service launched under the National Retail Payment System in December 2015. It allows immediate interbank transfers of up to P50,000 per transaction, 24/7/365. Users can send money using mobile apps or online banking; funds are credited in seconds. InstaPay is used heavily for P2P remittances and consumer transactions. It is operated by the Philippine Clearing House Corporation with clearing via PhilPaSS. InstaPay’s usage has surged – as of Feb 2025 it handled ~307 million transactions (~P1.46 trillion) YTD:contentReference[oaicite:40]{index=40}, reflecting widespread adoption among Filipinos.

Project Agila is a wholesale CBDC pilot by the BSP, launched in 2024. It tokenizes interbank peso settlements on a distributed ledger among participating banks, as a test of digital currency technology [oai_citation:18‡centralbanking.com].

PayMaya is a digital wallet service (Voyager Innovations) providing e-money accounts and virtual/physical prepaid cards. It enables P2P transfers, QR payments, and online payments for users across the Philippines.

PESONet is the batch automated clearing house operated by PCHC for peso credit transfers and debits. It processes payment files between banks in hourly settlement batches for transfers over a certain limit.
The Peso-USD Payment-versus-Payment (PvP) system links PhilPaSS and PDDTS to ensure simultaneous settlement of paired Peso and USD trades, preventing settlement risk [oai_citation:16‡fintechnews.ph].

PESONet is the Philippine National Retail Payment System’s batch credit transfer service, launched in December 2015. It is managed by the Philippine Payments Management Inc. and settles payments in deferred net settlement (usually same-day). PESONet caters to larger retail transfers (e.g. corporate payroll, bill payments) up to pesos 500,000 or higher. It is an alternative to paper checks. Participating banks send files to the Philippine Clearing House Corp. for clearing; net obligations are settled via PhilPaSS. By early 2025, PESONet handled ~18.7 million transactions worth P1.99 trillion (Feb 2025 data):contentReference[oaicite:38]{index=38}. It continues to grow as businesses and consumers move to electronic payments.

PayMaya is another major Philippine e-wallet, offered by Voyager/Smart. Users can register an account through the PayMaya app, top up with cash or bank transfers, and make person-to-person transfers, QR payments, and online purchases. PayMaya is interoperable with InstaPay/PESONet and participates in the QR Ph ecosystem. It competes with GCash to provide digital payment services. Like GCash, PayMaya is regulated as an electronic money issuer by BSP. It supports microtransactions and aims to promote financial inclusion.

GCash is a popular mobile wallet and payment app (Mynt/Globe) in the Philippines. It allows users to transfer money P2P, pay bills, and pay merchants via QR code, making it one of the largest digital money platforms in the country.

PRISM (Pakistan Real-Time Interbank Settlement Mechanism) is the country’s RTGS system, launched in July 2008 by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP):contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}. It handles large-value interbank transfers in PKR on a real-time gross settlement basis. All major banks participate, settling large payments and government transactions individually and immediately. PRISM operates during banking hours and provides finality of settlement, reducing systemic risk. It is the backbone for high-value and interbank payments in Pakistan:contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}.

Managed by the State Bank of Pakistan, PRISM (Pakistan Real-time Interbank Settlement Mechanism) is a real-time gross settlement system for large-value interbank and government payments. It provides instant finality and delivery-versus-payment for wholesale transactions among banks and government entities.

Launched in 2022 by the State Bank of Pakistan, Raast is Pakistan’s first instant payment system enabling real-time digital payments (person-to-person and person-to-merchant) around the clock [oai_citation:0‡sbp.org.pk]. It is designed for low-cost, instant credit transfers between bank accounts using unique IDs like mobile phone numbers [oai_citation:1‡sbp.org.pk].

1LINK is a consortium-owned interbank switch that operates Pakistan’s ATM and POS network and a real-time retail payment service. It links 27 member banks for shared ATM withdrawals/deposits and point-of-sale transactions, enabling cross-bank card usage. 1LINK also offers a 24/7 instant payment service (sometimes called AsiaPay) for immediate interbank fund transfers via mobile and internet banking. As a joint venture of major banks, 1LINK provides settlement and switching infrastructure (including the domestic card scheme PayPak) and gateways for e-commerce and QR payments. It processes hundreds of millions of ATM/POS transactions annually, underpinning retail payments in Pakistan.

1LINK Inter Bank Funds Transfer (IBFT) is a 24/7 instant retail transfer service operated by 1LINK. It allows customers to instantly push money between bank accounts using online or mobile banking (including OTP authorization), facilitating P2P and some bill payments.

Pakistan’s Branchless Banking (BB) wallets like Telenor’s Easypaisa and Jazz’s JazzCash are mobile-based electronic wallets licensed by SBP. These allow users to open mobile accounts, deposit cash at agents, and perform P2P transfers, bill payments and merchant payments via apps or USSD. BB wallets connect to banking rails (e.g. via 1LINK) and to SBP’s retail payment systems. They are interoperable with bank accounts and allow cash-in/cash-out through partnered outlets. In FY2024, BB wallet transactions reached 2.697 billion in volume (about PKR 8.8 trillion). Wallet adoption is widespread, especially for remittances and rural payments.

Raast is an instant retail payment system developed by the SBP, launched in December 2021 to enable 24/7 electronic transfers between individuals, businesses and government entities. It allows immediate settlement of small-value payments (original limit Rs 50,000, later increased) using aliases like mobile number or ID:contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}. Raast is used for person-to-person transfers, bill payments, remittances and government payouts. The SBP operates the network and participants include all commercial banks. Transfers via Raast settle in seconds and funds become instantly available. Raast rapidly grew after launch, facilitating digital transactions nationwide:contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}.

PayPak is the domestic payment card scheme (debit card network) operated by 1LINK. Launched in 2016, PayPak cards (EMV chip) are accepted at ATMs and POS terminals nationwide and offer a lower-cost alternative to foreign networks. It is now a major provider of debit payment processing in Pakistan.

PayPak is Pakistan’s domestic payment card scheme, introduced in April 2016 under SBP guidance and owned by 1LINK:contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}. It is a debit card brand that can be co-badged on bank accounts, intended to reduce reliance on foreign card networks. PayPak cards can be used at ATMs and POS terminals across Pakistan via the 1LINK switch. The scheme supports PIN-based point-of-sale, ATM withdrawals and domestic e-commerce. By 2024 it had over 13 million cards issued:contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}. PayPak transactions are settled within the country, lowering transaction costs. 1LINK operates the network while banks issue and acquire PayPak cards:contentReference[oaicite:8]{index=8}.

sistemas.descricao: BLIK is a popular mobile payment system (launched 2015) that uses one-time codes and QR for real-time payments at merchants and between individuals via smartphone apps.

Euro Elixir is an ACH system for euro transfers in Poland. It processes euro retail payments via SEPA infrastructure (STEP2) and settles them in TARGET2 [oai_citation:24‡numeral.io].
TARGET2-NBP is the Polish segment of the euro area RTGS system (TARGET2) operated by Narodowy Bank Polski. It settles euro payments in real time for Polish banks [oai_citation:19‡numeral.io].
SORBNET2 is the real-time gross settlement system for Polish zloty, operated by Narodowy Bank Polski. It provides immediate settlement of large-value PLN payments [oai_citation:20‡numeral.io].

Express Elixir is Poland’s nationwide instant payment system (launched 2012). It uses ISO 20022 messages and provides immediate transfers (up to 100k PLN) 24/7, including settlement for BLIK mobile payments [oai_citation:23‡numeral.io].
Elixir is the main ACH system operated by KIR for zloty transfers. It batches credit transfers, direct debits and cheques in three clearing sessions per business day [oai_citation:21‡numeral.io].

SICOI (Sistema de Compensação Interbancária) is the retail clearing system operated by Bank of Portugal. It processes checks, commercial bills, direct debits (SEPA), credit transfers (SEPA and local), instant transfers, and card payment clearing [oai_citation:25‡bportugal.pt] [oai_citation:26‡bportugal.pt].

MB WAY is a mobile payments app connected to the Multibanco network. It allows users to send money by phone number, pay with QR codes, and make online payments. It has nationwide adoption (28 banks) [oai_citation:28‡ppro.com].

As a member of the Eurozone, Portugal participates in TARGET2, the European System of Central Banks’ RTGS platform for euro. TARGET2-BP (run by the Bank of Portugal) handles large-value interbank transfers and real-time settlement of bulk payments across euro-area banks. Portuguese banks use TARGET2 for international and high-value EUR transactions. It is connected to domestic systems, ensuring cross-border euro transfers settle instantly between central bank accounts. TARGET2 is a key component of Portugal’s payment infrastructure for large-value and time-critical payments.
SIC (Sistema de Liquidação Contínua de pagamentos) is the Bank of Portugal’s RTGS system for euro. It settles large-value interbank payments with finality.
Multibanco is the nationwide ATM and EFTPOS network operated by SIBS, linking 27 banks. It supports cash withdrawals, POS debit/credit transactions and is the infrastructure behind MB WAY.
TARGET2-PT is the Portuguese segment of the euro area RTGS system (TARGET2), managed by Bank of Portugal, enabling cross-border and domestic euro settlements.

SICOI (Sistema de Compensação Interbancária) is the clearinghouse for retail payments in Portugal, operated by the Banco de Portugal. It processes and nets interbank credit transfers, direct debits and card/electronic payments submitted by banks each day. In 2024 SICOI cleared 4.7 billion transactions (about €776.7 billion):contentReference[oaicite:44]{index=44}. This covers almost all non-cash retail transactions (98%+). SICOI settles net positions via the central bank or TARGET2 accounts. It is the backbone of Portugal’s retail payments, enabling multilateral netting and reducing settlement risk across banks.

Multibanco is Portugal’s national interbank network run by SIBS (Sociedade Interbancária de Serviços). It connects ATMs and POS terminals of 27 banks. Through 12,700+ ATMs (2024) and POS, it allows cash withdrawals, transfers, mobile top-ups, and bill payments. Multibanco also encompasses MBNet (internet payments) and Via Verde (toll payments) services. It processed over 75 million ATM/POS transactions monthly (2014 data):contentReference[oaicite:46]{index=46}. Multibanco’s integrated services make it a versatile payment system used extensively by Portuguese consumers.
This subsystem of SICOI enables instant transfers in euro between accounts at any time. Transfers are settled in real time by Bank of Portugal [oai_citation:27‡bportugal.pt].

The Palau Stablecoin (PSC) is an experimental digital currency project of the Republic of Palau, backed 1:1 by the US dollar. Launched as a pilot in partnership with Ripple, PSC was issued on the XRP Ledger to test programmable payments in Palau’s USD-based economy:contentReference[oaicite:12]{index=12}. It enables instant peer-to-peer transfers and conversion with physical USD at participating banks. The government funded the pilot but PSC has no legal tender status and remained limited to testing. Palau’s central authorities view it as a digital extension of the US currency. Operations included issuance, transfers and redemption mechanisms governed by the pilot project. No live adoption figures are published; the project was in a pilot/research phase:contentReference[oaicite:13]{index=13}.

LBTR is Paraguay’s RTGS system (Liquidación Bruta en Tiempo Real) operated by the Central Bank of Paraguay. Launched in 2013, it settles large-value payments (including USD/EUR transactions) individually and immediately [oai_citation:8‡cbpn.currencyresearch.com].

LBTR (L플qu𝆜n Bruta en Tiempo Real) is Paraguay’s real-time gross settlement system operated by the Central Bank of Paraguay (BCP). Launched in the 1990s, it settles high-value and urgent interbank payments (above 5 million guaraníes) on a one-by-one basis. Banks and financial institutions use LBTR for large transfers, securities settlement and settlement of net results from retail clearing. The BCP regulates and operates LBTR, ensuring immediate finality of large-value transactions between participants.

SML (Sistema Multilateral de Liquidez) is a multilateral clearing mechanism established in 2018 among Mercosur central banks. Paraguayan banks use SML to settle multilateral net positions for cross-border payments, enhancing efficiency [oai_citation:10‡cbpn.currencyresearch.com].

Paraguay’s ACH is a deferred net settlement system under the SIPAP arrangement, operated by the Central Bank of Paraguay. It processes batch credit transfers and direct debits in local currency each business day.

Bancard is the national card clearing and processing association in Paraguay. It clears transactions for major card schemes (Visa, Mastercard, Cabal) within the country, enabling merchant and ATM card payments.

Bancard S.A. is the Paraguayan banks’ payment network and card association. It operates the POS switch for debit and credit card transactions and manages QR payment connectivity. Bancard issues co-branded debit/credit cards and provides a unified platform for electronic merchant acquiring and online e-commerce. Bancard also launched an interoperable QR payment standard (via PagosPy). It facilitated rapid growth in card and QR usage (e.g. QR transactions reached 49M in early 2025:contentReference[oaicite:24]{index=24}). Bancard is a private entity jointly owned by banks, under central bank oversight, ensuring nationwide acceptance of electronic payments.

Paraguay's Instant Payment System (SPI) is a 24/7 real-time transfer platform launched in May 2022. It enables immediate fund transfers (in under 1 minute) between accounts and wallets across banks, free of charge [oai_citation:9‡cbpn.currencyresearch.com].

The Paraguayan ACH is an interbank clearinghouse for retail credit transfers and direct debits (e.g., payroll, utility bills). Operated under the BCP framework, it processes batch transactions for participating banks. Payments submitted are cleared in batches (typically twice daily) and net settled via LBTR. The ACH is used for larger retail payments that are not time-critical. It complements SPI by handling higher-value transfers beyond SPI limits. The ACH is regulated by BCP and involves major banks interchanging payment files according to agreed schedules.

SPI is Paraguay’s instant payment system, launched May 2022 by the Central Bank (BCP). It enables immediate 24/7 transfers of up to ₲5,000,000 (about US$700) between banks. SPI transactions settle in real time, with funds available instantly. It is used for person-to-person, business-to-person and e-commerce payments through banking apps and mobile wallets. SPI quickly became the dominant retail channel – by 2025 it handled 95% of payment volumes in Paraguay:contentReference[oaicite:22]{index=22}. The BCP owns and oversees SPI, requiring its use by banks and non-bank payment providers to promote digital payments.
National payment app
Bill payment system

QPS is the central interbank payment and settlement system of Qatar, operated by Qatar Central Bank. It is an RTGS platform (SWIFT-based) that allows immediate settlement of funds and securities transfers between banks [oai_citation:29‡qcb.gov.qa].

QPAY is an online payment gateway service launched by QNB (Qatar National Bank) in 2005 for e-commerce. It processes debit and prepaid card transactions for merchants. QPAY provides 24/7 transaction authorization and routing for online merchants in Qatar, integrating with banks for settlement. It supports secure authentication (two-factor) and tokenization. While QPAY was originally a QNB service, its function is akin to a national e-commerce switch. It enables Qatar-based online retail payments and is co-branded on many merchant sites.

Qatar Mobile Payment (QMP), launched in 2020, is Qatar Central Bank’s national mobile wallet framework. It allows interoperable e-wallets: users can download any licensed mobile payment app (from banks or fintechs) and perform peer-to-peer transfers and P2M payments. QMP uses phone numbers as identifiers and supports QR payments. By 2025, about 1.344 million mobile wallets were registered under QMP, with 189,000 transactions in May 2025:contentReference[oaicite:51]{index=51}. The platform promotes financial inclusion by enabling instant transfers between mobile wallets, independent of issuing provider.

NAPS is Qatar’s centralized card payment switch, established in 1996. It connects ATMs, POS and e-commerce terminals of all major banks. NAPS routes debit and prepaid card transactions across banks and also connects Qatar to GCC networks and Egypt. It supports 24/7 transaction processing and was one of the first in the region to implement full EMV chip technology for both acquiring and issuing:contentReference[oaicite:50]{index=50}. Member banks share the NAPS infrastructure to accept payments and withdrawals using national and international card schemes. Settlement is done bilaterally among banks.

The Electronic Cheque Clearing (ECC) system, launched in 2003, is Qatar’s cheque imaging and clearing platform. It converts paper checks into electronic images and data, allowing banks to exchange cheques digitally. The system ensures efficient clearing and fraud prevention. Member banks deposit cheque images daily; the system provides acceptance/rejection and forwards clearing files to the settlement engine. ECC streamlines cheque processing nationwide, reducing physical document exchange and enabling same-day clearing.

QATCH is Qatar’s centralized system for interbank direct debit and credit transfers (launched 2010). It allows bulk payroll processing, salary payments and direct debits among banks. QATCH supports intra-day bulk credit transfers (e.g. company payrolls) and standardized direct debit clearing. It is integrated with the Wage Protection System (WPS) for automating salary payments. Banks submit files that are cleared and net settled via the Qatar Central Bank accounts. QATCH provides efficient electronic clearing of non-card bank transfers.

The Wage Protection System (WPS) is Qatar’s payroll compliance system that requires all companies to pay employee salaries through approved bank accounts. Under WPS, payroll files are submitted to authorized banks or exchange houses, which then disburse salaries via QATCH transfers to beneficiaries. The system ensures timely salary payments and reduces under-the-table cash payments. It is managed by the Qatar Central Bank in coordination with the Ministry of Labour, using the QATCH infrastructure for settlement.

QMP is an instant, interoperable mobile payments switch launched by Qatar Central Bank. It connects all licensed mobile payment providers in Qatar for 24/7 instant transfers via mobile apps (using phone number or QR) [oai_citation:30‡qcb.gov.qa].

Fawran is Qatar Central Bank’s instant payments service, launched in March 2024. It enables real-time interbank payments any time (including holidays). Customers can send QR code or alias-based transfers via mobile banking apps and internet banking, and funds are delivered to recipients instantly. Fawran processes small-value and larger retail payments, providing immediate settlement. In May 2025, Fawran handled 17% of total transaction volume (about 9.18 million transfers):contentReference[oaicite:53]{index=53}. The system is aligned with Qatar’s financial sector strategy to modernize payment infrastructure and reduce reliance on cash.
National payment system
Online payments

Plăți Instant is Romania’s domestic instant payment scheme (launched 2019), enabling near-real-time RON transfers 24×7. It is administered by TRANSFOND under BNR regulation. Individuals and businesses use it for immediate peer-to-peer and peer-to-merchant transfers via IBAN or QR proxies. Settlement is immediate with irrevocability. By 2023 it processed ~75 million instant transfers [oai_citation:7‡transfond.ro]. This system complements the batch ACH (SENT) by providing immediate finality.
Managed by the National Bank of Romania, ReGIS is the core RTGS for time-critical transfers (typically a few thousand large payments per day):contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}.

SENT (STFD-TRANSFOND Electronic Net settlement) is Romania’s interbank ACH, clearing low-value RON credit transfers, direct debits, checks and bills [oai_citation:2‡upet.ro].%20Bartalis.pdf#:~:text=carried%20out%20only%20by%20BNR,Compensation%20is). Operated by TRANSFOND under BNR oversight, it processes payments in multilateral batch sessions (files up to 1,000 items, settled three times daily [oai_citation:3‡upet.ro].%20Bartalis.pdf#:~:text=carried%20out%20only%20by%20BNR,Compensation%20is)). All SENT-cleared items are net-settled in ReGIS (the RTGS). In 2023, SENT handled ~158 million credit transfers and ~75 million instant RON transfers (as part of its instant component) [oai_citation:4‡transfond.ro].

Visa and Mastercard cards are widely used in Romania for retail and online payments. Their transactions are settled through Transfond’s infrastructure and ReGIS:contentReference[oaicite:10]{index=10}.

Launched by Transfond in 2023, Plăți Instant provides 24/7 real-time transfers (settlement within seconds) between accounts:contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}. Its usage grew rapidly: 13.5 million instant payments in 2022 and 75 million in 2023:contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}.

RoPay is a mobile payment service (launched 2018) enabling instant transfers between bank accounts via mobile app and QR codes [oai_citation:9‡transfond.ro]. Users link their phone number to their bank account. Under BNR and TRANSFOND oversight, RoPay routes payments through the instant payment infrastructure (Plăți Instant). It allows 24×7 person-to-person and merchant payments using a QR scan or mobile app. It's essentially the mobile front-end for the instant scheme [oai_citation:10‡transfond.ro].
RoPay is Transfond’s mobile instant-payment app (launched 2025). It enables 24/7 peer-to-peer transfers using a phone number linked to a bank account:contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}.

SENT (Sistemul de Compensare Electronică Automată) is Romania’s national ACH for credit transfers, direct debits, checks, etc., run by Transfond:contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}:contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}. In 2022 it processed about 173.6 million RON credit transfers:contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}.

ReGIS (Romanian Gross Settlement) is Romania’s central-bank RTGS, launched in 2005 [oai_citation:0‡upet.ro].%20Bartalis.pdf#:~:text=50%2C000%20lei,March%202018%20it%20has%20been). It settles large-value interbank transfers (typically >50k RON) in real time, providing final, irrevocable settlement. It is operated by the National Bank of Romania (BNR) and uses the SWIFT network for communication [oai_citation:1‡transfond.ro]. ReGIS also serves as the settlement engine for other payment systems (such as the national ACH).
Interbank payment system
Retail payment system

The NBS Clearing System processes net-settled low-value payments in dinars (credit transfers, direct debits) that are below the RTGS threshold. Settlements are calculated at designated intervals, with final settlement on NBS accounts. It serves salaries, supplier payments, and other routine transfers.

Serbia’s automated clearing house (ACH) processes bulk low-value transfers (e.g. salaries, vendor payments) between banks. Transactions are netted and settled in periodic clearing cycles each business day.

DinaCard is the national debit/credit card scheme established by the National Bank of Serbia. It is used for domestic ATM withdrawals and POS transactions. DinaCard allows domestic transactions in dinars, and has alliances with international networks for cross-border acceptance.

DinaCard is Serbia’s national payment card network, created by the NBS. It processes ATM and POS transactions for domestic cards. In 2022 DinaCard usage grew significantly, and DinaCards are accepted at virtually all POS terminals and ATMs in Serbia:contentReference[oaicite:13]{index=13}.
Visa credit and debit cards are issued by Serbian banks and accepted by merchants and ATMs nationwide. Visa is one of the main card schemes used in Serbia.
Mastercard (and Maestro) cards are widely used in Serbia for payments and ATM withdrawals. Major banks issue Mastercard cards, and acceptance is widespread.

The NBS RTGS (Serbian RSD Real-Time Gross Settlement System) is operated by the National Bank of Serbia (NBS). It processes large-value and urgent transfers between banks in Serbian dinars in real time. Transfers above RSD 300,000 are mandatory on RTGS. It runs during business days and ensures instant final settlement in central bank money.

Operated by the National Bank of Serbia, the RTGS (also known as SAMOS) handles high-value interbank payments in real time. It settles transactions continuously during the day, processing on the order of ~200 million payments annually (2023):contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}.

The NBS Instant Payment System (IPS) is an instant payment platform launched in 2018 by the National Bank of Serbia. It enables 24/7 real-time credit transfers in dinars between consumers and businesses. Funds are credited to payees almost instantaneously. All banks connect to IPS, allowing transfers via mobile apps or internet banking at any time.

The Instant Payments System (IPS) is managed by the National Bank of Serbia. Launched in 2018, it enables immediate fund transfers between customers’ accounts 24/7. By 2023 it had 22 participating banks and handled about 66 million transactions (~$6.7B):contentReference[oaicite:11]{index=11}.

Mir is Russia’s domestic card payment network (launched 2014) [oai_citation:16‡en.wikipedia.org]. It is operated by NSPK (under Bank of Russia) and provides local clearing for Visa/Mastercard and Mir cards. Over 400 million Mir cards have been issued (Q4 2024) [oai_citation:17‡cbr.ru]. Mir processes POS and ATM transactions within Russia, including contactless and mobile (Mir Pay) payments, bypassing foreign schemes.
sistemas.detalhes: Operated by the National Payment Card System (NSPK), a subsidiary of the Central Bank of Russia (CBR). Established in 2015 as Russia's response to international sanctions, it processes debit/credit transactions through a proprietary network. The system functions independently of Visa/Mastercard using EMV chip technology and supports contactless payments via Mir Pay. It processes domestic transactions while partnering with UnionPay for international acceptance. Mandatory for government payments including pensions, salaries, and social benefits .

sistemas.descricao: 24/7 instant transfer service using phone numbers
sistemas.detalhes: Operated by the Central Bank of Russia with NSPK as processing partner. Enables real-time P2P transfers using mobile numbers or QR codes. Supports bill payments, merchant transactions, and government disbursements. Transactions complete within seconds and settle through CBR infrastructure. Fee structure: Free for transfers under ₽100,000 monthly; 0.5% fee above threshold .

sistemas.descricao: CBDC pilot for retail and government payments
sistemas.detalhes: Central Bank of Russia-operated digital currency functioning as third form of national currency alongside cash/non-cash. Uses two-tier distribution: CBR issues to banks, which distribute to users via digital wallets. Supports programmable smart contracts for conditional payments (e.g., welfare disbursements). Piloted since August 2023 with 15 banks and 2,500+ wallets. Scheduled for mass adoption starting September 2026 with mandatory implementation timelines for banks .

sistemas.descricao: Core interbank settlement backbone
sistemas.detalhes: Operated by CBR to ensure stability of 28 payment systems and 354 money transfer operators. Includes RTGS for high-value settlements and netting systems for retail transactions. Processes 85.4% of retail payments electronically. Provides settlement finality in central bank money and oversees compliance with financial stability standards .

sistemas.descricao: Sanctions-evasion channels using digital assets
sistemas.detalhes: Informal networks facilitating cross-border transactions via cryptocurrencies like USDT. Used to bypass financial sanctions by converting rubles to crypto through exchanges like Garantex. Supported by legislation legalizing crypto for international trade. Integrated with alternative banking partners in friendly countries .

sistemas.descricao: Mandated payment channels for public funds

The Bank of Russia Payment System (BRPS) is the RTGS platform for high-value interbank payments. It clears government and interbank transfers in real time; by 2020 it handled ~93% of payments by value, about 7 million transfers per day:contentReference[oaicite:11]{index=11}.

The Faster Payments System (SBP), launched in 2019, is a 24/7 instant transfer network by the Bank of Russia. It allows P2P and P2M transfers via mobile number or QR across participating banks:contentReference[oaicite:13]{index=13}. As of April 2025 it had processed 28.7 billion transactions (143.3 trillion RUB):contentReference[oaicite:14]{index=14}.

Mir is Russia’s national debit/credit card scheme (by NSPK) introduced in 2015. It has become widely used for salaries, pensions and consumer payments. Over 400.6 million Mir cards were issued by Q4 2024:contentReference[oaicite:16]{index=16}.

SARIE (Saudi Arabian Riyal Interbank Express) – sorry, SARIE is the Bank of Russia’s RTGS for ruble – it settled all large-value payments in 2012 reference [oai_citation:11‡bis.org]; large transfers are settled in real time. Each licensed bank holds a nostro account with the central bank; transfers are processed via SWIFT messaging [oai_citation:12‡eccb-centralbank.org]. SARIE provides finality for interbank and customer-initiated transfers on gross basis.

The Faster Payments System (SBP) is Russia’s real-time P2P platform (launched 2019) [oai_citation:13‡cbr.ru]. It lets individuals instantly transfer money using a phone number or QR code 24×7, with immediate final settlement. SBP is operated by Bank of Russia (settlement) and NSPK (clearing). Over 200 banks are connected; by May 2025 SBP had processed 30.2 billion transactions (RUB151.7T) [oai_citation:14‡cbr.ru]. It supports P2P, P2M (merchant) and bill payments.

The Digital Ruble is Russia’s central bank digital currency, being piloted by the Bank of Russia [oai_citation:19‡cbr.ru]. It is a tokenized digital form of the ruble for payments by individuals and businesses. Users hold digital wallets at banks and can transfer digital rubles for P2P, P2B, etc. The pilot (2021 onward) involves thousands of users and tests wallet interoperability and retail use cases [oai_citation:20‡cbr.ru].

MTN MoMo is Rwanda’s largest mobile money service. It lets users store and transfer money via their mobile phones using USSD or app. Customers can send P2P transfers, pay merchants, top-up airtime and pay bills. Settlement is handled through interbank netting (via eKash/RIPPS). It has wide rural and urban adoption.
Contactless payment system

eKash is Rwanda’s national instant payments platform (launched 2023) enabling 24/7 transfers across banks, mobile money, microfinance and fintechs [oai_citation:23‡equitygroupholdings.com] [oai_citation:24‡africanenda.org]. Operated by RSwitch under BNR guidance, eKash uses ISO 20022 messaging [oai_citation:25‡africanenda.org]. It allows real-time P2P, P2B and merchant payments via mobile apps, USSD or QR. Transactions are net-settled daily through RIPPS. By mid-2023 eKash had achieved full interoperability among all banks and MNO wallets [oai_citation:26‡equitygroupholdings.com].

eKash is the Rwanda National Digital Payment System’s instant payment service. Launched in 2022, it provides 24/7 real-time P2P and P2M transfers across banks and mobile money platforms:contentReference[oaicite:20]{index=20}:contentReference[oaicite:21]{index=21}.

Airtel Money is a mobile wallet platform by Airtel Rwanda. It offers services similar to MTN MoMo via USSD and app – users can deposit cash at agents, transfer to other Airtel Money users, pay bills, and buy goods. It interconnects with eKash for cash-out to bank accounts.

RIPPS (Rwanda Integrated Payments Processing System) is the RTGS operated by the National Bank of Rwanda. Commercial banks maintain pre-funded accounts at BNR and settle interbank transfers in real time:contentReference[oaicite:19]{index=19}.

The Rwanda Integrated Payments Processing System (RIPPS) is the National Bank of Rwanda’s RTGS, processing interbank settlement for large-value transactions [oai_citation:22‡africanenda.org]. Banks hold nostro accounts at BNR; RIPPS settles transfers in real time. It has been upgraded to 24×7 operation and aligned with ISO 20022. Settlement of positions (from clearing) is final in central bank money.

MTN Mobile Money and Airtel Money are popular mobile payment services in Rwanda, enabling P2P transfers, bill payments, and merchant payments via phones. These wallets interoperate through RSwitch’s infrastructure:contentReference[oaicite:23]{index=23}.
SmartCash is Rwanda’s shared ATM and POS card network (operated by RSwitch). It provides customers with ATM withdrawals and point-of-sale payments on one network.

RSwitch (a private company in partnership with BNR) runs Rwanda’s national e-payment switch. It enables interoperability between banks, MTN/Airtel mobile money, and card services. It switches and clears transactions (like SmartCash ATM/debit cards) and settles via the central bank:contentReference[oaicite:22]{index=22}.
National debit card switch and scheme
sistemas.detalhes: Operated by Saudi Payments (SAMA subsidiary) since 1990. Connects all ATMs and POS terminals in the Kingdom, processing domestic debit transactions. Mandatory for Saudi banks with EMV contactless functionality (Atheer). Co-brands with Visa/Mastercard for international acceptance. Processes NFC payments via mada Pay app and supports cash withdrawals at merchants (Naqd service) .

sistemas.descricao: 24/7 real-time credit transfer platform
Centralized bill presentment and payment system

Mobile-based payment apps
Fintech innovation testing environment

In 2021 SAMA rolled out an instant payments layer on SARIE. By 2024 the system was processing ~593 million real-time payments per year (a 50% CAGR over 3 years):contentReference[oaicite:47]{index=47}.

Mada (formerly SPAN) is Saudi Arabia’s national debit card network connecting all ATMs and point-of-sale terminals:contentReference[oaicite:49]{index=49}. Introduced in 2015, it handles the bulk of card transactions. Card use in e-commerce and at PoS terminals has grown dramatically, reaching 10.4 billion PoS transactions in 2024:contentReference[oaicite:50]{index=50}.

SADAD is a centralized bill-presentment and payment platform:contentReference[oaicite:52]{index=52}. Launched in 2004, it lets individuals and businesses pay utilities, telecom bills, traffic fines etc. It processed ~364 million transactions in 2024:contentReference[oaicite:53]{index=53}.

Smartphone wallets such as Apple Pay, Samsung Pay and STC Pay are integrated with the Mada network. These have accelerated cashless usage, contributing to ~79% of retail payments being electronic by 2024:contentReference[oaicite:55]{index=55}.

SARIE (Saudi Arabian Riyal Interbank Express) is the central RTGS, launched in 1997 [oai_citation:50‡bis.org]. Operated by SAMA, it settles high-value interbank riyal payments in real time via SWIFT messages, eliminating settlement risk [oai_citation:51‡bis.org]. SARIE also settles other systems’ obligations (e.g. securities, equities).

Sarie (note lowercase) is Saudi Arabia’s instant payment platform (launched 2021) [oai_citation:52‡whitesight.net]. It enables instant bank-to-bank transfers 24×7 for payroll, P2P, and bill payments. Developed by Saudi Payments (with IBM/Mastercard), it handled 593 million transactions in 2024 (50% CAGR) [oai_citation:53‡whitesight.net]. Sarie uses an API-first ISO 20022 architecture, allowing transfers via mobile/QR aliases.

Mada (formerly SPAN) is Saudi Payments’ national card switch [oai_citation:55‡bis.org]. Introduced in 2015 under SAMA, it connects all ATMs and POS terminals across Saudi Arabia. Mada processes domestic VISA/Mastercard transactions and has become the default for e-commerce [oai_citation:56‡whitesight.net]. It supports contactless, tokenized payments (via smartphones and wearables).

SADAD is an electronic bill presentment and payment system (launched 2004) [oai_citation:58‡bis.org]. It allows individuals and businesses to pay government and private bills (utilities, telecom, fines, etc.) through bank channels. SADAD has over 300 billers and grew from 266M tx in 2020 to 364M in 2024 [oai_citation:59‡whitesight.net]. It is integrated into online banking and mobile apps, often transparently to the user [oai_citation:60‡whitesight.net].
Mastercard (and Maestro) cards are similarly available and accepted. They are used where Visa is accepted, providing an alternative international card option.

Previously, banks cleared paper cheques via a manual process at the central bank. SOLATS’s launch automates cheque clearing. Cheque usage has declined (about 155,945 items cleared in 2022):contentReference[oaicite:23]{index=23}.
Visa cards (debit and credit) are issued by Solomon Islands banks and accepted at select merchants and ATMs, particularly in urban areas and tourist locations.

Solomons Automated Transfer System (SOLATS) is the RTGS platform newly launched by the Central Bank of Solomon Islands in 2024. It settles interbank payments in real time, replacing the previous manual cheque clearing. SOLATS enables banks to transfer funds instantly and supports various payment options including electronic and mobile channels.

Bank South Pacific (BSP) offers a mobile banking service in Solomon Islands (*277# USSD code) allowing customers to view balances, transfer funds, pay bills and top up airtime. This service enables digital payments to reach remote users via their mobile phones. It uses BSP’s core banking infrastructure.

The Solomon Islands Automated Transfer System (SOLATS), launched in 2024, provides CBSI-operated RTGS and ACH services. It automates both real-time high-value settlement and batch retail clearing, replacing the prior manual interbank transfers:contentReference[oaicite:22]{index=22}.
Mobile payment service
Widely accepted

Banks in Seychelles use a centralized clearing process at the central bank to clear paper cheques. Cheque use is declining as digital payments grow, and the system is being phased out (cheque usage was slated to end by 2025).

SEFT (Seychelles Electronic Funds Transfer) is the automated clearing system used by Seychelles banks for bulk domestic payments such as salaries and bill payments. It nets transfers and settles them through CBS accounts on each settlement day.

The Central Bank of Seychelles (CBS) operates an RTGS system for settling high-value and urgent transactions in Seychellois rupees between commercial banks. The RTGS ensures immediate finality in central bank money for large interbank transfers, including monetary policy operations. It was implemented around 2014-2015.
Mastercard and Maestro cards are common in Seychelles. Banks issue Mastercard cards, and they are accepted at nearly all merchants and ATMs, providing an alternative to Visa.

The Seychelles Electronic Funds Transfer (SEFT) system is an online clearing system introduced by CBS for retail payments. It processes electronic transfers between banks on the same day. SEFT replaced a manual interchange of cheques and shortens clearing cycles to same-day settlement. It is accessible online to banks for submitting payment instructions throughout the day.
Eboo is a digital wallet licensed by the Central Bank of Seychelles. It enables instant mobile transfers and payments via an app or QR code, operating 24/7 to facilitate cashless transactions.
Visa cards (debit and credit) are widely used in Seychelles. Banks issue Visa-branded cards, and they are accepted by merchants and ATMs across the islands.

Seychelles maintains an Electronic Cheque Clearing system for clearing paper cheques. Banks submit images or MICR data of cheques to the central clearing house, which nets out positions between banks and settles via SEFT/RTGS at the central bank. This system speeds up cheque processing and settlement.

Airtel Money is a mobile wallet service offered by Airtel Seychelles. Customers can use their mobile phone to send money, purchase airtime, and pay merchants. It is accessible via a USSD code and integrated with local banks for cash-in/cash-out transactions. Adoption is medium in Seychelles.
Primary payment method

Swish is a widely-used mobile payment application launched in 2012 by Swedish banks (GetSwish). It allows real-time transfers between smartphones by phone number or QR code. Swish payments are settled instantly via RIX-INST [oai_citation:16‡finofo.com]. Over 5 million users conduct billions of transactions annually.
Digital identity

RIX-RTGS is the Swedish central bank’s real-time gross settlement service for high-value transfers during banking hours. It is operated by Sveriges Riksbank and connects banks and clearinghouses. Approximately SEK 550 billion is settled per day on RIX-RTGS [oai_citation:13‡finofo.com] (average payment ~SEK 20M).

RIX-INST is Sweden’s instant payment platform (available 24/7) for low-value payments, run by the Riksbank. It was connected to TIPS in 2022 and since 2024 it settles Swish mobile payments [oai_citation:15‡finofo.com]. RIX-INST ensures immediate credit of payee accounts around the clock.

PayNow is a nationwide instant transfer service introduced in 2017. It allows users to send and receive money instantly via proxy identifiers (NRIC, mobile number or UEN) instead of account numbers. PayNow transactions are cleared via the FAST/RTGS infrastructure. It is widely used for peer-to-peer transfers and e-commerce payments.
Super-app wallet
Visa credit and debit cards are commonly used in Singapore. Nearly all banks issue Visa cards, and they are accepted by most merchants and ATMs across the country.

The Interbank GIRO system facilitates bulk recurring payments (e.g. bills, salaries) in batches. It nets debits and credits among banks and settles the net positions through MAS on a scheduled basis each day.

FAST is Singapore’s near-real-time gross settlement service for retail payments, launched in 2014. It allows customers to transfer funds instantly between banks any time of day. FAST handles day-to-day transfers such as bill payments and everyday transactions, with all banks and finance companies participating.

GIRO is the Automated Funds Transfer System for recurring credit transfers (bill payments, payroll, etc.) between bank accounts. It allows organisations to debit customers on fixed schedules. Both Direct Debit and On-Demand GIRO services exist, with a batch settlement process at end of day.
Dash is Singtel’s digital wallet that integrates with FAST and PayNow. Users can top up Dash and send money instantly via FAST/PayNow or pay merchants via QR codes, facilitating 24/7 mobile payments.
MAS Electronic Payment System (MEPS+) is Singapore’s RTGS for large-value interbank transfers in Singapore Dollars. It settles wholesale and urgent payments in central bank money on business days.

The MAS Electronic Payment System (MEPS+), now part of FAST, is the central RTGS platform operated by MAS for interbank settlements in SGD. It processes high-value transactions, liquidity management, and acts as central counterparty for ancillary systems. Its queue management allows liquidity optimisation.

FAST is an interbank real-time transfer service that operates 24/7. It allows instant bank-to-bank transfers up to SGD 200,000 between participating banks and institutions:contentReference[oaicite:15]{index=15}, heavily used for retail and corporate payments.

NETS (Network for Electronic Transfers) is the main domestic payment network in Singapore, handling debit card transactions and Singapore’s contactless payment (Nets FlashPay) and QR code (Nets QR) systems. It is a private sector switch that clears and settles ATM/POS transactions between banks and merchants.
Mastercard (including Maestro) cards are also widely used in Singapore. They are issued by major banks and accepted by all major merchants and ATMs alongside Visa and NETS.
National payment system

Slovenian banks participate directly in TARGET2 (T2) for high-value and urgent euro-denominated payments. TARGET2 settlement is final in central bank money. All Slovenian banks with euro accounts have access to T2 through Banka Slovenije.
Mastercard (including Maestro) is widely used in Slovenia. It is issued by major banks and accepted at most merchants and ATMs.

Slovenia relies on the pan-European STEP2 clearing platform (operated by EBA Clearing) for euro credit transfers and direct debits. Banka Slovenije connects domestic banks to STEP2 to process SEPA payments with pan-European participants. This effectively serves as the national ACH (retail clearing) system.

Bankart (the Slovenian clearing house) together with Nets launched a domestic instant payments system in 2018. It enables real-time transfers 24/7, supporting fast mobile and online payments in Slovenia:contentReference[oaicite:21]{index=21}.

Slovenian banks participate in the SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (via TIPS) for sub-second EUR payments. This allows individuals and businesses to send money instantly to accounts in Slovenia and across the Eurozone.

TARGET Instant Payment Settlement (TIPS) provides Slovenian banks a 24/7 platform for instant euro transfers compliant with SEPA Instant scheme. All participating banks hold dedicated accounts at Banka Slovenije for instant settlements. Payments are settled in real time with immediate finality.
Visa credit and debit cards are common in Slovenia. Slovenian banks issue Visa cards, and they are accepted at virtually all merchants and ATMs.
The Bank of Slovenia’s RTGS is part of the Eurosystem’s TARGET2, settling high-value euro payments in real time between Slovenian banks and other Eurosystem participants.
Bankart operates the national card network for Slovenia. All major banks issue Bankart/Maestro or Visa/Mastercard debit cards, and Bankart switches domestic POS/ATM transactions within Slovenia.
Slovenia uses the SEPA Credit Transfer scheme for regular interbank payments. Banks send batch credit transfers, which are settled periodically through STEP2/TARGET.

Visa cards (credit and debit) are widely used in Slovakia. Banks issue Visa cards and they are accepted at merchants and ATMs nationwide.
Mastercard (and Maestro) cards are commonly used in Slovakia. They are accepted by virtually all merchants and ATMs, complementing Visa and Tatrapay.

TARGET-SK is the real-time gross settlement system operated by the National Bank of Slovakia for euro payments. It provides real-time settlement for high-value interbank transfers and ancillary systems:contentReference[oaicite:18]{index=18}.

Slovak banks participate in the SEPA Instant Credit Transfer scheme through the Eurosystem’s TIPS. By end-2024, about 27% of credit transfers in Slovakia were instant:contentReference[oaicite:20]{index=20}, enabling 24/7 immediate transfers between banks.

TARGET-SK is the Slovak instalment of the Eurosystem’s TARGET2 RTGS system, operated by Národná banka Slovenska (NBS). It handles real-time settlement of large-value and urgent euro payments in Slovakia. All Slovak banks with TARGET accounts participate directly.

Tatrapay is Slovakia’s national payment card scheme. Slovak banks issue Tatrapay debit cards for domestic use alongside Visa/Mastercard. It processes POS and ATM transactions within Slovakia to reduce fees.

SIPS (Slovak Interbank Payment System) is a domestic retail system run by NBS for processing SEPA Credit Transfers and Direct Debits. It connects Slovak banks to the STEP2 pan-European clearing by EBA Clearing. Payments are settled in net batches via TARGET2.

NBS provides access for Slovak banks to the TARGET Instant Payment Settlement (TIPS) system. Since 2022 all major Slovak banks joined SEPA Instant Credit Transfers (SCT Inst) and use TIPS to settle them in real time (24/7). From 2025 instant payments are mandatory, increasing usage.

SIPS is Slovakia’s retail payment system. It handles batch settlement of SEPA Credit Transfers and Direct Debits by Slovak banks, operating as an ancillary system of TARGET2:contentReference[oaicite:19]{index=19}.

Afrimoney (formerly Zain Money) is Telecel’s mobile financial service in Sierra Leone. Customers can deposit cash at agent outlets and send money to other Afrimoney users instantly. It also supports bill payments and airtime top-ups. It is a widely recognized mobile money option in the country.

Orange Money is a telecom-based wallet offered by Orange Sierra Leone. It enables users to send money and pay for services through their phones, and is widely used especially where banks are inaccessible.
The Bank of Sierra Leone operates an automated clearing house for bulk low-value payments. Salaries, vendor payments and other recurring transfers are netted and settled in batches each day.
Visa cards (credit and debit) are common in Sierra Leone. Banks issue Visa cards and they are accepted at ATMs and merchants throughout the country.

The BSL Automated Clearing House processes net settlements of lower-value credit transfers and direct debits in Leone. It nets out participants’ daily payments and settles the net amounts via the RTGS. It handles salaries, merchant payments and other routine bulk transfers.
The Bank of Sierra Leone’s RTGS system processes high-value and urgent interbank transfers in real time. It is used for government and corporate payments and connects all licensed banks.

A national instant payment system (switch) launched in 2025 connects banks and mobile money operators. It allows real-time transfers from mobile wallets to bank accounts and vice versa, achieving interoperability. For the first time in Sierra Leone, payments can be made instantly across different systems, boosting efficiency of digital payments.

Orange Money Sierra Leone (by Orange Telkom) is a mobile wallet service enabling cash-in/out, peer-to-peer transfers, and merchant payments. It is one of the leading mobile money platforms in Sierra Leone, widely used especially in urban and rural areas.
Afrimoney is a mobile money service provided by Africell in Sierra Leone. It allows customers to deposit and transfer funds via their mobile phones and pay for goods at partnered agents.
Mastercard (including Maestro) cards are also used in Sierra Leone. They function like Visa cards, issued by local banks and accepted across merchant networks and ATMs.

The Bank of Sierra Leone (BSL) operates an RTGS system which settles high-value interbank transfers in Leone. It was implemented in 2013 with support from the Caribbean Monetary Authority. All banks can participate for urgent transfers, and the system replaced manual cheque-based settlement.

Launched in 2025, the Sierra Leone Instant Payment Service (on the Salone Payment Switch) allows instant 24/7 transfers between bank and mobile money accounts. Initial rollout included 7 banks and 2 mobile networks, enabling immediate customer-to-customer payments:contentReference[oaicite:14]{index=14}.

PagoPA is Italy’s centralized payment platform for fees, taxes, fines and utilities. Banca di San Marino provides PagoPA access for payments to public authorities:contentReference[oaicite:43]{index=43}.

The Central Bank of San Marino manages a national payments system for domestic euro transfers [oai_citation:45‡bcsm.sm]. All Sammarinese banks are connected via the Rete Interbancaria Sammarinese (RIS) secure network [oai_citation:46‡bcsm.sm]. This system handles domestic credit transfers, direct debits (SEPA) and local cheques. Banks maintain central accounts at the central bank for settlement. San Marino uses IBAN/BIC standards like SEPA for account identification [oai_citation:47‡bcsm.sm].
Visa and Mastercard cards (via Italian banks) are commonly used in San Marino for consumer and business transactions.
San Marino uses the Euro, accessing Italy’s TARGET2 RTGS for large-value euro payments in and out of the country.

Orange Money is a mobile money service offered by Sonatel in Senegal. It allows users to send/receive money, pay bills and buy goods using their mobile phone. Transactions are often initiated via USSD or smartphone apps and settled through Orange’s wallet accounts. Orange Money has very high adoption in Senegal, particularly for domestic remittances and utility payments.

Coris Money (also called CashMob, Kash Mobile) is an electronic money account issued by Coris Bank. Customers can open an e-wallet to send mobile transfers and pay with a virtual card, backed by the bank’s license.

Wari is a digital payment service that provides money transfer and bill payment via agents and a mobile app. It was one of the first electronic payment providers in Senegal, with a nationwide agent network.

GIM-UEMOA is the regional card scheme (switch) managed by the BCEAO. It processes domestic card (POS/ATM) transactions in the WAEMU region:contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}, connecting national card networks across member countries.

Orange Senegal’s e-wallet allows users to send money, pay bills, and store value via mobile phones. It is a leading mobile money provider in Senegal. The industry grew to 38M registered accounts and PPP$230M value in 2023:contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}.

Wave is a private mobile money platform (by Wari) launched in Senegal around 2018. It provides an easy-to-use mobile wallet for cash-in/out, P2P transfers, and merchant/bill payments. Wave emphasizes low fees (often free transfers) and is accessible via smartphone app or USSD. Adoption has been growing, especially among younger urban users.

SICA-UEMOA (Automated Clearing System of the UEMOA) is the multi-country clearing system managed by BCEAO covering West African countries including Senegal. It processes batch net settlement of low-value retail transactions such as credit transfers, direct debits, and cheques in CFA francs. Each UEMOA member has a national component in SICA, and settlements are ultimately cleared via the BCEAO RTGS.
Visa is an international card scheme whose debit and credit cards are issued by Senegalese banks. Visa cards are accepted by most merchants and ATMs across Senegal.

Operated by the BCEAO (regional central bank) and used by all regional banks, STAR-UEMOA settles payments in central bank money:contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}. It processed about 1.68 million transactions (CFAF 1,040,806 billion) in 2023:contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}.

Free Money is the digital wallet offered by Free Senegal (telecom operator, formerly Tigo). Launched in 2014, it provides similar services to other mobile wallets, including money transfers, bill payments, merchant payments and airtime top-ups. It was originally built on Comviva’s platform (Mobiquity Money) and has a subscriber base in the millions. Free Money aims to expand digital finance offerings through this platform.

Managed by the BCEAO, SICA-UEMOA clears and settles retail payments (bank transfers, cheques) among WAEMU banks:contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}. It processed 28,339,223 transactions (worth CFAF 78,210 billion) in 2023:contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}.

STAR-UEMOA is the regional RTGS operated by BCEAO (Central Bank of West African States) for the West African Economic and Monetary Union (UEMOA). It enables instant settlement of high-value and priority payments in CFA francs between banks in Senegal and other UEMOA member states. It connects participants through the SWIFT network or BCEAO’s private infrastructure and settles obligations in central bank money.

Wave is a US-backed fintech mobile money platform operating in Senegal. It offers instant money transfers and cash-in/out via a large network of agents. Since its launch, Wave has rapidly gained users across the country.
Mastercard (and Maestro) cards are issued by banks in Senegal as part of the international payment network. Mastercard is widely accepted at merchants and ATMs nationwide.

KashKash is a digital wallet available in Senegal for money transfers and payments. It operates as an e-money service targeting digital transactions, complementing other mobile money offerings in the market.

Wizall Money is an e-money platform in Senegal for transfers and payments, under license from the financial firm Wizall. It allows users to send money and pay for goods via their mobile wallets, targeting both urban and rural customers.

Zaad is the mobile money service provided by Telesom in Somaliland. It allows users to send money and pay bills via their phones. It is a key payment platform in Somaliland and part of Somalia’s broader mobile money sector.

Visa cards are issued by some Somali banks for customers. They are accepted at a limited number of ATMs and merchants in major cities. Visa plays a role particularly for international remittance reception and urban payments.

Hawala networks (money transfer businesses) are the dominant remittance mechanism in Somalia. Mastercard (including Maestro) cards are also present in Somalia. Banks issue them alongside Visa. Acceptance is limited but follows Visa’s presence in key locations.

EVC Plus is a mobile wallet offered by Hormuud Telecom, Somalia’s largest operator. It enables instant mobile payments and transfers. Mobile money penetration is very high (about 73% of adults use mobile financial services:contentReference[oaicite:30]{index=30}).

Sahal is the mobile money platform of Golis Telecom, serving the Puntland region of Somalia. It provides money transfer, payment and airtime purchase services via mobile phones. It competes regionally with other wallets like EVCPlus and ZAAD.

EVCPlus is a mobile financial service by Hormuud (a major telco in Somalia) launched in 2011. It dominates Southern Somalia’s market, enabling users to send money to each other, receive salaries, pay bills, and access remittances using mobile phones. EVCPlus accounts hold value and transactions are recorded via USSD or app.

ZAAD is a mobile money service launched in 2009 by Telesom in Somaliland. It is widely used for person-to-person transfers, merchant payments, and international remittances. ZAAD has extensive agent networks and is particularly prevalent in urban areas of Somaliland.

sistemas.detalhes: As a member of the CEMAC monetary union, Chad relies on the BEAC-operated SYGMA RTGS for large-value payments in Central African CFA francs (https://cenfri.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/Payment-systems-in-SSA-Note-2.pdf#:~:text=%5BPDF%5D%20Payment%20systems%20in%20sub,SYSTAC%29%20that) (https://cenfri.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/Payment-systems-in-SSA-Note-2.pdf#:~:text=These%20systems%2C%20which%20are%20operated,SYSTAC%29%20that). SYGMA settles interbank transfers, central bank operations, and other high-value transactions in real time across all banks in Chad and the region. Adoption is High among banks: it is the mandatory channel for any fund transfer above the threshold (e.g. ≥100 million XAF) (https://www.businessincameroon.com/finance/0207-5523-beac-launches-the-regional-committee-for-method-of-payment-monitoring-in-the-cemac-zone#:~:text=BEAC%20launches%20the%20Regional%20Committee,involving%20over%20100%20million%20FCFA) (https://www.businessincameroon.com/finance/0207-5523-beac-launches-the-regional-committee-for-method-of-payment-monitoring-in-the-cemac-zone#:~:text=It%20involves%20the%20automated%20gross,involving%20over%20100%20million%20FCFA), as well as for final settlement of net positions from clearing houses. The system significantly reduces settlement risk and delays. While transaction volumes are modest given Chad’s small financial sector, SYGMA ensures that government payments (like oil revenues or treasury transfers) and large corporate or NGO transactions clear safely. It operates daily with participation of the Chadian Treasury and all commercial banks. The value processed via SYGMA constitutes the bulk of payment value in the economy, though in count it’s minimal compared to retail transactions (which are mostly mobile money). Overall SYGMA usage in Chad is similar to CAR, with all institutions integrated and reliant on this regional RTGS backbone.

sistemas.descricao: Regional clearing of low-value payments (see C.A.R.)
sistemas.detalhes: Chadian banks use the SYSTAC automated clearing house – shared across CEMAC – for the net clearing of cheques, small electronic transfers, and other retail payment orders (https://cenfri.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/Payment-systems-in-SSA-Note-2.pdf#:~:text=%5BPDF%5D%20Payment%20systems%20in%20sub,SYSTAC%29%20that) (https://cenfri.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/Payment-systems-in-SSA-Note-2.pdf#:~:text=These%20systems%2C%20which%20are%20operated,SYSTAC%29%20that). SYSTAC operates in batch mode, aggregating transactions throughout the day and calculating multilateral net obligations for each bank, which are then settled via SYGMA. Adoption is Medium among formal financial institutions. Given Chad’s limited banking penetration, SYSTAC’s transaction volumes are relatively low, primarily comprising payroll transfers, government supplier payments, and the declining use of cheques. Regionally, SYSTAC processed ~1.1 million transactions in 2020 and rising (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=The%20Interbank%20Monetary%20Group%20of,and%20services%2C%C2%A0the%20central%20bank%20explained), but in Chad mobile money far exceeds bank-based retail volumes. Nonetheless, SYSTAC is critical for interbank interoperability of traditional payments. It allows, for example, a N’Djamena bank’s customer to deposit a cheque from another bank or to send a domestic transfer to a different bank. The system thus supports the conventional banking payment ecosystem even as digital alternatives grow outside it.

sistemas.descricao: Central Africa interbank card/mobile interoperability network
sistemas.detalhes: Chad participates in GIMAC, the regional interbank network that links payment channels among CEMAC countries. Through GIMAC’s infrastructure (the GIMACPAY switch), Chadian banks’ ATM/POS networks are connected and mobile money services are becoming interoperable across providers (https://www.mfw4a.org/news/gimac-payment-card-now-available-across-cemac#:~:text=GIMAC%20payment%20card%20now%20available,Chad%2C%20Equatorial%20Guinea%20and%20CAR) (https://www.mfw4a.org/news/gimac-payment-card-now-available-across-cemac#:~:text=terminals%20in%20Cameroon%2C%20Congo%2C%20Gabon%2C,Chad%2C%20Equatorial%20Guinea%20and%20CAR). GIMAC has rolled out a unified “GIMAC Card” accepted across Cameroon, Congo, Gabon, Chad, Equatorial Guinea and CAR (https://www.mfw4a.org/news/gimac-payment-card-now-available-across-cemac#:~:text=GIMAC%20payment%20card%20now%20available,Chad%2C%20Equatorial%20Guinea%20and%20CAR) (https://www.mfw4a.org/news/gimac-payment-card-now-available-across-cemac#:~:text=This%20card%20allows%20users%20to,Chad%2C%20Equatorial%20Guinea%20and%20CAR), so a Chadian bank card can withdraw cash or make payments in any member country. Additionally, local mobile wallets (e.g., Airtel Money Chad) can interconnect with others via GIMACPAY. Adoption in Chad is nascent but Growing: GIMAC’s network was extended to Chad around 2019, and banks have started issuing GIMAC-compatible cards. In 2022, GIMAC saw explosive growth in usage regionally, reaching 7.3 million transactions (https://trendsnafrica.com/cemac-countries-electronic-money-transactions-grew-ten-fold-in-two-years/#:~:text=The%20Interbank%20Monetary%20Group%20of,BEAC). In Chad, usage remains low due to fewer electronic payment users, but momentum is positive as more ATMs and agents join. GIMAC’s presence is expected to reduce transaction costs and foster cross-border trade (e.g., enabling a Cameroonian mobile wallet to send money to a Chadian wallet). As such, GIMAC is gradually enhancing Chad’s payment landscape by increasing interoperability and electronic payment acceptance.

sistemas.descricao: Phone-based e-wallets dominating domestic P2P payments
sistemas.detalhes: With less than 10% of Chadians holding bank accounts, mobile money services provided by telecom operators have become the primary non-cash payment method. Airtel Money (by Airtel) and Moov Money (formerly Tigo, now Moov Africa) allow users to deposit cash at agents and send money via mobile phone, pay bills, and buy goods. Adoption is High and rising: millions of Chadians use mobile money for remittances and daily transactions, given the vast distances and limited bank branches. Regionally in 2022, 96% of total payment count was via mobile money. In Chad, World Bank data shows mobile money accounts far outnumber bank accounts. While transaction values per person are low, the aggregate impact is significant for financial inclusion. Mobile money transactions are instant (within the same network) and typically denominated in CFA. Until recently, each provider’s wallet was a closed loop, but now GIMAC interoperability is being implemented. This will further boost usage as customers of different telcos can transact seamlessly. Mobile money in Chad is regulated by BEAC as e-money issuers. It has largely supplanted cheques and bank transfers for the general population, though it still operates alongside the cash economy. Overall, mobile money is a backbone of Chad’s payment system, especially in rural and unbanked segments.

sistemas.descricao: SYGMA is the real-time gross settlement system used by Chad and other CEMAC countries for large-value, time-critical transfers in XAF. (See Central African Republic’s SYGMA entry for details.) It is operated by BEAC and settles high-value interbank and financial market payments with instant finality across the six member states.

sistemas.nome: SYSTAC (Système de Télécompensation en Afrique Centrale)
sistemas.descricao: SYSTAC is the shared ACH for CEMAC countries, including Chad. (See CAR’s SYSTAC entry.) It nets low-value transactions like cheques and electronic transfers among banks, with daily net settlement via BEAC. This system enables efficient clearing of routine payments within Chad and across its regional neighbors under a common framework.

GIMACPAY provides the switching infrastructure for card withdrawals/payments and some mobile money interoperability across CEMAC, including Chad. (See CAR’s GIMACPAY entry.) It links ATMs and POS devices so that, for example, a debit card issued by a Chadian bank can be used throughout the region. It also lays groundwork for integrating mobile money with the banking system via a common platform.

Airtel Money is a leading mobile money service in Chad, operated by the telecom provider Airtel. It enables users to deposit cash into a mobile wallet, then send money to others, pay bills, and buy airtime using their phone. Given low banking penetration, Airtel Money has become a key payment method in Chad, though overall mobile money usage is still growing (around 15% of adults as of a few years ago) [oai_citation:55‡facebook.com]. Customers transact via USSD menus and agent networks. Airtel Money transactions are instant within the Airtel network, but not yet interoperable with bank accounts except through cash-in/out. The service significantly improves financial inclusion by providing basic payment capabilities in both urban and rural areas.
Mobile payment service
Competing mobile wallet

The WAEMU Instant Payment System is a new regional initiative launched by BCEAO in 2024 to enable instant, interoperable payments across all WAEMU countries including Togo. The system operates 24/7 and supports all types of accounts (banks, e-money issuers, microfinance institutions). It features QR code payments, payment requests, and aims to enhance financial inclusion across the region.

SICA-UEMOA (Système Interbancaire de Compensation Automatisé) is the regional ACH system for WAEMU countries operated by BCEAO. It processes retail payments including transfers under 50 million CFA francs, checks, bills of exchange, and promissory notes. The system operates in batch mode with end-of-day settlement through STAR-UEMOA.

STAR-UEMOA (Système de Transfert Automatisé et de Règlement) is the regional RTGS system operated by BCEAO for West African Economic and Monetary Union countries including Togo. It processes large-value and time-critical payments with real-time gross settlement. The system supports cross-border payments within the WAEMU region and serves as the settlement mechanism for other regional payment systems.

PromptPay is Thailand's flagship real-time payment system operated by National ITMX (co-owned by major banks) and overseen by the Bank of Thailand. It allows instant payments between any two accounts at different banks using proxy identifiers like mobile numbers, national ID numbers, or QR codes. The system supports P2P transfers, P2B payments, bulk payments, bill payments, and government disbursements. It processes over 538 transactions per person annually and handles $1.47 million in daily transactions.
Leading e-wallet

BAHTNET (Bank of Thailand Automated High-value Transfer Network) is Thailand's RTGS system for high-value and time-critical payments. Operated by the Bank of Thailand, it provides real-time gross settlement with immediate finality for transactions typically above 10 million baht. The system connects all major banks and financial institutions, supporting government payments, interbank settlements, and securities transactions through DvP mechanisms.

SMART (System for Managing Automated Retail Transfers) is Thailand's ACH system for processing bulk payments, salary disbursements, and recurring transactions. The system handles lower-value payments in batch mode, supporting direct credits and debits. It serves as the backbone for corporate payments, government salary payments, and utility bill collections.
Limited services
Dominant payment method

In December 2019, the National Bank of Tajikistan launched a modern Automated Transfer System (ATS) covering RTGS, ACH and a fast payments switch (IPS), provided by software vendor CMA [oai_citation:22‡cma.se]. It supports multi-currency interbank transfers and links to a National Processing Center for Remittances (NPCR) for mobile and cross-border transfers.

R-TiMOR (Rede Transferência iha Momentu Reál) is Timor-Leste's integrated payment system launched in 2015. Operated by the Central Bank of Timor-Leste (BCTL), it enables electronic payments between individuals, companies, and government organizations. The system supports both real-time gross settlement for high-value transactions and batch processing for lower-value payments. It features direct integration with the Ministry of Finance's GRP system for government payments.

Mosan Service is Timor-Leste's first authorized e-wallet service operated by Telemor Fintech. Licensed by BCTL in 2018, it provides mobile money services including money transfers, deposits, withdrawals, and merchant payments. The service operates through a network of 718 agents across the country, targeting financial inclusion for unbanked populations. Account limits are set at $500 maximum balance and $300 daily deposits.

P24 (Payment 24 hours) is Timor-Leste's national card switch system launched in 2018. Developed by SIBS International, it enables ATM and POS interoperability across banks and supports card-based transactions. The system connects to e-wallets and mobile payment services, with plans for regional connectivity to Indonesia and other ASEAN countries. It includes automated clearing house functionality for card transaction settlement.

DEPS is Tonga's domestic electronic payment system launched in 2021 by the National Reserve Bank of Tonga (NRBT). It includes real-time gross settlement capabilities, automated clearing house functions, digital check processing, and a central securities depository. The system processes both large-value time-critical payments and retail payment transactions, supporting the country's move toward digital payments.

LINX is Tonga's domestic card processing system that enables ATM and POS transactions across participating banks. The system provides local card processing capabilities and supports both debit and credit card transactions. It serves as the national card switch connecting banks and enabling interoperability for card-based payments.

sistemas.detalhes: Operated by the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey (CBRT), FAST enables 24/7 real-time fund transfers using mobile numbers or ID numbers. Transactions settle within seconds through CBRT infrastructure, supporting P2P, P2B, and G2P payments. Integrated with mobile banking apps and features QR code functionality. The system uses ISO 20022 standards and processes transactions through a centralized switch with immediate settlement finality .

Operates during business hours with immediate finality. Forms the backbone of Turkey's payment infrastructure with integrated risk controls .

sistemas.detalhes: 7 payment systems
