Contactless smart card

The Taiwan Clearing House (TCH) operates the check clearing system (CCS). Participating banks send check images/data to TCH, which calculates net positions. The net owed is settled on the CIFS RTGS. Check usage is declining but still accounts for millions of clearings annually.
CIFS processes NT-dollar interbank retail and large-value payments and is the backbone of Taiwan’s domestic financial infrastructure.

FISC (Financial Information Service Co.) operates FIS, which switches and clears low-value payments. It handles interbank remittances, ATM cash withdrawals/transfers, and supports POS. Most banks use FIS for retail transactions, linking into the RTGS for final settlement [oai_citation:67‡cbc.gov.tw]ww.cbc.gov.tw/en/cp-497-76129-FC1BB-2.html#:~:text=,interbank%20ATM%20withdrawals%20and%20transfers).

The National Credit Card Center of R.O.C. (NCCC) clears interbank credit card transactions (Visa, MC, domestic). It nets issuers and acquirers each day. The net positions are settled via the CIFS RTGS [oai_citation:68‡cbc.gov.tw]ww.cbc.gov.tw/en/cp-497-76129-FC1BB-2.html#:~:text=,tw).

Taiwan’s domestic debit/electronic card transactions are handled by networks connected to FISC. A national ATM/POS switch links banks’ POS terminals and ATMs, allowing interbank use of cards. Taiwan also has a domestic electronic money scheme (e.g. IC Card transit). These are integrated into FIS for clearing.

Operated by Taiwan’s Central Bank (CBC), the CIFS is a real-time gross settlement system for high-value NT dollar transactions [oai_citation:64‡cbc.gov.tw]ww.cbc.gov.tw/en/cp-497-76129-FC1BB-2.html#:~:text=,interbank%20ATM%20withdrawals%20and%20transfers). Created in 2002 (from manual transfers), it now settles interbank funding, securities trades, bond and FX swaps, and net obligations from other clearing systems. 85 institutions (39 banks, post office, branches, clearing orgs) participate [oai_citation:65‡cbc.gov.tw]ww.cbc.gov.tw/en/cp-497-76129-FC1BB-2.html#:~:text=1).
Dominant mobile money service
Competing mobile wallet

TACH is the automated clearing house in Tanzania for processing batches of interbank cheques and transfers. It operates under the Bank of Tanzania’s oversight. Transactions are netted and settled (at least on the same day) via banks’ accounts at the central bank [oai_citation:23‡bis.org]. (TACH is part of the legacy payment infrastructure, to be complemented by instant payments.)

Tanzania has extensive mobile money usage through operators like Vodacom (M-Pesa), Airtel, and Tigo, which allow sending/receiving funds via USSD and apps. With over 63 million mobile wallets by 2024 [oai_citation:27‡ippmedia.com], these services form a critical part of the payments ecosystem (interconnected via TIPS for interoperability).
TISS is Tanzania’s RTGS platform operated by the Bank of Tanzania. It settles high-value interbank transfers and net positions from TACH at central bank accounts in real time during business hours.

Launched in 2020 by the Bank of Tanzania, TIPS is a 24/7 real-time payments infrastructure for low-value transfers [oai_citation:24‡ippmedia.com]. It connects banks, mobile money operators, and other PSPs to enable immediate P2P/P2B transfers. TIPS was developed in-house to facilitate financial inclusion and has attracted all major players (over 63 million mobile wallets by 2024) [oai_citation:25‡ippmedia.com].
Banking super-app
Government payment platform

PROSTIR is Ukraine's national payment system developed by the NBU to facilitate electronic payments, cash withdrawals, and contactless transactions. Launched in 2017, it uses EMV chips and ISO 8583 standards, achieving ~98% POS acceptance. Supports co-badging with international schemes for foreign transactions.

Operated by the National Bank of Ukraine (NBU), SEP is the central RTGS infrastructure (ISO 20022-based) for final settlement of transfers between banks and the treasury. Introduced in 1995 and fully electronic since 2002, it ensures immediate and irrevocable settlements (24/7). It processes over 99% of interbank payments and averaged 1.2 million payments per day (UAH 653 billion) in 2023.

The NBU has explored a central bank digital currency (CBDC) called the e-hryvnia. It is envisioned as an electronic currency fully backed by reserves, intended to facilitate digital transactions. Currently, e-hryvnia is in research and pilot stage; no official issuance has occurred. Technical frameworks have been drafted, but it remains under development [oai_citation:3‡bank.gov.ua]ank.gov.ua/en/payments/e-hryvnia#:~:text=Skip%20to%20content).

The NBU launched an instant payment service (SEP Instant Transfers) enabling funds to move between bank accounts within seconds at any time (24/7). Implemented in late 2024 on SEP 4.1 with ISO 20022, it permits transfers by mobile number or other proxy, settling in under 10 seconds. All commercial banks are connected, allowing businesses and individuals to transfer money on weekends and holidays [oai_citation:0‡uzdaily.uz]ww.uzdaily.uz/en/central-bank-launches-an-instant-payment-system/#:~:text=This%20system%20allows%20to%20make,smooth%20and%20timely%20money%20transfers).

PROSTIR is a national card payment scheme developed by the NBU, supporting domestic debit cards and POS payments in UAH. It aims to improve payment security and reduce dependency on foreign card networks. Launched in 2020 and operated under NBU oversight, it is interoperable across all banks and ATMs in Ukraine. PROSTIR allows cardholders to pay and withdraw cash at domestic terminals, using a unique '9704' BIN range and local processing.

Launched in 2023 under SEP4.1, this service enables real-time credit transfers between banks and clients within 10 seconds using IBANs, mobile numbers, or emails. Mandatory for Ukrainian banks, it supports P2P/P2B transactions with immediate funds availability. Transaction limits initially set at UAH 50,000.

The e-hryvnia is a central bank digital currency (CBDC) being developed by the NBU. Initial 2018 pilot used anonymous wallets; 2025 pilot will involve real users with AML compliance. Use cases include targeted social aid, virtual asset transactions, and cross-border payments.
Dominant mobile wallet
Competing mobile wallet

FedNow, launched July 2023, is the Fed’s instant payment platform for near-immediate interbank payments in USD. It runs 24/7. In Q1 2025 it handled 1.31 million payments ($48.6 billion) [oai_citation:29‡frbservices.org]ww.frbservices.org/resources/financial-services/fednow/quarterly-volume-value-stats#:~:text=Error%20fetching), reflecting rapid adoption. FedNow expands instant P2P and business payments nationwide.

This is a premier electronic funds-transfer service operated by the Federal Reserve, designed for critical, high-value, same-day transactions. It functions as a real-time, gross settlement (RTGS) system, meaning each transaction is processed individually and settled immediately, with final and irrevocable transfers of funds. The Fedwire Funds Service is available 24/7 and is utilized by banks, businesses, and government agencies for purposes such as settling commercial payments, interbank positions, and federal tax payments. A significant modernization effort includes the implementation of the new ISO 20022 message format for Fedwire Funds Service by July 14, 2025, enhancing its capabilities and global alignment.
Batched electronic funds transfer system
Electronic processing of paper checks
Dominant card payment schemes
Private high-value payment system
Private-sector instant payment system

The ACH network facilitates efficient, low-cost batched payment services, primarily through FedACH products and services offered by the Federal Reserve. This system is widely used for direct deposits, bill payments, and various business-to-business (B2B) and consumer transactions. Key services include FedACH SameDay Service for quicker processing and FedGlobal ACH Payments for international transactions. The ACH network's operational rules are governed by NACHA, a non-governmental entity that sets guidelines underpinning a vast volume of domestic transactions.

CHIPS, run by The Clearing House, is a private USD clearing system for large-value payments (mainly international). It nets payments throughout the day and settles once daily for finality. On average it processes ~$1.8 trillion per business day [oai_citation:27‡theclearinghouse.org]ww.theclearinghouse.org/payment-systems/Articles/2024/04/CHIPS_Network_Migrates_ISO_20022_04-10-2024#:~:text=Financial%20institutions%20in%20the%20United,26%20in%20settled%20payment%20value), making it a key channel for dollar liquidity.

RTP, launched 2017 by The Clearing House, is a real-time rail for instant USD payments (up to $1M, recently raised to $10M). It connects 850+ institutions (70% of U.S. accounts). By Jan 2025 it had processed over 1 billion payments [oai_citation:31‡theclearinghouse.org]ww.theclearinghouse.org/payment-systems/Articles/2025/02/RTP_1Billion_TRX_02-03-2025#:~:text=New%20York%20%E2%80%93%20The%20RTP%C2%AE,44%20billion), with daily peaks >1.6M.

U.S. banks clear paper checks via image exchange (Check 21). Check images are routed through clearinghouses (e.g. the Federal Reserve’s FedImage). Check usage has declined (from ~14.5B in 2000 to ~4.7B in 2021).

Mobile P2P and e-wallet apps (Zelle, Venmo, PayPal, Cash App) run on ACH or card rails. Zelle is bank-led (11B payments in 2022, ~$490B) and Venmo (PayPal) is merchant-led. These apps have tens of millions of users and account for a growing share of peer-to-peer transactions in the U.S.

The FedNow Service represents a significant advancement in the U.S. payment landscape, offering a new instant payment infrastructure developed by the Federal Reserve. Launched in July 2023, it enables individuals and businesses to send and receive payments within seconds, 24 hours a day, every day of the year, ensuring immediate fund availability. This system is designed to provide rapid access to funds, which is critical for managing cash flows and avoiding late fees. The adoption of FedNow is projected to grow substantially, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 31.7% by volume between 2023 and 2028. While the Federal Reserve does not provide a direct consumer app, banks and credit unions integrate FedNow into their existing platforms to offer instant payment services to their customers.
Processes recurring payments like payroll, invoices, and government benefits. Settlement within 1–2 business days. Handled 33.56B transactions ($86.2T) in 2024. Migrating to ISO 20022 by 2025.
Payment network
Neobank platform

The Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU) operates an RTGS system (AGATA, migrating to RTX/S) for immediate settlement of interbank UYU payments [oai_citation:35‡bcu.gub.uy]ww.bcu.gub.uy/Ingles/Paginas/Payment-Settlement.aspx#:~:text=settlements%20occur%20immediately%20and%20irrevocably%2C,instruction%20per%20instruction). It settles large-value transfers, FX trades, and government transactions instantly. It also settles net positions from retail clearing.

Tuapp is an open mobile wallet launched by state telecom ANTEL and state bank BROU [oai_citation:36‡inswitch.com]ww.inswitch.com/blog/tuapp-uruguay#:~:text=Image). It allows peer-to-peer transfers, QR code merchant payments, bill pay, and government subsidies without requiring a bank account [oai_citation:37‡inswitch.com]ww.inswitch.com/blog/tuapp-uruguay#:~:text=Tuapp%20is%20the%20first%20application,mobile%20phone%20operator%20he%2Fshe%20has). It has over 700,000 active users and was used to distribute 1.3 million COVID-19 subsidies [oai_citation:38‡inswitch.com]ww.inswitch.com/blog/tuapp-uruguay#:~:text=700K%2B%20Active%20Users).

Uruguay’s interbank clearing house nets retail payments (checks, ATM/POS transactions, electronic transfers) daily. Banks send transaction batches to the clearing; the net obligations are settled through the RTGS. This includes check and card clearing.
Operated by Banco Central del Uruguay, clears interbank and high-value transfers in real time. Also supports deferred net settlement for ACH instructions. Handled over 120 million operations in 2023.
Mobile payments
Digital wallet

Humo is a UZS-denominated card scheme launched by Uzbekistan’s Central Bank in 2019 to complement UzCard. By 2022 it had ~7 million Humo cards issued [oai_citation:45‡flow.stitch.money]low.stitch.money/post/fintech-in-uzbekistan#:~:text=According%20to%20the%20CBU%2C%20as,to%20reach%20140%2C000%20units). Humo cards function like debit cards at ATMs/POS and are interoperable with UzCard terminals since 2023.

Payme, founded in 2013, is another major digital wallet in Uzbekistan. It supports online/offline payments, transfers, and bill/pay top-ups. It has ~9 million users [oai_citation:49‡flow.stitch.money]low.stitch.money/post/fintech-in-uzbekistan#:~:text=discounts%20and%20has%20its%20own,wallets%2C%20as%20well%20as%20to) and offers cashback rewards. It was partially acquired by TBC Bank in 2018.

Apelsin is a mobile wallet originally from Kapital Bank, now part of Uzum. It provides P2P transfers, QR payments, and integrates with e-commerce. By early 2023, it was being rebranded and integrated with Uzum marketplace [oai_citation:51‡flow.stitch.money]low.stitch.money/post/fintech-in-uzbekistan#:~:text=,Uzum%20Market%2C%20a%20local%20marketplace).

Developed by the Central Bank of Uzbekistan, enables 24/7 instant interbank transfers for legal entities and entrepreneurs. Transactions settle in seconds, operating continuously including weekends/holidays.

UzCard is a domestic EMV card scheme (est. 2004). It issues debit cards linked to UZS accounts. By 2022 there were ~23 million UzCard cards in circulation [oai_citation:43‡flow.stitch.money]low.stitch.money/post/fintech-in-uzbekistan#:~:text=According%20to%20the%20CBU%2C%20as,to%20reach%20140%2C000%20units). UzCard cards are used for ATM/POS payments domestically and are widely accepted nationwide.

CLICK, launched in 2011, is a major payment platform in Uzbekistan. It allows bank transfers, bill payments, QR payments, and e-commerce purchases. It has over 11 million users in a 34M population [oai_citation:47‡flow.stitch.money]low.stitch.money/post/fintech-in-uzbekistan#:~:text=,wallets%2C%20as%20well%20as%20to), making it the most popular payment app in the country.

The Uzbekistan central bank launched an Instant Payments System in 2020 for round-the-clock transfers between bank accounts [oai_citation:40‡uzdaily.uz]ww.uzdaily.uz/en/central-bank-launches-an-instant-payment-system/#:~:text=Tashkent%2C%20Uzbekistan%20%28UzDaily.com%29%20,made%20online%20around%20the%20clock). All banks participate. It supports immediate P2P and B2B transfers any time, including weekends. From Feb–Nov 2020 it processed 3.5 million transactions totaling ~UZS 83.6 trillion [oai_citation:41‡uzdaily.uz]ww.uzdaily.uz/en/central-bank-launches-an-instant-payment-system/#:~:text=In%20the%20period%20from%20February,8%20trillion%20soums).

Domestic debit/prepaid card network launched in 2019. Processes transactions in soums with lower fees than international cards. Achieved interoperability with UzCard in 2023. Supports international usage via co-badging.
Uzbekistan's first domestic card scheme (2004). Processes ATM withdrawals, POS, and e-commerce transactions in UZS. Operates parallel to HUMO with interoperability achieved in 2023.
Integration with Italy
Common payment method

Vatican City uses the euro and relies on Italy’s banking/payment systems. Transactions (transfers, checks, etc.) are cleared via European systems (e.g. Italy’s TARGET2 for large transfers, SEPA for euro payments). The Institute for Works of Religion (IOR) would use ECB/European interbank systems.

Visa and Mastercard operate in Vatican City for card payments by residents and visitors. All transactions are in euros and processed by global networks. There is no separate Vatican-specific card network.

Vatican banks participate fully in SEPA via dedicated IBANs since 2019. Payments are processed through Italian RTGS and SEPA systems operated by Banca d’Italia. No independent domestic payment infrastructure.

ECACH handles electronic funds transfers across ECCU member countries including Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. Supports cheque imaging (Phase 1) and electronic funds transfer (Phase 2), enabling cross-border payments within the Eastern Caribbean region.
Primary payment method
Crypto payments

Pago Móvil is an interbank mobile payment system in Venezuela, connecting major banks. Users link their mobile numbers to accounts and can transfer funds via SMS/app. It has become a common way to send small payments between individuals.

Visa and Mastercard operations have been disrupted in Venezuela by sanctions and currency controls. Cards were disabled by issuers (2018) and partially re-enabled for some institutions in 2023. They still serve USD accounts and ATM withdrawals in limited fashion.

sistemas.nome: LBTR (Sistema de Liquidación Bruta en Tiempo Real)
sistemas.descricao: Central Bank of Venezuela's RTGS system launched in 2010. Handles high-value interbank and urgent payments with immediate finality. Uses SWIFT MT formats over FedLine/SWIFTNet. Operates on weekdays (08:00–14:00).

The petro is a cryptocurrency launched by the Venezuelan government in 2018, purportedly backed by oil reserves. It was meant for certain transactions and to bypass sanctions. Adoption has been minimal (mostly propaganda); it is not widely accepted in practice.

The Central Bank of Venezuela (BCV) operates the domestic payment infrastructure for the bolívar. It includes an RTGS for large interbank transfers and a clearing house for retail payments. However, hyperinflation has caused many transactions to shift to USD/dollar channels or informal markets.

BiopagoBDV is a mobile wallet/service from Banco de Venezuela using biometric authentication (fingerprint, face) for payments. It integrates with ATMs and PoS for quick transactions. It was introduced to modernize e-payments, but has limited adoption.
Dominant e-wallet
National QR standard

ViettelPay is the mobile wallet service from Viettel (state telecom). It supports transfers, bill payment, and merchant QR scans. With ~25% market share [oai_citation:60‡2c2p.com]c2p.com/blog/vietnam-payment-methods#:~:text=Below%20are%20the%20top%20digital,Looking%20ahead%2C%20Vietnam%27s), it leverages Viettel’s large subscriber base for wide reach.

NAPAS (National Payment Corporation of Vietnam) manages the country’s payment network. It connects 20,600 ATMs and 741,000 POS devices across 68 banks, serving 80 million accounts [oai_citation:52‡en.napas.com.vn]n.napas.com.vn/#:~:text=NAPAS%20is%20currently%20managing%20and,including%20banks%20and%20financial%20companies). NAPAS provides domestic card clearing, ATM switching, bill payments, and launched the FastFund 247 instant transfer service (24/7) [oai_citation:53‡en.napas.com.vn]n.napas.com.vn/#:~:text=NAPAS%20FastFund%20247%20Service). It is central to Vietnam’s electronic payments.
Processes high-value RTGS and deferred ACH instructions for all banks. Governed by State Bank of Vietnam (SBV). Migration to ISO 20022 underway with completion planned for 2026.

MoMo is Vietnam’s most popular mobile wallet (super-app). It offers P2P transfers, QR payments, bill pay, and tickets. It holds roughly 47% of the e-wallet market in Vietnam [oai_citation:57‡2c2p.com]c2p.com/blog/vietnam-payment-methods#:~:text=Below%20are%20the%20top%20digital,Looking%20ahead%2C%20Vietnam%27s), with millions of users and wide merchant acceptance.

ZaloPay is an e-wallet integrated with the Zalo messaging app. It enables QR payments, transfers, and online purchases. It holds about 17% of Vietnam’s e-wallet market [oai_citation:59‡2c2p.com]c2p.com/blog/vietnam-payment-methods#:~:text=Below%20are%20the%20top%20digital,Looking%20ahead%2C%20Vietnam%27s) and is especially popular among young users.

VietQR is the unified national QR code payment scheme, managed by the State Bank of Vietnam. It allows interoperability between banks and e-wallets. Payments are made by scanning QR codes (NVBC standard); NAPAS supports VietQR in FastFund with limits (max 500M VND per txn) [oai_citation:56‡en.napas.com.vn]n.napas.com.vn/#:~:text=NAPAS%20FastFund%20247%20with%20VietQR,Service).
Main clearing hub for cards and retail transfers since 2004. Supports ATM, POS, real-time interbank transfers, VietQR, and e-wallets. Processes over 30 million transactions monthly.

FastFund 247 is NAPAS’s real-time retail payment service launched in 2020. It enables instant account-to-account transfers anytime using account number or VietQR. Transactions settle immediately, improving everyday payment speed and availability [oai_citation:55‡en.napas.com.vn]n.napas.com.vn/#:~:text=NAPAS%20FastFund%20247%20Service).
Dominant method

The Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV) operates the central payment system. It processes interbank transfers and net settlements for banks. Large payments may be processed via offshore correspondent banking in AUD/NZD due to liquidity. Domestic interbank transfers settle on the RTGS ledger maintained by RBV.

sistemas.nome: VANKLIA (Vanuatu Automated National Clearing and Interchange)
sistemas.descricao: Launched in 2023 as a greenfield ISO 20022 system. Replaces manual cheque clearing and supports RTGS, bulk ACH, instant payments, and card clearing. Designed to boost digital financial services and inclusion.

Mobile money wallets are widely used in Vanuatu. MTN Mobile Money and Digicel’s M-Paisa allow P2P transfers, merchant payments, and bill payments via mobile phones. They are crucial in rural areas with limited banking access.
Visa and Mastercard are the main card networks used in Vanuatu for debit/credit transactions. No local card scheme exists; Vanuatu’s ATMs and POS terminals connect to these international networks.
MyCash is Digicel Samoa’s mobile money service. It allows P2P transfers, bill payments and airtime top-up via mobile phones:contentReference[oaicite:42]{index=42}.
SATS is a new national RTGS launched in 2023 by the Central Bank of Samoa for real-time interbank payments:contentReference[oaicite:40]{index=40}:contentReference[oaicite:41]{index=41}.

MyCash (formerly M-Paisa) is Digicel Samoa’s mobile money service. Users deposit cash at agents and then send P2P transfers, pay merchants or bills via their mobile phones [oai_citation:43‡digicelpacific.com]. It allows QR and contactless payments. Launched by Digicel, MyCash has expanded inclusion by allowing the unbanked to transact digitally [oai_citation:44‡digicelpacific.com].

SATS is the Central Bank of Samoa’s new RTGS launched in 2023 [oai_citation:41‡ifc.org]. It enables immediate electronic interbank transfers 24×7, replacing manual cheque clearing. Retail and government payments settle in real time with finality, significantly reducing clearing delays [oai_citation:42‡ifc.org]. It was developed with international support to boost financial inclusion and reduce cash usage.
Local banks issue Visa and Mastercard debit/credit cards, which are accepted for POS and online payments in Samoa.

Within the IPS, the ACH portion nets small-value transfers (e.g. payroll, retail credits) on a periodic basis. Net obligations from these clearings are settled via the RTGS. This structure mimics European-style payment clearing.

The Central Bank of Kosovo (CBK) operates a single interbank system (IPS) comprising an RTGS component (for real-time large-value transfers) and an ACH component for batch clearing [oai_citation:63‡bqk-kos.org]ww.bqk-kos.org/repository/docs/SistemiIPagesave/Kosovo%20-%20Blue%20Book%20-%20FINAL%20%28english%29.pdf#:~:text=1,PSD%20is). It processes all euro-denominated payments between banks and the government in Kosovo.
Operated by the Central Bank of Kosovo, the IPS includes both RTGS and bulk payment capabilities, migrated to ISO 20022 in 2016.
Primary payment method
Informal transfers
Built by BPC’s SmartVista, WeNet is Yemen’s national instant payment platform connecting more than 6 banks, offering 24/7 retail payments and interoperability.

Multiple Yemeni mobile network operators have introduced mobile money wallets to increase financial inclusion. For example, MTN Yemen’s SabaFon launched Saba Pay, and Yemen Mobile offers mPay. These allow P2P transfers and bill payments via USSD or apps. However, adoption is hampered by conflict and limited banking infrastructure.
Yemen banks use the SWIFT network for large interbank and cross-border payments. Operates with traditional SWIFT MT formats.
UNMoney consolidates all money transfer companies into a unified platform to streamline domestic and international transfers.

Yemeni banks use SWIFT for international transfers and internal ledgers for local payments. However, dual currencies and divided government (north/south) have fragmented systems. Electronic interbank transfers exist but are unreliable. Cash remains the default for most transactions.

Hawala is a traditional informal system used in Yemen for domestic and international transfers, leveraging trust-based networks of money brokers. It is widely used for remittances from abroad. Although not a formal scheme, it is a key channel when formal payment systems are disrupted.
SnapScan is a South African mobile wallet app that lets users pay merchants by scanning QR codes on their smartphones. It links to the user’s bank cards for instant payments, popular in retail.
Zapper is a mobile payment platform that allows consumers to pay via QR codes and manage loyalty rewards. It supports credit/debit card payments through the app and is used in South African retail.

South Africa participates in the SADC-RTGS (formerly SIRESS) for cross-border payments within the Southern African Development Community. This system, operated by SARB, settles payments in real time among participating central banks.

The Automated Clearing House (run by BankservAfrica) nets bulk retail payments (e.g. salaries, bill payments, debit orders) between banks. It settles the aggregated net positions multiple times per day.
Visa credit and debit cards are widely used in South Africa. All major banks issue Visa, and Visa cards are accepted by virtually all merchants and ATMs nationwide.
Mastercard (including Maestro) cards are also widely used in South Africa. They complement Visa, with broad acceptance by merchants and ATMs across the country.
Vodacom’s M-Pesa was a mobile money service launched in 2010 that allowed P2P transfers via mobile phones. It had limited uptake and was discontinued in 2016.

South African Multiple Option Settlement (SAMOS) is the RTGS platform operated by the SARB for settling large-value payments in ZAR. It provides immediate final settlement in central bank money for interbank transfers and monetary policy operations. SAMOS was introduced in 1998 and modernized with SAMOS II in 2018.

BankservAfrica operates the National Payments System (NPS) clearing functions, including cheque clearing, bulk payments, and ATM/POS switches. It runs the Automated Clearing Bureau (cheques), Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) system, and SASWITCH for electronic payments. Bankserv nets obligations and settles through SAMOS.

SASWITCH is the domestic network switch for card payments, owned by major banks. It interconnects ATMs and POS devices so cards issued by any bank can be accepted anywhere. Transactions are routed through SASWITCH and settled via Bankserv. It enables EFTPOS, ATM withdrawals and card payments on local cards.

PayShap is the new interbank instant payment service launched by South African banks and overseen by SARB in 2023. It allows 24/7 real-time transfers using bank-generated proxies (mobile numbers or IDs). It aims to boost retail payment digitization and lower fees for instant transfers.
Mobile payment service
Competing mobile wallet

Zambia’s Automated Clearing House processes bulk payments like salaries and recurring payments. It clears vouchers and checks in scheduled batches, typically next-day or same-day. Net positions are settled on the RTGS.

sistemas.nome: Mobile Money (MTN Mobile Money, Airtel Money)
sistemas.descricao: Mobile money services by telecom operators (MTN and Airtel) are extremely popular in Zambia. They allow users to deposit cash into mobile wallets and send/receive payments via phone. With wide agent networks, they serve rural and urban customers, often exceeding bank electronic transaction volumes.

ZAMSWITCH is Zambia’s national interbank switching system. It connects all ATM and POS devices of member banks, enabling any bank’s ATM card to work anywhere in the country. ZAMSWITCH also links to international networks (Visa/Mastercard) for card payments.

The Bank of Zambia runs an RTGS system for interbank settlements in kwacha. All commercial banks connect to ZAMSWITCH, the national electronic payments switch, to transfer large sums in real time. It also settles netted obligations from retail clearings.
NFS links all financial products such as ATMs, POS, wallets, and mobile to promote financial inclusion. It uses an ISO 8583 message format.
Zambia participates in the SADC RTGS project for cross-border transfers using the South African Reserve Bank’s platform. Settlements are made in ZAR.
ZIPSS is Zambia’s RTGS operated by the Bank of Zambia. It provides settlement for large interbank payments and is compliant with ISO 20022.

sistemas.nome: ZIPSS (Zambia Interbank Payment and Settlement System)

sistemas.descricao: Mobile payment service
Competing mobile wallet

The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (RBZ) implemented the RTGS$ (later ZWL) digital currency for electronic settlements. The RTGS network clears interbank transfers in local currency. This effectively became Zimbabwe’s primary currency after abandonment of the old dollar, although foreign currency and inflation complicate its use.
Operated by the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe, upgraded in 2024 to support ISO 20022 messaging and dual currency (ZiG and USD).
ZIPIT allows users to send and receive money instantly between banks and wallets. It supports merchant payments and P2P transfers.

Visa and Mastercard networks operate in Zimbabwe for ATM withdrawals and card payments, denominated in USD or ZWL. Local banks issue Visa/Mastercards. The national ATM switch (Link) connects to these networks as well.

OneMoney (formerly Telecash) is Telecel’s mobile wallet. It offers P2P transfers and payments via USSD/app. Market share is smaller than EcoCash, but it provides additional financial inclusion for Telecel subscribers.

EcoCash is Zimbabwe’s dominant mobile money platform. It lets users deposit cash and transact via phone. In 2023, EcoCash’s daily volume exceeded that of traditional payment systems, with ~112 trillion ZWL electronic flows (33% y/y increase) [oai_citation:61‡precisemrc.co.zw]ww.precisemrc.co.zw/blog/show/99/electronic-transactions-dominate-national-payment-systems#:~:text=The%20Reserve%20Bank%20of%20Zimbabwe,the%20period%20of%20one%20year). Over half of Zimbabwean adults use EcoCash for payments and transfers.

Checks still clear via Zimbabwe’s interbank clearing house. Volume is small compared to electronic channels, but the clearing house (via RTGS settlement) nets any remaining paper cheque transactions daily.
